1.s: Davey Holcomb, a young boy with a reputation for making mistakes, learns there's a positive side to failure.
q: When it got next to Davey, it crashed right over!
Well, that was just a coincidence.
No, that was just the beginning.
I broke your machine, Mr. Whittaker! I broke it!

When you're a Christian, nothing you do in faith is really a failure. God's gonna use it somehow — maybe not in the way you expect. But He'll use it. You just have to be patient, and persistent, even if it takes... well, years.

2.s: Craig Moorhead’s middle school friends like having him around because he makes them laugh. However, when Craig faces a problem that isn’t funny at all, and his friends aren’t so friendly anymore, he realizes that just having a sense of humor isn’t enough to keep his friends.
q: Your son Craig — he’s funny.
He's no stranger than most boys.
It kinda reminds me of the story of Joseph in the Bible.
Yeah? How’s that?
You know, a cone of many colors...
I want you to shut up for a while.
You want me to shut up? Is that what you said? You want me to shut up? Okay, I’ll shut up. You won’t hear another peep out of me. I wouldn’t DREAM of talking on and on when someone asked me to...
Knock knock!
Who’s there?
Orange you gonna open the door? It's cold out here!

If you look at anything at all that God created, you’ll find a little reminder about how much He loves us and how He wants us to live — even raspberry seeds. You just gotta look at them the right way. You know, I think the Lord planned it like that.
Well, if you don't like it, take it home and give it to your dog!
I thought you liked my dog.

3.s: A huge power failure leaves Odyssey without any light. Several kids stranded at Whit's End find out what life without electricity is all about -- and how much fun it can be.
q: Now, the first thing people usually do at a time like this is panic.
Then it looks like we're doing things in the right order!
Momma, don't let your housekeepers grow up to be cowboys!
You're not making a movie without a permit, are you?
Permit? I didn't know you needed a permit to make a movie!
You don't, Bobby. Not as long as you own private property or you're not obstructing traffic or something like that. Isn't that right, Officer Harley?
Well, it isn't exactly wrong. Not that it couldn't be, mind you 'cause ignorance of the law is no excuse! But as far as wrong goes, yes, you're right!
Hi, it's me. Listen, I'm really sorry about yesterday.
Well, I hope so! I'm glad you called, Jim!
Jim? Who's Jim? Sandy, is that you?
Uh... is this 555-7475?
Communicate, communicate, just open up your heart and communicate. We gotta share ideas, there’s no time to wait, and the best way to do it is communicate.

4.s: Even though teenager Connie Kendall has just moved into Odyssey, she can hardly wait to go back to California…and 10-year-old Bobby has secretly made up his mind that he's going with her.
q: You're worried cause Connie
Well, as a matter of fact, yes! That's a big part of it!
Then you can relax.
Cause I talked it over with Connie and she's not going off by herself to California after all.
Oh, she's not?
No way. I'm going with her!
I'll talk about Jesus on the mount of transfiguration. Okay?
Mr. Whittaker?
Well, you can take your pick of Scripture references. The story is in the book of Matthew, Mark and...
Mr. Whittaker!?
Freddy, I'll be right with you! Marianne Josephs
I mean, you never know when your next discovery might be. Why, excitement could be waiting for us right on the other side of that door!
Uh, yeah. Could you tell me how to get to Front Street?
Who were Shadrach, Meesh... a-lack...
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
Yeah, yeah! What he said!
That sense of adventure is hard to hold on to, but sometimes it's just a matter of how you look at things. You never know when your next discovery will happen.

Every time you come in contact with another human being, something happens. Neither one of you is quite the same ever again. You can't drift through life thinking you're never going to influence anybody. God made each and every one of us dependent on other people. He wants us to feel some sort of responsibility towards each other. What type of world would we live in if we didn't care for one another?
Any place you live is what you make of it.

5.s: Mr. Whittaker tells a "fractured" version of a famous Christmas story, starring an unusual couple named Madge and Guy.
q: Your face! What is it?
Oh, it's just this thing I keep on the front of my head. You know, a couple of eyes, a nose, a mouth...
Come on, I've got a few cents left over! Let's go down to that little place on the corner and split a child's portion, diet-mini-cheeseburger!
It's right here in the want ads.
No thank you, I've got some right here.
Is this Pop's Top Notch Top Shop?
Nice delivery.
Why Madge darling! Are you crying? What is it?
It's when your face gets all red and tears run down your cheeks.
No, no, dear. I mean, what's the matter?

You mean besides the fact that it's Christmas Eve and I haven't done any shopping and even if I did I couldn't buy what I want because what I want is something really special and all the money I have in the world is one dollar and eighty-seven cents?
Yeah, besides that!

6.s: The morning after Christmas, a young girl who's already bored with her presents wanders into Whit's End looking for something to do.
q: I don’t like it back here. It smells bad.
It’s an alley — it’s supposed to smell bad.
How many cats do you see here?
What do you need, a calculator?
Seven, okay?
Uh, well, can I ask you... uh... well...
If I had such a good family, and with all I had going for me, how come I ended up in a broken-down shack in Forest Creek? Isn’t that the gist of it?
I didn’t mean to be rude. I'm sorry.
Oh, no, no. You weren’t rude, child. I was rude. You were just naturally curious, that’s all.

7.s: Connie makes a resolution to be more patient no matter what, which turns out to be far more difficult than she imagined.
q: ...By the way, tell her we got a dog too. A beautiful golden Labrador retriever. You know what we call her? Kitty!

You see Connie, you believe that deep down everyone is good and if we all just somehow tap into that inner goodness we can make the world a whole lot nicer. Well I'm sorry, but that's just not the case. The Bible says that all have sinned and fallen short of the glory of God. That's why I just shake my head and laugh when I hear someone make a promise to be a better person. That's like treating the symptoms and ignoring the disease.
But you can't just sit back and do nothing! I mean, doesn't the Bible say the Lord helps those who helps themselves?
No, it doesn't. Besides, I'm not talking about doing nothing, I'm just saying that the cause of the problems runs a lot deeper than a simple promise can reach, no matter how good your intentions are.
So I was right when I said it was hopeless.

No, there's hope, lots of it. You're just putting it in the wrong place. You've got to look deep down on the inside, way down into your soul. That's where the changing has to start. That's why the Bible says "Don't be conformed to the world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind." What that means is we have to let God renew our mind. He's got to change us on the inside before results start showing on the outside.

8.s: A boy plants fear in the heart of his younger sister as she anticipates her first major dental appointment. Unfortunately for him, his plans backfire.
q: What’s the magic word?
Well, that works too.
Frisky doesn't go to the dentist.
That's because he's a dog, sweetie. Uh, Bob, why don't dogs go to the dentist?
Bob, how about I give you a more distinctive choice?
Like, what would you like, Bob? A bottle of Tabasco, or some angel foodcake?

9.s: Sixth-grader Johnny Bickle tries to figure out how to practice the Golden Rule.
q: Anybody? Anybody at all? Anybody who's breathing will do!

10.s: Shirley Ziegler is afraid of just about everything. But when a real emergency comes up at Whit's End, she is forced to face her worst fear.
q: Danny, maybe you should tell Connie about this table.
The table, tell Connie that it wobbles.
It does? Oh, yes, it does! Doesn't it?
Connie, I think you've better have a look at this table.
Why, what's wrong with it?
It's wobbly. I don't think it's safe for children my age.
You don't think it's safe? What are you going to do, drive it home? You know, I really worry about you kids sometimes.
You're not afraid of me, are you?
No, of course not!
Well, see boys?
Except when you wear your big black overcoat. It's kinda creepy.

11.s: A young girl named Joey tries a variety of bizarre methods to get her friend Stefanie to go on a diet.
q: I've got just the thing! The NFL diet!
NFL? Like the Football league?
Yeah! Every time she reaches for food, you tackle her!
Oh, hi, Whit! Caught this suspect committing a 414.
What's a 414?
Grand Theft Mozzarella!
Freeze! Police! Back away slowly, go for the cheese and you'll have it!

12.s: Connie reads the story of Jeremy Forsythe, a boy who tells his mother a fib about some missing money. Both Jeremy and Connie learn that one lie leads to another.
q: Now, what we're going to have to do here is gather all the pertinent facts, and you know the quickest way for us to do that is?
By getting a real police officer?
No, but that was a good guess. The easiest way to gather all the pertinent facts is by using what we call in the trade the four W's. That's who, what, where and when.
What about why?
Make that the five W's.
And let's not forget how...
All right, the five W's and an H! Anybody want to add any more letters?
Sounds like Jeremy's getting himself in pretty deep. I think I know how this is going to turn out, too.
Well, maybe you do, maybe you don't. The only way to find out is to keep reading.
Well, take my word for it, son: even when you're grown up, someone's still making decisions for you.
Roger, I need you to do something for me!
See what I mean?

13.s: Young Bobby gets a note from Amy, who thinks that he's the cutest boy in school. Bobby, however, wants to stay as far from Amy as possible.
q: So, what kind of poison is the cafeteria serving today?
I can't tell. It smells like my dad's sneakers.
Let me see. Is meat supposed to be green? And what are those little round purple things supposed to be?
Look, Jeff. I have to eat this stuff! I don't want to think about it.
David Harley

14.s: Middle-schooler Rachel Weaver is late for everything. But when Connie threatens to kick her off the volleyball team, Rachel tries her very best to be on time.
q: Okay, everybody on the bus!
Alright children, we don’t want a riot here. Let’s have a little orderly dispersal: I want everybody to line up alphabetically according to their height!
We're waiting for Rachel Weaver
Rachel Weaver?
You need to learn to be—
Punctuated! I know, Dad. John Whittaker
Oh, no! I’m late for school again!

Rachel Weaver, you’re late for school again. Just for that, you’re going to have to come in every Saturday... for the rest of your life. And next time, wear something besides pajamas when you come to school!

15.s: Phillip Callas gets angry during baseball practice and tells his younger brother Dean to go home. When Dean doesn't return home, the police get involved and try to track down the boy.
q: And if they dared you to jump off a bridge, would you?
This is a project about building. You don’t know anything about building.
Yes I do. I helped you and Dad build the doghouse out back. Remember?
Yeah, I remember. You just about killed us. You chased Spike all over the yard trying to measure him. You made me spill paint all over my pants. You made Dad hit his finger with the hammer.
Dad said bad words.
Yeah, and I wanted to.

16.s: Chris Gottlieb, a man in a wheelchair, and Meg Stevens, a girl with a lot of questions, form an odd friendship when they help each other out.
q: There are no stupid questions.
Well pardon me, I stand corrected.
Pardon me again, I sit corrected.

17.s: Monty Whittaker-Dowd, Whit's grandson, comes to visit for the summer, and learns a few lessons along the way.
q: Well, you know, Whit. It just occurred to me, if Monty wants to. He could be a Coyote.
Well, he can play on the team. The Coyotes. Little League, Whit!

The boy thought that loving the puppy meant giving him what he wanted, but in this case the most loving thing was to give him what he needed whether he liked it or not. It was the little boy's job to recognize the hidden danger the puppy couldn't understand.

You see, we all have to live by the rules Monty. I don't just make them up, you know. God is the one who sets down the rules about what people do and how we ought to treat each other. And if I love you, if I really love you, not only will I obey those rules myself, I'll do what I can to see that you do too. I don't get any pleasure out of it. I do it because I love you. and because that's the responsibility God's given me, at least for these few weeks.

18.s: Whit, Jana, and Monty finally resolve their problems.
q: How'd you know to come down here? We were just trying to call ya.
Call me? Why?
Yeah, Jeff had been patrolling down by your store just now. He heard some glass breaking. He picked up a kid crawling in your back window. Says he's your grandson.
Oh! Thank the Lord!
I wish everyone'd look that relieved when I've told them they've been vandalized.

19.s: Whit’s best friend, Tom Riley, tells Connie the story of how Whit's End was created amid tragic circumstances.
q: Whit, you old grump.

Mr. Glossman has a lot of bright ideas on how to modernize this city so it can make more money. But there's some of us here who like the old things, Mr. Whittaker, who don't want our town to become all chrome and glass, and your wife was one of those people.

UPF proposes to rebuild the recreation center. And I'm quoting now: "As a place of adventure and discovery, filled with books and activities, fun and games, arts and crafts, and uplifting conversation. But most of all, it will be a place where kids of all ages can just be kids."

So, I think you'll agree that the single biggest cause of juvenile delinquency in the country these days is young people! Now, I realize that may sound like a generalization, but if you take a look at a cross-section of all J.D.'s — uh, that stands for "juvenile delinquents" — you'd probably find that most of them — most of them — are between the ages of five and eighteen years of age. Coincidence? Maybe. But do we really wanna take the chance? I, for one, don't think so!

20.s: Billy Barton, the bully of Odyssey Elementary, gets into a fight with Mike Caldwell. When Mike wins, he becomes arrogant and lets stardom go to his head.
q: Just remember David and Goliath.
I don't own a slingshot.
But you do have something better.
Billy Barton
Here Freddy, hold these.
Sure, Mike, anything I can do to help!
Good, then you fight Billy Barton
Anything you need held, I mean.
You're a real pal, Freddy.
Mike Caldwell
Stand still! Are you crazy?!?!
Bring a bun and some mustard.
A bun and mustard? Why?
Cause I'm gonna turn ya into hamburger, that's why!
Mom, would you take a good look at me?
Sure, but why?
You might wanna remember me as I was.
Billy, have you ever heard of David and Goliath?
Yeah, they're a new rock group, right?

21.s: When a model train car goes missing form Whit's End, many kids suspect Michelle Terry, a girl with a bad reputation.
q: Whit! Hury up. Warren's mom is honking and the vacuum is eating the carpet.
Hah ut oh. Come on Warren we better get down there before the vacuum starts honking and your mom starts eating the carpet.
Fine, I didn't have any cavities. Of course, I never do.
Really? You know my mother was that way. She never got any cavities either. Of course she had false teeth. I wonder if that had something to do with it?
Help! Call the police! The FBI! The National Guard! Somebody dial 9-1-1!
Whoa whoa whoa-oh slow down there Warren. What's the matter?
Somebody stole my Silver Streak.
Well after looking at this with an expert eye, there is only one possible conclusion.
And that is?
The Silver Streak is missing.
You did do it, didn't you. Didn't you!
Yah, I did it.
You mean you planed this whole thing?

Planned? It didn't take much planning. When you were talking on the stairs with Connie I had just enough time to grab the Silver Streak and put it in my nap sack. Then after I helped Connie, I got all my stuff and left. Only I went around to the back, I was just gonna throw the silver streak away, but when I saw that the wheels had broken off I came up with this idea.

22.s: In an effort to get attention, young Nicky does whatever he can to get his parents to stop thinking about their soon-to-be-born child.
q: Where was the daddy cat?
Um... well, uh, I think he had gone to work.

23.s: Ten-year-old troublemaker Scott Williams is let off the hook when he is caught trying to steal apples from Tom Riley. Unfortunately, Scott doesn't extend the same mercy to others.
q: Say, Mr. Riley, I heard about the excitement out at your place this morning.

Yeah, Nicky Creshaw heard from Steve Perry that Michael Turner was over at Thelma Gardner's, who said that she saw seven police cars, a fire truck, and an ambulance with the sirens going full blast pull out on to your road!
Well, that... that was nothing. David Harley
Okay, I'll whistle for him. Yoo-hoo! Scott Williams
Uh, oh. I know that tone on Tom Riley

24.s: Middle-schooler Philo Sanderson loves pulling practical jokes, but Whit is disturbed when Philo says that his lucky rabbit's foot keeps him safe.
q: You'll get more protection out of a deodorant spray than from that silly good luck charm!

25.s: Officer David Harley tries to find a missing boy named Steve Larson.

26.s: Officer David Harley tries to find a missing boy named Steve Larson.

27.s: Freddie Hart learns that it takes more than different surroundings to make him a different person.
q: Go ahead, Freddie, tell us your hobbies.
Well, I don't know. I like to hang around the house with my mom and dad. I was thinking about starting a butterfly collection.
Is there anything else you like to do? I saw on your report that you like music. Do you play an instrument?
Not yet, but I'd like to learn how to play the harp.

28.s: Mr. Altman teaches his class that the men who fought in the Vietnam war were killers. This doesn't sit well with Kirk McGinty, whose father died in the war fighting for his country.
q: Mr. Altman, here in Odyssey, we still take words like honor, and duty, and heroism very seriously. They still have a meaning here.

I know that when all this is done, a lot of bad things will be said about what we were doing over here. Some of those things I'm sorry to say are true. That happens in war sometimes. I know that sounds like I'm trying to excuse the inexcusable, but I'm not. If the people who are against this war could just talk to some of the Vietnamese and hear the gratitude they express for helping them I think they'd begin to understand a little better. That's what makes the price of freedom worth paying. And if I ever have a son someday, that's something I wanna tell him.

My husband, and all the other Americans who fought in Vietnam or any other war paid that price for us. And our children. And the people of those countries in which they fought. Let this monument serve to remind us and future generations of their sacrifice.

29.s: Jack Davis and Lucy Cunningham-Schultz wonder about a strange family in town and Jack is convinced they are up to something.
q: I'll bet those things he carries out in the middle of the night are his experiments. Just like Frankenstein.
Hi Whit, sorry I'm late!

30.s: Laura-Jean Fremont is embarrassed by the things her parents do. Whit then tries to help her learn what great people they really are.
q: Laura, your Mom and Dad are two of the most lovely people I know. I can't for the life of me figure out why you're so ashamed of them.
I'll tell you why. It's because.. It's because they're hicks!
Laura, I admit they're not high society. But that's part of their charm.

You know, there are two great things about shopping in a store in Odyssey. One is the bargains that you get here. And the other is the fact that they play really great music over the speakers. See what I mean?
The Bible doesn't say to honor your mother and father as long as they dress properly or act the way you want them to. It simply says to honor them: no conditions.
School's out!!

31.s: The Barclay family of four takes off for a Florida vacation, but they get stranded when the family car breaks down.
q: It felt like a cow!
Um, it was too small to be a cow, Jimmy.
A little cow? Don't they make little cows?
I got everything in that I need.
Open it up, Jimmy.
Yes, I do. I see a pile of comic books, a baseball glove, your piggy bank, your play army boots, a yo-yo, a cassette player and tapes, three model sports cars, and -- what’s this?
My Overlords of Space Laser Blaster.
But where are your clothes?
I'm wearing them.
No, I mean the clothes you're going to take on vacation.
I’ve got ’em on.
Jimmy, you have to take more clothes than that.
Why? These are the ones I like to wear anyway.
I know, and one day I'm going to peel them off you and give them a decent burial.

It took three more tries before Mom would let me leave. And I had to take out most of the good stuff, too, like half of the comic books and the army boots. Just for some clean underwear, socks and shirts that make my neck itch. Grown-ups just don't understand what's really important. I thought this was supposed to be a fun vacation.
Come on, Donna. Mom said to turn off the TV because we have to pack.

Be quiet, runt. I don't wanna pack for that stupid vacation. I don't wanna go, and I don't think Mom and Dad should make me. You guys go. I'm twelve years old, and I'm big enough to take care of myself.
Can I open it now?
No. You can only open it when you’re absolutely, without question, no doubt about it, as bored as you’ve ever been in your life.
Ok, so Dad's not a mechanic. That's all right. He got it fixed before we left in the morning. Well, almost fixed. We have to push the lighter in to turn on the windshield wipers.
Oh, we're only 52 minutes late. That's a record for us.

My parents are really confusing sometimes. Why would they want to take work on a vacation? I don’t get it. I don’t like to work when I have to. Why should I do it when I don’t? You won’t catch me trying to sneak my math books on this trip.

All that excitement for a piece of tire rubber. Anyway, we drove for a little while and then stopped at one of those diner kind of restaurants where all the waitresses call you "honey" and look just like my Great-Grandma Benson right before she died.
There's more to life than your friends in Odyssey, Donna.
Yeah, all you guys ever do is sit around wondering what to do.
Be quiet, Jimmy.

32.s: The Barclay family of four takes off for a Florida vacation, but they get stranded when the family car breaks down.
q: So we went back to Chester’s house. Of course, as soon as anything was said about food, Donna Barclay
Should we try to hitch-hike, maybe?
Are you kidding? You never know what kind of lunatic will pick ya up.
How do you know all this stuff?
We learned about it in Sunday School. How do you know about the overlords of Ganthum, and the rebel pirates from Alpher 67?
Not in Sunday School, that’s for sure.

Hi, kids! I’m John Avery Whittaker and you’re holding Whit’s Boredom Buster. You’ve probably spent a fair amount of time trying to figure out this little contraption, huh? Well, the time you spent playing with it was time you weren’t bored. Neat, huh? And it just goes to show you that something as silly as this can be fun — if you set your mind to it. Now the Boredom Buster is going to turn off, and you should find something even more fun to do. Bye!
If this is some kind of trick—

It isn’t. It’s Mr. Whittaker’s invention. He called it “Whit’s Boredom Buster.” He gave it to me before we left, and said not to open it until I was absolutely, without question, no doubt about it, as bored as I’ve ever been in my life. I’m not bored, but you are. Besides, if you’re gonna sit and think about Odyssey, you may as well hold a piece of it.

Mom and I lost the egg tossing contest. She threw it a little too hard and it hit me on the top of my head. She said it was an accident, but she was smiling and I don’t think I believe her. Donna kept pouting under the tree, and no one could get her to play any games. And then I remembered something.

33.s: Irwin Springer, a middle schooler interested in history, falls when trying to get a book and imagines that he visited the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Revolution American Revolution] and witnessed the signing of the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_of_independence Declaration of Independence].
q: Well, we've had quite an adventure, and I don't even know your name or where you're from.
I'm Irwin Springer from Odyssey.
Well Irwin Springer from Odyssey, I thank you for saving my life.
Likewise, I'm sure. And you are?
My name is Hale, Nathan Hale.
Nathan Hale, the Nathan Hale!?
You've heard of me?
Who hasn't heard of you?!
Oh wow, oh wow!
Oh, wow? Is that some sort of Indian greeting?
I don't know, sir. He does seem to say it often, though.
Well, in the interests of maintaining good relations with the people of Odyssey, I say "Oh wow" to you, Irwin Springer.
Thank you, sir!
Look at him go. You'd think he was looking for buried treasure or something.
Who's to say he isn't?
Can you swim?
Well, there's no time like the present to learn.
Benjamin Franklin looked and sounded just like you!
Really? Poor fellow.

34.s: Connie doesn't like Odyssey and feels she is being swamped by Christians. So she wants to go back to California. But when Whit gets hurt, she realizes how much he means to her.
q: ...Oh, it took only a few stitches...
...and eighteen stitches are not just a few.
Hello, Tom. What are you doing out in this weather?
Oh, you know how I am when it comes to storms, Whit. Everything just gets so, so, uh, wet.
I hate it. I hate it. I hate it! All this rain and wind.
I don't know which is worse staying in here or trying to run back. We're both wearing raincoats and rubber shoes so we shouldn't get struck by lightning.
Struck by lightning?
Well it's either that or fighting a tornado. You know, they issued a tornado watch on the radio.
What? Let's get out of here!
Stay right here. I'll be right back. Do not move.
Even if I could I wouldn't.

35.s: Ned Lewis' V.B.S. class is a mess and he must perform a sketch in front of the entire church! If everything goes well, the church will consider starting up a Drama program, but things don't look too good for Ned.
q: We talked it over. Me, and Junior, and Hank, wanna play those three guys, uh... Poolrack, Toolshed, and a Billy Goat.
Hank, the gold star goes on the page, not your forehead.
They kept wanting to change the script. You know how Nebuchadnezzar ordered that everyone was supposed to bow down to the idol when the music played?
Well, they wanted the music to be rock and roll. Then they started playing cards when they were in the fiery furnace.
And among these young men were Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
We threw three men into the furnace, but now I see four men walking around in the fire, unbound and unharmed. And the fourth one looks like the son of the gods.
Give me oil in my lamp, keep me burning, burning, burning.

36.s: Brad and Sherman hit the air waves with their very own radio station: 'Kids' Radio.' But without proper support, the project is headed for trouble.
q: Why don't the other kids see you are such a nice guy?
I don’t know. I guess nobody got close enough to notice.
Uh, Mr. Adams, before you go, I had an idea for a radio program, I thought I'd like to try out on you.
Oh? Let's hear it.
Well, it's kinda like the old time radio dramas, and it takes place in a small town and a big building they call a discovery emporium.
A discovery emporium?
Yes. And it has a special Bible room, and the county's largest train set.
Yes. And it's run by a grandfatherly inventor and kids come in and they have all kinds of adventures together. What do you think?
Stick to selling ice cream, Mr. Whittaker. Stick to selling ice cream.
Radio's changed a lot since I was a kid, that's for sure.
You had radio when you were a kid?
It's going to be real nice weather today. It's also partly cloudy, or partly sunny. Kinda a little of each. So don't go to the pool or you'll get a lopsided sun tan.

37.s: In the first Camp What-A-Nut adventure, Donny McCoy learns about being short, Chas Wentworth is put in his place, and Ned Lewis deals with a crush.
q: Well, we didn't feel real comfortable about being known as the Stinking Swamp Campers!
Wow, it really gets dark in here!
Here, I'll turn on my flashlight.
Ah! Thanks Chas, but I don't need a light, especially not right in my eyes!
I can find my way in the dark! Oh!
Watch out for the suitcase!
Thanks a lot- Ah!
Watch out for the other one, too.
And another thing that don’t make sense, I read a big headline: “Employee Arrested When $50,000 Found Missing”. Now, how could it be found if it was a missing?!
So, what do you think of the place?
It's far out.
I'm glad you like it.
No, I mean we're really far out! That's some drive up here.
Well, that's the idea. You wanna pick a place that's remote so kids can get away from civilization for a while.
Well, couldn't they get away from civilization a little closer to the city?
What do you mean yelling at me like that, you little... Oh, hi Mr. Whittaker!
Frank, that's a nice...what is this?
It's a 1/32nd square model of downtown Odyssey.
Great, that's great. Keep up the good work. Wow, can that kid whittle!
In science class I tried mixing some chemicals together to make glue. But all I got was kicked out of the class.
I entered the fishing contest, but every time I got a bite, the fish would pull me out of the boat.
Another said "New! Grandma's Old Fashioned Cookies." Now how can it be 'old fashioned' if it's brand new?!?!?

38.s: Donny McCoy gives his account of what happened at Camp What-A-Nut. He describes his encounter with a bear, and the rest of the camp's encounter with a skunk.
q: N.L + G.M. Oh, those are nice initi'.
Those are my initi'!
Well, she told me when she was making this that it was something for her true love!
Eh! That's a'wonderful! Congratulations!
No! It's not a'wonderful!
Well, we'll just have to sit up here until she gets either tired or bored and goes away, but until then I'd suggest we do two things.
Well, the first is to keep praying.
I've been doing that. What's the second?
Whoah! Hold on tight!
You know what my poppa used to say, "Marco, if you're gonna go out for revenge, you'd better dig two graves."

39.s: Whit and Jami Martin solve a forty-year old mystery after finding a skeleton in a hidden room in the basement.
q: Everybody should have a library card.
Do you see the transistor, Jami?
Yes, it's back by the door.
Door? What door?
Well, I guess he's not home.
But somebody is!
Wow, it's a note of some kind. It's typed.
What's it say?
"Leave well enough alone."
Hello? Who's that? The lights have gone out. Well, what do you want?
Stay out of my way!

40.s: A secret room is discovered in Whit's End that holds the skeleton of an old janitor from The Fillmore Recreation Center. Whit and Jami Martin attempt to discover some answers.
q: Then you leave me no choice but to exercise my right as a citizen and pursue this case until justice is done!
I told you yesterday, it's a closed case.
But it can't be a closed case as long as there are unanswered questions.
Tom, you're beginning to sound like a parrot. If you think you know where the money is hidden, why don't you say so?
Poor Spencer. You know, somehow it's just not fair to lose a life over something so worthless as money.
I guess that's why the Bible says money is the root of all evil.

41.s: Jack and Lucy use their imaginations to their fullest, when Whit tells them the story of Jonah and his encounter with a 'big fish'.
q: Boy, you'd think in the stomach of a fish you could find some peace and quiet! Why don't you kids go out and play in some other fish?!
And for my disobedience, I wind up here, in the belly of a whale.
I usually wind up in my room when I disobey.
I'll trade places with you anytime.
No, thanks. Boy, this story was fun up until now. Now I feel bad.
You and me both, kiddo.
There's a man crying in the streets.
Give him a hankie and send him home. What do I care? I'm a king, not a babysitter.
Ah! My whale-mates!
Wait! You can't throw us overboard!
We can't? Why not?
Because, uh... because, um... you tell 'em, Lucy!
Uh, uh, uh, oh, because, uh... it wouldn't be nice, that's why!
Way to go, Lucy.

42.s: Terry's boring summer takes a drastic turn when he and his father are ambushed by a terrorist.
q: I work for the government, just like a mailman.
Yeah, but this is a little bit different then delivering letters!
So Catspaw, we meet again.
Why do you keep calling him Catspaw? His name is George, George Johnston!
I can't believe this. You're just my Dad! How can you know something vital to national security!?
Well, son, someone has to.
You've been quiet for the last couple of hours. What's the matter, didn't dinner agree with you?
Well, the bag of peanuts was kinda tough, but the two syrups for dessert were great.

43.s: Leslie seems to have trouble with telling the truth. "Over-Exaggeration" seems to be her middle name.
q: But, the bus pulled up... and the door opened... and... and it was him!
Our bus driver, Crazy Eddie!
Hello, my pretties! Welcome to my weirdsmobile. All aboard!
Ok, pal. You want to explain why you were doing 65 in a 30 mile an hour speed zone?
Well, I... uh, I was slowing down for the turn!
Since you came late and have a torn dress, I want you to go first, Laura.
I'm Leslie, so you must mean Lisa.
You know, Leslie, I've discovered that there are times when I don't like a lot of things because I'm upset with something completely different than the things I don't think I like.

44.s: Leslie still hasn't learned her lesson and continues to tell stories. However, this time one of the stories may actually be true!
q: So let me get this straight. A cowboy with a big, floppy hat and silver spurs rode up to you on a purple hook-and-ladder fire engine, and asked to use your mother’s new umbrella?
Yeah, that's it.
Well, Leslie (a)

45.s: A Halloween party at Whit's End strives to teach the children of Odyssey to celebrate Saints and not demons on October 31.
q: Do you wanna be a dummy all your life?
Only if I have to.

46.s: Connie experiences the story of the Shepherd and the Giant using 'The Environment Enhancer', a new creation by Whit.
q: Before you knock it, why don't you try it?
You mean the machine?
Sure. I need a guinea pig, and you'll do just fine.
Were you able to find out anything about my friend?
No, but thanks for reminding me.
That's it? Sticks and stones?
Of course not.
Well, that's good.
I also have my sling.
You can't win against that giant with some sticks and stones and a leather strap! You need something more!
But I do have something more. I have the Lord God of Israel on my side.

47.s: Whit tells a story about the difference a single vote can make.
q: Wow! If he were alive today, he'd be dead!
Y-you talked!
I know. It's amazing what you can do on radio, isn't it?
Well, for what it's worth, Horace, I'll back ya. I caught your speech a couple minutes ago and it sounded good—a real barn burner!
Which is the second reason I don't believe it was coincidental.
And that is?
I don't believe anything is coincidental.
You know, it amazes me how you can take any subject and relate it to God or the Bible.
Thank you. I'll take that as a compliment.

48.s: Superstar basketball player "Lightning" Livingston opens a sports store in Odyssey, but a scathing exposé reveals more than megafan Jimmy Barclay wanted to know.
q: I realized that people are people: sooner or later they'll let me down. But I've also realized that the only hero I ever need to have is Jesus Christ. He's the only one that will never let me down.
And who are you?
Uh, uh, my name is, uh, uh.
It's Jimmy. Jimmy Barclay.
Yeah! Bimmy Jarclay!
There are all kinds of rumors about why Lightning retired from basketball early.
Mr. Malone, even the kids around here know that spreading rumors is a bad thing.
You know, Howard, there's dumb and there's real dumb. That was real dumb.

49.s: At Thanksgiving dinner, Whit tells the story of how his stepmother changed his life.
q: You both got back just in time.
To eat? Oh, good. I'm starved.
Well Agnes, it takes time to cook a good turkey dinner.
That's what I've always tried to tell Tom, Whit. It's not as easy as you thought it was, is it?
Nope. Especially on the turkey.
My my this room is a mess.
No it isn't I just cleaned it up this morn.. That wasn't very funny.
Then why are you smilin’?
How do you know I'm smiling?
Because a smile isn’t just somethin’ you see; it’s somethin’ you hear as well.
I remember an ol’ Scottish prayer that my mother taught me when I was a wee girl. It goes like this: “Lord, I thank thee a thousand times for the roses. Help me to thank thee for the thorns as well.”

That's why I’m thankful for Fionna Donneral. She helped me get over my mother's death, she got me into the habit of reading the Bible everyday, and led me to Christ. And all those roses came out of the thorn of her blindness.
I'm thankful that my Dad didn't pick me up; because if he did, I wouldn'ta learned what to be thankful for.

50.s: Donna Barclay tries to cope when her best friend, Karen Crosby, becomes ill with cancer.
q: Where, O death, is your victory? Where, O death, is your sting? The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law. But thanks be to God! He gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
Karen is the only one I'd go to a hospital for.
My books! Thank you, you're a life saver. If I had to watch one more soap opera or game show, I woulda thrown my water jug at the TV screen.
You know what they say about hospital food.
It's true. Mrs. Murray and I were playing marbles with our peas.
If you pull back that curtain, you'll find out!
When I get out of here I'll come back to see you.
Bring me a cake with a file in it.

In the land of fadeless day Lies the city foursquare; It shall never pass away, And there is no night there. All the gates of pearl are made, In the city foursquare; All the streets with gold are laid, And there is no night there. All the gates shall never close To the city foursquare; There life’s crystal river flows, And there is no night there. There they need no sunshine bright, In that city foursquare; For the Lamb is all the light, And there is no night there. God shall wipe away all tears, There’s no death, no pain, nor fears, And they count not time by years, For there is no night there. Thank you.

That's what I've been thinking. No matter what happens now, we'll see each other again because we both love Jesus. Sooner or later we'll be in heaven, and then we'll have all of forever to be friends.

51.s: Connie encounters old friends who remind her of how different she was before coming to Odyssey. Meanwhile, Eugene Meltsner starts working at Whit's End and promptly changes how the shop works.
q: My name is Eugene Meltsner, and I'm a science student and, might I add in all modesty, a recognized genius at the Campbell County Community College.
Hi, Whit, I'm sorry I'm late.
Hi, Connie; are you late? I hadn't noticed.
Your timing couldn't be better, Hubert.
Eugene, I just can't understand a word you're saying. Are you one of those foreign exchange students?
Whit's End. Is that a pun?
Well, sort of.
I hate puns.

Good morning ladies and gentlemen. We'll be arriving at the Los Angeles bus terminal in just a few moments. Now would be a good time to start gathering your things. I'd offer you hot towels, but if I get out of my seat we'll crash.
See, in California, they don't care. I can be free out there. I can be whoever I want to be!
Who is that, Connie?
I don't know. I guess I'll find out.

52.s: In California, Connie must make a decision about Christianity. In Odyssey, Eugene is inadvertently causing problems at Whit's End.
q: You know I've been really confused, and well I thought that by going to California everything would become clear for me. I could be myself and I wouldn’t be confused anymore and you know what?
Well, that's exactly what happened. I've got it all figured out and now I know what I want to do.
You, you do.
Well, what would you like to do?
I want to pray with you.
Yeah, well, I’m not sure of all the right words, you know, forgive me for my sins, and, um, well, I want to ask Jesus Christ to come live in my heart.
Oh, Connie, Connie, you don’t know how I prayed to hear you say those words.
Yes, I do. I think your prayers made it all the way to California.
In Odyssey, on the bus, you! What do you guys do, call each other and say, "Tag! Connie's in your area now! Go get her!"?
No, we don't have to.
What is that supposed to mean?

God loves you, Connie. He's nuts about you, and he wants you to love him back. That's why it seems like he's been sending people after you. I had no idea you'd been meeting other Christians. I just had the strong feeling to come and see you.
It's like I told you, Connie. God's crazy about you and if you won't go to him, He'll send people to you.
Oh. Well, Tom he means well. This is good experience for him.
Good experience? Well, I'll try to remember that when I experience my first heart attack.
Time out now! Everybody off the field!
Uh, I beg your pardon?
Eugene, I do appreciate your efforts around the shop, but you're missing something very important in what you're doing!
I am? What am I missing?
Oh, I beg to differ, Mr. Whittaker. I couldn't function at all if my heart weren't actually--

No, no, no, not your physical heart, Eugene. Your emotional heart. You see, you've automated nearly everything in Whit's End, but Whit’s End isn’t about automation, machines, or inventions—it’s about people. Now, you can make it more efficient with your inventions, but…can you make it warmer? Friendlier? Loving?
Connie, God will bring people into our lives to show us his love and mercy and lead us to him. You’ve been fighting it, but it’s there all the same.
Well, I’ve been fighting it all right.

Sometimes it’s the people who fight the hardest who want it the most, and yet God keeps sending his love through those around you. Sometimes there’s one special person who seems to shine with the love of God and they keep on loving you no matter what you do.

That’s okay, now. You see God brings people like that into your life to bring you to him. That’s one of the ways he operates. He shows his love for us through others. It’s like a reflection, but the real love is found in Jesus Christ. He died for you, for your sins, cause he loves you so much. John 3:16 says, “For God so loved the world,” you, Connie, “that he gave his only begotten son that whoever will believe in him will not perish but have everlasting life.” And Romans 5:8 tell us that, “God demonstrates his own love towards us, in that while we were sinners Christ died for us.” It’s okay, child. I think you’ve known this for a long time. Isn’t it time you accepted it? Connie?
I’ve made a decision.
I wanna go home.
But wouldn’t you rather…
I can drop you off if you want.
Not my dad’s home, Pam, home. I’m going back to Odyssey.

53.s: Lucy promises Heather she will keep a dangerous promise, and Eugene and Connie try to prove who is the better worker.
q: Oh Whit! I'm sorry I'm not on time. I wanted to be. Especially on my first day back and everything... He's not here.
No, he's not.
Lucy! You scared me!

54.s: The Barclays forget the true meaning of Christmas.
q: John Avery Whittaker
Greetings and felicitations of the season.
I figured as much.
Happy Holidays, Connie.
Merry Christmas, Eugene. I'd hug you too, but I don't have time for the explanation of the process.
John Avery Whittaker, now I want you to stop for a minute. You're goin' like a house afire. It's just not like you to get caught up in this Christmas rush.
What a terrible, rotten Christmas!
You forgot horrible. It's a terrible, horrible, rotten Christmas!
Yeah, that too.

55.s: Tom and Whit reflect on the things that happened over the year.
q: Yeah, It's been a busy twelve months that's for sure.
Oh you can say that again.
It's been a busy twelve months that's for sure.
Happy New Year, John Whittaker
Happy New Year my Tom Riley

56.s: Whit tells Jack and Lucy the story of Noah's Ark.
q: Honey, I'm home.
Hello, dear. How was your day?
Not bad. I worked on our vineyards in the northwest corner, planted a new field of crops, and talked to God. What's for dinner?
Well, He told me about his plan to destroy all of mankind and all the animals. Where's today's paper? I want to see who won the game.
Just imagine, Darling, I get to be a shipbuilder, sailor, and zoo keeper! Hehe!
Ay, you're only 480 years old, what’s a new career?
How long did it take Noah to build to Ark, Mr. Whittaker?
Well, some people figure it took about one hundred and twenty years.
Oh, that's not ba—a hundred and twenty years?!
Listen folks! I want you to get out of my yard before I call the police!
I am the police. Do you realize your ark over there is double parked?
I know, I know. The dove. Are you sure you don't want to try the raven again?
No, no. We'll stick with the dove, thank you. Uh, would you...
The window. I got it.
Lord, if there is any dry ground out there, please let the dove find it. Amen. Alright my little dove, well, you know the routine! Maybe I should try the parakeet.
Will I live to be 950 years old if I have faith like Noah?
Jack, if you have faith like Noah, you'll live forever.

57.s: When Jimmy Barclay realizes he's spent all his savings on pizza and video games, he finds it difficult to confront his father.
q: You thinkin’ what I’m thinkin’?
I think so... what are you thinkin’?
I’m thinkin’ we just found Jimmy Barclay
Oh. Then I’m not thinkin’ what you’re thinkin’. But if you’re thinkin’ now, what I think you’re thinkin’, then you’re thinkin’ a good thought, I think.
Would you come on?!
Well Jimmy, you know you’re gonna have to go home.
But George Barclay
You don’t know that.
You don’t know my dad!
Three thirty? Oh, no!
What’s-a matter, kid? What happens at three thirty? You turn into a pumpkin or somethin’?
No, not a pumpkin — dead meat. Three thirty is when George Barclay

58.s: Tom Riley tells a story about when he was young. In it, he and his sister are assigned to take some medicine to a woman across a woods.
q: I'm not young, I'm 11 years old.
Tom, if you fall in and drown, I'll never speak to you again!

59.s: Robyn Jacobs tries to figure out how to study the Bible.
q: When you stop and think these are God's words, it just sort of gives you the shivers. Doesn’t it?
Oh! What dummy set this thing for five o'clock? Oh, yeah, I did!
You just have to take it by faith.
Oh... "faith." Hey, I bet John Avery Whittaker
Pamela!!!!!!!!!

60.s: Jimmy prays to get a bicycle and it happens. Donna is confused about the nature of prayer and so Whit gives her an object lesson.
q: How do you pray, Connie?
On my knees. I used to try it flat on my back, but I kept falling asleep.
See, Donna? All you need is a mustard jar.
Mustard seed, Jimmy. Mustard seed.
Wow! What is that?
Nothing right now. Maybe you should ask what it's going to be.
All right. What's it going to be?
A vending machine.
A vending machine? You mean for Cokes and candy bars and stuff like that?
Nope. For prayers.
I've got a button for just about everything. Money when you don't need it, good grades on a test you didn't study for, the latest fashions, the newest toys, popularity. What should I add?
Boy, I can think of a whole bunch of things!
What is prayer?
It's talking to God.
Close, but no. How about talking with God?
Donna Barclay

61.s: A skit about the role of all the members of the Christian body.
q: When people don't go to church, it can't do what it's supposed to do either.
Brian Headly? Oh, , yes, I'm here, too, because I saw myself come in.

62.s: While Whit is gone for a few days, Connie tries to become just like him, but fails in various ways.
q: Sometimes you make a lot of sense, Eugene.
Sometimes???

63.s: The Barclay family tries a new budget.
q: That’s why I need a new one. A genuine Rostan Harringbone with real synthetic fur lining. They’re on sale at Greenway’s Department Store: 20% off.
I think you’re 20% off.

This may come as a terrible shock to you all, but this family is not independently wealthy. I mean, these things all take money, and although I never thought I’d hear myself say this, money doesn’t grow on trees.
We know that. That’s why they make credit cards.
Very funny, Donna.
I don't believe there's any real "problem," Mr. Whittaker. ... I believe it's all a matter of personality.
Yeah! I have one, and he doesn't!
For instance, when I speak, I use English. When Miss Kendall speaks, she uses... ...what do you call that again?
I said we want your money to feel at home here. In fact, we want it to stay at home here! It's all a part of our motto.
Which is...?
We'll teach you how to be responsible with money — even if it kills you!

64.s: Robyn Jacobs struggles with her struggling school partner: Oscar Peterson.
q: Uh huh, Oscar Peterson
It ain't over 'til it's over, Robyn.
It ain't over 'til it isn't over?
Oscar Peterson
Reading is to the mind what exercise is to the body. Joseph Addison.
Doing research is a pain in the neck. Connie Kendall.
Alright! Alright! Keep your shirt on!

65.s: Connie attends a Bible study with a questionable leader, while Donna hangs out with a girl who may not be honest.
q: You’re not just anybody; you’re John Avery Whittaker. Rumor has it that he never gets sick.
Thank you. What’s your name?
I’m Donna, Donna Barclay.
Don’t tell him your name!
Come on, Rachael. You should do what he says.
What kind of things did Mr. Grayson teach?

Oh, that the Bible is just a bunch of stories that weren’t true and that Jesus wasn’t really God, he was just a good teacher. I wanted to argue with him, but he was so smart. He had an answer for everything I said. Now I don’t know what I believe.

Connie, if Mr. Grayson taught that the Bible is just a bunch of stories and Jesus isn’t God, then Mr. Grayson is wrong — absolutely, without question or doubt, wrong. The Bible is the Word of God. Jesus is God, crucified for our sins and raised from the dead on the third day. Now if that’s not true, then our faith is in vain.
What happened to you? I told you to run.
Why? I didn’t do anything wrong.
Uh-oh! You got that sound in your voice like my mom when she’s about to lecture me.
Chicken soup. Thanks, Dr. Kendall. I’ve already had so much chicken soup that I might start sprouting feathers.
Is everything alright?
Yeah, it’s okay. Why?
You’re watching 'Macho Headbanger: Private Eye' on TV.
Oh yeah... I am, aren’t I?
You hate 'Macho Headbanger: Private Eye'.
Oh yeah, I do.

66.s: Digger Digwillow learns that the Bible isn't boring, by way of the Imagination Station, in the story of the crucifixion and Easter.
q: Every time I come in here you've got something new on display. What's this contraption you're working on now?
Well I'm calling it the Imagination Station.
Good grief, it's a Saturday traffic jam in the bible room.
Excuse me lady.
Mind your manners boy.
Sorry mister I thought you were.. Never mind. What kind of place is this? Guys with long hair and robes? I saw something like this in Ben Hur.
I'm John Mark. Who're you?
Digger, Digger Digwillow.
Digger, Digger Digwilow. A strange name to match your strange clothing.
I don't get this. Wait. Your master and his disciples?
Surely you must know of him. Everyone in the land has heard of him.
I-I'm not sure who you're talking about.
Oh you must know. I'm talking about Jesus the Christ. Our Messiah.
This is a dream. This has got to be a dream.
I told you the one I kiss is the man. Only then should you arrest him.
Are you Jesus of Nazareth, the Christ?
Oh yeah, the story of Jesus. He taught people and they killed him and stuff.

67.s: With the help of Whit’s new invention, young Digger Digwillow travels back in time to witness the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ.
q: Hey, what about me?
You're free to go, Barrabas. Jesus has taken your place.
What do you mean? He's dead. It has to end here.
No, it doesn't. The best is yet to come.

68.s: Lucy Cunningham-Schultz is assigned to write a school report on evolution.
q: I just can't. I'm a Christian, Mr. Winthrop, and I believe that God created man - not that he evolved from an amoeba...
Another dumb movie.
Yes, evolution affects our lives in ways we're just beginning to understand.
You can say that again, buster.
Hi, can I help you? Well now Connie, this is something different. It's been a long time since I’ve waited on you as a customer.
I had one guy take a pamphlet so he could tear it up in front of me — right in front of my face! I wanted to punch him, but... thought it wouldn't be a very good witness.
Robert said my mom needs a spiritual revival. But I was thinking that Robert needs a brain transplant.
Well, is there anything else?
Well, some new clothes, maybe...
I mean, anything else happen to you.
It's like all those boring old books, by those guys that's—what's their names? Uh, Charles Shakespeare, William Dickens, and F. Scott Fitzgerald Kennedy.
I tried to be a witness, like Peter, and sounded more like Porky Pig: abee, abee, abee, get saved, folks!

70.s: Officer Harley returns to Odyssey and is caught up in a mystery involving bootleggers and hidden caves!
q: Ah, Trickle Lake, ey? It's not too far from here! Right near, uh... Trickle Lake!
What do Jack Davis
You mean you're gonna teach me to drive in that old, beat-up truck? I thought we were gonna —
Connie, I may be nice, but I'm not stupid.
You want me to drive?
Get in the truck.

71.s: Officer Harley returns to Odyssey and is caught up in a mystery involving bootleggers and hidden caves!
q: Well, you know what I always say...
Yes, we know, we know.
Ignorance of the law is no excuse!
Ah, I love comin' back Odyssey
Not so fast, John Whittaker
David, are Jack Davis
Uh, Officer Harley if you don't mind, Whit. I'm in the middle of an arrest.
Yes, sir, Officer Harley!

72.s: Donna is assigned by her church group to befriend grumpy old Mrs. Hooper at the nursing home.
q: Well, do I get a kiss good night?
Get lost, Richard!

73.s: Against Whit's express orders, Eugene and Connie tamper with a top secret computer room--and the mysterious program Applesauce is unleashed.
q: Mabel, please load program—Connie, what are you doing in here?
Please repeat command. I do not have a program called "Connie, what are you doing in here?”
You know, train? Wooo-woo?
Oh, Eugene, what have we done?
I think we've killed Whit's End!
I'm sorry. This grieves me. But Eugene, Connie, because of what you've done today, you're fired—effective immediately. You are no longer employees of Whit's End.
Sticks and stones.

74.s: The gang from Odyssey goes on another trip to Camp What-A-Nut. This time the guys and girls compete in various events and Lucy meets a new friend named Jill who leads her into trouble.
q: No, Alison, there's no TV! I'll have someone lock it in the camp office until the end of the week.
You can't do this to me! It's unconstitutional! It's cruel! It's unusual punishment! Please, no! Give me my TV!
Oh, I forgot to tell you—I talked to the camp director, and he thinks you're right. The girls should be given a chance to compete with the boys at some things.
Yep, so tomorrow afternoon we're gonna compete with them in archery, canoes, and a relay race.
That's great.
AAAAHHHHHHHH!!!
Robyn, what's wrong?
Get it out of my sleeping bag!
What? I don't see anything!
A bug! It's crawling up my sleeping bag to attack me! There it is! Quick, stomp it, squish it, smash it!!
You mean this? This is the barrette for your hair.
Oh, that's where it went.
Whatchacall—woah!
We'll show 'em, we can be just as tough as they are! ...Anyone seen my teddy bear?
I've shown you how to use these bows and arrows, and I have to, uh, whatchacall tell ya: I didn't think you could hit the broad side of a barn, but I was wrong. That's all you've been hitting.
What are you doing?
Trying to... fit the arrow in my bow...
Well it helps if you keep your eyes open!
Mr. Zachary, did you see that? I almost made it to the target!
Very good, Jimmy! I bet the arrow would go a little further if you let it go at the same time you let go of the string....!
Wow! Great idea!
Listen, I think maybe it's time for the big leagues.
That's right. Let's get this canoe out of the swimming pool, and see how ya do in the lake!
Can I still keep my life preserver on?
Did you know that with new Floorshine from Jackson & Jackson you could get these dingy floors sparkling clean in just one step and no soapy buildup?
Just keep scrubbing, Alison. Just keep scrubbing.
How you holding up, Allison? Any symptoms of withdrawal? Flashbacks? Hallucinations of mouthwash commercials?
No, I think I'm okay. I have this to comfort me.
Oh, that's great! What is it? Your Bible?
No... a copy of last week's TV guide.

75.s: While a counselor at Camp What-A-Nut, Connie has to discipline Lucy, and the boys find out they're not particularly skilled at any outdoor activity!
q: And the crowd goes wild as Oscar Peterson
Hey, Robyn! You got mud on your new T-shirt!
Hey, that's cheating! Jimmy distracted me!
Nah nah nah na nah nah!
As soon as the guys hurry up, we'll get started. Are you ready, guys?
Hey, hey, we're praying for God to give us kindness and compassion against our enemies — do ya mind?

76.s: Eugene is stuck with a problem that seems to be without solution while working at the college computer lab. When he finds a solution, it seems to become more disastrous than ever.
q: I'm what you call a renaissance man. I dabble in a lot of things.
How old are you, Nicholas?
Eleven years, three months, 2 days, ten hours and 54 minutes old, not counting daylight savings.
You mean you're...you're not sending me back to the orphanage?
We are not sending you back to the orphanage.
Yahoo!! I-I mean—thank you sir; I am extremely grateful.
Now maybe things can get back to normal.
I wouldn't count on it, Mr. Whittaker. I wouldn't count on it.
I hereby expel you from this institution for your participation in the grade-changing scheme.
Oh! I'm crushed! I'm heartbroken!
You crack me up!
Are John Whittaker

77.s: The mysterious Dr. Regis Blackgaard wants to open an "amusement house" for children. When it seems he won't win the city council's approval to build, he resorts to questionable methods. (Part 1 of 2)
q: Nice Lucy Cunningham-Schultz
Yes, she is, and we'd like her to stay that way!
Eugene, do you know him?
Know me? We used to work together, ain't that right, Multsey baby?
We were briefly employed with the same organization.
Connie, this is my boss.
How do you do, Miss Kendall. My name is Blackgaard. Dr. Regis Blackgaard.
...we worked with the five C's.
The five C's? What's that?
Campbell County Community College Computers.
Oh, that's clever.
Yeah, and cute too.
Well, I don't know if I should see him or not.
Oh, what do you think you should do?
I think it'll still hurt to see him again, I mean, we didn't exactly part under the best of circumstances.
Well, then you probably shouldn't see him.
But I really want to, I mean, something's happened up at camp and I think he would like to hear about it.
Then maybe you should go see him.
Uh..I don't want to seem pushy, I mean even though it's been a while, he might not have cooled down yet. And I don't want to do anything that would bug him.
Well, then I guess you shouldn't see him.
But I have to, I need to tell him how wrong I was and I don't blame him for anything.
Then go see him.
I can't do that, he fired me!
Will you cut that out! Yes I'll see him, no I won't see him, yes I'll see him, no I won't see him. I feel like I'm at a tennis match and I'm the ball!!
You looked like you needed help, Dr. Blackgaard.

78.s: The mysterious Dr. Regis Blackgaard wants to open an "amusement house" for children. When it seems he won't win the city council's approval to build, he resorts to questionable methods. (Part 2 of 2)
q: Well, what do you think? Are you going to hire her?
No. Whittaker's hold on her is too great. However she can still be used for our immediate purposes.
You mean to get Whittaker out of the way for the vote.
Yes. But it must be done carefully so they don't suspect anything.
You silly little coward!

You dare even think about disobeying my orders! Just remember, my fine young man, that I hold your future. We both know that you're guilty of far worse acts than changing the grades of a few eggheads at the college! Perhaps you'd like me to pick up the phone and tell the authorities about them?
No, no, no—please!
That's better. You're a smart fellow, Richard. I'm going to need people like you when I take over this town.
Hey, look at that!
What? My goodness! Look at all that smoke!
Someone must be having one huge barbecue!
That's no barbecue, something's on fire! Something near Tom's place!

79.s: The Barclays take the best vacation they've ever had — without leaving Odyssey!
q: The budget?! It’s always the budget! We haven’t been able to do anything since we got that stupid budget!
Told you she’d go nuts.
Well then, we’ll just have to be very gentle when we tell her.
Tell who what?
Oh, hi honey!
Hi! What’s going on?
Well, I’m afraid I have some bad news for you-
Yeah, we aren’t going anywhere on vacation this summer.
That’s your idea of gentle, Jimmy?
You can’t beat around the bush about these things, Mom. It’s best to get it over with quickly.
Now let that be a lesson to you kids: always leave your campsite cleaner than when you found it!
This is so weird!
What? What’s the matter?
We’re in our living room, Dad!
Well, this is a switch!
What do you mean?
If I remember correctly, last year you were the one who wanted to stay here.
Yeah. We had to practically drag you out and strap you into the car.
Why the change?
Well, I’ve had a hard year. A lot of things have happened.

80.s: Nicholas Adamsworth uses the Imagination Station to experience the story of Onesimus from the the book of Philemon in the Bible.
q: OK, that takes care of the programming. Now to make my interior adjustments. "'Step into my parlor,' said the spider to the fly"...
Hi Mr. Whittaker! Bye Mr. Whittaker!
Oh-Wha-?! Nicholas! Nicholas, what are you doing?
Well, I can see that! Who are you hiding from?
Just Eugene!
Sorry! He's not home!
Now Nicholas...
No one here by that name!
Are you familiar with the New Testament?
Well, I don't know how familiar I am with it, but I've read it several times.

81.s: Robyn Jacobs thinks she can earn money the "easy" way by starting her own business, but she soon learns it's not so easy after all.
q: Hey, look, it's Robyn Roter! Hi, Greensleeves. How's it going?
I'm not in the mood, Jack. Hi, Oscar.
Is that a new dress?
It's pretty! I had an aunt who was buried in a dress like that.
Thanks, Oscar.
All right, guys. You win. If you help me finish the lawns I said we'd do, I've give you what you want.
You'll give us seven dollars and seventy-five cents?
No. I'll give you all of it: the whole ten dollars.
But you can't! We only asked for—
Quiet, Oscar! Be quiet!
My little girl's becoming quite the financier.
No. I just wanna make money.

82.s: Jack Davis and Oscar Peterson solve the mystery of a strange kid and an armload of lumber.
q: Elementary, Mr. Watson. AAhh! What was that, a security alarm?
Nope, was my bad joke buzzer. They're on special for $9.95.
Boy, hardware stores carry everything these days.
Oh! Look at my walkie talkie! How am I gonna explain this to my dad? "Well, dad, it's like this: I fell into a moat."
I greeted her the way all great detectives greet women. Hiyah, doll face. What's the latest news?
The report of your damaged body if you don't call me by my real name.
Nah, it's twenty after!

It is summer. The weather is hot: too hot. My dad explains it as a condition when a weather front stalls because there isn't enough arctic current to push it on. My dad talks like that sometimes. Watches too much TV.
But what are we gonna do? We don't know who he is, where he's from, what he's doing, or how to find him.
Ha! Minor details.
We tried to act casual so Mr. Watson wouldn't know what we were up to.
All right you two, if you're gonna act casual, do it somewhere else. This is a store, not a waiting room.
This case could be bigger than I thought. It was time to come up with a cunning plan.
What did you say?
Nothing. I was just narrating.

83.s: Dr. Regis Blackgaard and Richard Maxwell uses a modem to hack into Whit's End to try to steal a computer program, producing some tragic side effects.
q: Hey—instead of taking the bus, let's walk back to Whit's End. Whaddya say?
Are you sure, Mr. Whittaker? That's quite a distance for a man of your—
Uh, careful, careful.
Uh... social position.

84.s: Dr. Regis Blackgaard attempts to steal the "Applesauce" program from Whit while Richard Maxwell formulates a plan to get revenge on his employer.
q: You saved my life! Why?
Two reasons. For one, you have a lot of explaining to do.
Yeah? What's the other reason?
Your life is worth saving.
Oh... oh, this is wonderful! Applesauce is finally within my reach. After all these years, I'm finally going to get it!
Ya got that right, heh heh heh...

85.s: Robyn Jacobs and Esther Langford, a home-schooler, switch places for a day.
q: Say, who's this handsome young gentleman you've brought with you?
He's not a handsome gentleman, he's my dad!
Oh, thanks a lot, Robyn!
Oh, uh. I think we're being paged.
We are actually here to engage in a time-honored tradition.
Yeah, our annual back-to-school chocolate soda!
Oh? How long have you had this tradition?
What time is it now?
How do you like school this year, Robyn?
You're kidding, right?
Sorry, I guess that was a pretty dumb question!
It means that Esther learns at home, instead of going to a real- uh, I m-mean a regular-, uh, formal school. Help?!
You actually jumped her and beat her?!
Yeah. How else are you going to win at checkers?
Perhaps some math problems would be best.

86.s: Isaac Morton wants to be just like Jack Davis, but when the two are partnered up for a school assignment, it seems clear that Jack doesn't want anything to do with Isaac.
q: Are you cutting me from the team, Mr. Zachary?
Cutting you? Now, Isaac, "cutting you" is whatchacall a very harsh word! It sounds like a brutal slice, a severing, a destructive act of whatchacall—
You're cutting me from the team.
Oh, Isaac, it's not that you're not good, it's just, you know, whatchacall.
I can't believe it! If someone else does C.S. Lewis after all I've gone through, I'm gonna be really mad. Unless they're bigger than me. In that case I'll probably go home and have a good cry.
This reminds me of the story of Isaac Morton
Mmmm, I don't think so.
Well, sit back and we'll get started on it right after this.
Wait a minute... that's my line.

87.s: Robyn Jacobs and Jack Davis use the Imagination Station to experience the story of King Ahab, Queen Jezebel, Elijah, and the drought.
q: ...It's wet, and it stinks, and I'm cold. It's terrible.
Excuse me, don't forget the rats... It's wet, it stinks, it's cold, and the rats like to nibble at your ankles.
Hey the food is bad too you know. You can't put together a list of complaints about this prison, without griping about the food.
Right, so what do we have? Let's see it's wet, it stinks, it's cold, the rats like to nibble at your ankles, and the food is bad.
Did you mention the plumbing?
I don't think I did. Do we have any?
Then we should mention it.

88.s: Robyn Jacobs and Jack Davis accidentally get sent to Elijah's time and experience a great adventure with Elijah in the Old Testament!
q: Boy, I never thought I'd be happy to see you again.
Yeah. Likewise.
He did not say his friend was so pretty — even in beggar clothes.
Are you kidding?
Pass me some of that brown stuff over there. I like it.
You mean the rabbit?
Rabbit? I've been eating Bugs Bunny?
Good grief, Robyn.

89.s: Connie, Donna Barclay and Oscar Peterson all get the chance to see what would happen if everyone was treated fairly.
q: So, what's for breakfast?
Let's see, there's eggs, bacon, toast, juice, cereal, and milk.
Mmm, I'm starved!
Well, it's all there in the fridge. Have at it!

90.s: In a pinch about losing her bike, Robyn lies about the people who stole it.
q: They looked like real bad guys. And... and they talked funny.
My Tony Peterson
Never mind, Oscar!
They wore black sweaters. You know, sorta like crooks on TV? And they talked funny! Like they had containers!
Yeah, containers! You know, to straighten your teeth?
I think you mean retainers.
Yeah, that too!
You sure you're telling us everything?
Well, yeah, Dad. That's all I can think up—uh, I mean, remember.
I think you might want to sit down.
We are sitting.
Oh yeah, you are.
We've gotta keep Oscar Peterson

91.s: Jimmy Barclay dreams about working with Dan Isidro, a missionary to Nicaragua.
q: Well what's the matter with you?
Nothing, I wanna go home, that's all. I always have to wait forever for you and mom every Sunday morning after the service!
Always, Jimmy? Forever, Jimmy? I mean, do we need an attitude check, Jimmy?
Something happened in Sunday school, right? Mr. Whittaker made you read one of those verses with long names again?
Nice headline. But what's this?
It's the missionary, of course!
It is? With a plate on his head?
That's a safari hat. I kinda made it to look like a halo, you know, being like a saint and stuff?
Ah. But, uh, what happened to the rest of him? Is that supposed to be his body there?
No. You can't see his body, because he's in a pot.
Yeah! And there's the fire at the bottom. Neat idea, huh?
A fire and a pot and...what are all these figures in the background here?
The cannibals doing their native dance.
Right. See, he's a missionary to them, and they decided they were gonna—
Hold, hold, hold it! Don't—don't finish, I don't wanna know.
Where did you get such crazy ideas?
History homework!
Really? They say history doesn't teach us anything anymore!

92.s: Whit tells Calvin the story of brothers Horace and Grover McAlister, illustrating how far less productive revenge is than work.
q: I don't think of it as cheating really, I think of it as making my own advantages.
Mr. Schnook, am I to understand that our father expects us to engage in some sort of...contest for this land?
Well now, I wouldn't exactly call it a contest... it's a... more like a... yeah, it's a contest.
Well, wipe my nose!
You're gonna read our father's will to us!
Now uh, technically, this isn't a will. It's uh, merely a letter stating your father's last wishes concerning his property. It's what we call in the law profession... yeah, it's a will.

93.s: Whit flashes back to the times he had as a signalman for the Navy in World War II.
q: It's up to you, sir.
If it was up to me, I'd be back in New Jersey eating pizza.
It feels like I've been 16 forever!

94.s: Whit tells Connie the story of the battle in which he was wounded in World War II.
q: Four hands are better than two, what?
Reginald Duffield

95.s: Donna realizes she is still bitter about Karen's death a year after she has died. At the same time, Jimmy and Oscar Peterson put on a Shakespeare play.
q: You ever think about her, Ferg? No. I guess cats don’t do things like that. As long as someone's feeding you you’re happy. Maybe cats have the right idea. Don’t get too close to someone, ’cause they might go away, and then no one will be there to feed you.
When all else fails, attack the enemy straight on!
Don't look now, but your actors have arrived.
Well, it's all right now that I've had my tea.
...A lot of my lines seem like, well, something like a girl would say.
With good reason, Jimmy; Juliet is a girl.
I want people to laugh cause I make 'em laugh, not cause I look funny — don't say a word, Oscar.
You know this is the second time this week I've been blindfolded? Must be a blindfold sale going on somewhere.

You're angry, Donna...and you're angry at yourself for feeling this way. I know...the feelings are terrible. Horrible. But what you need to understand, Donna, is that they're just feelings. Reactions. You can't help having them any more than you can help breathing. And it's all right to have them -- as long as you don't let them control you.
That's so easy to say.

I know, I know. And difficult to do. But there is a way, Donna...by taking your feelings to God. Letting him have them. Totally and completely. He wants them, Donna. He can turn them into something wonderful if you let Him.

96.s: Whit's granddaughter, Jenny Whittaker-Dowd, is given a special violin solo which causes friction with the other children.
q: Remind me to introduce you to one of my employees, Jenny. I think you would get along with him nicely.
Is he from California?
No. I'm not even sure he's from this planet, but you'll like him. His name's Eugene Meltsner

97.s: Frustrated that his mother always insults his father, Monty Whittaker-Dowd tries to find a way to escape from his family problems.
q: It's not a snow "man", Monty, it's my snow "friend".
Snowfriend? Good grief Jenny, where do you get this stuff? For once, couldn't you be normal and build a snowman?
Precision of language, Monty. I couldn't decide if it's a male or female, so I decided to call it my snow-friend. "Say what you mean, mean what you say." That's my motto.
"Go stick your head in the snow." That's my motto.
There you go with your adolescent trauma again.
You're a man, aren't you?
That depends on whether my mom wants me home before dark, or wants me to mow the lawn.
I can talk to kids all over Odyssey, but I can't get through to my own Monty Whittaker-Dowd

98.s: The Barclay family finds a family huddling in their shed and are uncomfortable with them staying. After the family has left, the Barclays realize they have made a big mistake and go looking for them.
q: I'm sure your [dune] buggy's all right. I mean, it seemed to be built pretty solid.
Yeah, it said on the box the company uses only the best plastic.
Good thing those people from this morning aren't still here. After Jimmy ruined the silverware in the dishwasher, we only have four complete settings left.
Why do you care about silverware - you eat with your fingers!
If we’re gonna have them back, they’ll need a place to sleep!
They can use my room! I love sleeping on the couch!
I'm sorry, Jimmy.
It's all right, Dad. Just remember this the next time I do something dumb.

99.s: The Barclays go skiing, Donna Barclay develops a crush on her instructor, and George comes to grips with his daughter growing up.
q: How much longer till we get there?
Bout an hour kids.
Dad, you said that an hour ago.
Yes, and it's just as true now as it was when I first said it.
Dad, you're lost aren't you?
Lost? Me? George Rand McNally Barclay lost? Honey, hand me the map.
Whooa! Puppy love alert! Puppy love alert! [...] You're acting all silly and dazed [...] loony, wacky, giggly and goofy. And what were those other dwarves' names?
In some countries you'd be married.
Let's go skiing next summer!
It doesn't work that way, Honey.
Oh, wait a minute, wait a minute! There's that book that I bought a while back that I've been wanting to read.
The one you brought last vacation and never read?
Uh, right, son. That one.
Oh, it's not that cold.
Dad, when you opened the door, three penguins waddled out!
What are you getting at, Mary?
Ohhh, I wonder if maybe our daughter has a little-
Wa-wa-wait, Mary! If you're thinking what I thinking you're thinking, don't even think it!
Well, I mean, she wasn't enjoying this trip and now she is!
Let's not talk about it! I mean, she's only 12 and-
Oh, look at her smile! George, I think our daughter is developing a crush!
I can't wait for the day this family is old enough to go on a trip without all this bickering!
Dad! I already know how to ski!
Hey — maybe this year you can learn to do it standing up...!

She's so sensible! Probably doesn't go much for older guys with shiny new sport scars that do 0-60 in 2.3 seconds. He's tall, good-looking, muscular and athletic. She's young, naive, impressionable, vulnerable. What could possibly come of it?
Donna, I forbid you to ever set foot out of this cabin ever again!

100.s: Monty feels like he's in competition with his gifted sister, Jenny, so Whit, Tom Riley, and Eugene take him on an ice fishing trip to Summit Lake.
q: Eugene, it is not an environmental expedition. It's a fishin' trip. A fishin trip.
But Mr. Riley, I don't see anything wrong with studying the cold-blooded vertebrate in its natural habitat as long as we're already there!
I have said it before and I will say it again. Sometimes I just wonder 'bout Eugene Meltsner
Who wants hot cocoa?
I'll be in my tent.
Make room! Make room!
Well, hi, Tom! What are you doing?
Well, I come to see if I can catch any fish. My fishing spot's deader than, uh, a dead thing that's dead.
It's not right for Eugene to be so... so... Eugene-like!
Hi Mr. Riley, hi Eugene.
Well, hello there Monty.
A most felicitous morning to you, Montgomery.
Huh? Oh, Thanks.
Eugene, did you hear the way Whit and I spoke to each other when he came in?
Well, that's the way you're supposed to say hello. No fancy shmancy words, just a nice simple howdy-do, or hi or hello. Understand?
Very well, Hello Guinevere.
A most felicitous morning to you, Eugene.
Huh? Hold it, hold it now, Jenny. Did he tell you to say that?

101.s: Connie directs one of Whit's plays called 'The Sower and the Seeds', but when her cast starts abandoning her, she has to find ways to deal with it.
q: Actually, uh, I did the play while I was in elementary school. It was called 'Little Flip-Flop Meets Mean Old Mr. Gum'. It was an anti-litter program!
Have you tried?
Yeah, I've tried. I start with a pencil and a blank piece of paper.
And, I end with pencil and a blank piece of paper!
The computer club has something urgent? What could be urgent?! It has a fractured floppy disk? A cracked keyboard?
I guess everything is taken care of now, Eugene?
Down to the last microbyte!
Monty, you can't leave!!
Hey! This is one thing I can do as good as my sister! Goodbye!
The news of it has spread...
The news of it has spread... Um...
Even out to these lonely...
The news of it has spread even out to these lonely... Um...
And nethermost...

102.s: Robyn and Connie find a hidden attic at Whit's End and stumble upon a forgotten mystery involving an old pipe organ, a greedy professor and "the greatest treasure."
q: Start from the center, and play a deaf cabbage!

103.s: In an attempt to get out of gym class, Curt Stevens and Oscar Peterson join The Odyssey Owl, but their lack of experience causes problems.
q: Where would any of the great writers be if someone didn't let them work on their school newspapers? Charles Dickenson would have never written classics like 'David Coppertoe' or 'Oliver Twister'! William Shakespeare couldn't have penned those immortal words, "To be, or not to be" or "Romeo, Romeo, let down your hair."
That was Rapunzel!
Or the time you told him you had a rare tropical disease?
I should have used a different colored magic marker.
You remember that award-winning article in the Odyssey Times about the embezzling at the Acme Corporation?
Yes. You mean you...
That's right! I read it.
