All right you bunch of gumdrops, two more laps and in ya go! Curt, Oscar - put a little effort into it, will ya?
We're coming!
Yeah, so's Christmas, but I don't have that long!
They make us run around and around on this track, and for what? We're not learning anything!
Mr. Peterson
Running around in circles?
Yeah. That's what he says he does every day at work.

Come on, Mrs. Medlock! Give us a chance! Where would any of the great writers be if someone didn't let them work on their school newspapers? Samuel Clemens would have never met Mark Twain! Charles Dicksonson would have never written classics like David Coppertone or Oliver Twister! William Shakespeare couldn't have penned those immortal words: "To be, or not to be! Wherefore art thou?" Or, "Romeo, Romeo, let down your hair!"

104.s: Jimmy uses the Imagination Station to travel back to the 1800's! He meets up with a fellow named Abraham Lincoln in Washington, D.C., but events soon take a drastic turn!
q: Far be it from me to compare any of my measly Imagination Station
Just sit down, and after I close the door, push that white button.
The one that's flashing?
That's the one.
This is worse than free ice cream day at Whit's End.

105.s: Jimmy uses the Imagination Station to travel back to the 1800's! He meets up with a fellow named Abraham Lincoln in Washington, D.C., but events soon take a drastic turn!
q: John Wilkes Booth. That's why his name is so familiar. He's the man who shot Lincoln!
What'd you say boy?
They're gonna kill Lincoln! I've gotta warn the president!
You can't change history, Jimmy.
Then why'd you send me through this?
So you could do what you're doing now. React to it. Learn from it. And hopefully use that knowledge to try and change the only thing that can be changed: the future.
Oh, and Jimmy?
You still think Zapazoids is better than the Imagination Station?
No, I think the Imagination Station is better. But just barely.

106.s: Curt Stevens runs for student council, but lies a lot in his speeches, while Phil Phillips attempts to cash in on Odyssey businesses. Including Whit's End.
q: It’s not what you call something, but what it is. The name, the label on the outside doesn't change what it is on the inside — the same with how you look on those posters. Uh, you got that?
That's great, Mr. Whittaker. You should be a politician.
I didn’t understand a word you said, but it sounded like it made perfect sense.
Well, it is serious. I couldn't do my job without my squeegee.
Well, the job's done, Whit. The window's all clean. At least as clean as they'll ever be with all these kids running around.
I'm sure you did the best you could.
Well, I don't know why I bother, when I know they'll be dirty again tomorrow.
Hold on, Whit. Make that out to Walton's Hygienic Maintenance and Engineering Company, please.
Here's your check, Bernard.
Transaction note.
The bank's gonna start calling them transaction notes.
Gotta keep up with the times, Whit. It's the only way to survive.
See you tomorrow, Whit, if we don't both die in our sleep.
Boy! How did you know he was a fake?

Because a good marketing person has more respect for people’s intelligence — the same with good politicians. And that’s what I was trying to tell you, Curt. Just because you change the name of something, doesn’t mean you change what it really is. You see, my train set is the same train set, whether I called it the Iron Bucket, or something like The Fireball 5000. Fireball 5000 sounds more exciting, but it doesn't really make it a faster train set. It’s all just a name game.
Gotcha, Mr. Whittaker.

A lot of people like to play the name game with other things, too — like doing things that are wrong. They think that by changing the name, it’s not wrong anymore. But a lie is still a lie, even if you try to call it ‘rhetoric’ or ‘campaign promises’. You get my meaning, Curt?
Yeah, Mr. Whittaker. I think I’m getting the idea.
It’s like.. like salt on a potato chip. It gives the speech flavor to... taste good.
You're making this up!
I’m not! Ask any politician. Potato chips always taste better with salt on them.

107.s: Robyn is intent on proving that a chain letter won't cause her bad luck, but it would seem that there is some magical force working against her.
q: Just cleanin' a few of these second story windows. What does she think I'm doin' up here on a ladder? Knitten' a sweater?
But you'll get bad luck if you don't, Robyn. I had a great Aunt once who had nothing but bad luck.
What happened to her?
Once she got her purse stolen after a hurricane went through her neighborhood, and her house caught fire from a short circuit in a gift electric blanket for her water bed.
Really? All that happened to her at the same time?
Yeah. Well, over six years.
Look: it's called a chain letter. I think we won some sort of contest!
Whew! Nice to know Whit's trash smells as bad as everyone else's.
If you rub a rabbit's foot, it'll bring you good luck.
Good luck for who? Not the rabbit, that's for sure.
Take the pill, Robyn. And keep your fingers crossed.
DAD! Why are you saying that?
Saying what? I just don't want anything else to happen to you. You escaped the bike crash - knock on wood - and now we're going to get you all better. Cross my heart.
We even hung a horseshoe over your door.
A horseshoe?!
We probably should have taken it off the horse first.
I don't believe it! Leave me alone! I'm not superstitious!
"Superstitious"? That word has thirteen letters in it! Thirteen is bad luck!
You're late for your meeting, Robyn! You'll have to run!
But be careful of the sidewalk!
Step on a crack...
And break your mother's back!

108.s: Isaac Morton is pressured to join the "Bones of Rath" to fit in, and hopes to prove to himself that he has courage.
q: If I become a Bones of Wrath
A police record?
No! Fame, prestige, power...
Cuts, bruises, fractures...
Or else what?
Or else I'll call you a barnyard animal!

109.s: Jimmy and Donna Barclay tell their parents two different versions of how their TV caught fire.
q: I’d tell you the rest, Dad, but... Adventures in Odyssey
You want to hear bathwater? Ha, I’ll let you hear bathwater.
Yes, Jimmy? May I help you?

I don't know.

[A car] looks better on the road than a computer!

Boys — they're so weird!
Life would be a lot easier without girls.
Have you tried: Telling her to get lost and then throw mud on her?

Invite me to the wedding!

Uh, oh. Come on, Traci Needlemeyer

How fascinating.

Why does everything have to echo in dreams?... echo in dreams... echo in dreams... echo in dreams.

Curt Stevens

I hate baseball. I'd rather be working on my minibike.

Do ya know him, Bart?
I thought you didn't want to be rescued.
Are you kidding? I'd rather be rescued and have to deal with my dad than sit around here and have more counseling sessions with you.
Thanks, Rodney. I like you, too.

Don't look at me — I gave up playing with dolls a long time ago.

Apology accepted, Donna.

Apology accepted.

123.s: Jimmy Barclay falls into a world of fantasy and magic, as he and his cousin Len Barclay battle the forces of evil. But does Jimmy realize what he's gotten himself into?

Jimmy, I wanna talk to you!
Speaking of storms...
Girls. Ya can't live with 'em and ya can't live with 'em!
I like Len Barclay
Castles and Cauldrons
I'm glad. There are some things it's good to be afraid of.

C'mon, everybody — there's a victory celebration going on over at my place. Let's get over there!
But, Mr. Whittaker... we lost.
Only the game, Robyn. Only the game.

Why don't you just put Boswell down and let him eat it up? Okay, bad suggestion.
Connellsville Furniture. How interesting.

You're weird, Jessie.

P-p-pass it on through? No, I can't pass it on through; that would mean a loss of money to the store! It might reflect on my paycheck. Are you trying to take food out of my mouth or something??

When I take a look at someone, I want to see the heart and the spirit. What a person is on the outside doesn't last. But on the inside, there's a soul that goes on forever.
Would you consider yourself a bigot?
Me? No way. Is that what this is all about? I thought you were talking about being prejudiced!
You want to talk to some people who know about bigotry, you have to take a drive down to Sloughburgh. I used to work with a guy from there. Its only a few miles, just across the state line.
You won’t sell me a soda?
In a word, NO. I don't sell to sitters, but if you give me a quarter, I'll let you use a hose around back. Just don't put your mouth on it.

We do not collect the money then. We do it later.

Oh, I thought so. But once all this is done we finally get to the headliner. Pastor Fire-and-Brimstone steps up and reminds us of what wretched creatures we are...once a month or so, he'll invite folks to come forward, but the rest of the time he just wraps up with another little ditty or a closing prayer to catch what we missed the first time around...Then everybody shakes your hand off again, and they all go out front and smoke cigarettes.
Nobody smokes.
I mean there are lots of old people at church, I mean look at you!
Well, thanks Connie.
Well, uh, you know what I mean.
You'll never guess what's in this magazine.
A cure for the chickenpox?
Will you forget about the chickenpox?!

152.s: The Barclays decide to listen to their pastor and sacrifice something they love to do... watch television! But it turns out to be a lot more difficult than anyone expected.
q: I think I'll go home and watch Young Hearts Turning.
Thanks a lot, Benedict Jezebel!
We can sacrifice the TV!
What are we gonna do, burn it on a bunch of rocks?
You were talking about that dumb soap opera, "Young Stomachs Turning."
"Young Hearts Turning. And we weren't!
They think Kyle is going to ask Jamie to marry him, because he broke up with Monica!
It was Heather.
... Donna! Mr. Whittaker!
You forgot me, Jimmy.
A friendly store where everyone knows each other — oh, it just warms my heart.
I think the pastor was on to something. The challenge, I mean, to sacrifice something at home.
Uh, oh. We're in trouble.
Look, the pastor talked about sacrificing something we consider important to us, you know, giving it up as a... tribute to God.
I'll give up spinach!
Ah, nice try, Jimmy, but I was thinking of something else — something near and dear to all of us.
I want to know why you were so anxious to go to bed.
I wasn't anxious, you were anxious.
I was not! What makes you think I have anything to be anxious about?
Your anxiousness makes me think you have something to be anxious about.
I don't believe it. You acted awfully anxious for someone who says you didn't have anything to be anxious about.
That's because you made me feel anxious by being anxious.
You wan'a have a go at Zappazoids while you wait?
Sure! Well, uh no thanks.
The end of the world must be coming and I must be standing in the middle of it. Why not?
We're giving TV up for a month and Zappazoids was part of the deal.
But, that's like giving up breathing or having your nose hairs plucked out!
You're telling me! Nose hairs?
I'm a man of principle!
You mean you're a man who GOES to the principal!
Uhhh... yup.
I should have put masking tape over Jessie Morales

153.s: Curt wins a contest to become the city's most powerful official for 24 hours.
q: Well, I meant every word I understood.
Miss Plumduff, my first official act as mayor will be to expose corruption at every level of our city's government.
Yes, starting with your nephew. The chain on his bike broke and the baseball card on the back tire fell off. Have him arrested and released immediately.
What do you think the city will do now?

Oh, I'll recommend appointing a full independent panel to conduct a full inquiry into the circumstances behind this scandal, which means, of course, by the time the panel comes to any conclusions, no one will care anymore because we'll have assured the people in the meantime that this administration will be rethinking its current policy of land grants, when a more broad-based detail policy can be submitted—which, when it is submitted, will be inconclusive and open to misinterpretation and thus of questionable help to the government.
You're really crackers, aren't you? Straight from the pack, 100% saltine. You make it sound like you've done this before.
Plenty of times. You didn't really think anything changes in government, did you?

And finally, as your mayor, I will tighten the belt of our city government around the waist of indifference and reckless bending. So what if I meet up with a few celebrities? Just remember, a penny saved is a penny earned. And the early bird catches the goose that laid the golden egg! Even if it is only one day, I'm gonna make sweeping changes to make our fine city the apple of this country's eye — a silver lining on a dark cloud — a short walk down a long pier.
It seems as though you're trailing behind two other personalities.
Adolf Hitler and Saddam Hussein.
Whose big idea was that?
It was all a part of your plan to tighten the belt around the government's waist!
I meant everyone else's waist, not mine!
I'm Brown, from The Sun!
Really? Are you peeling?
In order to simulate the economy, facsimile growth and prime the pumps for productivity, the city is going to give geographical incessitives to Acme Amalgamated. So take that, Mayor of Connellsville!
Keep an eye on things. If they get violent, throw yourself at their mercy.
What a brilliant idea, Mr. Mayor!
Ah. Only moderately.

154.s: Jimmy Barclay begins his journey of adolescence, while confronting his changing voice and his first crush.
q: I'd play Juliet to your Romeo any day...
I've been kinda busy since our vacation to Florida... uh... three years ago.
I'm in love with Connie Kendall!!
Artie Powell

155.s: On a trip to Chicago, Whit and Connie get caught up in a dangerous mystery involving a portable computer, the Department of Defense, and some familiar--but not very friendly--faces.
q: Do things like this always happen to you when you come on these trips?
No, this is the first time...
Oh, great! Make me feel welcome, why don'tcha...
There's our shuttle, Connie. Let's hurry. Hold that van! Oh — we're gonna miss it.
HEY! WAIT FOR US!
I knew I brought you along for a good reason, Connie.
"Property of John A. Whittaker, Whit's End, Odyssey." It truly is a small world! Whittaker.
Yeah? Well, you better watch it, bub. Cause I know John Avery Whittaker and he—
What a coincidence. So do I.
Huh? Who said that?
I did. Hello, Miss Kendall.
Yes, Dr. Regis Blackgaard at your service.
All the biggest airlines fly here. The terminal covers miles! It's so big, the baggage claim is in a different time zone!
You're kidding!
Yeah, I'm kidding.
Hey! What are you checking for? Bombs? Drugs? Bootlegged tapes of the Praise Kids in Concert?
They better not have touched my hairdryer!

156.s: On a trip to Chicago, Whit and Connie get caught up in a dangerous mystery involving a portable computer, the Department of Defense, and some familiar--but not very friendly--faces
q: You have more loopholes than a spaghetti strainer!
Ah, yes, that Odyssian humor...

Don't you understand that when you go out for revenge, you've gotta dig two graves! One for the person you're after and one for yourself! Richard, there's no such thing as revenge, not really. It never replaces what you lost. It never restores. It doesn't even satisfy. You're out of the detention center now; you've got your whole life ahead of you! Now please, give me the gun!
Laugh now Whittaker, but I'm not finished with you. Not by a long shot.
Those are a lot of maybes.
Six, to be exact.
No, no, no, no, no, Miss Kendall! Don't try to think! Leave that to me.
Alright, nobody move!
What are you going to do — frighten me with rude expressions?
Not so fast, princess!!
Please don't hurt me, please!!!!

157.s: When Eugene discovers a tombstone with his father's name on it, he tries to find out if he still might have living relatives.
q: Can you imagine being related to Eugene? I think I'd rather pull out my fingernails with a pair of rusty pliers.
All those brains, he doesn't have the sense God gave a rabbit.
Oh, Mr. Walton. I hadn't noticed your presence.
What presents? I don't have any presents, just a bucket! I wish he'd clean his glasses.
That's so formal, Eugene! Just call him Cousin "Bernie!"
Feel better now, Mr. Walton?
That was my lemonade...
I refuse to be related to Eugene Meltsner!
Leonard... Leonard Meltsner!
Seems like you can't swing a dead cat these days without hitting somebody who's trying to save some plant or animal. What do you call 'em, endangered, uh... endangered...

158.s: A movie crew comes to Odyssey to film a movie about Whit's End! But the Odyssey gang soon learns that Hollywood isn't interested in the facts.
q: If these kids spill one more drink, I'm going to use the bucket as a lethal weapon!

You oughta see this baby. It's so white you could turn it on its side and use it to ski on. More doors than a bus station locker room. And so long you'd have to be double jointed just to turn the corner.
A movie here? About the people of Odyssey? Oh, wow! I wonder if they need any female announcer types.
You're in my story, Bernard. Don't you want to perform as yourself?
Me? Not a chance. I'd rather leave that to someone like Robert Redford, Charlton Heston, Jimmy Stewart. You know.
That may be hard to do.
Anyone good then. Someone who can catch me as I truly am.
That may be even harder to do!
My pleasure. If I remember the story correctly, you're quite the character.
Uh... character?
Very funny, a real curmudgeon.
Oh, no. Not me. I wash windows. Super shine. You see?
I don't exist, Whit.
There's one more character I wanted to talk to you about. Eugene.
What'd you do? Turn him into a calculator?
After I refused to let them mangle my hair, they got another actor who's- How can I say it? Um--
A geek, Eugene. The actor's a geek.
It's the only thing about this film that's accurate.
I beg your pardon?!

159.s: Richard Maxwell returns to Odyssey to try and ask forgiveness from the townsfolk. It's hard for Richard, as some people don't want to forgive what he's done.
q: Once again, you've saved my life in more ways than I deserve. Boy, that was poetic.
What does Richard Maxwell
Well, Richard Maxwell
Is that a yes?
A conditional yes, yes.
I'll take it.
If it wasn't locked down you'd take it.
I am... sorry, Mr. Riley. And I hope you can forgive me... one of these days.
Just get out. Get out.
I knew I should forgive Richard Maxwell

160.s: Bart Rathbone tries many shortcuts to get his new business, The Electric Palace, opened in only a few weeks.
q: Rodney, you scared me.
Why, doing somethin' you're not supposed to?
Our grand opening is in three weeks. Turn around and show 'em, Rodney.
Opens in three "weks?"
Uh, that's supposed to be three weeks. Rodney!
They got the point!
There's only one "l" in "electric."
I told ya, Rodney.
Hey, I'm in charge of promotion, not spellin'!

Come one, come all to the grand opening of the Electric Palace! You'll find high-voltage savings on current models. Prices so low, they're shocking! Bolt over to the Electric Palace and see "watt's" happening. Just say, "charge it!"
I just want something a little more... punchy, that's all.
Punchy?! If it were any more punchy, it'd have two black eyes and a broken nose!
Hey, that's good! Can you put that in somewhere?
No, I don't think so.
Don't call me "pop"!
No, sir; I don't know what I'm talking about.
I'm backed up against a wall here!
No, you have plenty of space! Look!
It's a figure of speech!

161.s: Isaac Morton takes a ride in The Imagination Station and learns more about David and Jonathan and finds out how to be a true friend.
q: Why do you make these adventures so real, John Whittaker
Aw that's too bad.
Samuel? Samuel!
That's my name don't wear it out.

162.s: Connie tries to keep Jessie and Donna interested in a project without having them fight constantly.
q: Connie, I really thought a woman of your age would know better.
Wha... what do you mean, a woman of my age??!!
Uh oh, what's this? The two of you are gonna gang up on me now? Maybe ridicule me for not putting my clothes in chronological order?
..."chronological"?
and Connie, I'm sorry about saying what I said about you.
That's okay... What'd you say about me?
You don't wanna know.
I don't? Why don't I, was it that bad?

163.s: All the girls are jealous of Monica Winters. They all want to be like her, but Melanie and Traci find out that Monica's life may not be as great as they thought.
q: Do you know how old she is?
Monica? Oh, fifteen or sixteen, I guess.
She's eleven.
Guilt by association.
Or, haven't you heard of freedom of speech?
Yeah, I heard of it. I think it's a shame when people take advantage of it like this.
You mean, when they say things you don't like.

164.s: Bart Rathbone urges Odyssey to celebrate the 1960s, but Whit has reasons not to celebrate.
q: Would you look at that guy's hair? It looks like his head exploded!
It's just a parade.
A parade that is all a part of Bart Rathbone's scheme to make money. What's he calling his shop this week? Rathbone's Electric Castle and Rock and Roll instruments of destruction?
Great get-up, huh? Aw, they don’t make ‘em like this anymore.
Small wonder.
Imagine finding a pair of old bell-bottoms, paisley shirt, turtleneck, and a chic-a-dill-ick headband all in the same place!
John Whittaker
I spent five years so strung out on drugs I didn't know which end was up.
Sure. That's one of the things everybody talked about in the sixties. "Get high, expand your mind!" But nobody said it would ruin my life.

The leaders, the music—everybody wanted to "turn on". Free drugs, free love, free everything! They...we invited the world to join along. But nothing's free, Connie. Nobody said anything about the cost.
Okay, so I'm getting the idea. The sixties weren't so good.

Not so good? Connie, not only weren't they good, they were dangerous. Yeah, some parts of it were alright, but the upheaval of the sixties has everything to do with the problems we're dealing with now. You see Michael over there?
You mean that guy in the corner?

He's your age, Connie—your age! And he's battling cocaine addiction. He didn't have anything to do with the sixties; he wasn't born then. So why the addiction? Because we said, "If it feels good, do it!" in the sixties and the seventies and the eighties. Your generation and the generation to come is suffering the effects of that!

My ideas? They were wrong, okay? They sounded good—made for nice poetry. But they didn't work. Not in this world, not with the people the way they are. We failed, Connie. We didn't help the world. We didn't change anything! In fact, we made it worse. We wanted freedom without responsibility, and now the consequences are two decades of a drug epidemic, abortion, AIDS, and people who think only about themselves!
But how can you blame the sixties—an entire decade—for our problems?
I don't blame the sixties. I blame myself.
Because this thing we call the sixties was made up of people like me who got everything wrong. And I guess running this clinic is the only way I know to say I'm sorry.
Oh, yeah? Yeah?! Well, I never liked your music, anyway! You guys ever hear of Lawrence Welk? He could run circles around you guys... without destroying a hotel! Ugh...so much for the sixties.
You'll have to take a... trip with me.
Trip? You mean like drugs?
No. A trip in the car, actually.
Uh... what are all these numbers here? The number for the police station?
No. The bill for the damage. The decimal point is on the far right.
We take cash or credit card.

165.s: Bernard Walton tells the story of Esther to Melanie and Robyn Jacobs.
q: One man's Mede is another man's Persian.
How are the Jacobs girls today?
Yeah, you know. Upset.
Oh, good. For a second I thought you were gonna start riding the rails.
Nothin worse than a squirming kid when you're trying to tell a story.
There was a certain jewish man named Mordecai who was at the palace.
Why was he there?
Uh, I think he worked there.
What kind of work did he do?
Uh, I don't know he was probably a window washer. It's a very noble profession you know.
And when King Xerxes saw her his eyes nearly popped out of his head!
When his majesty has a thorn in his foot, isn't it best to remove it before infection sets in?
I wouldn't know, I've never had a thorn in my foot.

166.s: Bernard tells the story of Esther to Melanie Jacobs and Robyn Jacobs
q: There you go. A chocolate sundae with raspberry sauce.
Thanks, Mr. Walton.
You're welcome. Hope your folks have good health insurance.
75 foot… for what purpose?
To hang, uh, one of the king’s officials.
Mordecai, excellency.
Haman, you would execute the very man who saved me from assassination?
Majesty, it’s all a mistake.
Silence. Servant, where is this gallows?
It stands in Haman’s courtyard.
How convenient. Hang Haman

167.s: Dr. James Dobson comes to Odyssey! Whit and him talk about the upcoming video series and Dr. Dobson gives some advice to Melanie Jacobs.
q: It’s just you’re my biggest fan. Uh, I’m your biggest fan. I mean, my wife is your biggest fan. She listens to your broadcast everyday. You and Mike Carp.

168.s: Lucy Cunningham-Schultz, Connie, and Eugene think Whit's life is in danger when a medicine man visits town and places a curse on him!
q: I'm Connie. From the Kendall tribe.
Eugene Meltsner, are you out of your mind?!
It's not like a story is gonna walk in the front door!
Don't look now, but I think one just did.
...make owner fall through air, and die.
Die? Yuck! I hate my voice on tape!
If Whit has something to say he'll tell me.
That's very mature, Connie.
Haha, yeah. And it's also about to kill me.

169.s: A stranger holds Eugene and Connie hostage when he decides to hold up Whit's End.
q: I'm gonna hide behind the counter with Brain Boy here.
Boy, you two were made for each other!
We're just friends, actually.
I thought we'd all hold hands and sing. What do you think? I'm gonna tie you up!
You two yak more than a couple of ba-, uh, yakking things!
Congratulations for doing something intelligent. It's not often you're complimented for that.
It's over here behind this picture.
I knew there was something about that picture!
Because it is a painting of a safe?
Well, yeah...
You kids secure now?
Yes; my fingers are getting quite numb, thank you very much.
I think mine's a little loose.
How 'bout that?
Much better!
What happened to the lights? You on some kind of timer or somethin?
Maybe Whit forgot to pay his electric bill.

170.s: Robyn Jacobs hasn't been studying for her tests and her grades are beginning to slip. In an effort to increase her marks, she tries to find a good way to study.
q: Studying, there are few things I appreciate more than an evening burning the midnight oil. Pouring over text after text in search of things I haven't learned or mastered. Alas, such evenings are very rare now.
Because you're almost finished with college?
No. Because I know almost everything there is to know.
You'll have to pardon my momentary lack of comprehension, but what in the world are you talking about?!
May I inquire to the source of your depression?
She just lost a hundred dollars.
Tell the whole world, Melanie!
You misplaced one hundred dollars? Then I would suggest an immediate search of the area and perhaps a call to the police.
She didn't lose the money out of her pocket; she just didn't win it...
Why don't you remind us of what Manifest Destiny is?
Uh... It was when... The boat called the Manifest Destiny was sunk by... um... England and everybody got mad.

171.s: Whit and Eugene head to Mexico to help Dan Isidro. But when they get there, they set off on an adventure they hadn't planned on to find the Cross of Cortes!
q: Whit, I know where Eugene is.
What? Where?
Down there in the arena!
Mr. Whittaker... HELP!
I'm much better with French and Greek.
What is the Cross of Cortes?
Mr. Whittaker, it's the crucifix worn by Hernan Cortes when he defeated the Aztec nation and conquered Mexico.
Well that much I do know.
Well legend holds that the cross is embodied by some sort of supernatural power.
Yes, making the wearing almost invincible in battle, much as the sword Excalibur did in the King Arthur stories.
Yes, only the cross really exists.
[reading from a letter] 'Just in case you were thinking about backing out of the trip, ha ha....' Don't ask, Eugene.
Well, I'm part of his home church, he probably heard it through the grape vine!
Your church cultivates grapes?!
¿Coma esta el baño?
El baño esta por aqui.
A key? I don't need a key. I NEED EL BAÑO!!!

172.s: Eugene, Whit, and Dan Isidro look for the mysterious 'Cross of Cortes'.
q: Dan, it's only a cross. It can't save anybody.
And now, mi corazón, you will give them both to me.
Maria, th-that's a gun!

173.s: Whit and the gang use Kids' Radio to tell Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol with an unusual twist.
q: What, through that very dirty window?
Remember, ignorance of the law is no excuuuuuuse~! Whooooo~!
You're not going to take me to the cemetery to show me my future? Here lies Ebenezer Stooge, pauper, hated by one and all?

Well, I'd like to, but I can't. It's not in the budget. Besides, you don't have to see all that to know the right thing to do. The lonely grave will only be your future if you want it to be, Ebenezer. It's up to you. But if you do want to change, being thankful for the right reasons is a good place to start.
I'm confused, Spirit. The Wretcheds, the people at the mission — they have nothing. And yet they are still thankful.
And you have everything, but are not.
Well, it doesn't make any sense.
It would if you knew what they knew.
What? What do they know?
That true happiness does not lie in things, but in the Maker of all things.
You mean, God?

Yes. The one who truly understands that can be thankful in any situation, whether rich or poor, well-fed or hungry, in good health or gravely ill. Earlier, this afternoon, you asked Bob Wretched what God has to do with Thanksgiving. Well, that is what He has to do with it. Take Him out, and the holiday becomes meaningless.
I'm so happy I could bust!

174.s: The Myers family comes to Odyssey with a secret: Father and husband Ernie Myers is in jail.
q: When the gavel came down and the judge sentenced my husband, we were sentenced, too. Except we wound up in a different kind of prison. But it's just as lonely and dark.

175.s: Connie's uncle, Joe Finneman, remembers the December 7, 1941, attack on Pearl Harbor and a hero who tried to stop it.
q: That's how I met Sam. Have I ever mentioned Sam?
Why don't you show a little trust in your own people?
Because I'm Japanese. That's why.
Maybe I'll go back and have a little crow sandwich or something. Oh, boy; will I ever learn...?
I'm berry busy.

176.s: Connie and Eugene take another Christmas trip in the Imagination Station to meet King Herod, three wise men, and the baby Jesus.
q: My name is Gaspar.
And I am Eugenius, the thirsty.
I am Proclus the commander of the Roman Garrison.
Yes, yes I know who you are. Welcome. But I was referring to the vision of loveliness standing behind you.
This is Connie.
Water. I'm so thirsty. No, that's the one thing I mustn't think about. I'll think about something else. Food, yeah that's it. I'm not thirsty, I'm hungry – for a big plate of water!
They say talking to yourself is a sure sign you've been in the desert too long.
Huh? Oh, hello. Yes, I suppose that could be true although when there is no one else to talk to one's own self does present a willing and captive audience.

177.s: Eugene Meltsner and Connie Kendall get separated in the Imagination Station when they return to finish their adventure following the birth of Jesus.
q: You're the fourth wise man?
Indeed. Fitting company, ey?
Oh, brother.
Do not grieve for him, Connie. He found the peace and hope you and I know.
Even though it means death?
My son, he found a reason to live that was worth dying for.
Yes, our Messiah!
Simeon! What do you think we should do? Do you think it's a trap?
What makes you so sure?
Because I have seen the eyes of those who search for peace, for hope. I've seen those eyes in my own reflection while waiting for that child. And I see it in the eyes of Proclus.

178.s: Eugene moves in with an unlikely roommate—window washer Bernard Walton!
q: I'm not against what other people think! I mean, it's not my fault they're wrong!
To borrow the colloquialism, I am without perspiration.
Look, since my wife is gone, maybe we could enjoy ourselves with some bachelor kinds of things.
It's no wonder you and Whit are friends. Manly activities, Eugene! Things that men enjoy doing!
Oh, you mean things like wearing the same pair of socks for several days, or shaking up a soda can to see who hits the ceiling with the spray!
Now let's, uh, punch the highway!
You mean "hit the road."
Hold on, hold on. Don't you college boys know how to take care of your equipment? That computer screen is filthy.
Oh, I've been meaning to clean it. Anyway if...
Never leave until tomorrow what you can put off today, er, something like that.
Mr. Whittaker, the man used a squeegee on my computer!
Mr. Walton, are you alright?
Apart from being pinned under my scaffolding and suffering from countless bruises and probably even a broken leg, I'm just dandy. Why do you ask?
I came here to apologize, and apologize I shall. Ahem. Mr. Walton, I'm sorry for being so much like you.
A stubborn, know-it-all, to borrow the colloquialism.
That's an apology!?
College kids. They think they know everything just because they can punch a few buttons on a computer.
The doctors want to keep me overnight for observation. What do they want to observe me doing? Using the bedpan?
You're the only guy I know who could ruin gratitude by saying thank you!

179.s: Robyn Jacobs and her father, Dale, have a clash of wills over music from a band called the Bones of Rath.
q: So, so, you are interested in the Bones of Rath, huh?
That’s right Bart. See I’m ah...
Hey, you and everybody in Odyssey. They are the biggest thing since sliced peaches.
I figure everything'll be all right once the National Guard hit 'em with the riot hoses.
"As Crusty as Bones of Wrath
Be Electric Palace
That's an accordion? I thought that they recorded a traffic jam.
Besides, we have a right to free speech. It's guaranteed in the first appendix.
Ah, Bill of Rights.
The first Bill of Rights, yeah
Lyrics? I don't remember anyone playing a lyric. Wow, they must be more talented than I thought!
I wasn't even sure Rodney Rathbone

180.s: Isaac Morton sets out on a quest to keep himself pure from all worldly things.
q: You're throwing away your Disney Read-A-Long records? You think they're impure?
I don't know. Better safe than sorry, I figure.
Who knows how this stuff might influence me at weak moments.
Do you know what your mother would say if she saw that you threw away her Life magazines?
Thank you son?
You know, Jerry Morton
Strike me down with a pair of dirty trousers!
Isaac, you're throwing away my collection of National Geographics!
Yeah? What could possibly be impure about them?
Have you seen those pictures from Africa, dad?

181.s: Curt Stevens and Lucy Cunningham-Schultz compete to be elected student body president, but Curt's campaign turns underhanded.
q: Hi, Lucy! Glad you could make it!
Why not? I cover all the accidents around school.
Would this be the Curt-Stevens-offering-candy-as-they-come-out-of-the-bathroom-so-they-will-say-what-I-want-them-to-say poll?
You’ll find [the poll] states that I’m in the lead.
There’s a revealing statement on the intelligence level of the voting public.

182.s: Isaac Morton finds a bag filled with money and wants to keep it, but it's up to Judge Eugene Meltsner to determine what will happen to the loot.
q: Representing Rathbone is, uh, Rathbone!
Peacocks and pelicans, no!
Young Rathbone, you'll have the chance to tell your side of the story later. But for now, you will keep your muscles immobile and your oral cavity tightly sealed!
He means, keep still and be quiet.
I believe I said that.

183.s: Connie reads three stories from Whit about moderation, which include a talking toaster, two farmers, and a young prince.
q: Why don't you live in a style more befitting your financial status?
Now you sound like Eugene.
Well, there's no reason to get insulting...
I'll cut you all off from your power sources!
What a dream. Better turn off the ol' alarm,
You're Welc—AAH! What?!
Now, can we talk about my timing mechanism? I think it's a little slow.
WWHHAAAAAA, OOOH OOOOHH HOOOO HOOO HOOOOOO~!!!
I didn't know the sole of my shoe was pink! Oh, that's my foot.
And God... thank you again for my wise friend John Whittaker

184.s: After a journey in the Imagination Station, a brave knight follows Isaac into modern times.
q: Come, Squire, let’s be off!
I think I already am.
That box didn't contain any souls, it was a radio!
I'll be right with you, I-yie-yie-yie-yie-yie!!!
The lower-level communication device requires your presence!
Uh, translated!
Huh? Oh! You're wanted on the phone downstairs!
No harm done. Ya know, it's not every day someone gets thrown out of their car by a... a Sir William

185.s: Lucy befriends a shy, would-be writer from her school named Emily, who starts writing for The Odyssey Owl.
q: It's Emily Fowler. I can't keep track of her anymore!

186.s: A young Bernard Walton faces a difficult task as a school crossing guard.
q: People never say what they mean anymore.
Minutes ticked by slowly. My life flashed before my eyes. Eh... pretty boring.
Thanks for standing up for what's right, Bernard!
I think you were doing more than 20 when you drove up, principal.
Don't push it, Bernard!

187.s: Whit tells the story of a young adult named an American who puts his life on the line in a foreign country to save an irresponsible prince.
q: James Armer and Prince Roderick
As alike as two peas in a pod.

188.s: Robyn must make a choice when she's asked to go to an unchaperoned party with the most popular girl in school.
q: Look at this coffee table. Has somebody been tap dancing on it with cleats?
You know what I was thinking.
Yeah. Was somebody tap dancing on the coffee table with cleats?

189.s: No one believes Rodney Rathbone when he claims he's discovered a con artist in Odyssey.
q: And being the kind, generous, good-natured person that I am, I decided to help him out!
Please, do I look like the kind of person who would try to profit from my fellow student's misfortunes?
In a heartbeat.
Eh, you know me pretty good, don't cha?
I plead the fifth commandment!
Sounds more like the ninth commandment to me: "thou shalt not lie"?
Now let me get this straight. You're telling me that Mark Reed is going to rob my house on Saturday?
That's right, Mr Barclay.
And at the same time, he's going to be taking our picture at the church?
What is he, twins?
No, no. He's not gonna do it; his crony is.
His crony is gonna take our picture?
No. Reed is gonna take the picture. His crony is gonna rob you!
Oh, I get it. You don't believe me. Is that it?
Well, how should I put this? Uh, no.
But why? It's the truth.
Rodney, correct me if I'm wrong. But aren't you the guy who forced my son to sell chocolate candy bars door-to-door for a charity called "The Send Rodney to Disney World Fund"?
Well, uh, I've never been there.
Not even Bart Rathbone
I got this great little gadget from my Dad's shop, a radio scanner that picks up on car phones.
It's totally legal, and it works great. That's how I know all the times and places of the break-ins.
You're telling me that you followed Mark Reed around this whole area for several days eavesdropping on his car telephone?
And you wonder why people don't believe you.
But I did. Honest!
I'm finding a little difficult to believe you know the meaning of that word, Rodney.
I thought at least you'd believe me. You're supposed to be the guy who gives everyone a chance.

That's just the point. I have given you a chance, chance after chance. Everybody has. Now you're expecting me to believe that you're trying to be honest by telling me that you did something dishonest. Well, it just doesn't work that way. Trust and a reputation of honesty have to be earned.
But, how else was I supposed to get the information?
You still have convinced me that any information needed to be gotten.
Look, Mr. Whittaker, I admit I've pulled some scams in the past.
Yes, you have.
And the reason I pulled them was because I knew there was something in it for me. That's what makes it different. This time there's absolutely nothing in it for me.
Really? What about revenge? "Robert M. Lee", remember?
Well, at first maybe I wanted to back at him, but not now. I'm just trying to keep some people from getting their houses ripped off. You gotta believe me, Mr. Whittaker. Please!
Well, there's no reason why I should believe you Rodney, but since you feel so strongly about this, the least I can do is check into it.
He's gonna do a big story about me and how I exposed the criminals and saved the town, and should get a medal or something.
Rodney, you've learned a lesson about honesty, how about a lesson on humility?
Huh? Humility? Haven't I been humiliated enough already?! I mean I had to tell this story to everybody in town...

190.s: George Barclay follows his son, Jimmy, into a special Imagination Station program created for Jimmy for his birthday. George felt rushed and tried to get it over with quickly, but he learned to give up other things and spend time with his son. They “traveled” to ancient Egypt's land of Goshen and see the Passover.
q: More wood for the fire, Jew!
Yes, sir. I'll never complain about mowing the lawn again.
What is this, a guilt trip?
Well, whatever it takes, George.
You don't know Ra?
Well, only as part of a cheer, but...

191.s: George Barclay follows his son, Jimmy, into the Imagination Station. They “travel” to ancient Egypt's land of Goshen.
q: Well, boy — what do you say?
I say don't go, Pharaoh. You'll lose.
Well, Jimmy, it looks like I'm yours for the rest of the day!
No — strike that. I'm yours from now on.
Thanks, dad.
And... that's just how an adventure should end.

192.s: Donna Barclay wants to wear an outfit to a school banquet that her father thinks is immodest.
q: It all started in Donna's room when I couldn't get her attention because she had her stereo on.
Right, so you walked in.
Who's telling this story?
We both are!
I hadn't finished doing my hair. I wanted you to see the whole outfit.
Well, I'd like to see the whole outfit too, Donna. I mean, I see you, but not the outfit.
My Dad said he's got to get used to me growing up. How's he going to get used to it unless I start dressing grown-up?
Or acting grown up.
Donna Barclay
I'm not sure why I told John Whittaker
Tell me, Jack, honestly. What did you think of [Donna's dress]?
Well, I like it a lot, but...
For all the wrong reasons.

193.s: Jimmy Barclay records an embarrassing secret about Eugene … and airs it on his Kids' Radio show.
q: This is rather embarrassing to admit Mr. Whittaker, but I don't have a driver's license.
You don't have a driver's license?!
Please Mr. Whittaker lower your vocal amplification! This is not information I wish to share with the world at large.
Shocking, shocking, absolutely shocking. It's amazing the things you hear when you... oh, uh, it looks like we have a guest! Mr. John Avery — hey!
Due to circumstances beyond his control, the rest of the Jimmy Barclay Show will not be heard today.
Didn't you take the test?
Of course I took the test!
So what happened?
I failed it! I flunked it!
A couple of days ago Jimmy Barclay

194.s: When Eugene needs help getting his driver's license, he turns to Connie for help.

195.s: Connie's father surprises her by visiting Odyssey … and brings even more surprising news.
q: Forget the trip, Dad!
EUGENE, KILL THE MUSIC!
You still have feelings for Bill Kendall
No, no, I said I was over my anger. When you've loved someone, the hurt never really goes away.
You may not believe this, but, I still do love June Kendall
You're right. I don't believe you.

196.s: Harlow Doyle, Private Eye, opens an office in Odyssey, and his first big case is to help Jessie find her lost faith.
q: Jumpin' whale gills Miss Turner, you better call the police!
Do you think Harlow Doyle
Not with a coon-skin cap!
Jessie Morales
What did Jessie Morales
ARE YOU NUTS?! THE OTHER WAY!! THE OTHER WAY!!
You let her talk to you like that?
It'll take a bigger fish than that to get up early enough to catch me!
Can I have another cookie?

197.s: Whit tells the story of Paul Revere, his famous ride, and the "shot heard 'round the world."
q: You must both leave for safety at once!
Safety? Not while there's a breath left in my body! Bring me my sword!
Hancock, we've been over this a thousand times! You cannot go into battle! You're too valuable to us elsewhere!
I shall go into battle and none shall say me nay! Where's my gun and my boots?
Sleeping, eh? You wouldn't have been listening to our conversation, would ya?
Listening? With the way I snore?
Wow! Paul Revere was there from the start!
He was! He witnessed the shot heard around the world, a shot that rang out for liberty!
What a brave man!

Yes he was, because he lived in a time of bravery. But you know, his time really wasn't so unlike ours, and he wasn't any more brave than we are. He simply had a task to do, and he did it. Our task is to make sure Paul Revere's midnight ride is remembered, and that what he rode for, liberty, is preserved.

198.s: Things get out of control when Isaac and Eugene join in a charitable treasure hunt that also include some very realistic-looking water pistols.
q: I have an idea! No, I don't.
Everybody freeze! To borrow the colloquialism.
What's gotten into him?
It's the water pistol. All of a sudden he thinks he's Rambo.
I've always worried about that boy, Whit.
They just don't make tools like they used to.
Well, they do, but they're more expensive now!
What's the next clue, Isaac?
"Finding the next clue shouldn't be torture; it may be the apple of your eye. Under a bushel or in the orchard. All you have to do is try" ...What do you think?
Whoever wrote that needs to take a course in poetry.
This place is a looney bin!
Well, Brad — can I call ya "Brad"?
Sure, but my name's Bryan.

199.s: Connie learns the importance of time-management skills when she takes on more work than she can handle.
q: I have all the time I need to do the things I have to do. In fact the only thing wasting my time right now is Y-O-U. So if you'll excuse me, I have work to do.
YOU, EUGENE!!
The no factor. Did you come up with that yourself?
Just the title. The concept has been around for a long time. And I think you should apply it right away.
Hey, do you think I can use the no factor the next time my mom asks me to clean my room?
AHHHH!! TOO COLD! TOO COLD!! AUGHH! TOO HOT! TOO HOT!!! Too hot. That's what I think of Whit's End. Nooo...
Wow, I'm gonna be published in The Odyssey Times

200.s: Eugene joins Bernard Walton for a family reunion – and uncovers a dark secret about his grandfather Meltsner's past.
q: He cheated me just as sure as you're standing there!
I'm sitting.
Don't get saucy.
Hello, Grandpa Borealis.
I'll sic the dogs on Eugene Meltsner
We don't have any dogs.
Then I'll sic the cat on him!
Your grandfather was a great man, but he didn't talk much. You know why?
Uhh, 'cause he was thinking?
What are you looking for?
The cameras. This is one of those "Funniest Home Videos," isn't it?

201.s: Isaac starts selling fans door-to-door during a heatwave in Odyssey – and learns a hard lesson about choosing friends and making money.
q: Would I lie to you?
I’ve never lied to you before.
You haven’t had time.
Isaac, son, congratulations. I think you have been Derek (a)
Isaac Morton

202.s: Philip Glossman arrives in Odyssey, hoping to build a highway through Tom Riley's land.
q: I sure do miss Timothy Riley

203.s: Lucy goes out to the Harlequin Dinner Theatre to interview the new owner – only to discover that it’s R.E. Blackgaard! Is Whit’s arch-nemesis back in town? There's only one way to find out.
q: And may I commend you for this makeshift stage you've concocted on this horrid gazebo.
Consider yourself commended.
Ladies and... gentleman.
Well if you kind friendly folks will excuse me, I'll be on my way. Shakespeare the door.
Now wait a minute, why don't you come into my office and...
No thank you Mr. Whiter. I'm leaving now. Good day to John Whittaker
Shakespeare the door.
It's still here sir.

204.s: Jimmy Barclay decides he's too old for Whit's End and the Imagination Station, but comes to a new discovery through an imaginative boy named Lawrence.
q: You? You don't want—maybe you didn't hear me: This is a new adventure in the Imagination Station!
Yeah, I—I heard you, but I'll pass. Uh, see ya.
I feel like Christopher Robin just left Pooh Corner.

205.s: Whit, Tom, Bernard and Eugene head for the hills to do some camping, and find themselves in the midst of a deluge.
q: Begone, O ursine creature! Begone, O forest dweller! Stay away! Get thee hence!
And look at that. Is that somebody's coat?
That's no coat. It's Tom!
All right, who wants to ride shotgun?
Oh, I didn't know we were going hunting as well.
Get in the truck, Eugene.
Uh, yes, sir.
Last one there is a rotten low-density micro-disc! Tally-ho!
You think he might have had an accident as a child?
Eugene Meltsner

206.s: Melanie Jacobs gets a big surprise when her pen pal suddenly arrives in Odyssey for a visit – and she's blind!
q: Honey Jenny isn't abnormal either. She just has a physical handicap. Like some people can't hear or walk. It makes her unique especially since she makes up for it in other ways.
Yeah I know. Her other senses make up for her being blind.

I'm sure she works hard at that but I'm talking about other things. Like she's very nice and kind and pleasant to be with. So maybe you should think about all the things that are special about Jenny instead of letting her blindness get in the way.

207.s: Private Investigator Harlow Doyle gets pulled into a case involving a missing camera, a Bible contest and the always-suspect Rodney Rathbone.
q: All right, Rathney, what's the problem?
What's the problem?!
I asked you first.
It all started when I took Denver Thor
You took a whole city to Whit's End?!
Where's Denver Thor
In Colorado! Oh, that Denver.
Start talkin', and use your mouth.
Yep, yep, yep. Tall, dark-headed, sneery voice — kind of reptilian-looking, ya know?
Reptilian-looking?! Rodney Rathbone
I have personal experience with being ignorant.

208.s: Charles Chunky Thompson winds up saving the day in spite of a a rainstorm, a cranky old woman and a backed up sewer system.
q: Mom, I can't sleep!
Count sheep.
I can't count sheep. It makes me hungry.
Count horses!
Good night, Charles!
Can I help Charles Thompson
Basic motor skills, perhaps?
Calling what I do "fluid management" is like calling a pothole a "pavement deficiency."
Thompson, when the dirty water goes down the drain, where does it go?
Back into the pipe?
You beat all, Thompson.

209.s: Lawrence Hodges joins Christopher Columbus for his incredible trip across the seas by way of the Imagination Station.
q: Step lively there!
Step lively he says. I'd like to see you stepping lively with forty pounds of chain around your neck.
Up the stairs, boy. And no talking.
Right. No talkin'. How 'bout fainting?
Land ho! Land ho! Oh, wait, it's just some clouds. Never mind! Never mind!

210.s: Whit and the gang at Kid's Radio give up-to-the-minute news reports about Abraham, Lot and a city called Sodom.

211.s: Whit programs the Imagination Station to show what life after death might be like. Against the advice of Tom Riley, he tries the program on himself … with dangerous results.
q: Just push the button when you're ready, Whit.
Thanks, Connie.
No, I am serious. You're messing around with somethin' you don't have no business with.
It's only the Imagination Station.

I don't care what it is. You said the whole thing seemed realer than real. And that's what makes it so dangerous. Look, you know that Jesus took the sting out of death. Death is our doorway to God. But it's not something we should want or try to create! It's a locked door until God and God alone opens it for us!

Is this your impression of a mad scientist? Tampering with things that are none of your business? You know what happens to them in the late show and the movies. If the monster doesn't get 'em, the mobs do!
Let's see if this thing works.
What? Mr. Riley? I-It's only been a few seconds!
Let me out! Let me out!
That's enough, Eugene! I get it now!
But—what happened?!
I want you to erase that program, Eugene, understand? Erase it, now!
But Mr. Whittaker won't want me—
Don't argue, Eugene! It's too dangerous to keep! Just erase it, erase it! I have to get back to the hospital!

Whit? I don't know whether you can hear me or not...maybe some of what I'm sayin' will echo through. See, I tried your program in the Imagination Station, and I think I have it figured out. I think I understand what happened to ya. You did a good job on your death program, Whit—too good a job, in fact. You made a program that gives just a taste of what life after death is for a Christian. The reunion with loved ones...the warmth, the beauty of goin' to be with God... I don't know how you did it, but... you did! You made it... beautiful. And attractive. But that's the problem, Whit. Now... now you correct me if I'm wrong, but I figure you made it look so good that you wanna be there—that you wanna give up on livin'. Well, Whit, I have to tell you that you're wrong! You're wrong! I mean—I can't second-guess God, but it's like I told you before—death is the passageway to be with our Lord. It's not a door we should pass through unless God says it's time to go—that's the glory and the mystery of it! As believers, we may long for heaven, but we must remain here as servants until the Master calls us! So Whit... I figure the Imagination Station gave you a glimpse of somethin' you shouldn't have seen yet. So I'm askin' you to come back. D'ya hear me, Whit? I'm askin' you to come back! I think—I think you should come back to us! Please... please, Whit. Come back.

212.s: Whit programs the Imagination Station to show what life after death might be like. Against the advice of Tom Riley, he tries the program on himself … with dangerous results.
q: You look terrible.
Well, thank you. You don't look so bad yourself.
You know, I always said those inventions would hurt him one day, I just knew it!
Look, don't get yourself all bent out of shape here; let's just find out a few more of the facts before we pass judgment.
Spoken like a true Whittaker.
Jen... is he here? Can I see him?
Just turn around, John.
Hi, Dad; how ya doin'?
Only someone as smart as Eugene would do something so stupid!

I-It was the most horrifying thing I've ever experienced. I—I've never felt such loneliness or isolation. It was as though I were completely separated from—everyone and everything... completely and thoroughly alone. Not like I was off by myself somewhere, but... but as though I were... nonexistent in a dark void of solitude. I was alone, Connie! Utterly alone in a—in a burning blackness and I've had nothing but nightmares since then!

For Whit, death will be a place of wonder, miracles... beauty and reunion—heaven, Eugene. But for you, who's never accepted Christ, death is... well, it'll be a place of isolation and separation. If Whit got a tiny taste of heaven, then... maybe you got a tiny taste of hell. Do you understand? Eugene?
...Do you really believe that, Connie?
With all my heart.
Then you'd better explain it all to me... in detail.
That was a very dangerous thing to do, Dad. Trying to capture life after death in a computer program wasn't a very smart idea.
I guess it wasn't.
I should'a listened to you Tom.

I was tampering with things that aren't any of my business, but I learned from it. Getting lost in someone's imagination, memories, even dreams of the future is a... well, it's a limited experience. There are greater adventures to be found in the real world. Which leaves only one question.
And that is?
When can I get out of this hospital and get on with them?
Well, Eugene? What are you gonna do?
What indeed, Miss Kendall? What indeed?

213.s: Connie and Eugene try to ensure that Whit gets his rest while recovering from being in the hospital.
q: Why do birds suddenly appear every time you are near?

"The Pilgrim's Progress in the Similitude of a Dream". "As I walked through the wilderness, uh, of this world, I litted... lighted... on a certain place, wh-where was a den." "Where was a den"? No offense, Whit, but this writer needs to learn something about English.
Well, I'll be sure to tell him.

"As I laid me down in that place to sleep, and as I slept I dreamed a dream." What else would you dream? "I dreamed, and behold, I saw a man clothed with rags standing in a certain place, with his face from his house...(What?) With his face from his own house.
No offense, Whit, but was this thing a big seller?
Well, I can't make heads or tails outta this, but I mean, who's going to believe a character by the name of "Obstinate"?
It's an allegory, Tom.
Huh, doesn't surprise me. It's not much of a story!

Miss Turner, please dictate a memo to myself: Remind me to get my jogging shoes out of the closet. Sign it "Harlow Doyle, Private eye." Thank you in advance, Miss Turner. This is Harlow Doyle; over and out!
Mr. Riley?! I thought I asked you to leave!
You did, and I didn't. So nah-nana-nah-nah!
What?! That’s preposterous, how can you expect us to do the intelligent thing at a time like this?!
Excuse me but would everybody line up against the wall and identify themselves? I'd like Whit to show us who the kidnapper was.
What! Who are you?
Me? Harlow Doyle, Private Eye.
A peculiar-looking fellow with shifty eyes.
It looked like Eugene Meltsner
It looked like Eugene up close, too!
Mr. Whittaker isn't sick, but being held captive against his will!
One and the same. I know the type -- meek and passive on the outside. But inside rages the violent fires of a volcano, ready to explode in a colorful cataclysm of -- Uh, what was I talking about?

214.s: A nativity display at Odyssey's city hall sparks a controversy over the “separation of church and state.”
q: We also have six shepherds and four wise men. So we'll be giving Jesus gold, frankincense, myrrh, and a pen-and-pencil set!
There's something going on around here, and I am going to find out what it is.
Meaning you're gonna make me find out what it is.
Exact-a-mundo!
You really should read more history.
How'd you like to be history, Eugene?
But what would Mr. Rathbone have against our nativity scene?
Indeed! It's doubtful he knows what the Constitution is, let alone what it says!
Are you cheatin' again?
No, pop! This time I took your king fair and square.
You know I don't play that way. And don't call me "pop!"
Would I not be of more service, not to mention completely typecast to say one of the wise men?
You told me the beard makes you itch.
What do you think this donkey costume is going to do?

215.s: Whit and some of the kids from Odyssey go caroling.
q: I don't suppose I'm the only one who thinks this is appropriate.
What do you mean?
A birth in a stable.
Just imagine it. Jesus our savior was born in a place like this.

216.s: Teenager Eric Myers is accused of stealing from the soccer team's cash box.
q: Night-night!
Time for you to get back into bed, young man. But first, we’re going to have a little talk about you taking other people’s property.

217.s: Whit, Connie and Jenny discuss four situations to see if they can spot the differences between the good and bad things people do and the reasons why they do it.
q: Heather didn't have a VCR, but Sherry did. So why didn't Sherry tape the program and have Heather see it later?
H-how about some more lemonade?

218.s: Edwin Blackgaard finds himself in dire straits financially and reluctantly agrees to teach an acting class in Odyssey – after he receives an anonymous donation.
q: You want to play a particular kind of turnip, Eugene?
That was just me talking. I do that a lot.
Tell the good people of Odyssey that Edwin Blackgaard is going to teach the people how to... act!
I thought it was highly imaginative of him to do a production of "Oklahoma" set in Alaska!
I see by the gaggle of parents gathering at the door that we are over our time.
I've scraped more talent out from under my fingernail.
Eugene is a poor... whatever he is who also works at Whit's End.
What is this, sir? I'm a techno geek , who wants to be a musician but doesn't have the talent!?!
There's no point looking a gift horse in the mouth... even if it needs dental work.
Is this what it's come to, Shakespeare? To waste my time and talents listening to country folk butcher lines from "Our Town" and "Arsenic and Old Lace" and "The Importance of Being Earnest"?
I'd rather die.
Fair enough, sir. I'll just make us some tea while we wait for the bank to repossess all our furniture.

219.s: The Barclay family holds a yard sale to tidy up their cluttered attic.
q: Wait a minute, Mary, what are you doing with that whiffle ball set?
I’m putting it in the “to sell” stack.
You can’t do that; I want to keep it.
George, it’s a plastic ball and bat — that look like they’ve been through a meat grinder.
Well, they were chewed up by Sparky. I loved that dog; they’re the only reminder I have of him.
All right, we’ll both tell him.
At the right moment!
“At the right moment”? When’s that?
A month after I move away to college!
I thought he'd give up.
George Barclay
If we were the nation of Israel leaving Egypt, what would we take with us?
The nation of Israel? Sheeps, cows, loincloths — what does that have to do with anything?

220.s: Bart Rathbone holds a big contest and the winner gets a date with television star Chad Pearson. It's a prize every girl in Odyssey wants … except the winner!
q: Thank you, thanks, Burt, thanks, everybody. I'd like to thank everybody who sponsored this event and made it such a fun thing for me. I'm very excited about my day with Katie Kennell!
That's "Bart" and "Connie Kendall."
Oh, right. Hi, Connie...and don't forget to shop at the Electric Place!
Well, I'll be right back. I need to go to the restroom and wash up a bit. No cameras, please.
Hold on. I was running the errand for Whit, so he should be the winner!
Oh, I don't think Nick Grant would appreciate that!

221.s: Whit tells Lucy Cunningham-Schultz the story of the hymn "It Is Well."
q: I didn't know you sing.
Well, I'm sure a lot of our choir members think I can't. But I do my best.
I tell you, Philip, dealing with bureaucracy is no picnic!
Yes, it must be very difficult having all that money.

222.s: The appearance of a piece of cloth supposedly from Jesus' robe creates great hubbub in Odyssey.
q: You know, suddenly I'm beginning to feel very... warm.
No really, Whit, I think it's because of this cloth!
I think it's because you're leaning up against the hot plate.
Huh? Ow, ow!
What does the cloth, feel like?
A cloth, Dale! That's what it is!
Really? What a let down!
No, we haven't seen the ghost of John the Baptist!
This sort of stuff has been going on for years. People finding a splinter from the Cross; a strap from Peter's sandal, or the Apostle Paul's toupee!
No, it [the cloth] wasn't delivered by space aliens!
The "Jesus cloth?"
That's the name Lucy Cunningham-Schultz
No, I don't.

223.s: A debate about the existence of God, a stalled elevator and a ticking bomb are all part of Whit's visit to a local radio station.
q: I know it seems like magic but if you'd just listened to the beginning of the program, you'd know it was a tape of the best of the Cryin' Bryan Dern Show.
Oh. Well, I guess that makes sense.
I'm so happy. Now I'd love to stand here and give you another lesson in basic radio 101, but I have a show to do with your boss. Shall we, Mr. Whittaker?
Park the car, will you Connie?
I'll be in as soon as I find a space.
Try the one between your ears, honey.
Trapped in an elevator with Bryan Dern — a fate worse than death!
There is no excuse for you!
One thing you should know, Mr. Dern, is that Lou Dodsworth
Oh. Well, it's nice to know I'm popular.
Please, God, I don't wanna die!!!

224.s: Whit hears the story of how Tom Riley's son died … from the man who claims to be responsible.
q: P.D., I do know of one friend who will never hurt you or let you down.
Uh huh. I can introduce you to him if you want me to.
Where does this friend of yours live?
Right here, in my heart. His name is Jesus.
What Timothy Riley

225.s: Middle-schooler Erica Clark tries to find joy in every situation, but nearly has an emotional breakdown in the process.
q: I did what any self-respecting, red-blooded girl would've done: I beaned him with my Life Sciences book!
Are you going to Whit's End?
Yeah, if I don't get hit by a car on the way.
What is all the banging around up there?!
That was Erica Clark
I'm trying to be full of happiness!
You sound more like you're full of hot air!

226.s: Lucy takes an Imagination Station to first century Bethany where she meets Marta, Miriam, and Eleazar preparing a feast for a special guest – Jesus!
q: Ah! Mary (c)
Jesus the Christ. Hmm... the Messiah.
You would be wise to keep that kind of talk to yourself, Eleazar.
It would certainly ruin your afternoon to be stoned right here in the streets for blasphemy.
If nothing else, it would put your guests off their food!
And peace be with you, rabbis.
I love Jesus Christ
Can you really love Him without believing in Him, too?

227.s: Lucy takes an Imagination Station to first century Bethany where she meets Marta, Miriam, and Eleazar preparing a feast for a special guest – Jesus!
q: Jesus Christ
What could happen to Jesus Christ
You're a poor assassin, Ishod. You should keep your knife in its sheath so it doesn't reflect the moonlight.

228.s: Eric Myers makes a secret promise to help a despondent widow, but the promise will keep him from the season's most important soccer game.
q: Did ya make up your mind about the game tomorrow?
I can't be there, coach. I have to keep my promise.
The game was supposed to be today, and they changed it. You see, I made a promise.
Did you cross your heart?
Then you don't have to keep it.
Yes, I do. A promise is a promise, whether you cross your heart or not.
Really? So when you promised last week to take me to Whit's End, you still have to do it, even though you didn't cross your heart?
Brooke, I don't wanna go to Whit's End.
But, you promised! And a promise is a promise.
Oh, come on.
That seems to be common about problems, doesn't it? Always being so... uh... problematic.
Yeah. Especially this one.

229.s: Kids' Radio tells the story of a king's generous invitation to his son's wedding and the subjects who rudely reject it.
q: Ooh, it even has a name! Huh, huh, huh. Yuck.

230.s: Lawrence Hodges gets tangled up with the Bones of Rath. His need to find a father figure results in several hilarious flights of imagination.
q: You calling me a sissy?!
Well, if the dress fits!
Your behavior has been terrible! You've been surly, ornery and rude!
Four more and you'll have the seven dwarves.
Do I still have to pay for the broken flower pots?
Just asking.

231.s: Through Whit's new invention, BEAVRS, Connie learns some of the names of God.
q: My name, Constance, means "firmness of mind." Fits, huh?

232.s: Whit attempts to explain the kingdom of heaven to Eugene.
q: I still don't get it. If something like that happened to me I'd want to talk about it.
Well, that's one of the differences between the two of you.
Are you saying I talk a lot?
But you also need to know that all your studying may fail you when it comes to understanding God, His ways and the salvation he offers us.

The Apostle Paul wrote in his first letter to Corinth that God has made the wisdom of this world look foolish, for it was after the world in its wisdom had failed to know God that He in His wisdom chose to save all who would believe by the simple-mindedness of the gospel message.
Well, that certainly would explain some of the things that don't seem to make sense.
You see, Eugene, our minds can only grasp so much about the nature of God, of eternity.
After that, it’s a matter of the spirit—our spirit links up with His in an eternal relationship that gives us the right perspective to understand Him better.
Mr. Whittaker... I think I want to believe, but I need help with my unbelief.
Eugene, that’s as good a start as any.
Eugene Meltsner
Are you accusing me of lying?
Connie Kendall
Believe it, Eugene.

233.s: Lucy Cunningham-Schultz struggles over a job offer from a liberal school newspaper, and Connie pushes Eugene to make a decision about faith.
q: I guess you could call me a "secret agent" of God's will.

234.s: After George Barclay loses his job, the Barclay family wonders what they will do for income.
q: The best is yet to come!
The pickin's mighty slim out in the park, but I did manage to bag this squirrel!
Eh... That looks more like a rat, Dad.
Squirrel? Rat? It's meat, ain't it? Fire up the stew-pot, Mary! We're gonna eat tonight..... No... we can't... No!
Now why are you kids home so early?
Oh, we got run off by the police again.
You know, they don't like us begging in front of City Hall!

235.s: When his father returns from prison, Eric Myers comes face to face with his own lack of forgiveness.

236.s: A new invention of Whit's – called the Room of Consequence – lets Jimmy play out what might happen if he disobeys his parents.
q: It's something new. I'm calling it the Room of Consequence. You see, instead of sending you back, this'll let you play out the future.

I've rigged this room to play out the options and consequences for certain decisions. You'll get the whole picture as if you're doing it for the first time - not only you, but everyone it involves, because your decision will often affect how other people act. You'll get to see it all.
Every time you're tempted to do something bad, I'll be the one who tries to talk you out of it.
Oh, yeah, like in the cartoons. Only, there's supposed to be a good guy on one shoulder, and a bad guy on the other.
You don't need a bad guy. You do all right by yourself.
He can't play with it. You're taking it back to the store.
You just can't trust anybody anymore!
You're telling me.

237.s: Bernard Walton and Eugene tell the story of the Fiery Furnace.
q: Eugene, what are you boring Marsha with now?
Uh, I don't know. Are you bored, Marsha?
No, right now I'm frustrated.
Ah, then you have been talking to Eugene.
It must still have some loose connections...
Then you two have a lot in common.
I shall be scant inches away should you require my assistance!
I require your assistance like I require a third nostril.
Obviously, they were young men made in my old mold.
No, they broke your mold, Eugene.
Why, thank you!
Anyone who talks to you can tell you were still in it at the time.
There, there, King Nebuchadnezzar
Give Eugene Meltsner

238.s: Courtney Vincent hopes to become a world-class ballerina, but a car accident abruptly ruins her dreams.

239.s: Isaac Morton finds himself at the mercy of a techno-bully who has the ability to change grades and alter school records.
q: He's just Nicholas Adamsworth
Computers are the gateway to the future, the pathway to advancement for kids like me.
That’s a shame. Nicholas Adamsworth
There are a number of guys in our school who would very much like to hurt me very badly. I don't like to be hurt. It's very painful.
Didn’t you hear about the storm last night?
I would have to be in another country not to hear the storm.
About the storm. It blew out Nicky’s computer equipment. He lost everything.
What does that mean?
He can’t get into the school files anymore. He can’t do anything anymore.
You’re kidding!
What happened was, he was messing around with some financial network, and they were able to trace it back to him. He’s in big trouble.
You can stare now, but a week ago, I was your best friend.
Ah, yes, Mr. Skinner?
I’d like to see you in my office — now.

240.s: Lawrence Hodges and Jimmy banter as announcers on Kids' Radio and can't agree on who makes the better Odyssey Coyotes sportscaster.
q: No, Jimmy. I'm sorry, but I completely disagree with you. The regular fries are just not as tasty as the crinkle cut.
You're crazy! They're the exact same thing, just- just in different shapes!
You just look at the package of crinkle cut fries. Check out the ingredients. You know what's in the list that's not in the list of regular fries?
Sodium acid pyrophosphate! And that makes all the difference!
Kids' Radio will be right back after this moment of silence for the American troops in...
Since you don't have baseball anymore, I assume we'll see you in church this Sunday, huh?
I don't know, Mr. Whittaker. You know the doctor wants me to rest the arm and all.
Oh, I see. All that heavy hymnbook holding.
You really think I'm a good pitcher?
Well, with a little more discipline and tough practice schedule, I think you can be just as good, if not better than, say... my little sister?

241.s: Youngster Danny Schmidt wonders about death and eternity when his mother's unborn baby dies as a result of miscarriage.
q: First off you'll have to give up all your privileges.
You know. Special stuff. Like staying up late, or playing over at a friends house.
Well, that's not so bad.
That's only the beginning. Wait until you have to do the "s" word: share!

242.s: Kids' Radio tells the inspiring stories behind popular hymns written by Christian greats Martin Luther, Philip Bliss and Fanny Crosby.
q: Listen, before you go I have a little something special for you.

Yes. It's a poem I wrote when I was eight years old. "Oh what a happy soul am I. Although I cannot see. I am resolved that in this world contented I will be. How many blessings I enjoy that other people don't. To weep and sigh because I'm blind, I cannot and I won't."

243.s: To win a contest, the Rathbones go on a frantic quest to become a perfect family.
q: What is that?
Classical music. It aids the digestion.
I think it's workin'. I'm startin' to feel sick.
Look, I know you think you understand what you thought you heard me say, but what you thought you heard me say was certainly not what you thought I meant.
Welcome to our humble commode!

244.s: Whit is pulled into a perplexing mystery when a strange man arrives at Whit's End and claims to have lived there as a small boy.
q: Why you getting so involved in this, Whit?
I dunno. Because there was something about Kenneth Anderson
Beeeeewaaaaaaaaare...

245.s: Whit is pulled into a perplexing mystery when a strange man arrives at Whit's End and claims to have lived there as a small boy.
q: Indulging it will only hurt Kenneth Anderson
I think he's pretty close to the edge already.

246.s: Bernard Walton tries to improve his image by being in play about his life, which is being produced by Edwin Blackgaard.
q: I have to fight fire with fire.
You're not gonna burn down the Electric Palace, are ya?
Tut-tut-tut-tut-tut, Shakespeare. Let's not be hasty. Pray continue, Mr. Walton.
Huh? Okay. Our Father, who art in heaven—
No, no, no. I mean, tell me more.
Is there something wrong with Edwin Blackgaard
I'm not sure.
Shakespeare! Bring down the curtain. Bring down the curtain!
But sir, you're both standing under it!
I don't care! Bring it down!
It wasn't that bad, was it?
No, no, no! You were simply being you. You can't help being what you are. I should never have tried to make a silk purse out of a sow's ear.
In fact, you have my personal guarantee that if we don't do a better job for less money, your windows will still be dirty!
I started with just a rag and a bucket, and now I've got a... a squeegee and a bucket!

To begin my life with the beginning of my life, I recall I was born, born a pauper to a pawn. With a squeegee in my hand... And that squeegee is available for all your window-cleaning needs! Just call Walton's Janitorial Service at 555-6629!

247.s: Erica Clark gets in the Room of Consequence to see what it's like to be 22 years old.
q: I suggest you find something safe and simple to do for the next 35 minutes.
Or adulthood won't be an option for you.
I want to be real old, like 22.
I got asked out on dates by old men. Can you believe that?
Ew, like how old?
I dunno. In their twenties, I guess.

248.s: Edwin Blackgaard produces a live broadcast about monsters from outer space, but the broadcast is a little too real for some listeners.
q: Well, as they say in show business, break a leg.
Of course. Equal wishes for your various limbs as well!
Something's coming out with tentacles. It's huge! It's monstrous!! It's-it's-AUGHH!!

Dale! Dale? Well, ladies and gentlemen, I'm sorry but we seem to have lost contact with Dale. I've been informed that the police are at the scene now and well we'll break here until we have an update.
Help! Get your oily tentacles off of me. Help! Ed, it's got me! The rumors are true!! The rumors are-!
AAAAAH! I WANT MY MOM!!
I WANT YOUR MOM TOO!!

Hellooo! Mr. alien! I am Eugene Meltsner and I am your friend. Do you understand? I am your friend. Ow! Cease and desist! Wrapping your tentacle around me is not conducive to good communication. Ow! STOP!
Eugene!? Eugene!
I'll have to get back to you Ed!
Terrible. Just terrible.
Are you crazy running in front of me like that? I could've hit you!
I'm sorry about that ma'am. Harlow Doyle, private eye, here. I thought you might want to know that the city is under attack!

You'd better grab your water pistols and run for the hills! The aliens are coming! The aliens are coming! Warn your neighbors and your friends and maybe even a few distant acquaintances. The aliens are coming! The aliens are coming!
I would certainly be amenable to the effort.

249.s: Harlow Doyle investigates an attendance decline at Connie’s Tuesday night Bible study.
q: It happened that way in the Bible, didn’t it?
Well, so did parting the Red Sea, but that doesn’t mean we stop building bridges.

250.s: Kids' Radio retells John Bunyan’s classic book The Pilgrim’s Progress with many familiar Odyssey characters taking roles.
q: Do I look like the kind of guy who runs away from danger?
Actually, yes.
Good point. Let's go.
Keep going? Through that? Why it's thicker than a really thick thing!
Might I offer you a bit of sage counsel?
Sage counsel?
The Bog of Discouragement. This place looks terrible!
Oh, I don't know. A few flowers, a little bulldozing...

251.s: Kids' Radio retells John Bunyan’s classic book The Pilgrim’s Progress with many familiar Odyssey characters taking roles.
q: What are yous doin' on my private grounds?

252.s: When it's apparent that a petty thief is on the loose in Odyssey, Rodney Rathbone convinces 10-year-old Henry Thomas to take the law into his own hands.
q: A brilliant idea!
That's what we need, a brilliant idea.
You know, you two might just start a trend.
You mean of people painting their hair blue?
Actually I was thinking more of responsibility and forgiveness.
Hey! There's something here I didn't notice before! Look!
By George, you're right! It's... dirt?
I'm Sam Johnson, and I don't do anything. I'm a kid!
Is that with an "i" or a "y"?
"Kid" is spelled with an "i."
Oh. Well I was talking about "Johnson," but since you brought it up...
Sounds like you need a detective! Want me to help you find one?
What about you?
Well... okay. Though I wouldn't advise it.

253.s: Whit takes middle-schooler Courtney Vincent on an Imagination Station tour of Christmases past.

254.s: Bart Rathbone's TV trivia contest pits Eugene and Connie against a college student named Katrina Shanks, who seems to have captured Eugene's heart.
q: You're playing well, Katrina.
