You're not so bad yourself.
The tension's so great, you could comb your hair with it!
Name one international bird that is known to bark like a dog. Do you know?
Well, who wouldn't know? The Senegal Finfoot.
Connie Kendall
Look at me — I'm pesperating here!

255.s: Lawrence Hodges claims that agents from Destructo have kidnapped Harlow Doyle near a mysterious cave.
q: Well, gents, our work here is done.
What are you gonna do with us?
The only thing we can do.
Yep. Leave ya here.
Well, that's not the only thing you can do; you can kill us!
Yes, it is a nice scent, isn't it? Perfect for those pressing social engagements... like jail!
Great barrier reef! Whit's End — a bedrock of evil!
The police can't stop Destructo
Asking politely.
Begging and pleading for mercy.
No! By infiltrating and destroying their headquarters!
Well, yeah, there's always that, but you know...

256.s: The Barclays win a contest for an all-expenses paid vacation to Hawaii, but the Rathbones are coming along!
q: You're our tour guide?
That's right. Don Iowa, guest liaison.
Ooh, I just love Hawaiian names - how do you spell that?
No, your last name.
Anything else?
Two aspirin, please.
Coming right up.
What's the matter, you got a headache?
I can't believe you volunteered us to go to The Electric Palace just as Rick Rancid was about to start, Lawrence.
Sorry, Jimmy; I didn't know what I was thinking.
I may have to kick you out of the fan club for this!
You'd look pretty silly attending the meetings all by yourself.
That's true.
There are five tickets, and only four of us.
It would have to be somebody close to us...
Have I ever you guys how much you mean to me?
And someone who would appreciate the educational value of the trip...
My next school report is on Hawaii's flora and fauna. If only I had some samples...
Who could it be? Who? Who?
Oh, come on guys!
I know! Lawrence!
Can you think of anybody?

257.s: The Barclays win a contest for an all-expenses paid vacation to Hawaii, but the Rathbones are coming along!
q: He was great? What about me? I'm the one who braved the waves!
Braved the waves? You rode the board on your hands and knees!
You expected me to stand all the way up?
Who wants pork rinds?
A luau is supposed to be a happy feast! You people are bringin' me down!
That's what happens when you rent from a place called "Jack's Pretty Good Wheels."
Look at the size of the pig they're roasting!
I know, it's almost too big for the spit!
They spit on that pig?
No, Doris. The spit's what they turn the pig on to cook it over the hot coals. See?
Oh, yeah. Just so they don't spit on it.

258.s: The Barclays win a contest for an all-expenses paid vacation to Hawaii, but the Rathbones are coming along!
q: He must have caught an updraft.
It's carrying him off.
Yeah! Toward Pearl Harbor!
I want Doris Rathbone
Captain Quid
I'm never going to see my children again.
This is unbelievable.
I'll say. He took the pork rinds!
Oh, great. We're stuck out on the ocean in a soggy, rickety old rust bucket.
Soggy, aye. Rickety, perhaps. Old rust bucket, maybe. But rat-infested?
I didn't say rat-infested!
I know, but she's also rat-infested.
Find an oar!
I wish there was some way to cheer Lawrence Hodges
The only way for that to happen is for his father to walk through the door.
Oh, good, you're still here. You folks didn't happen to see my hat when we came ashore, did you? I sat it down next to the other lady, and, uh...
Dad? Dad! Dad!
Lawrence! I can't believe it's you!
How'd you do that?
Old Hawaiian custom. Happy endings.

259.s: Middle-schooler Sam Johnson tells his friend Elliot Richie to stop his weird science experiments, but then Sam takes an Imagination Station trip where he meets another young man who tinkers with inventions.
q: Here's some money, Mr. Whittaker. Uh, keep the change.
Uh, thanks, Rusty.
They're up to something...
They sure are. He was 15 cents short.
Every great man was once a Thomas Edison
Mr. Whittaker, I can't believe I caused all of that. Just because I didn't keep my mouth shut.

Well, most of us suffer from that problem. It's easy to criticize, to pour cold water on people's ideas and dreams. But encouraging people, even those that want to do seemingly impossible things, can be very hard. Yet, it's probably what they need from us the most.

260.s: Eugene comes to Connie for advice to win the heart of Katrina Shanks, who seems to be interested in another man.
q: You're a boy, which naturally means you don't know the first thing about girls. I'm a girl, which—
Which naturally means that you know everything there is to know about boys and girls!
Now, would you care to explain to me what that tirade was all about?
Tirade... it was nothing. Lines from a play I'm working on. It's called, "The Large Foot Pushed Deep into the Mouth."
Of course! Don't allow the facts to get in the way of your opinion!
"Goes without saying?" "Enjoyed our meetings?" Eugene, I said to be sweet and romantic, not submit a budget to your department head.
My mind is racing, you see. And alas, they do not exist.
Please accept this token which Katrina Meltsner
Well, naturally I assumed that my attentiveness would communicate a certain level of feeling.
Eugene, your actions communicate only that you're a walking encyclopedia — no more, no less!
Well, thank you!
Pardon me while I shrivel into profuse embarrassment.
An amendment: pardon me while I die of embarrassment!

261.s: A bully makes young Danny Schmidt afraid of walking to school.
q: Danny, what happened to your eye!?
I told you I had an eye problem.
Danny, you have to go to school.
Because you need your education, in order to get a good job, so you can take care of your parents in their old age! Out of bed.

262.s: After losing his job, George Barclay and family are trying to cope with not having a regular paycheck. Jimmy and Donna pray for their dad to get a job, but get a very unexpected answer.
q: Where'd you learn to pray like that?
What do you mean?
You sounded like an adult. What'd you do, read it somewhere?
Cut it out. It's rude to critique people's prayers. I wasn't talking to you anyway.
Did they like your new tie?
...Did they like his tie, Mom?
Well, I picked it out.
The best is yet to come.
Donna, Jimmy... I'm pregnant.

263.s: Edwin Blackgaard and Sam Johnson come to the conclusion they need to be "bad" once in a while to get noticed.
q: Would you like it if someone bad-mouthed your dad?
You did one time.
Uhhhhh... did you like it?
Well, neither do I.
Is that the only reason you wanna do good things—to get noticed?
No, I wanna do them because I know it's right. But being right all the time doesn't get me praise from teachers or free ice cream from Whit's End!

You heard me; so what? Sam, doing good is its own reward, and I got news for you: it always pays off! Sometimes in ways you can't see—in fact, most times in ways you can't see. But it always does, because doing what's right pleases God! And that's the most important thing, now, isn't it?
That's right, Blackgaard. Joe, Frank, Bubba, and the rest of us. Now get out of here. We're gonna save your theater!
After all I said about you? Why?
Because it's our job!
How are we going to PAY FOR IT??!! You know, I must remember this moment. It's a good association exercise for anger... AND FURY!!!

264.s: Jimmy Barclay discovers that all that "worthless stuff" he neglected to learn in school was more important than he thought.
q: These are math and science questions, the answer being critical to saving a person's life.
(discouraged) Right...
Open up, Hodges! We know you're in there!
Oh, no! Destructo!
Open up! Or we'll huff, and we'll puff, and we'll... knock your door in!
Maybe I'll run off with the circus and become a lion tamer.
You'd probably have to get good grades in zoology.
Then I'll become a pilot.
Engineering, physics, aeronautics...
A bus driver.
Mechanics, math, civil law!
Well, then I'll become a politician!
(pauses) Hmm. Well you've got me there.
But I don't like science, Mom! In fact I hate science! I'd rather have splinters pushed under my toenails, and South African killer bees cover my whole body than do any more science homework!
That can be arranged.

265.s: A carelessly uttered word from Eugene creates havoc as it becomes the fashionable insult for the kids in Odyssey.
q: Ready for the test?
I think so, but I’m a little fuzzy on the French and Indian war.
That is the test, Charles.
Oh, then I guess I’m not as ready as I thought.
Your choices have left you somewhat... maladroit.
What?! What did you call me?
What did he call her?
I think he called her a malatroid.

266.s: Whit tells Lucy Cunningham-Schultz about the creation of the Bible Room, and the discussion leads Katrina Shanks to a very important decision.
q: That is depressing! Aren't you depressed?
Well, I wasn't...
I believe that... I'm in love with Katrina Meltsner
Please don't take offense.
Oh, I won't. Unless you're going to criticize my mustache.
Philo Sanderson
I guess you could say that that's what Whit's End has always been about: to redeem not only rooms, but lives.

267.s: Eugene's relationship with Katrina takes an unexpected turn when his computer disk filled with unsent love letters goes missing.
q: "Non-system disk or disk error. Replace and strike any key when ready."
See? Replace what? Strike what? I was ready to strike the computer and replace it with an abacus.
Eugene, Connie...they're getting stranger all the time. Must be something in the water.
There. That's not bad. I don't know why people complain about computers so much. It's a breeze.
Oh, no! I left Katrina in my laptop!
Would I snoop around in something that wasn't mine?
In a heartbeat.
What?! You eat while you're working on your computer? Don't you realize the damage you could do with a careless crumb or a spilled drink?
It's a computer, not the Ming Vase Collection. What good is the thing if it's not a sturdy working machine? I mean, you said when we bought it that it was a wonderful tool.
A tool, yes, but not a sledgehammer or a—or a TV tray! You have to treat a computer with care and kindness. They're delicate creatures who must be maintained with respect!
It was a mix-up, and "she" took it.
"She"? What "she," my chest constricts to ask!?
Well, she thought it might be for her!
Which "she," Miss Kendall?? And why would she think it was for her?!
BECAUSE HER NAME WAS ON IT!!
Eugene, your eye is twitching.
Well, Katrina saw her name on the disk, so she... uh... took it home with her.
She took my disk. The disk with my journals, and poems, and undelivered letters, to the last person I ever wanted to see them!
Yeah... I’m sorry, Eugene.
Oh, it’s quite alright. If you’ll excuse me, I should go to Katrina’s dorm room and... explain.
Yeah, I guess you should....
...Good night.
He took that better than I thought.
WAAAHAHAAHAAAHAAHAHAAHAHHAHAAA!!!!!!!!!!

268.s: Donna Barclay tries to cope with all the change going on in her life by adopting a stray dog.
q: OK, OK. I’m giving Normal
Terrific. That way he can see how late he’s keeping us up.
OK, everyone is present and accounted for, so a quorum is definitely present!
Excuse me, but will the chair please speak in English? Boy, you send a guy to seminary...
As much as it pains me, and for reasons heretofore stipulated, I must vote my conscience and cast a "no" to Normal
Come out and play, Dad! You should see Harry fetch a stick: he never brings it back!
Donna, it's three in the morning. Would you please do something about your dog?
What am I supposed to do with him?
Don't tempt me.

269.s: Upset that her father has canceled his visit to Odyssey, Connie unleashes her anger on men in general.
q: I’ve met pit bulldogs with better attitudes!
If you need me, I’ll be weeping in the corner booth.
If you need me, I’ll be shaking nervously in the corner booth.
You mean, you're saying you just, uh... complimented me?
Well... your shirt, yeah!
Excuse me, Mr. Whittaker, but I... I think I feel faint!
I just wanna be left alone, okay? I have a headache.
Self-inflicted wound, I believe.

270.s: Connie's uncle, Joe Finneman, is reluctant to reveal the true story of what he did in a remote village in the South Pacific during the waning days of World War II.
q: Uncle Joe, you fought in World War II, that alone makes you worthy of an article! You're a piece of living history!
Connie, Dale. There is no story. Now really. Ok?
Ok, I read ya. But you need to know that I'm gonna keep digging. I think you do have a story and I think it deserves to be told.
Whit was wounded at Guadalcanal. Were you there?
Uh huh. For three months.
Ooh, Australia, that's where they did the Sound of Music.
That's Austria.
The name's Joe.
GI Joe? He's a GI Joe!
GI Joe! GI Joe!
No, no. Just Joe. No GI.

I think you'll be interested in hearing this. Sometimes it's difficult for us to see the forest through the trees. When most of us look at Joe Finneman, we see a man who fought bravely and was wounded to rescue a group of children he didn't even know from an almost certain death. But when Joe Finneman looks at Joe Finneman, he sees a man who ran. Both from his unit and from those children. So, was he a hero? Well, if you think heroism is never doubting or being afraid like they show on TV and in the movies. Then no, he wasn't a hero. But if you think of it as doing the right thing when it counts, then Joe Finneman is every inch a hero in my book. And remains so for setting the records straight. So here's to you, Joe. It's my sincere hope that someday you'll be able to step back here with the rest of us and see how great the forest really is. I'm going to go back to watch the rest of the parade now, Uncle Joe. But I just wanted you to know that the only person around here who thinks you're a coward is you.

271.s: Danny can't seem to force himself to practice the piano for the talent show at Whit's End.
q: Danny? Danny?
I said we're at the Little Theatre. Are you all right?
Uh, sure. I was just thinking.
About Star Surge?
How'd you know?
You keep referring to me as Ed McHam.

272.s: Bernard tells the story of Jacob and Esau – and the cunning deceit that nearly destroyed the brothers. (Part 1 of 2)
q: You mean to tell me you've never heard the story of Jacob and Esau?
Will I get in trouble if I say no?
And they wonder why society is going down the tubes.
Who cares? He gave away wealth and power for a little bit of stew. What was he? Nuts?
Well, it might seem that way, but the Bible puts it differently. It says Esau despised his birthright.
What does that mean?
Well, he didn't have much respect for his family. And he made it even more clear when he went out and married two women his parents didn't approve of.
Two women? I thought that was illegal!
So Rebekah came through again. Pretty sneaky.
Maybe. But you need to understand that none of this happened by chance.
Nope, there was a greater power working here. The Lord God.
Can I have that piece of pie now?
Sell me your birthright for it?
Good girl. Take it.
Kids never watch the bucket.

273.s: Bernard tells Erica Clark the story of Jacob and Esau.
q: How these kids can get a flag pole dirty is beyond me.
People sure did a lot of running back then.
Well, they had to. Their cars were in the shop.
Just remember, God can heal the worst of relationships between brothers and sisters.
Meanwhile, you need to be patient and loving. And the next time Haley does something bad to you, short sheet her bed.
No. Kid believes anything I tell her.

274.s: Eugene decides to take a journey away from Odyssey to broaden his horizons and gain new experience … only to find that the road to adventure intersects with Bernard's trip to San Diego.
q: It's been my experience that experience for the sake of experience usually isn't a very good experience at all.
I beg your pardon?
My pilgrimage will be to—there!
That's the sign for the women's room.
Oops! I'll try again.
Owners of pickup trucks often carry inexplicable and unnecessary items in the back.
I'm taking an extended—shall we call it an expedition?
Well, call it whatever you want, but tell me what you mean.
Eugene Meltsner
Possibly as a marketing question. Perhaps we need to convey a more sympathetic image.
Eugene, we're staggering down the road in the middle of nowhere. What else could we add to make us look more miserable? I had to ask.
I think of it as... a journey to myself!
Sounds like a very short trip.

275.s: Eugene and Bernard's cross-country journey gets waylaid in the middle of Iowa. There Bernard and Eugene meet Graham, a kid who desperately wants to leave his small-town life.
q: I'm thinking of a, uh, thing. You have twenty questions to guess what it is.
I don't wanna play anymore.
Oh, is that Woody over there? He certainly is an attractive animal. A large attractive animal.
It's a pig. Pigs are ugly.
Well, perhaps not to another pig.
Well, Eugene. You wanna go watch a pig? Or does that fail to stimulate you intellectually?
Actually, I would enjoy a good pig watch.
Eugene, there is hope for you yet.

276.s: In Colorado, Eugene meets a group of people who are just like him. Bernard is not so fortunate; he fights a traffic ticket in court.
q: My name is Elizabeth.
Oh, hi, how're you doing?
How am I? Well, contrary to all of the negative factors that have been impressed upon me in the previous six to seven days, I feel rather energetic, if not vigorous! How are you?
Excuse me, I...need some air. Okay, Bernard, now what? You're in a room full of Eugenes! Maybe I can just sit in a corner somewhere and they'll leave me alone.
Give a man a hammer, and he goes power-crazy!
The what? What'd he say? These new fangled houses can't just have living rooms anymore.
I'd be hard pressed to think of any place I would rather have been tonight.
I can think of a couple. Prison. Antarctica.

277.s: An old prospector, a torn map, and a legendary gold mine interrupt Eugene and Bernard’s journey to California and infect them with gold fever.
q: I know. We'll do what the pioneers did when they traveled across the frontier.
Shoot bears?
No, tell stories.
This is it. This is it! An actual river of gold nuggets. It's even more beautiful than the old man said. I'm rich! Rich! HAHAHA! I'm actually rich!
Actually, I'm rich!
Come down from that rope, Eugene.
"Fat chance", to borrow the colloquialism!

278.s: In Hollywood, Bernard and Eugene meet the Smith-Hammer family. Bernard tells a little girl about Jesus, and Eugene is cast to star in a movie.
q: Just take a deep breath, Eugene. Aah, there's nothing like the smell of a new pick up truck. It's heaven.
Smells more like artificially-induced pine scent and upholstery cleaner.
Eugene, you're about as much fun as a root canal!
Put your calculator away, Eugene, or consider being stranded on the side of the interstate in your estimations!
Oh, then it's Hollywood, here we come.
Why don't they put names on these gates?
It's possible they don't want pesky tourists to know who they are.
I'm not a pesky tourist.
Yeah, he's a character in my new movie.
Is that Shakespearean?
Sort of; it's called "Biker Bimbos From Belview Go Bonkers."
Obviously a philosophical work.
Did you hear that, Eugene?
Yes, I did, Kelsey, but I'm still wondering how he got the x-ray machine in his van.
Mr. Smith-Hammer made it very clear that you're to be treated like a houseguest until further notice.
Oh? Wonder what that means?
That means until he doesn't want you around anymore.
Oh, I see. Well, considering Eugene's people skills, I'd better eat fast.

Perhaps I'm uncomfortable with all of this... artifice, the fakery, the make-believe! Now, correct me if I'm wrong, but I get the impression that everyone in this town is acting—acting like a friend only so long as it serves a purpose, acting as though they care when they really don't, acting as though the entire world revolves around what happens here without any regard to the rest of the world!
You got all of that from a day in Hollywood?
No, Kelsey—from a day with you! Frankly, I'm not sure how you cope with such a life.

You cope by doing it the same way. You cope by becoming a big star, making tons of money so you can buy whatever you need, including friends. You cope by becoming powerful enough so you can create your own world, Eugene!
I think that's very...sad. To be so young, and so cynical. Couldn't it be argued that by creating your own world, you're actually missing out on the real world? True friendships? True feelings?
You're quaint, Eugene.
Philosophically speaking, Kelsey, don't you ever wonder what would remain if the artificial world you've created suddenly collapsed? What would you have left?
No, Eugene, I don't wonder—I don't want to know.

279.s: In Hollywood, Bernard and Eugene meet the Smith-Hammer family. Bernard tells a little girl about Jesus, and Eugene is cast to star in a movie.
q: Yes, Mr. Walton.
The name's Bernard! She'll never get my name right...
You know, you need to give Kelsey Smith-Hammer
I would, except... Hubert was driving.
Hubert? Eugene!
Caring in Hollywood is too hard and it costs too much! Nobody can afford it!
May I kiss you good-bye, Eugene?
If you insist.
Anytime you're in town, guys, don't hesitate to, uh, call our answering machine.
Ah, yes, Odyssey. Where, fortunately, Gone...
Thank Heaven.
Then drive on, "Bernie!"
Why, in a flash, "Hubert!"
Bernie, are you talking to Tammi Smith-Hammer
Well, I uh... I, uh, uh... I...
I wanna tell you something. I'm a patient man. I pride myself on my tolerance—

Look, Foster, unless you have some other profound words of comfort to give her, then yes, I've been talking to her about Jesus. And I'm gonna keep talking to her about Jesus. Are you gonna ask me to leave again or can I finish bandaging her feet?
So, Eugene, you're a big hero, huh?
Well, I-I helped where I could. It sounds as if they kept you busy!
Oh, well... you know... L.A. makes such a big production out of everything.

280.s: Bernard and Eugene return from their long road trip to Odyssey, where things always stay the same. Or so they think.
q: Look at City Hall. I haven't seen it so decked out since President Eisenhower came through. They set up a podium and everything.
That's one of the best things about Odyssey. Whit's End is always the same.
Say good bye to who?
Quiet. Say good bye to who, Connie?
To Whit! He left Odyssey!
Wait a minute. What are you doing?
What else? I'm going to run to the airport! I can't let Mr. Whittaker get away!
So why are you runnin' in da middle of dis field?
Why are you drivin' in da middle of dis field?
You know this guy?
Not something I'm about to admit.
Eugene, you never cease to amaze me.
It's nice to meet you all. I'm Jack, Jack Allen.
Eugene... well, it's been quite an adventure.
Indeed. Thank you.

What? A letter from Mister Whittaker! What is it? A Note? Dear Eugene, I'm sorry I missed you. We've been trying to find you but I'm afraid we won't be able to before I leave. There's a lot I could say, but time has suddenly become very short. So rather than embarrass you by saying how much I've come to love you and how I will pray for you every day, I'd like to leave you with one simple thought:
The best is yet to come.

281.s: Tom Riley, Connie, and Eugene find that running Whit's End takes more time than they thought. Tom asks an old friend of Whit's, Jack Allen, to help out.
q: My tooth's coming out! My tooth's coming out!
But if he doesn't come back, who will be Mr. Whittaker?
What do you mean?
If Mr. Whittaker doesn't come back, who will take his place?
No one will take his place. Whit will always be Whit. He's just in a different place. That's all.
Leapin' lolla-pollooza! A mass break in! This is even bigger than Whit's disappearance. It's time to investigate!
If anybody knows about strange, it's me!
This could be the biggest thing since individually wrapped cheese slices! What am I standing here for? Harlow Doyle, pah-rivate eye is on the job!
Why did you fall out of the tree that way?
Is there another way to fall out of a tree?
Why were you hiding in that booth?
He wasn't? Well, what—you weren't?
No, I weren't. Uh, I wasn't!
If anybody else is hiding in a booth, you better let me know right now!
Scrubb! How did all of you get in Whit's End
Through the door.

282.s: Jimmy Barclay attends a basketball camp with Phil McFarland, a teen who thinks he knows everything there is to know about the game.
q: All the knowledge in the world doesn't mean a thing unless you apply it.
Congratulations, Rusty.
Thanks. And thank you all. Because without you, there would've been no one to clap for me.

283.s: Connie and Eugene try to see Jack's secret painting, and Katrina Shanks tutors a difficult student.
q: Perhaps gophers are like humans. They enjoy something challenging to sink their teeth into.
Just so they don't bite off more than they can chew.
You're playing a word game, Eugene? I thought you hated puns?
In their proper place, puns can be a helpful mental exercise.
Miss Kendall, as I've so often observed in the past and your own experiences confirm it: curiosity in your hands is like a dangerous weapon in the hands of a maniac—out of control and likely to harm!
To respond in kind, "yeah!"
I would humbly suggest to be careful not to jump to any conclusions.
Oh, I’d never count my chickens before they hatched.
But you might kill two birds with one stone.
Not when a bird in hand is worth two in a bush.
Unless bird of a feather flock together.
Well, then, I’d be forced to fly the coop.
There was poultry humor in that remark.
Oh, Eugene, that’s a foul thing to say!
Well, I was just winging it.
I wanna say first that you’d better never talk to me like that again.
I don’t care who you are or how you dress or how old you look—that tantrum of yours was worse than a spoiled two-year-old!

Be quiet until I’m finished! Second—don’t you ever threaten me or any adult you come in contact with again, you understand? You think you can wreck my career? Well, imagine the quality of your life without a proper education!

Now you’re gonna turn around, go back to that classroom, and give me a heartfelt apology. And we’re going to study until you can take that test confidently and never have to resort to childish outbursts to cover for bad grades again!
...Why should I?
Because I’m telling you to! And my guess is that considering your obnoxious attitude, I’m probably the only tutor left in Odyssey who will help you get through school!
Well, we looked at Jack Allen
Tactfully put, Miss Kendall.
If it's all right, I have to run some errands in Connellsville

284.s: When Courtney Vincent's diary disappears from her locker, events conspire against her hopes of being elected president of the student council.
q: It's all over school how you accused Shannon Everett (Ellis)
I've gotta get my notebook back.
If I'm elected I think my first job will be to create a new committee.
What kind of committee?
A student council ethics committee.
(laughs) Good call.

285.s: Because George Barclay's demanding schedule is exhausting him, Jimmy and Donna are determined to make sure he takes a day off.
q: Mary Barclay
Hello, Jimmy Barclay
I decided to take a break from studying and do a cheerier activity! Paying the bills...
We're going to get our haircuts!
Or, hairs cut, if you want to be precise.
Is it just me, or are you three acting funny?
Hey, Dad, let's toss the football around!
Eh, I'm not in the mood, Jimmy. You go ahead.
You want me to toss the football around by myself?
I say we all rise to congratulate Odyssey First Church's new kind of, sort of, in between pastor, for the time being...
You want to kidnap George Barclay
But you're so pregnant you can barely reach the steering wheel.
Oh, what a lovely compliment. Thank you, darling.
I also know that whenever we're tested, God is also there to give us strength. He never calls us to something He won't empower us to do.
One for all and all for one. Or something like that.

286.s: Philip Glossman returns to look for toxic chemicals on Tom Riley's farm. Meanwhile, Odyssey's mayor resigns, so Tom Riley and Bart Rathbone compete for the office.
q: Philip Glossman

Hello? It's Bill. You know perfectly well which Bill. I wanna know what you're trying to pull with Tom Riley. I don't like it. This was never part of the deal. I don't care, I never agreed to it you hear me? I won't have any part of it. Fine, if that's what I have to do then I'll do it, but you can count me out.
You should run for mayor, Tom Riley

Look, I wanna thank all of yous from the press for coming here to the Electric Palace. My friends, my name is Bart Rathbone, speaking to you with his own voice here. With the announcement of his retirement, Mayor Jenkins has left shoes that will be very hard to fill. I am talking about the kind of shoes that can only be made out of integrity and trust. Them kind of shoes. Big shoes. Shoes that only a man with big feet can fill. Well, ladies and gentlemen of the press, I am here to announce that I am the man with big feet. That's right. I am throwing my hat in the ring of shoes.., of shoes! Cause, uh... these boots are made for walking, and carrying a big stick, and I'm no heel!

We're back with Cryin Brian Dern's afternoon zoo. We've been talking to mayoral candidate Bart Rathbone. Though most of you know him as the owner of the Electric Palace, as well as one of the sponsors of this show. But hey, that doesn't mean that we won't ask some tough questions. Bart, is that your real hair, or are you wearing a hair piece?
Only my hair dresser knows for sure, Brian.
It's the warmth of Tom Riley
Vote for me, and yous will get exactly what you deserve!

287.s: Philip Glossman arrives in town to run tests on Tom Riley's farm. Meanwhile, Mayor Bill Jenkins steps down which forces both Tom and Bart Rathbone to run for mayor.
q: Bart, we can't continue this debate unless you follow the rules.
Rules, schmules! This is a free country. Anybody should be able to do what they want! That's the difference between me and Riley. I'm into freedom and he's a, whaddayacall, an intolerant hatemonger.
Did I stutter?
Gentlemen, please.
Nah, let em go! This is getting good!
Unlike you, Riley, I believe in toleration. And as mayor, I won't put up with anybody who isn't tolerant!
You won't tolerate intolerance?
So you're intolerant of people who tolerate intolerance.
Yeah! My first act as mayor will be to form a committee to investigate intolerance and stamp it out!
But what about things like free speech?
What about things like that? People can have free speech.
As long as they agree with you.
Well, yeah. Nobody likes disagreeable people.
Okay, Tom Riley
My name is Jack Allen, and by a sudden lapse of reason, I was the one both candidates agreed should moderate tonight’s debate.
We're supposed to start in a minute and I just thought I'd peek in and... you know, say something clever!
Like what, Bart?
I dunno... ah, I couldn't think of anything. So how about, "may the best man win."
Thanks, Bart.
Thank you, Bart.
Course that means you may as well call it quits now, if ya get my drift!
Get out, Bart.
We recorded a tape of the agents confessing that they rigged the test results!
Excuse me! Ah, hold on, hold on. Philip Glossman here. On behalf of the state government, I demand that you give me that tape.
With all due respect, Mr. Glossman... we'd rather make two dozen copies, and then give you the tape!
You think Tom Riley
I'm afraid he'll lose more than the election, Sam.
Get 'em, Frank!
Stop in the name of the environment!

288.s: Kids' Radio tells the story of a talking toy chicken that enslaves its owner in a web of strange demands.
q: I have a friend who talks so much, when she goes to the beach her tongue gets sunburn.
Is that your face, or did your neck blow a bubble?
Know what you get when you cross a cow with a porcupine? A steak with a built in tooth pick. Bawk, bawk bawk bok bok!
I know it's silly, Henny. You're just a toy. But there's something about you that makes me feel good.

289.s: Donna Barclay is annoyed to find herself a source for sermon illustrations, and her brother, Jimmy, wonders if God may be calling him to the ministry.
q: I changed the letters in Jimmy Barclay
Great! Now what do you want me to do, Lawrence?
I think you should wear a bow tie.
I'll look like my George Barclay

290.s: Jason Whittaker, Whit's son, gets sidetracked from his move to Odyssey when he's called to Europe on a mission. He has to find a missing friend who has been kidnapped by the terrorist organization Red Scorpion.
q: We know who you are, Tasha Forbes, Agent 2362!
Now why would a toy shop need a subsonic transmitter?
...It's cheaper than direct dialing?
Anything else, Mr. Whittaker?
Eh, just that box. Oh and the phone. Here, let me unplug it. There ya go. Where do you want it?
Uh, top of da box. Didn't you just unplug that?
Uh, yeah. This happens sometimes. It's a really weird phone. There that should take care of...
Like you said. Weird.
Why don't you just take the box out to the truck and get going? I'll just keep the phone with me.
Yeah, sure. Whatever you say. I don't think it's just the phone that's weird.
You'd think the agency's deputy director would have better things to do than play games!
Life can't be all paperwork, 1131. Oh, I guess I can't call you that anymore, can I?
Nope. Now I'm a name, not a number.
Are you all right?
You're the one who got bashed on the head, and you're asking me if I'm all right? I'm fine. Now would you mind telling me what you're doing here?
I got your message. I'm here to rescue you.
Oh, I see. And you decided the best way to do that was by getting yourself captured.
You know me, always keep 'em guessing.
Wh-who is this?
He's a friend of mine—Jason Whittaker.
What's the matter?
Oh, I'm sorry. It's just that I knew John Whittaker
You know my father?
Unfortunately, your father and I didn't always see eye to eye. In fact we usually ended up on opposite sides. I regret that. But there were things he didn't know at the time.
The name's Bond—James Bond.
Here is the syringe, Mustafa.
My allergy shot! How thoughtful of you.
Very amusing. Let us see how amusing you are with the virus coursing through your veins!

291.s: Jason Whittaker, Whit's son, gets sidetracked from his move to Odyssey when he's called to Europe on a mission. He has to find a missing friend who has been kidnapped by the terrorist organization Red Scorpion.
q: Are you searching for something?
Uh, yeah, a phone jack. I need to plug in my phone.
I don't believe this room has one; however, I believe there is a phone down the hall in the office.
Well, I like my phone better. I know that sounds strange, but you know, it fits my ear, and it's, well...nicer, and it's—it's...
It's ringing.
It's also kinda weird. It does that sometimes.
Remember I told you that "T" in TA418 stands for Tasha?
Well, the "A" stands for Avery.
Let's take a walk.
Okay...as long as we can stay outside.
Jason! You don't think you can trust me?
You treacherous dog! You would betray me?!
Oh, please, not that again.

I know about TA-418. I've always known. Do you think I ever cared about your petty revolution or your mosquito of a group? There's so much more going on here than you can possibly understand, or even imagine! But you have fulfilled your purpose; for that, I thank you. Of course, you also stabbed me with a needle, and for that...make it look like an accident, Abdul.

292.s: The O. T. Action News team breaks the story of Joshua, Rahab, and a standoff at the walls of Jericho.
q: These are the ones who helped us! They have our protection.
What he said! What he said!

293.s: Jack Allen and Jason Whittaker find a mysterious codebook in Whit's workroom that leads them to a secret gang called the Israelites.
q: That's John Whittaker
Something you obviously inherited. It seems to me you spent weeks trying to build a rocket ship that would take you to... where did you want to go?
Ah, the planet Gilbatron in the Beakner galaxy.
You used to play around with codes when you were young, didn't you?
Well, a little. Actually, you could say I still do. As a hobby.
Anything interesting in the newspaper this morning?
Charlie Brown told Snoopy that he's getting a new food dish, but other than that...
I meant on the front page.
Why do you keep calling him Uncle Jack?
Because he's always been like an uncle to me, but he thinks I'm too old to call him "Uncle" now...maybe he's right. Are you right right, Uncle Jack?
Of course, I didn't expect us to get lost for an hour.
It's these small back roads. You have the map; where are we going?
I can't tell. This map only has the major roads. Watch out for that... oof! Pot hole.
I was wondering if you ever heard of a group called the Israelites.
The Israelites.
Course I have.
They're all through the Old Testament. Don't you ever read your Bible?

294.s: On Christmas eve, Jimmy produces a live Kids' radio presentation of the birth of Jesus--which includes an unexpected real birth.
q: No way! I am not playing a bratty, self-centered character.
Why not? You were born for it.
...and Mary (a)
No, no, wrong tape!
They seem like a nice couple. I hope they get to the hospital—duh, the, the, the stable, quickly!

295.s: Jason programs the Room of Consequence so that Erica Clark can actually live in Medical Center of Love, her favorite soap opera.
q: ...Derek will never love me!
No! Not again! Derek loves you — he just doesn’t communicate it very well!
Victoria? Get me my travel agent. I want a one-way ticket to Alaska.
Hang up that phone, Holly.
Derek! What are you doing here? I thought you were in the hospital!
I ignored doctors’ orders, ripped out my own IV, and jogged two miles to say this to you: Holly, I love you.
Now, before I go in, Mr. Whit’s son...
Please, call me Mr. Whittaker.
A little thing like five thousand miles can’t separate us!
I'd like to speak to Miss Donahue, please.
Miss Donahue? Who’s that? There’s no one here by that name. And how dare you accuse her of rigging the awards!
I don't have any secrets.
Are you sure?
I'm in the seventh grade. What kind of secrets would I have?
Oh, Derek! But... what about Hailey?
Hailey? I never loved her.
Oh, Derek! Wait a minute... what about Alexandra?
Alexandra means nothing to me.
Oh, Derek! Oh yeah... and Lillian. What about her?
Oh no! She mentioned... Lillian!
Lillian? We’re just friends. Besides, she moved to San Francisco. Too long of a commute.
Oh, Derek! You’re so... practical.

296.s: Erica Clark loses her friend Kim Peterson at a birthday party and Jack Allen has a problem with Jason Whittaker bringing video games into Whit's End.
q: Uh oh, Pharaoh's men have me cornered.
Part the Red Sea! Part the Red Sea!
Wow! Look at all these kids.
Yeah, there's been a line to play your video game all day long.
Oh, that's great! You know, I'm thinking about bringing out some more. I could do the whole Old Testament in video games. Set it up in chronological order. You know, David and Goliath, Jonah...

297.s: Two young boys, John Whittaker and Jack Allen, venture into a secret cave and fight off pirates in their quest to find Blackbeard's buried treasure.
q: Right down t' my socks.

298.s: Bernard Walton and the gang at Whit's End create a new television variety show.
q: In a certain era, there lived a trio of swine who struggled to construct protective domiciles from the imminent attack of the malevolent Canis lupus.
(very bad singing) I hug you. You hug me. We're a hugging family. Hi, kids. I'm Blarney, the Rhinosaur. I hug you.
Tapestries! Where are my tapestries?
Why didn't they play cards on Noah's ark?
Because Noah sat on the deck!
What man in the Bible had no parents?
Joshua, the son of Nun!
You know my morning kids program?

Yeah, 'Soapy Waters and the Suds Factory'? Oh, sure. I like him. "Listen to me, all you mothers, fathers, sons, and daughters; it's time to clean your TV screens with me! I'm Soapy Waters." Heh, heh, heh…
Aluminum siding! I'm tellin' ya, you can't go wrong!

299.s: Lucy Cunningham-Schultz tries to write a news article about Zachary Sellers and find out why he's in a wheelchair.
q: There's no controversy. I just talked to Mrs. Manco. They've decided not to put diced tomatoes in the tacos.
Look, if you'll leave me alone, I will personally go up to Mr. Burton
Alright, if that's the way you want it, answer a question for me. Why do Lucy Cunningham-Schultz

Let's just face it, you want the dirt. You want to know exactly what put me in this wheelchair and so does everybody else. Fine, I'll make everybody happy. I had surgery on my legs last month because I tore some ligaments. There. You're not writing this down.
I don't believe you.
Okay, fine. Um, I was skiing and fell off a mountain.
Is that the truth?
I was bungee jumping and the cable broke.
What really happened?
I was filming a rock video and stepped on some dry ice.
His name was Hal Cunningham. I was Cunningham before my mom got remarried. He was a reporter for the Odyssey Times. I guess that's why I always wanted to be a reporter.
I... didn't know.
How could you? All you care about is feeling sorry for yourself!
It takes a Zachary Sellars

300.s: Donna Barclay is tired of everyone expecting her to be the perfect pastor's child, but her rebellion goes too far.
q: Here you go, Normal. Anyway, Stewart Reed Barclay
Hey, Mom, Stewart Reed Barclay
He did! I heard him. His first word was carrot. Where's the baby book?
He was just gibbering, Jimmy. Why would he say carrot?
Maybe he likes them?
Oh, would you change his diaper?
He doesn't want to be changed; he wants a carrot.
Trust me on this one, Jimmy.
Donna Barclay
It'll be like going out with... Moses.
Well, Moses' daughter. You'd have to do everything right. You never know when you might be breaking a commandment you don't even know about.
I'm serious. You'll have to watch every step you take. You date Donna, you date the preacher.
Jimmy, hurry. You're missing it. We're trying to find all 50 states in Mr. Baker's liver spots.
Oh, brother.
Oh, look! I believe it's Florida!
Fifteen minutes to digest?! What did they eat — wood chips?
Then, why did you call this meeting?
Well, Mrs. Erskine called it. She suggested that we ask you if there is anything we can do to help.
Mrs. Erskine?

Yes. That’s right, George. And I just want to say that... I’m sorry. I did exactly what you’re talking about. I expected you and your daughter to be perfect, and that’s just not right. So, I’d like to apologize.
Well, thank you, Mrs. Erskine.
Well, uh... what was it I was talking about?
Keeping Donna Barclay
Thanks, Jimmy.

301.s: Sam Johnson wants to renew his friendship with Butch Evans even though Butch is now a member of the Bones of Rath.
q: I got a new bike. It's a 10-speed.
Oh, boy, I bet it goes fast.
It does, I even got a speedometer for my birthday. I got it up to almost forty-five miles an hour once going downhill.
Really? Can a person breathe going that fast?
I have a question to see if Sam Johnson
What did the mother bullet say to the daddy bullet?
We're gonna have a be-be!
You really don't know any dirty jokes?
Well, maybe you can make one up. Let me help you. Try to think of the three most disgusting things you've ever heard of.
Okay, I got mine. You got yours?
All right, I'll let you use mine. Number one...
I don't wanna hear this.
You know, you're really not getting into the spirit of this. Maybe we need to smear some pimento cheese or something on your face. That'll get you thinking disgusting thoughts.
All I know is that I'd still be your friend if you quit being Butch and started being Brian again.
Brian's gone.
That's too bad. Let me know if he comes back. I miss him.
Let's find out who it was and just pound him.
We gotta do more than pound him.
You mean, you wanna do something in addition to pounding him?
Oh, okay. Just as long as pounding is included.
Okay, so Wednesday we're beating up Todd, right?
I thought we said Thursday!
No, Thursday we're egging the nursing home.

302.s: Kids' Radio stages a share-a-thon to benefit a local homeless shelter.
q: Let me ask you this: How many of you have more spaghetti strainers than you even have packages of spaghetti?! I have one word for you: give.
I pledge 12... uh...
Hurry, we're running out of time!
Mugs! Yes, I pledge 12 mugs and they all say "World's Greatest Grandpa!"
That's another reason for sharing: because Jesus asks us to.
I'm Roy, and I need to spend some money.
Well, you came to the right place.

303.s: Danny Schmidt goes against his parents' wishes when they tell him not to watch a video because it goes against their beliefs as Christians.
q: Come on, Danny. What was it called?
Maybe it was something like Slime Creatures From Sludge City?

I don’t want to be different anymore. I want to watch Slime Creatures, and play Demon Racers, and watch Power Reptiles and Police Detectives, and... and... whatever I want to do, not what you want me to do.
I’ll tell you something you can do right now — you can leave the table and go to your room.
Right now! You don’t talk to us like that. Now go to your room and cool down.
I just did something stupid at Jeff’s and kind of learned the hard way that my parents were right.
Well, at least you learned.

304.s: In the Imagination Station, Rodney Rathbone and Sam meet the biblical Peter, Barnabas, and a violent man named Saul.
q: The Noah's ark display. Tiny the elephant's trunk just moved. To borrow from the police vernacular, I think I have Rodney Rathbone
So what do you say, Sam? Ya wanna try the program?
Great! At last, a victim.
For fifty days wages, I'll be Ricky Ricardo if ya want.

305.s: In the Imagination Station, Rodney Rathbone and Sam meet the biblical Peter, Barnabas, and a violent man named Saul.
q: He didn't do anything to him Rodney. Look. Something came out of his eyes.
Gross. It looks like fish scales.

306.s: When Rodney steps through a skylight at Whit's End and breaks his leg, the Rathbones take Jason Whittaker to court.
q: I'm Jason Whittaker. Who're you?
Howard J. WEa-zle.
Wi-ZEL, It's French.
Attorney at law?
Correct. Give me back the card.
I'm just admiring the new skylight we put in the roof.
Jason, it's smoked glass. You can't really see anything.
Ah, ah not true. You can see the glow of the moon as its incandescent rays bathe the office with an eerie somnambulance.
Have you been talking to Eugene again?
Anyone with an ounce of common sense knows that they shouldn't climb on someone else's roof, especially in the dark!
The court isn't interested in common sense--only the law.
Hang on, Rodney Rathbone
Rodney, don't be a dolt.
Anyone dumb enough to do what youse did deserves what he gets. And don't call me Pop.
No, no, no. Don't speak.

Our society places a great deal of importance on "individual rights." It seems a day doesn’t go by that someone isn’t telling us they have the right to do something. And, it’s true. Rights are very important. But there’s a flip side to them that is hardly ever discussed these days. It’s called responsibility. As the old song says, you can’t have one without the other! But these days, people are trying to. And the sad thing is, they’re succeeding. They’ve created a whole new class for themselves called, 'victims." "It’s not my fault," they say, 'Don’t blame me, I’m a victim! It was the way I was raised! It was the neighborhood I grew up in. I’m not responsible." And so, we excuse. And even reward all sorts of bad behavior. And little by little, our society decays and crumbles. Don’t let that happen. You can stop it! You, me, we, the people. We make the laws. We can stop the decay. We just have to have the courage to do it.
Rodney's been through enough i'm sure he's learned his lesson- right Rodney?
Ey! If yas need any help fixing the skylight, give us a ring! I'll sell ya the parts wholesale! (Plus ten percent.)

307.s: Charles Edward Thompson has a terrible time writing poetry in middle school, but he refuses to ask anyone for help.
q: I put on pants every day. To go to school or to play. I like pants. Sometimes I wear pants of blue, or brown to go with my shoe. I like pants. Sometimes I feel sorry for ants. Because they can't wear pants. I like pants. Pants cover my legs so that I can go. Without them I would be cold I know. I like pants. I like them so.
Ah, I love the sound of desperate Charles Thompson
Is your sister as smart as you?
...Maybe even smarter.
You have to have something called humility.
Oh yeah, I know all about that. I’m humiliated just about every day.
No, not ‘humiliated’, Charles — ‘humility’. It’s admitting that you’re not perfect, that sometimes you need other people’s help.

308.s: Lawrence Hodges battles his doctor over getting braces while his mother battles the school board over a new curriculum.
q: A bite of this apple can't do any harm. Just a bite... AAAGGHH!
It doesn't matter who wrote it, if it's wrong.
We're not suggesting that the curriculum be changed; we're suggesting that the board drop the curriculum completely.
On what grounds?
On the grounds that you have a seven-page, single-spaced list of errors in front of you.

Don't you see what's happening here? We're opening the door for the kind of education that suppresses children's understanding, not releases it! It's a viewpoint that limits their grasp of the thoughts and philosophies that made us what we are as a nation. This curriculum isn't a balanced look at events, but someone's agenda! It isn't trying to teach history; it's trying to indoctrinate. It's doing what we used to accuse the Communists or the Nazis of doing with their history books—altering or ignoring facts in order to push a particular perspective on students!
You're fortunate you only swallowed a little of that paint—though what in the world made you paint your braces is beyond me!
Well, you said to use my imagination to make my braces fun!
Well, but Lawrence, I didn't mean disconnecting your brain! How could you be so old and not know better?

309.s: A mystery is triggered when two armed men hold up Holstein's Books and take a hostage--a blind girl named Jenny Roberts.
q: What are you doing?
I'm changing shirts.
Go in the other room, will you?
Jenny Roberts
Don't be such an idiot. She's blind, remember?
Well, I'm going in the other room.
Don't count your chickens before there are eggs.
If I can be of any service, just call me by name. I will be behind the counter. Just say, 'Fred Holstein, we need your help' and I will -- how do you say? -- zipper like a mad dash over.
That's one way of saying it.
Must be rough going all the way to the bookstore just to get hijacked.
You should try it sometime.
Hey kid, what's your name?
Abraham Lincoln.
Have you ever thought of working for the police, Eugene?
What does it pay?
You can't afford the pay cut.
I returned to my room after one of my classes and my dorm room had been burgled!
Ooh! Did they take much from your cash register?

310.s: A mystery is triggered when two armed men hold up Holstein's Books and take a hostage--a blind girl named Jenny Roberts.
q: Excuse me while I assist this person whom I have never seen before.
But Fred, if you never saw her before, how do you know it's her?
Oh my, that is an excellent question. I'll get back to you on that.
Was the book in an envelope of some kind?
Oh, no! Slap your tongue!
I can only suspect that they were not knowledgeable thieves with knowingness.
How're you doing Jenny? You must be getting tired.
Yeah, I am. but I don't wanna stop. I don't want the trail to get cold.
The old hit em with a large reference dictionary trick. Know it well.

311.s: A mystery is triggered when two armed men hold up Holstein's Books and take a hostage--a blind girl named Jenny Roberts.
q: Be forewarned: I am equipped with a very heavy paperweight -- and I am not afraid to use it!
I haven't done anything. You have me confused with someone else. What's the charge?
Suspicion of armed robbery and kidnapping.
No way! It's a case of, you know, mistaken identity.
Jenny Roberts
I don't want trouble and I don't wanna have to hurt you.
Is that what you said to Jenny Roberts when you kidnapped her from Holstein's Bookstore?
I think you know her better as Abraham Lincoln.
Then I shall apply all my faculties to help form a solution!
Hmmm. Think about it too, please.
Come on, Marty, gimme a break!
Have Russell Kosh

312.s: Jack Allen and Erica Clark both come up with ideas that help the community; however, neither of them gets credit for it.
q: It's like I've always said, Abby. The poor have got to eat, too.
Like you've always said?!
I never knew Bart was such a good tap dancer!
You said it!
It means, well, being a leader. 'Cause without leadership, nobody's really in charge... and when no one's in charge, well... you got no leader.
Well said, Bart. Well said.

313.s: Courtney Vincent gets into an intense rivalry with her cousin Hannah, and radio shock jock Cryin' Bryan Dern tries to outdo a competing radio station.
c: What is He Saying Contest Singer
q: You know, I was thinking about it, and I wonder if maybe that song needs something. I dunno, maybe, uh, WORDS?! And I think the accordion player could use A SEDATIVE!
Okay, we still don't have a winner in the ‘What Is He Saying contest’; I'll play the clip again. What is he saying?
I think he said, “The monkey man has no place in the circle of confusion”?
If you really hate polka so much, you should turn to Q94. They got some great music, and you could win a big screen TV.
...Oh, I think we have a winner! My friend, YOU are more annoying than this music!
I'm just gonna play another song. This one is called...'The Sheboygan Shuffle'. Somebody knock me out, I'd like to be unconscious for awhile.

And that was, once again, my favorite song. Stay tuned and I'll play it again in a couple of minutes. This is Cryin' Bryan Dern, making it up as I go along! I'm now in my 25th straight hour. It's been one day, and, oh, 30 cups of coffee since I took over the studio and I'm feelin' great! And if anybody tries to come in here and get me...that includes you, Casey, I see you out there, sneaking around...if you get any closer, I'm gonna take this coffee here and pour it into about $50,000 worth of equipment! People, there's nothing scarier than Bryan Dern when he gets his second wind! Lemme play my song again. I'm giving away polka CDs. Lots and lots of polka CDs. Be the seventh caller right now and you get a copy of 'The Best of the Schmitkee Trio!' What a fabulous edition this will be to someone's music library. Call now! Yes, congratulations, you're my seventh caller.
What's your name, sir?
Johanne Schmingee.

Well, Johanne, you have just won hours and hours of polka fun! This CD, and I don't think I'm exaggerating here, could be the polka standard by which all other polkas are measured! The Schmitkee trio has always been a lighthouse in a sea of polka mediocrity...eh, well, for me at least.
Me, too! This is the most wonderful thing that's ever happened to me in my life!
Play it long, play it loud, Johanne, and my deepest apologies to Johanne Schmingee's neighbors!
We have forty-seven different kinds of cookies.
Forty-seven? Oh, boy...maybe I should just pull up a chair.

This is Cryin' Bryan Dern goin' into my 94th hour of being on the air. Whaddaya wanna do? Maybe I should play a song. Uh...here's one. I can't tell you what it is, because my contact lenses have become a permanent part of my eyeballs and...everything's kinda blurry. I can't seem to get this disk in the player. Forget it. Maybe I should sing a little song...I'll do a little song that my mother used to sing when...wow. I never knew my thumb could do this. I know. Let's have a moment of silence for...somebody. Are we at war or anything? Give me some ideas people, will...yes, we have a caller. We have a caller! You're on the air.
Yes, my hamster's been kind of sick lately.
Perfect. What's your hamster's name?
Great! Let's have about an hour of silence for Binky. Wake me up when you're done.
I don't care. I have no control over my left eyelid anymore. Look at that.

314.s: A stranger tells Jack the story of the Ross family, and their courageous run for freedom to escape slavery.

315.s: A stranger tells Jack the story of the Ross family, and their courageous run for freedom to escape slavery.

316.s: A stranger tells Jack the story of the Ross family, and their courageous run for freedom to escape slavery.
q: You don't have to preach to me, reverend. I go to church.
And so I appeal to you in the name of Christ, your Master, to help us! Please... help us!

317.s: B-TV tells several Bible stories about envy, including Cain and Abel, David and Bathsheba, and Ahab and Jezebel.
q: This time it really is my fault. When I ate the forbidden fruit, the serpent told me I'd be like God. I had no idea something like this would happen!
No, no it's both our faults. We brought sin into the world. Envy is one of the worst.
You see envy can twist your heart so much, that in order to get at someone else, you'll even hurt yourself.

318.s: Jason Whittaker's new Imagination Station program seems to heal people with disabilities. Meanwhile, Connie's elderly grandmother arrives in Odyssey and her health takes a turn for the worse.
q: Sometimes Jack Allen
You know, when we first started talking about it, I thought we were just having a philosophical debate. I didn't believe you were going to follow up on it.
I get tired of discussing and debating. I like to take action. Why not try some of the things we talk about?
Because things can't go terribly wrong if we talk.
Just close Zachary Sellars
Zach, can you imagine yourself running for your life?
You better believe it.
Then, run for your life!
Bill Kendall
No, none of you guys are getting it. I don't wanna go home. I can walk in there, and I don't wanna leave it! I never wanna leave the Imagination Station, ever!

319.s: Jason Whittaker's new Imagination Station program seems to heal people with disabilities. Meanwhile, Connie's elderly grandmother arrives in Odyssey and her health takes a turn for the worse.
q: But I happen to think she was wrong in this case.
Oh, and you're the one who's going to tell parents they're wrong in how they raise their own children?
No, no, of course not. But Eileen Sellars
She was going after what you did to the Imagination Station!
Oh, I get it now. This is because you think she's right.
She's right inasmuch as you don't know what you're dealing with! You don't know what this'll lead to!
Come on, Jack; give me some credit, will you? I reprogrammed those machines to include learning and you approved of them.

Sure. I was for anything that would help the kids and turn down the volume. But we still don't know how much learning the kids are doing when they're dazzled by lights and noise! Don't you get my point? We don't know! And using the kids here as—as—as guinea pigs—
Guinea pigs?!
Yes, for what we don't know, it's dangerous! And that's why I'm against the arcade games and what you've done to the Imagination Station.
Okay, okay. Your opinions are duly noted.
Meaning you haven't heard a word I've said. Oh, Jason...
Why are you so afraid of this new technology? I mean, it's like a miracle of science!
Because there are no such things as miracles of science.
Silly girl; you're not praying for me. You're praying for you.
Yes. Even as you're praying for God's will to be done in me. You're praying for God's strength in you—strength for whatever happens. That's why I want you to pray.
Listen to me, Zachary Sellars
The truth is, I think we have the question turned around. Maybe the better question is, all things considered, why don't things like this happen more often?
What do you mean?
Well, it's a fallen world—a crazy world, in fact. We're subject to disease, death, handicaps, and accidents... it's a wonder things aren't worse than they are.
Y'know, I've had faith when I've been praying for Mildred Kendall
Hasn't it? Are you so sure?
She's still dying.

Oh, but for a Christian, isn't dying possibly another kind of healing? I mean, it's not like this world is the be-all and end-all of everything. Sometimes there's a greater healing than we expect. But that's God's business.
If it's His business, why do we bother to pray?
Because He tells us to. If we don't pray, how can we become more in tune with the mind of God—to feel His comfort even if we don't get what we want? Praying is the only way I know how.
Yes, Connie?
I never really asked you before, but... can I have a hug?
Oh, Connie... of course you can.
Come on, dear. Let's...let's go say good-bye.
Not good-bye, Mom. How 'bout..."see you later"?

320.s: The death of Connie's grandmother causes her family to ponder what death means for a Christian. Connie's father ponders what death means for a non-Christian.
q: Few things are more certain to make people search for meaning in their lives than when face-to-face with the meaning of death.
We're going to need every door in Odyssey fixed before Bill Kendall
Eugene, Eugene. A little sensitivity, hmm?

I guess the thing that comes to mind more than anything is Grandma's faith. To the very end, it was bright and strong. She knew that no matter what happened to her body, she'd be alive in Jesus. She never doubted it. It was as true to her as it is for us to expect the sun to come up tomorrow morning. You know, I was looking through my grandma's Bible this morning and saw some verses she underlined. There in Romans chapter 8, where the apostle Paul talked about all the things that couldn't separate us from the love of Jesus. He listed death first. Grandma knew that. She also underlined the verses in 1 Corinthians 15, where Paul says that death has been swallowed up in victory. He said it has no power. It has no sting because Jesus conquered it on Easter morning.
Wait. Did you hear yourself, Mom?
With Dad. You sounded like a Christian for a minute there.
Well, you know I've always been sympathetic.
Being sympathetic isn't the same as believing for yourself.
That's true.
What are you thinking?

Connie, I look at your father and it reminds me of what life is like without faith. It's awful. And here you are, a teenager, and you're able to cope better than he can, even better than I can. Now I suddenly realize that I've been right in the middle, somewhere between you and your father, sort of riding your coattails of faith but really living like him. I don't want to do that anymore.
You know what you have to do, right?
Yes, you've made that clear in the past. And maybe this is the best time, right here with you and your grandma. I want to know Jesus the way you know Him. Will you introduce me properly to Him?
Mom, I'd love to!

321.s: To teach about Bible memorization, Kids' Radio spoofs three popular television programs. Kids' Radio renames them “Star Trip,” “Rescue 119,” and “Laffie the Wonder Dog.”
q: Space. One of the last places to be explored. These are the voyages of the Starship Aerobocise. On a five-year mission: To explore strange new worlds. To seek out new life with new spin-off series. To saturate the market with action figures and plastic pointy ears!
It's "Star Trip," starring William Shattered!
Romans 3:23. Romans 6:23! He's outlining the Roman Road! He's helping you witness to Matt

322.s: Eugene and Katrina's relationship takes a surprising turn after Eugene meets Katrina's father, Armitage Shanks.
q: You met your friend's father and it didn't go very well. It happens. You'll probably never see him again anyways, so just shrug and go on.
Just shrug and go on! You jest, Mr. Allen! How can I simply circulate my shoulders and return to everyday activities when the father of the woman I—
Yes, you were about to say?
I was about to say "the woman I—" ...Mr. Allen.
You love her.
Pray that God will bring someone into Eugene's life who will have an impact. Who will penetrate his defenses.
Pray for someone else?
Yeah. I'm sorry Katrina, but it won't be you. If I wasn't sure before, I'm sure now. In fact, you're probably getting in the way. Maybe we all are.
I said earlier that something drastic would have to happen to move your relationship with Katrina. I think the same is true for your relationship with Jesus.
When you say drastic, what specifically do you mean?
I don't know. I'm just thinking out loud. But it could be anything.
Maybe the problem has been... us. Me... even Whit, Connie, Jack, Whit's End—all of us.
Well, how so?

We've given you a very safe and reasonable environment, one that doesn't demand anything of you. It's as if you've been inoculated against Christianity, like the flu! You've been given enough of a dose in order to become immune to it. You've had just enough Christianity to become immune to its impact.
Well, I haven't thought of it that way...but—but I must nervously ask where this conversation is now taking us; you seem to have reached some sort of a conclusion.

Yes, I have. My conclusion is that I need to get out of the way so God can deal with you directly on His own terms. No more comfort, Eugene. No more easy way out. No more hiding behind the faith of the faithful.
I shudder to think what that means. Are you gonna stop having lunch with me? Are you gonna cease our occasional phone conversations? Are you planning to stay away from Whit's End from now on?
Eugene, it's already sorted out. I'm leaving Odyssey.
I'm going home to be with my family.
I've been paying Eugene Meltsner
Katrina Meltsner

323.s: Connie gets a dose of financial reality after she gets her first credit card, and Bernard Walton gets a new assistant.
q: Perhaps I need to do something different, something abnormal. At least for me.
I think... I’ll grow a mustache.
So, what'd they say?
Your card couldn't be authorized because you went over your credit limit.
Yes. And I'm very surprised.
Why? How much was my credit limit?
Two hundred and fifty dollars.
What? That's a mistake!
For whom? Are you sure you haven't spent that much?
In only a couple of days? No way! I just bought a few things, that's all. Not two hundred and fifty dollars' worth.
Connie, my guess is, if you looked through your receipts, your "few things" cost more than you thought.
I can't believe it!
But... where am I going to get that kind of money when the bill comes?
That's a very good question. I can't wait to hear your answer.
I talked Jason Whittaker
And why, may I ask?
I got a little carried away with my new credit card.
And I'm gonna have a whopper of a bill coming at the end of the month.
Boy, I've learned my lesson about credit cards. In fact, I'm not even carrying it around anymore. I'm gonna keep it at home until I'm absolutely sure I need it.
I've been doing a little shopping, that's all.

LITTLE?! Obviously, the meaning of the word has changed. It appears to me, Miss Kendall, as if you've been doing a lot of shopping. Have you come upon an inheritance of some sort? Or perhaps an oil well sprung up in your backyard?
Whether you meant it or not, you played out a Bible teaching in what you did today.
I did? That's weird!
Eh, not "weird," Simon. Happens all the time around here.

324.s: When an outbreak of vandalism hits Odyssey, the gang at Whit's End tries to find out who's responsible.
q: You know it’s times like this when I wish I was a superhero. Then I could catch these guys before they do stuff like this.
Yeah, that's just what we need—Super Sam!
Dum da daaa!
Nice mask. Last time I saw that kind of get-up was at Halloween.
The very idea of Tom Riley

325.s: A mysterious “clean-up” crew suddenly counters the vandalism around Odyssey. Connie has her suspicions about who is responsible for these new acts of goodness.
q: Those two comments were probably just a coincidence of some sort, phrases from bumper stickers if I remember right.
"Nothing's going on, Connie. Those two comments were just a coincidence!" Yeah, right! Like you even believe in coincidences, Mr. Jack Allen!
Well, this certainly is a turn of events to say the least. First the vandalism, and now good deeds. And no one really knows who is doing either.
Thanks, Pop. You won't regret it.
I already do regret it. I still don't like any of this. And don't call me--
Hey, I'm on the phone, Pop.
Tonight we find out the truth.
What’d ya do, break a fingernail?
Har, har. Hey, look, Rodney, a monkey who talks!
Oh, you're a really funny guy, ain’t ya?
Not as funny as your face!!

326.s: To help the gang called the Israelites, Butch spies on the Bones of Rath until his loyalty comes into question.
q: There are two things ya better learn about me, and fast. One: I don't like bein' questioned. And two: Nobody questions me, Brian Evans
Rodney and me were just taking a stroll through the woods. What were you doin'?
You know, strollin'. Just like you!
Just like me, eh, Butchy? I think you have some explaining to do. And if I were you, I'd tell us everything.
You don't understand something, Sam Johnson
The Israelites are finished. The Bones of Rath have won.
Do somethin' about your hair, huh?
Yeah? Like what?
Check the attic: maybe you can find a comb!

327.s: Jason and Jack clash about how to handle the growing crisis around Odyssey, leading to Jack's resignation from Whit's End. Meanwhile, Philip Glossman and Professor Bovril show up to investigate the tunnel under Whit's End.
q: In this case, I guess you could call me the Governor’s all-around... troubleshooter.
Troublemaker, you mean.
Connie. Have you offered either of these gentlemen anything to drink?
I could come up with something in my chemistry set—for Mr. Glossman, I mean.
Now children, let's be on our best behavior.
Look, why does it seem like we keep coming back to this same argument? I want to take action, and you want to do a fact-finding tour.
Because recklessly taking action leads to unforeseen problems!
So, you're... taking over the Israelites.
Well, I can't stop you... any more than I've been able to stop you from anything you've done over the past few months.
Well, you always said I was stubborn like John Whittaker
Stubborn, yes... but not like your dad.
Philip Glossman
He's the rather dubious personality from the state government who keeps trying to... how shall I say it?
Destroy Odyssey.
Jack's gone. This note is his resignation.
Jack won't be working at Whit's End anymore.

328.s: A new scandal erupts when Tom Riley is accused of unethical campaign practices.
q: Room service, Mr. Glossman!
Room service? I didn’t order any room serv—
I can’t believe you fell for that. It’s the oldest trick in the book.
What are you doing? We can’t be seen together. Do you know how dangerous this is?
Cool your jets. No one saw me.
How can you be sure? You may have been followed.
In this town? They roll up the sidewalks at dinnertime.
That's why I'm here—to stop him.
Uh-huh. Don't you mean to help him?
No, sir. I mean stop him! It's the least I can do.
What do you think about all this?
What do I think? What do you think I think?! I think it's terrible, that's what I think! What do I think...
I mean, if this isn't proof positive that Riley shouldn't serve as mayor, then I am a monkey's uncle!
Again, well said! Especially the monkey part.
Hehe. This town is as good as ours!
Well, don't get greedy. Remember who we're working for.
I always got blamed for everything bad that happened at Campbell County Detention Center, but the funny thing is, when you left, the bad things stopped.
Well, uh, it's nice to know you cleaned up your act.
I never forget.
Pop, what'd you wake me up for? I was just about to get a kiss!
How can you sleep at a time like this?
You mean, two in the morning? That's when I'm usually asleep!
That is no excuse.
How about a little kiss, Ginger...?
Ginger?! Rodney, wake up!

329.s: Dr. Blackgaard returns to Odyssey to challenge Tom Riley's position as mayor.
q: Ladies and gentlemen. Dr. Regis Blackgaard!
No! It can’t be!
Hello, Odyssey. I’ve come home.
I can’t believe it!
This is impossible! He’s... he's dead!
Just like me? Did you hear what he said, Shakespeare?
Yes, sir. Uh, sir...
My good man, I'll have you know there is no one just like me.
Edwin Blackgaard is one of a kind!
Edwin Blackgaard is incomparable!
Edwin Blackgaard is...
Regis Blackgaard
Oh, and Edwin...
If you see Mumsy, give her my love. And tell her she still owes me for the hip operation!
More secrets. Nobody ever tells me anything!
Who are you?
Well, my friends all call me Jellyfish. But, eh, you can call me... Jellyfish.
(lifts a very heavy suitcase) What's in here?!
But, sir, I thought we were packing light!
Why don't you pack really light and take only the good reviews?
What do our illustrious Tom Riley
You see, my dear Jason Whittaker
There we go. A fine-looking sign. By the order of Odyssey, until further notice, Whit's End is closed.

330.s: Despondent over his helplessness to influence the ominous events in Odyssey, Eugene creates a search program for the Imagination Station that lets him replay key moments of his life.
q: Dear God: my new Father in heaven; I am uncharacteristically at a loss of words. So please accept my verbal fumblings as I finally respond to Your promptings.
Well, stuff me with feathers and call me a pillow!
You look about as happy as a man who invested a million dollars in eight track tapes.
I beg your pardon?
Eight track tapes! You know; in the 70's, they were tape... Oh, never mind. It's no good if you have to explain it!
Good grief, Eugene, after all we've been through, you don't think I know you by now?

331.s: The Israelites clean up the Bones of Rath hideout, Lucy Cunningham-Schultz is kidnapped and pressed for information by Jellyfish, and Glossman finally succeeds in shutting down Whit's End.
q: What’s going on? What’s happenin'?
Don’t you know? It’s a rescue.
Who is that? Who are you?
Don’t get all bent out of shape. It's just... me.
Eugene, that's heavy! Why didn't you ask for help?
I believe I just did!
You're not here to think, Philip Glossman
Well, is there anything I can do?
Oh! Uh, as a matter of fact, there is.
Pray for me, Connie. I would be most grateful.
Yeah, sure! Nice to have you ask...
And now a message for the Israelites and all their friends at Whit's End!
Connie, get down! Now!
You should really have one of these on hand for protection. I got mine on sale at the Electric Palace.
Check and mate! Congratulations, Philip Glossman
For so long I have awaited this day... Whit's End is mine!
The salve used on William Ross
Hmm. Does this mineral have a name?
Well the locals call it One". I guess .
What? What's going on? A power loss? No! Not when I'm so close!

332.s: Rodney Rathbone tells Richard Maxwell about a laptop computer that may contain valuable information about Blackgaard's plans for Odyssey.
q: Are you crazy?
Yes! Now get out of here!
Well, well, well, Sleeping Beauty is waking up. How did you like your little shock, huh?
It wasn’t half as bad as waking up and seeing you. Having a good time, Myron?
Not as good a time as I’m gonna have!
Mind if I give you a piece of advice?
When you're doing something like this...
Make sure you lock the door! (jumps out) See ya!
Ya see, Rusty, when you've been around for as long as I have, you learn to do a little thing called CYB.
Yeah. Cover your bases. That's what this computer's all about. A little insurance policy.
Starting tomorrow we'll be having a slightly-damaged merchandise sale!

333.s: Bernard goes on a covert mission to get information from Jellyfish's laptop computer, and the police arrest Jason Whittaker.
q: Richard Maxwell
How compassionate of you.
Whoops! Wrong elevator!
No, no, no, Rodney, come right in. There's plenty of room.
I have a device that will access data though an infrared port and transfer it to a receiver by high frequency radio waves.
Indeed! May I ask how you acquired such a device?
No, you may not.
Let's just say I'm... very well connected.
Can your connections protect us against the legal ramifications against such actions? Tapping into another's computer sans permission is against the law, you know.
Not if you have a court order.
You are well connected. Have we sufficient grounds?
Well, how about suspicion of fraud, conspiracy, malice, racketeering, domestic terrorism...?
That's a good start.
Hey, you're an adult. You can't do this to me! Eugene, you're a witness!
Witness to what?
So, aren't you gonna say it?
I told you so.
OK. I told you so.
You didn't have to say it.
Right... to the Batphone.
Jack, why didn't you just tie me up and lock me in a closet??
I didn't realize that was an option.

334.s: The battle between Blackgaard and the gang at Whit's End draws to an explosive close.
q: What TA-418 does is attach itself to the virus's DNA and cause it to adapt to anything—air, dirt, water... that's what makes it so contagious.
And deadly. It's hard to believe that's even possible!
I know. But look around you! This whole scheme has been one concentrated effort to get that mineral. Regis Blackgaard
You're acting awfully calm about all this.
Calm? I'm terrified. But that can't stop us from doing what we have to do.
Mr. Walton, you're a genius!
Well, thanks, Eugene. It's about time you noticed.
Fools! Come after me in the tunnel... if you dare.

I'm not here to save the world, Doctor. I'm not here to save Odyssey or even Whit's End. I'm here for you—for your soul. That's the only thing that matters right now—not money or power or computer programs or viruses or world terrorism... it all comes down to your soul. Why don't you put down the detonator and give yourself up so you'll have time to redeem your soul?
The flaw in your proposal is that you assume my soul is redeemable. It isn't. I auctioned it off years ago.
Then you sold yourself cheap. Your soul is worth the life of Jesus Christ. To give it to anyone else is an incredible waste.
So I suggest you run for your life.
You don't want to kill me.
Oh, you fool! Why wouldn't I?! Goodbye, Jack Allen!
I just don't get why Regis Blackgaard

I know. It's hard to understand how a mind like Doctor Blackgaard's worked. I'd hoped to help him change it—one last chance. But a soul so corrupted, so saturated in evil, can only come to one end without Jesus. It's destined for the final conflict... and an eternity without God.

335.s: Katrina Shanks and Tasha Forbes arrive back in town, causing all sorts of romantic high jinks with Eugene, Jason, and even Connie.
q: Well, I think that went as well as could be expected.
Would a nervous breakdown be suitable at this time?
I want you to know that there is absolutely nothing between Connie and myself... other than a basic, sometimes-adversarial friendship!
There can't be! I've been waiting for you and she has a crush on Jason! Honest! It was as innocent as... it... could be. Oops.
Nicely done, Eugene.
I never said I had a crush on Jason! I don't know where you get this stuff! The idea of a crush never even... I mean... THANKS A LOT, EUGENE!!
So, uh, how do you guys know each other?
Well, we're friends who used to work together.
Oh, where was that?
Oh, it was at, the, uh—
Oh, uh, boring government work. We were both analysts. You know, white lab coats and pages and pages of manuals.
Sounds fascinating!

336.s: Katrina Shanks and Tasha Forbes arrive back in town, causing all sorts of romantic high jinks with Eugene, Jason, and even Connie.
q: You can't toss your hearts around like a football!
Do you love Eugene Meltsner
Do I love him?
I asked you first!
Tasha Forbes
Oh boy, she's in the kitchen, isn't she?
Hi guys, I dropped some pots and pans. I'll... I'll pick them up after I go... do something else.
Look, Connie
I believe I will go to the Kids Radio studio.

I just wanted to tell you that life moves in rhythms and cycles and we all go through periods when it feels like nothing is happening. But things are happening Connie, all the time. We just have to stay in tune enough to see what they are; how they fit together. So that even in times of quiet and boredom, God's handiwork is shown to us. That's the real adventure Connie.
