Learning to look and listen to our lives so we'll understand what God is doing.
Hm, guess I have something to think about, huh? Thanks Jack.

Your journey of faith could take you anywhere Connie, as long Christ remains at the center of who you are and all the rest will fall into place. Course, Jesus said it better naturally. He said, "Seek ye first the kingdom of God and his righteousness and all will be added unto you."

337.s: Erica Clark tries to look her best for school pictures; Sam Johnson worries about the upcoming Academic Olympics.
q: On my homework yesterday, I spelled my name with two L’s! I'm going crazy!
Your name doesn't have an L in it.
See! That's my point! I'm going crazy!

338.s: To buy new hockey equipment, Sam Johnson and Butch need money. Sam gets a job and nearly works himself to death while Butch resorts to gambling.
q: Some days you get your soul puréed and served to you in a melancholy milkshake.
"Mac McCorby: I can get you whatever you want, whenever you want it, whatever the cost and whatever the reason — whoever you are." That's quite a slogan.
Yeah, I had to shorten it for the bumper stickers.

339.s: Zachary Sellars and Eugene face their first difficulties as new Christians.
q: Would you like to lead us in prayer, Eugene?

Delighted. Dearest Elohim: We know that you were with the army of Jehoshaphat in 2nd Chronicles 20: 1 and following, and when he prepared his army to battle the Ammonites, which were of a great multitude, you told them not to fear; and though the Hebrew is slightly ambiguous in a few of the verses in this passage, we know you tell us the same. And we remember this today when we battle the Ammonites of anxiety, the Jebusites of injustice, the Perizzites of pride and yea, the Syrians of sinfulness. Glorious Yahweh, we see in Paul’s letter to the Thessalonians how he uses eschatological references as the basis for hope that determines the nature of daily life, and in a sense, we should do the same. And we ask these things in the name of our precious Redeemer and Savior, Jesu Christe, Emmanu-el, i.e. “God with us.” Amen.
O-kayyyy... I guess that qualifies as a blessing.
Of course, there's no reason to be afraid of the earth blowing up!
Before you go, would you like to try our little paperclip contest?
Uh, your what?
If you guess how many paperclips are in this jar, you can win a pizza party for your class.
My class doesn't need any pizza.

I'm attempting to curb the temptation to take what I have for granted — and at the same time, to understand the plight of the underprivileged. Not everyone in the world has 3 meals a day as do you and I. Alas, most of the world eats just a few times a week!
Okay, well, who wants cheesecake?

340.s: The Barclays are presented with a difficult choice when a small church in New England asks George to be their pastor.
q: So what denomination is First Church anyway?
Well--that kind of depends on the pastor.
Technically, I am an executive associate to the office of the president.
I'm Barry Lionel

341.s: The Barclays are presented with a difficult choice when a small church in New England asks George to be their pastor.
q: Look, there's no point in wrapping an onion up in Christmas paper. I like these folks too much not to completely level with 'em!
Well it's all in the way you look at things, Vivian—
Well, look at it from their point of view. Quit givin' em the nickel tour and lay out the cold, hard facts, Ellis!
[to his family] Do you all hear what you're saying?
I do! And I like what they're saying!
Thanks- thanks for the input, Ellis!
Nay! I vote nay!
Be quiet, Owen...
But... but what was all that about a meeting tomorrow? I thought it was a deacon's meeting!
Uh-huh. He's one of our deacons, ya know.
Hi, sorry I'm late, but I got caught on a trans-Atlantic phone call. Somebody needs to teach those French people how to speak English.

342.s: Edwin Blackgaard returns to Odyssey to take over the Electric Palace and reopen the Harlequin Theatre.
q: ...I'd like to thank you for allowing our two man troupe to bring a little Hamlet, to your little—hamlet.
Have you forgotten how we left? Under the cover of darkness, cowering with our tails between our legs like stray ducks?
I think you mean dogs, sir. Cowering out of town like stray dogs?
What difference does it make?!?
Sir? Sir, I really don't think you need to duck behind me anymore. No one seems to be taking notice of us. And those who are-
Good morning!
Good morning.
Sir, those who are taking notice of us are very cordial.
They're setting me up for the kill! Lulling me into a false sense of security! Be prepared to run, Shakespeare—especially if you see tar and feathers!
I'm a partner in the firm Dunkey, Dunkey, Dunkey, Dunkey, and McCormick. Actually, I'm the third Dunkey.
Well, congratulations. I'm so happy for you.
Well, that's just ducky, Mr. Donkey!
That's "Dunkey."
After all, if I were Odyssey
I... I'm speechless! I never expected to drink so deeply of the milk of human kindness. This token, this powerful symbol of acceptance and forgiveness, will ne'er be forgotten!
I thought you said you were speechless.
Money is a great way to clear Edwin Blackgaard

343.s: Charles Edward Thompson's attempt to act like a Good Samaritan is challenged when he meets an annoying boy named Glenn.
q: So, how's The Good Samaritan coming?
He's purple.
He was a grape-flavored Popsicle. But I figure, he'd be pretty purple anyways after getting beat up.
I mean, bad posture never killed anyone, as far as I know. The worst thing it could do is cripple you for life... and that's not even really likely if—
I DON'T have bad posture!
Pfft! Not if you're a chimpanzee...
Charles! Charles!
Do you always... breathe like that?
I’ve got better things to do than to get my hands dirty helping you! Stay away from me!

How could this guy ever live with himself again? He was the most selfish, horrible man who ever lived, and didn’t deserve to have any friends! And that’s exactly what happened to him! He never had any friends! After he passed by that man on the road, he went home and stayed there, and watched television and ate popcorn all day for the next twenty years, ’cause nobody wanted to be around him!
OK, we didn’t play in the thunderstorm!
But you said—
I know what I said. There was no party last night, OK?
Nobody showed up. It was my parents and me — that’s it. I handed out a hundred invitations to people all over this school, and nobody came.
Oh... sorry.
Yeah. That’s what everyone else said, too.

344.s: Zachary Sellars has a hard time adjusting when his mother starts dating again.
q: I used to have a 95 mph fastball!
Oh, you think this is funny, do you?
I’m surprised. I’ve never heard of about your legendary... 56mph fastball!
Well, yeah! It looks faster when you’re trying to hit it, I guess.
Did I ever tell you what Michael Sellars
I don't think so.

We were standing at the alter about to say our "I do's". The preacher was speaking these moving and elegant words. And your father leaned over to me and whispered, "You don't squeeze your toothpaste from the middle do you?" I started laughing. There in my wedding dress in front of 300 people. I was cracking up.
The Blake Anderson

345.s: Bernard Walton, Eugene, and the B-TV crew talk about compassion with the help of Marty the shoemaker.
q: I have it now. I'm all prepared. Compassion is a sympathetic consciousness of others distress together with a desire to alleviate it.
Feeling sorry for someone.
Wilt Bernard Walton
Did you know that one meaning of the Greek words for compassion is to be moved down to the pit of your stomach? Sort of like having a gut feeling.

346.s: A young Antonius sets off on a sea journey with his father and a prisoner--the apostle Paul.

347.s: The apostle Paul arrives in Rome for his appointment with the emperor.
q: What do you mean the treasury is empty?! There is plenty of wealth in Rome! Simply tax the people more!
The people no longer have need of gods! They have… ME!

348.s: Sam Johnson, Connie, and her mother, June Kendall, compare stories about giving in to peer pressure.
q: Ugh, you Jason Whittaker
You know, June, you've got a lot of spunk.
Oh, well, thank you, sir...
I hate spunk!
Why does "all the rage" cost all the money?
Hey. No one ever said looking good was easy.
This already sounds like a session of "Peer Pressure Anonymous".
Yeah. "Hi, my name is Connie and it's been two days since I last caved.
But there's one thing we all need to remember, something my dad told me when I was your age, Sam.
What's that?
We have direct access to the best positive peer pressure of all. That's Jesus. Dad used to say, "Remember, you plus Jesus are always a majority."

349.s: Brenda Perry's pen pal, Thor Douglas, comes to visit, and Brenda is panicked because she has to live up to all the exaggerations she's written.
q: The thought of impressing Brenda Perry
So, you're just not very good.
Who did your makeup here, honey?
The photography place.
I oughta hire them to do the spackling work in my basement.
Connie, I think Brenda Perry
Maybe one of us should say something.
Yes, quickly. This is making me queasy.
Ah, you noticed the resemblance, too.
You know, I think I'm going to miss Odyssey. Whit's End, Trickle Lake

350.s: Kids' Radio tells a Twilife Zone sketch of Kathy and Jeremy, two kids who have a propensity for wasting time.
q: I was entertaining some guests at my home, and we were eating dinner in my dining room. I needed to get up and get the mustard out of the kitchen and instead of saying, 'Would you please excuse me?', I said, 'I'll be right back... after these messages'. It was so embarrassing I could barely even eat.

Okay, people. We’ve got a fugitive on the loose, and we’re not gonna rest until we’ve searched every townhouse, farmhouse, dog house, outhouse, haunted house, halfway house, fish house, shrimp house, shrimp creole, shrimp salad, Cajun shrimp, fried shrimp, shrimp flambeau, steak ’n shrimp—
I’m not done, Ford. Shrimp gumbo, shrimp scampi—

351.s: As Connie tries to decide on a career, she experiments with several new jobs.
q: Ahhh, now I can eat my breakfast!
It's nearly time for dinner...
Hey, you can eat PopTarts (TM) any time of the day!

First question: If a train leaves the depot at 3 o'clock, traveling south at 6 miles per hour against a north-westerly wind of 30 miles per hour, and has only 65% of its weight capacity on board, what color would you paint the train?
What color would... Is that really what it wants to know?
If you're on a blue train at 2 in the afternoon, and a giant tomato hits it at a 45° angle, what would you say on a scale from 1 to 10?
Ahh... A truckload of prunes.
Ok! Welcome to the "figure out your life" club!
I know. How about secretarial work?
You mean like filing, mailing letters, answering phones, and stuff like that?
No. I mean secretarial work. Meaning that I need a secretary. My last one had a nervous breakdown. You interested?
In having a nervous breakdown?
If it'll help you do the job, sure. I think you'd make a terrific secretary.
Do you want me to lock up on my way out?
Oooh. Better not. The last time my secretary did that I was stuck in here for three days.
Obviously my test needs work. Not only did it have you working in box manufacturing, but it suggested Jason's personality was best suited to painting figurines of cartoon characters in Korea!
I don't think he'd have the patience for that.
Excuse me, young lady, but may I have a word?
Oh! Harlow Doyle, what are you-
Detective Doyle, if you please.
Oh, are you on a case?
Ha! Am I on a case! Am I on a case! Am I on a case?
Oh, I can see it now, Eugene in his little playpen with a telescope in one hand and a chemistry set in the other!
Don't be absurd! It was a microscope and a small blackboard and chalk so that I could do my physics equations.
I don't suppose it would hurt to try.
Ha, ha, ha! You have no idea how much it'll hurt!

352.s: An old postcard triggers Jason Whittaker's memories about the last weekend he spent with his older brother, Jerry.
q: Well, when I got into Jr. High, I wanted to follow Jerry's footsteps. You know, be a big track star. But while he broke school records, all I managed to break was the high jump bar.
On your mark, get set, stop!
Just kidding. I meant GO!
That's Plato? What happened to him?
Well he sorta turned into a flower child since you last saw him. Long hair and beads. That's the latest rage.
Yeah? On what planet?
There's no need to fear, really. God is with me.
Never forget, Leonard (Plato) Plateman
You scared me!! I scared you; you scared me!!
Are you alright?

353.s: Jason Whittaker and Tasha Forbes announce that they're getting married . . . tomorrow!
q: My faith should be the center of my life. It isn't always, but it should be. It's supposed to get in the way of everything I do, everything that I am.
You just never know what's going to happen next around here.
Tasha, I love you. And I think you becoming a Christian is the greatest thing you could ever do.
And if I don't?
I need to pick up Tasha Forbes
Called it in? What is it — a pizza?

354.s: Eugene and Bernard wind up on the same jury and must decide the fate of a young boy accused of burglary.
q: Now wait a minute! Hold it! There will be no name-calling here, you bonehead.
Ah, you smell that Mr. Walton? The smells of juries past coming into this very room to participate in the American judicial system.
I think you're confusing justice with floor wax.
You know Eugene, don't you?
Eugene... yeah, I've seen him around.
Well, what is it going to take to get him to change his mind?
Eugene, the next time you nominate me the foreman of anything, our friendship is over.
Let's see. We have eleven votes of guilty, and one vote of... it says: I am undecided at this... I can't read this scrawl... Undecided at this...
…Juncture, but my inclinations are that the defendant is not guilty.
Not that I would wish this on anyone, but we have to listen to Eugene. He's... right. All twelve of us have to agree. That's the law.
There is nothing worse than cold pot-roast. The gravy gets all rubbery.
Aren't you tired of these gangs running around, getting away with this kind of stuff? Why don't we convict this kid and show the rest of 'em that they can't do it. Come on, let's send a message.
And if he's innocent?

That's the price he pays for hanging around with criminals. And if we let criminals roam around free, then pretty soon this town will be afraid to walk the streets alone. Is that what you want for our town?

I'm sorry, Victor, but what I want is irrelevant to what we've been called here to do: discern the truth and render a fair verdict. Yes, I'd like to send a message, but the message I want to send is: our system of justice works.

355.s: Jason and Eugene get a cryptic message from Whit in the Middle East, which leads them on a wild investigation that could change Christian history as we know it.
q: Come on. Operate, you worthless hunk of—
Good morning, Jason!
Oh, hi Eugene.
Are we having problems with our answering machine again?
What was your first clue?
The fact that you have it dissected and strewn all over the counter.
It's about time you got here. I've been...oh. You're not the police.
No, uh, sorry.
Looks like you had a little accident here. What happened? Mix the wrong chemicals in your chemistry set?
Call the police and get a stand up comedian. Who are you?
Tasha! Sorry, Frank; she just walked in. What in the world are you doing here?
Is that any way to greet your fiancée?
Oh sorry. It's nice to see you.
It's nice to see you, too.
Now what in the world are you doing here?
Please, Jason Whittaker
Look, when it comes to the safety of my father, it's me against the world if necessary.
Eugene, how would you like to take a trip to the Middle East?
I'd have to think about it. Okay, I've thought about it. Let's go! By the way, your treat.
My Assyrian chamber pot!
This is all wrong, Tasha.
I know. But there's nothing else I can do.
Not even a kiss good-bye?
I'm on duty. See you.
I think I just found a clue!
You're kidding. In the bathroom?
I do some of my best work there.
Perhaps if we take the phrase word by word?
But... what about the movie?

356.s: Jason and Eugene get a cryptic message from Whit in the Middle East, which leads them on a wild investigation that could change Christian history as we know it.
q: Listen, Benjamin, your threats don't scare me.
They should. Now oblige us.
Us? What, do you have a mouse in your pocket or are you just schizophrenic?
Dad's hiding. And when my Dad hides, nobody'll find him. Hide and Seek was a nightmare when we were kids. We spent weeks looking for him.
How could you possibly know that I have a black leather wallet that was given to me as a Christmas present?
Well, because I gave it to you.
What? B-b-but it's not possible!
Hi, Eugene! It's good to see you again!
...Mr. Whittaker!
I wonder why the elevator's taking so long.
Jason, I-I really am sorry about this. Please don't take it the wrong way.
You lied to my father and put him in a potentially life-threatening situation. Oh, I won't take it the wrong way!
Right now, I don't care about the truth of Whit's parchment—if it exists! It could be nursery rhymes, for all it matters to me! I'm here to get the bad guys.
It's me, Eugene Meltsner! Let's go into the bathroom.
Eugene, that's a cleaning lady.
I think that's my dad one floor down.
It's good to see John Whittaker
That's his disguise, Jason!
I know, Eugene.

357.s: Jason and Eugene get a cryptic message from Whit in the Middle East, which leads them on a wild investigation that could change Christian history as we know it.
q: This place gives me the creeps!
As well it should. It's a tunnel of tombs.
This is curious.
It looks like a thistle bush, but I've never thought of a thistle bush as a sign of suffering—unless you fall into one.
Eugene, this is a good time to ask yourself—in what have you put your faith?
What indeed, Mr. Whittaker. What indeed.
I'd sure like to see a schematic of this.
So we have a single and a double deception.
To put it crudely, yes. All to get rich from Whit's remarkable find.
Huh, now would that make it a triple deception? I've lost count.
It's gonna take weeks to figure this out.

Eugene, listen to me. No matter what's in that box, God's word remains true. You haven't believed in vain. Our faith can't be based on the whims of science or archeological discovery. There's nothing to be afraid of.
Jason, darling, will you take his gun?
Sure, pumpkin. Whatever you say.
For centuries, people have tried to deny Christ's resurrection with lies, much as they try to do now, which is why our faith must be firmly grounded in the Bible. Right, Eugene?
Of course, Mr. Whittaker. The grass may wither and the flower fade, but the word of our God will endure forever.

358.s: Connie becomes coach of the Odyssey Coyotes baseball team and has a plan for boosting Sam Johnson's confidence.
q: I've seen better swings in the monkey cage at the zoo!
Leave your relatives out of this!
Odyssey Coyotes, meet your new coach.
Hi, everybody!
Are you sure you're up to it?
Oh, you just wait. You'll see. We're going to put together one of the best seasons the Coyotes have ever had. We'll be scoring touchdowns left and right!
Connie, that's um...
Football. I know. I was just seeing if you were listening.

Now, Connie, I can't let you go without asking you about being the only female coach in the league. Now, has it been difficult? I mean, I understand that Coach Mott has said you should stay in the kitchen and bake cookies.
I sent him a batch of my cookies actually and... now he knows why I don't.
Hey, guys! Let's hear it for the Coyote's real secret weapons: Sam Johnson and Connie Kendall!

359.s: Edwin Blackgaard has to borrow money from Bart Rathbone to pay his taxes.
q: My name is Leech.
I'm so sorry.
Shakespeare, the car!
Right out back, sir.
Ah! Well, then. The door!
Opening it now, sir.
Alright, Bart. What do you really want?
I'll write it down.
Probably your first born child.
Oh, good. I'm a bachelor. Although I suppose he could take Shakespeare.
Ooh! Must have been painful.
My bass drum will never be the same.
Oh, what a tangled web we weave...
When first we practice to deceive!

360.s: Connie tells the romantic story of Ruth, who risks all to stay committed to her family.
q: Aren't there any stories about love?
They're all about love. The whole Bible is about it: God's love for us!
Not love, Connie. Love.
Oh, love. You mean romance.
I am small in stature, it's true, but... big in heart.
I will not leave Naomi
Oh, time! Sorry, but I gotta get back to work.
Work? But you can't just leave us hanging.
Yeah, you have to tell us the rest of it.
Tuesday night, at our Bible study!

361.s: Connie tells Courtney Vincent and Jenny Roberts the story of Ruth and how she was so faithful to God that she became the great-grandmother of King David.
q: Sorry we're late Connie. We would have been here sooner but someone lost her cane.
I didn't lose it. My brother was using it to play pool.

362.s: Stopping in Chicago on the way home from the Middle East, Eugene learns that Katrina Shanks may be marrying someone else!
q: Eugene went two weeks without actual verbal contact with Katrina Shanks-Meltsner
Well, he had a rash or two, but I blame that on his The Search for Whit, Part 3
Did Eugene Meltsner
That’s a caftan he bought from one of the street merchants before we left.
Ah, he went native, huh?
You know Eugene.
What am I gonna do?! It's unbelievable! Katrina Shanks-Meltsner
What do you mean, what are you gonna do?
I believe my question was precise as it could be under the circumstances!
Look, she's not married yet, is she?
Then it's not too late for you to rent a car, drive up to Lake Shore Lodge, and bring her back to her senses! ...Providing you love her enough to do it.
Of course I love her!
Then fight for her!
Do you think that was wise, Jason?
What do you mean?
Basically, you just sent Eugene on a mission to storm Armitage Shanks
Yeah, you could be right. I just wish I could be there to see it.
No, John Whittaker
My senses have gone beyond the capacity to function. I can feel my pores fibrillating even as we speak!
You're making a terrible mistake, Mr. Shanks! You can't let this marriage happen!
I can't? You disapprove of me marrying Millie Shanks
...Why are you wearing a wedding dress for Katrina Shanks-Meltsner
I'm truly sorry, Katrina Shanks-Meltsner
Yeah, and they could have you playin' in a dump like this. Well, hey - just kidding, folks! Who loves ya, huh?

363.s: Stopping in Chicago on the way home from the Middle East, Eugene learns that Katrina Shanks may be marrying someone else!
q: Are you saying I'm paranoid, John Whittaker
Even though you're obviously jealous...
I am not jealous!
And in denial...
I am not in denial!
I'd rather not take up any more of your valuable time, sir.
This is Katrina Meltsner
This'll make a good homecoming to Odyssey. Just when I thought things were going to settle down for a while.
Settle down? I have a feeling things are just getting Home, Sweet Home

364.s: Whit finally returns to Odyssey--but Connie can't seem to meet up with him.
q: No pushing, no shoving, no red meat, and please make sure your seat backs are in the upright and locked position!
Home, sweet home, huh, Dad?
Amen, Jason. Amen.
Whit! Oh, Whit. You ol' globetrotting scalawag! Are you ever a sight for sore eyes! Welcome home!
It's good to see you again, Harlow.
Think so, huh? How do you know you're really seeing me? I might be cleverly disguised.
As what? Yourself?
Can't think of a better way to fool people.
Oh, Connie, Connie! Where have you been, little girl.
Oh you know me. Always late.
I'm here now.
Yes, yes. And I'm finally home.
My hearing ain't off because of the fireworks. It's 'cause you keep yellin' at me through that bullhorn!
I am not yelling at you through this bullhorn!

365.s: Jack Allen tells Eugene about a shocking incident from his past. Whit gets angry and says that he never wants to see Jack again.
q: I can't believe my auricular cavities!
Whenever you're in the middle of a dream, and you think it's going to be bad, you say real loud, "Go away bad dream, BOO!" and the bad dream will go away and you'll wake up.
Go away, bad dream.
BOO. Don’t forget the BOO.
No! Go away bad dream, boo, go away bad dream, boo, go away bad dream, boo.
Clara, I'm sorry honey, but this dream won't go away.

(reading letter to Whit from Clara) I'm glad you're still being brave, and remembering me, even as I remember you. You and Mr. Allen were right for giving me up to the Portlands...I couldn't be happier. So if you ever see Mr. Allen again and he still feels bad, you know what to tell him. (to Whit) What?
(chuckles) Go away, bad dream. Boo.
You know Clara
I can give her the next best thing!

Oh, listen to yourself. You're going against every principle you've ever taught! And why? Because of something you want! Is that what's best for Clara, Whit? Are you thinking about her...or just about yourself?
What was that? I said I was sorry, Mr. Chuckleford. I didn't know it was your seat until Clara told me.
You know you're very fortunate to have such a good friend as Clara Mr. Chuckleford. She really looks out for you.
But it's just a stupid toy.

What's that Mr. Chuckleford? Oh well I guess it's because no one has taught Annabella it's very rude to call people stupid or crazy. Yes, yes you're right. If she keeps it up, she won't have very many friends left. What do you think Annabella?
I... I think you're both weird!

366.s: Eugene considers joining a monastery to get over the pain of losing Katrina.
q: I am not muddled! Things have never been more clear... uh, clearer.
Brother Eugene has faithfully completed his six month vow of silence.
It was a miracle.
It is now time for our brother to break his vow of silence and share what he has learned with the rest of us. Yes, I see that hand of Brother Bernard the Cleansed?
Yes, Friar Whit, the brothers took a vote and we all think Brother Eugene should continue his vow of silence for another six months. It's been the quietest six months we've ever had.
Aaaaaahhmen.
Well, as much as I may agree, this order is not a democracy and votes don't count...he has earned the right to speak.
Brother Whit, would you agree with another three months of silence?
No, Brother.
How about a long day, and full foam earplugs for all?
Brother Eugene, come forward. After six months of glorious, uh, of muteness...we bid you share your new wisdom with us.

Thank you, Friar Mr. Whittaker. Fellow brethren of the monastic way, my journey through silence has been met by various and sundry provocations from the opposer, and not without dire distress and ventricular hemorrhaging of spirit. However, deep within the recesses of my being, I received the capacity to endure. Thus, I desire to share with you all now what this experience has achieved for me, and in achieving for me, I believe will also further advance the understanding of like-minded people everywhere.
That would be no one.
Ok, Eugene. I've finished the windows in the little theater, so tell the kids to keep their greasy little fingers out of there for a while.
What are these brochures? Are you planning The Search for Whit, Part 1
Oh, no. Not at all. I'm perusing sites of isolation where I might explore disciplines for the inner spiritual life.
As soon as I asked, I knew it was a mistake. You want to break that sentence down and translate it for me?
Has John Whittaker
No. And I sure wish he would. I don't like the way he's been pushing himself. I gotta persuade him to take some time off.
Considering how much effort we put into blocking God out with all our noise, it's no surprise that we have to work that much harder to be with him in silence.
Is someone there? I'm Eugene Meltsner. I come in peace. It's alright to talk if you want.
I look tired?
Those bags under your eyes aren't for your wallet and keys, Whit.

367.s: Whit must decide whether or not to accept an offer to return to the mission field, and so Connie sets out to prove that he is needed in Odyssey.
q: Do you have any dinner plans?
You're picking me up at seven.
Really? Oh! Okay...
Jack! Where did you come from?
I followed you up the stairs. You really oughta pay more attention to what's going on around you, Jason.
Do you hear what I hear?
Romantic music.
I haven't seen Jack Allen
(chuckle) You feed 'em, you love 'em, you nurture 'em, and before you know it, they're going out on dates!
Oh, where does the time go?
Good grief! What is this, a Marx Brothers routine?

368.s: The Rathbones sniff out a scandal when they catch Tom Riley visiting a mysterious woman at Hillingdale Haven.
q: Duck! There's Tom Riley!
Why'd you duck?
You said to duck!
I could write a book!
Oh, yeah. It'd have to be a coloring book, the way you write.
I don't know about this choke and dagger stuff.
Like any illness, God sometimes heals [mental illness] immediately; sometimes He takes His time. Sometimes He won't heal at all. His reasons are His own.
But where does that leave us?

It leaves us where we've always been: stuck with the frailty of our humanness, dependent on the power of God's will, and obliged to keep praying hard for people like Mrs. Riley—and the Tom Rileys of the world who help them.
You've got a son who's growing up to be a slob, just like his father, and you're talking about Tom Riley?
So are you [...] going to run for mayor again?
Now Eugene, you're not curious, are ya?
No, not at all. I was merely inquiring out of a fundamentally objective desire to know.
He's curious.
But what if the gang sees me carrying around a laundry basket? They'll start calling me sissy, too!
Oh, quit your griping. I had a cousin named Sissy once. It's a very nice name.
Turn with Tom Riley
If you say so.
Ma, you could've braked first!
Well, they always do it that way on TV.
Do we have a camera in the car?
Are you kidding? Bart Rathbone
Maybe next time Tom Riley
Maybe Tom Riley

369.s: Lucy Cunningham-Schultz and the Kids' Radio team take an in-depth look at Whit's End and the return of John Avery Whittaker.
q: Do you have to use such a long needle?
This isn't a long needle.
I'm here at Hal's Diner, a typical, greasy, spoon-feeding—
Hey, hey, hey! Watch what you say about the restaurant, kid.
A four star, highly-rated dining establishment where Hal Schneider, the owner, gave me his kind permission to record John Avery Whittaker eating his breakfast.
Spit and clay? Probably looked a lot like that man's oatmeal.
Thanks a lot, kid.
Did you get to ride a camel?
A few times, yes.
Did you run into any... you know... terrorists?
Uh, I don't think camels join terrorist groups.
Why don't you have any ID in your wallet?
What, are you nuts? I'm a private investigator. Strict secrecy is an imperative, unquote. If I kept identification in my wallet, why, then- why, then...
You'd lose it and no one would know who it belonged to!
Precisely! You know, you might be cut out for this kind of work, Connie.
Step aside, Glenn Adams
Yes! Dial 9-1-1!
What do you think tomorrow will be like?
Oh, I suppose it will be a typical day in Odyssey.
What do you mean by a "typical day?"
Anything can happen! That's what I like about this place.

370.s: Whit creates a program in the Imagination Station to show how other cultures celebrate Christmas.

371.s: Whit creates a program in the Imagination Station to show how other cultures celebrate Christmas.

372.s: Someone is getting married in Odyssey … but who? Is it John Whittaker and Margaret Faye, Eugene Meltsner and Katrina Shanks, or Jack Allen and Joanne Woodston?
q: Hey, did ya have a good trip? We got your postcard from Germany, and Belgium and London and Paris and Rome and..
Oh, I had a great summer. Just what I needed to satisfy my traveling bug.
I should hope so. Europe, Russia, China.
You gotta do it sometime Connie. You gotta tour the world.
Right, well you buy and I'll fly.
Did you know Maxwell's Flower shop is for sale?
Now Jack, how do you get from Bobby's chocolate hand prints to Maxwell's Flower Shop?
Turn left on 8th street?
Owning my own shop is something I've wanted to do for a long time. But not any shop. It has to be the right kind, something I can sink my teeth into.
Hey Biffy's Burger Joint's up for sale. You could really "sink your teeth" into that!
Only if you wanted food poisoning.
Watch out for the stop sign.
Ooohh, nice stop.
You want a first impression?
Margaret Faye
Times have really changed. I haven't been on a date with someone other than Maude Walton
I hope you brought plenty of pictures and souvenirs.
Yeah, I'll have everyone over and bore you stiff with details.

373.s: Someone is getting married in Odyssey … but who? Is it John Whittaker and Margaret Faye, Eugene Meltsner and Katrina Shanks, or Jack Allen and Joanne Woodston?
q: Oh, Mr. Holstein, you've already done more than enough.
Anyone can make sausages.
Oh, not like this they can't.
Did you say you wanted that Maxi-Deluxe without onions?
No-no-no — pickles, no pickles.
Oh. Ok, thanks.
Look, just forget it, I'll take the whole thing ju-... I'll be married by the time they fix that burger!
Connie, you're driving me crazy.
(At the antique shop) Would you gentlemen like some espresso or cappuccino?
Well, maybe. Is it new or antique?
I don't have any other friends! I mean not like her. I mean I have you and Connie. But I admire John Whittaker
That's not true.
It's like... it's like...
Catch the ball!
No, Hans! Don't throw the— (Ball hits Katrina) Katrina!
Boy, you're so impatient.
I didn't use to be. But ever since you picked me up at the airport...
I don't believe it.
They put everything on this maxi-deluxe burger except the burger!
Spontaneous? How do I plan for that?!
Eugene Meltsner

374.s: Someone is getting married in Odyssey … but who? Is it John Whittaker and Margaret Faye, Eugene Meltsner and Katrina Shanks, or Jack Allen and Joanne Woodston?
q: There's no problem in particular, John Whittaker
Well, knowing you both, I'd say the answer is no. Unless we're surprised by visitors from another planet.
Eugene, you are unbelievable.
Ah, I believe I am entirely based within the realm of plausibility.
But no one does a survey to decide who they're going to marry!
I asked you to marry me, and you responded by conducting a survey? Why didn't you bring in a census bureau?
It's an off year for them in this district!
Connie, your logic is... your... own.

375.s: Cody Carper is a pushover, and Jared DeWhite is bossy. Whit comes up with a way to help them work together.
q: Do you really think this is the best way to get friends? To buy them by giving away a car and a bat?
Well... it seemed like a good idea at the time.
Do you know what gullible is?
Isn't that a kind of fish?
Now I wasn't spying or anything, but why does Cody Carper
You probably would, wouldn't you? And give 'em directions, too!
Oh, I'm not very good at maps. Whenever I try to use the one at Odyssey Mall
It's coming closer!
I think it sees us. It's a bear!
What was that?
A sheep? Like Mary had a little sheep?

376.s: The kids in Odyssey think they have too much work to do at home, so they organize the first annual chores strike.
q: Allow me to quote from scripture... "All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy." Now, I realize that I'm not Jack, and that wasn't scripture, but I think that pretty much says it all.
Chores are the hands that squeeze my neck! The twisted metal of an emotional car wreck!
Ivan, I am your father.
Yes, and Mary Lou, the Ice Princess is your mother.

It's a hard thing to really verbalize you know? Because the way I feel about chores is something that's very emotional to me. I think maybe I had a bad experience with chores as a child. And it's something I have to block out mentally now. So horrible. Cause lately I've been having these nightmares. This huge vacuum cleaner sucks up dirt off the floor, then it starts going out of control. Beginning to suck up the furniture, and small appliances and finally it starts sucking the life out of me!

377.s: The Mulligan family takes in a teenager with an attitude--a relative named Nick.
q: Here, try some of this. I don't touch the stuff myself, but I hear it's good for emergencies.
(suspiciously) What is it?
To be my brother you'd have to start out by being a member of the human race. Excuse me.
Hey, hey! Is it something I said?
It's too dark out here. You can't see a thing.
I'm used to the dark, remember?
Where's the cougar?
Ol' Sylvester split like a cheap pair of jeans.
Hello, Nick. It's a pleasure to make your acquaintance.
Of course it is.

378.s: Jack and Joanne Allen open J & J Antiques and are immediately caught up in a mystery involving a millionaire and a long-lost painting.
q: You Whittakers! Is there anyone you don't know?
Um... no! Not really.
So how have things been around here, Jason?
You know Odyssey. Same old, same old.
That's what I like about it.
What is all this, Jason?
Well, John Whittaker
Look out! Connie—Connie! Hold on!
What? What's wrong?
Well, according to this information, G. Winston Smith may be a thief.

379.s: When Connie hears that a famous writer named Mark Herring is going to stop by Whit's End, she decides to make sure everyone is on his or her best behavior.
q: So you're telling me World War I never happened?
World War I, II, the Civil War, you name it—it's a lie.
We went on vacation to Virginia last year. There's all sorts of Civil War monuments.
Oh, yes. Brilliant scheme, that was. All of them built in 1986.
What? Who built them?

Adults. In 1984 the President got on TV. He said children are getting smarter and smarter, and soon they'll be smarter than us, so from now on we'll teach 'em lies. Everyone thought it was a great idea, and they've been teaching kids wrong stuff ever since.
You're a sad little boy.
And you're just as ignorant as the rest of the youth of America.
Are you saying John Whittaker
If he doesn't, he'll be thrown in jail, Sarah. You'd lie, too.
Don't you think it's a scam? Who does this? Rides a bike across the country. What if there's a thunderstorm?
Well, I imagine he takes shelter when he needs to.

I'll tell you what he does. After he bikes through the city, he rides the next 100 miles in an air conditioned camper. Until he gets to the next city. Everybody thinks he's out there working and sweating when he's really sitting on an exercise bike in a camper while he watches TV and eats fig bars!
See what I have to listen to?
It's all staged... just like when they faked that whole moon-landing thing! Which is... another conversation for another time.
You think Mark Herring
He wants to write about America. Not Mars.
I'll be good.
Why am I not comforted by this?

Okay, some more specific rules: If you're in the Bible Room, no using the harp in the David display as a slingshot. Along those same lines, no eating the manna in the Moses display—it's cardboard, Dwayne Oswald
They're [deer] smarter than you think, y'know that? I don't trust 'em.
Have you heard about the plot to put tiny microphones in every public restaurant in the world?
Yeah. I mean, how else could you explain those cheesy flowers at every table?

380.s: While Connie volunteers to work on Margaret Faye's campaign for mayor of Odyssey, she hears some distressing news about Whit.
q: Someone get the number of that truck! Oh, wait. It's you, Eugene.
Nice Eugene Meltsner
I don't want to hear it, Eugene Meltsner
I wanna bring ya to a gentler, kinder Odyssey. The kind of kinder Odyssey that only my kinder kind of kind guy can bring about. Kind of.
Surely. You can help us get all computerized and stuff! Come on, what do you say?
I'm... incredulous!
Is that a yes?

After all your dubious scheming and plotting to the detriment, if not outright damage, of the town of Odyssey and its denizens, how can you realistically expect that I would even consider, much less grant, your requests for my ministrations and assistance in your bid to attain office?
In a word, NO! NO! A thousand times, NO!
I get it, youse wanna think about it for a little while. Well, fine, fine; just give me your answer tomorrow.
Boy, you really put your foot in it that time. Is Connie Kendall
You have no idea.
Just remember, Connie. John Whittaker
He would be the first to tell you that.
What's this?
What's what? It's not a typo is it? I told that guy, "leader" is spelled with two e's!

381.s: While Connie volunteers to work on Margaret Faye's campaign for mayor of Odyssey, she hears some distressing news about Whit.
q: What? What's so funny?
This can't be happening!
I'm afraid it's true, Eugene. Connie has quit!
That's the way things are around here. Everyone gets told everything but me!
Eugene may have technical expertise, but you have personality.
Personality?
Yes! Connie, the kids don't keep coming back here just for my ice cream, and they certainly don't keep coming to hear Eugene's technical jargon. They keep coming because of you.

382.s: The Mulligans have a series of minor adventures at the new 'zoo' they are trying to form.
q: So do either of you two like animals?
It depends on how they are cooked.

383.s: B-TV explores Thanksgiving with stories about 10 lepers, a king named David, and Harlow the stonecutter.
q: Looks like this great day of thanks also contains a case of marital disharmony.
Ah, one of my presidents. And two of my princes. What can I do for ya, boys?
Oh, King, live forever!
Daniel, my brother, you are older than me; Daniel, you're a star in the face of the sky!
Ah me, ah me. I'd live thankfully, if only Harlow a stonecutter again might be!
Then wake up, dufus!

384.s: Whit tells Cody Carper the story of John Newton (1725-1807), a man who experienced God's amazing grace.
q: I still can't think of who to do this report on.
Well, how about something to do with grace?
You mean Mrs. Hawkins?
Think you could learn to use a whip as well?
I've felt a whip. I'd rather use it on others than have it used on me.
So what happened to John Newton
Just hold on. This story isn't over.
When we've been there ten thousand years/Bright shining as the sun/We've no less days to sing God's praise/Than when we've first begun!

385.s: Whit and Eugene travel to Pokenberry Falls to help George Barclay, who has lost faith that he should be a pastor … which leads to a bizarre series of events.
q: That's no man, that's George Barclay!
George Barclay
To Barry Lionel
We gave up a nice situation in Odyssey to come to this... crummy, drafty old town.
You forgot measly, Dad.
Crummy, drafty, measly old town!
Donna Barclay
Help me up, Jimmy.
Help you up?!!
I'd better go up and talk to Stewart Reed Barclay
Good idea. Spread the joy.
Oh, George Barclay
Don't you realize what this means?!
No Christmas bonus?

386.s: Whit and Eugene travel to Pokenberry Falls to help George Barclay, who has lost faith that he should be a pastor … which leads to a bizarre series of events.
q: Oh, my. Officer Ward Bond
This morning I was a warped frustrated old man. What am I now?
You're still a warped frustrated old man, but sir I need help. Wrong episode (Crnel)-->
Ha! A Happy New Year to George Barclay

387.s: The gang from Whit's End hosts a wacky New Year’s Eve celebration – in front of a live audience!
q: Our program tonight is being transmitted to...to...well, dozens of people.
Here bussy bussy... Here bussy bussy! Hey! Whaddaya know! It works!
Then I guess I don't need this bunny suit...
D'oh, I get all da weirdos...
Are we there yet?

388.s: The Mulligan family and their animals are threatened when heavy rains wash away a levy upriver from their farm.
q: Well, Winona, it looks like it's just you and me, girl. Oh sure, come on up. Oh, and pass the mashed potatoes, will you please. No, no—oh. Actually, I was hoping you'd pass them in the bowl. N-no, I'll get the gravy myself. No, really, but thanks.
You know, that's something I've been wanting to ask you and Traci. Ever since I moved in, all I've been hearing is God this and God that.
Is that a problem?
No. Not really. I think it's kind of...you know. Quaint.
You did say you were forty-two, didn't you?
Right, and if you're not careful it's gonna happen to you someday.
Boy, I hope not.
Well, Jessica. You're right about one thing. It's true. I really am privileged. I have one major advantage over you.
Yeah, and what's that?
I'm blind. And blind people don't see color too well. Not even when it comes to somebody's skin.
Jessica Mulligan

389.s: The O.T. Action News team tells the biblical story of Jephthah and his hasty vow.
q: Now, gentlemen, that kind of language—

390.s: Dwayne Oswald and Julie find old bones in a cave, and they pique the interest of Bart Rathbone, who is convinced they are the bones of Bigfoot.
q: My great-grandmother wrestled a grizzly bear on [...] that land. Had a tiny scar on her right cheek, and a bearskin rug to show for it.
What do you think I am? Dumb or somethin? Look dweebs, you gotta be a real dope to believe in Bigfoot!

391.s: Julie tells Dwayne that he's funny, which makes him want to be a stand-up comedian!
q: Waddaya do when your nose goes on strike? Picket!

That reminds me of a story. There were three prisoners who were gonna be executed by a firing squad. They put the first prisoner up against the wall and were about to shoot him when he yelled, "Earthquake!" And everybody ran for cover and the prisoner got away. Well, they finally realized there was no earthquake, so they brought out the second prisoner and put him against the wall. They were just about to shoot him when he yelled, "Tornado!" And everybody ran for cover. And again the second prisoner got away. When they realized there was no tornado, they put the third prisoner against the wall — a real dufus. The commander said, "Ready, aim-" and the dufus yelled, "Fire!" Badunch! Get it? Earthquake, tornado, fire? Firing squad? Get it?
How will it look when everyone is rolling over me?
Ah! Here Let's get outa here!
We'll get you for Dwayne Oswald

392.s: Eugene takes Mandy Straussberg on an Imagination Station adventure to show her where prayer has made a difference throughout history.
q: Based on my observational skills, I would have to say that we are... on a road in the middle of nowhere.
I can see that.

393.s: Jack and Joanne Allen throw Eugene Meltsner and Katrina Shanks a Valentine's Day engagement party. Eugene wants to give Katrina a ring, but Katrina's father gives her a family heirloom ring the same day.
q: What's wrong? You're all looking at me as if I've grown a third nostril.
See what? Have I grown a third nostril?
Eugene, Connie Kendall
Connie wants me to kiss her hello?
She wants you to kiss her hello?
We should all kiss hello? One big, sloppy smooch fest?
Well, when you put it like that...
Eugene! You bought me a ring? Ah! It's perfect!
I thought you would think so.
I have to put it on right away. Here, hold Daddy's ring.
Oh, Eugene! I love it! It's wonderful! It's magnificent! It's colossal!
I thought so, too, which is why it took the proverbial wind out of my sails when Armitage Shanks
I don't care about that, Eugene. I'll wear it on my other hand. This is my engagement ring.
I'm sorry, Eugene, but we're men. Let's call a spade a spade.
Mr. Shanks, had I given Katrina a shovel, then yes, we could call a spade a spade. As it is, we're discussing rings!
It's not fair. Are you thinking of eloping?
It's not polite to stand there smiling like that. Eugene Meltsner
Aw, that's sweet.
Ugh, I'm gonna be sick if it gets any sweeter.
I've got a bucket on the porch.
Wait until Katrina Meltsner
Are you sure you should tell her, sir? Won't she cry all the way home?
Are you kidding? I'll be crying all the way home!

394.s: Whit tells Jared DeWhite the story of Patrick, a slave boy who changed the history of an entire nation through his dedication to Jesus.
q: Ah, my dear Lochrue, you have the heart of a priest and the mind of a criminal. You should be in government.
Am I a piece of meat that you think you can simply pass around?!
In fact boy, you are.

395.s: Whit tells Jared DeWhite the story of Patrick, a slave boy who changed the history of an entire nation through his dedication to Jesus.
q: Patrick had to obey God. To disobey would have compromised his faith.
[We are] Emissaries of the Lord Jesus Christ.
Oh, Patrick wasn't a magician; he was a man of prayer. How it was that the soldiers saw deer instead of the priests is... well, that's — that's up to somebody else to explain.

396.s: Eugene nearly has a nervous breakdown when Bernard Walton keeps beating him in chess. Meanwhile, Heather tries to get her volleyball team to work harder.
q: There are times when I'm convinced this is a game Bernard Walton
Eugene, you just ended a sentence with a preposition!
Impossible! Prepositions are not words that I end sentences with! Oops.
Uh, just a minute, Eugene. Apparently Connie has a crush on me or something.
Today, Bernard Walton beats me at chess. Tomorrow, the earth will revolve around the sun!
The earth does revolve around the sun, Eugene!
Oh, I see what he's doing.
He's trying to get me to move my horse—
Away from his tower—
So that he can get my guy with a pointy head!
Bishop!! And I'm not quite clear why you think it's to your advantage to verbalize my strategy out loud!
Ah! So that "is" your strategy huh?
...no, of course not. Would you mind moving please.
Wait. Watch this move. Bishop to Rook 3, there! I seriously think Bernard
It's bedtime, Eugene.
Just how important is it to you to beat Eugene Meltsner
Meaning you have made your point already. You beat him every game. So what's the big deal if you lost one, y'know?
Connie! Are you asking me to throw the game?
He's an emotional wreck! Please, Bernard?
This is good for him!
Look at him! He's got his shoes on the wrong feet!
Have you slept at all?
Have you showered?
I've done both, actually. Although I can't remember when or where...
Right! I'll see you at noon!
Ok. This is starting to be fun, I think.
Lets play again.
Now I got to go back to work in 20 minutes...
Just a quick game. Quick game.
A quick game of chess?
We finished that last one off in 15 minutes.
Bernard Walton

397.s: A tornado hits Odyssey, and the Rathbones lose their home. Mandy wants to do something to help, but the rest of the town is more reluctant.
q: Melvin Steward, our intrepid newsman, looks like he’s about to have a stroke!
Good morning! Well, it was a good morning until Casey Parker
There’s no protecting our house as long as Rodney’s living there.
Thanks, Pop!
I don’t believe it! That tree went right through my room! I hope my stereo’s okay...
My brother’s as reliable as you are, Bart.
Uh-oh. We’re in big trouble...
Polly wants to meet Abraham Lincoln.
Whoa! Runaway garbage can!
Ah-ha! And there was light. ...And there was darkness.
The first day, and it wasn’t good.
This shelter is for decent citizens who need help, not weasels like you!
Hey, hey, I don't remember a sign saying "no weasels allowed."

398.s: After Rodney Rathbone wrecks Jared DeWhite's science fair project, Jared accuses him of all sorts of additional misdoings around town.
q: Some dirty low-down no-good louse took my cap! That really stinks!
I'm the vanguard of justice around here, and Rodney Rathbone

399.s: After her dog is involved in a tragic accident, Lisa Mulligan hears the biblical story of Job from Bernard Walton.
q: Why does everyone in the Bible sound like they were named during a sneeze?
I don't know. Be quiet.
I hate to tell you this, but J-O-B spells job.
Not in this case.
