Yeah, two of them, coming out of his skull!
That's crazy. Mandy Straussberg
But I told Doris Rathbone

444.s: Nick Mulligan's controversial friend Vince seems to have become a better person. • Bethany dreams a wacky version of the flood story.
q: I bet it was pretty nice growing up in Odyssey
We, uh, have a freezer to stock, uh, so we'll leave you two to catch up. Come on, Connie.
Nice meeting you, folks!
Do you remember what I told you when you stopped smoking? Who tempts people to sin?
Well, is that the role you want to play in someone's life?
But we didn't make it to Philadelphia in time for the signing of the Declaration of Independence, so Jefferson got mad.
To be, or not to be. To be, dooby dooby, do.

445.s: Through the Room of Consequence, Alex Jefferson experiences what life would be like if he could do whatever he wanted—without any rules.
q: Where'd you get that bike? It's awesome!
My folks got it for me. It's even got a mini radio. See?
I wish my parents were like yours, always giving me stuff.
Well, I guess my parents just find me more lovable.
Get me out!! Out! Out!!
Hey, Mom. Hey, Mr. Jefferson
That's "Principal Johnson." And will you please take your feet off my desk?
Good boy, Alex.
Uh, is it all right if I stay up late tonight?
Absolutely not. It's a school night.
Yes! Thanks, Mom! Thanks, Dad! You're the greatest!

446.s: After getting kicked out of Whit's End for poor manners, David Straussberg and Alex Jefferson decide to learn good manners. • Bethany Shepard has a dream very loosely based on the Seven Deadly Sins.
q: Tut tut there, Mandy, is that an elbow I see?
Oh, sorry! Alex, this diagram shows you need to lick the ice-cream in a clockwise direction, not counterclockwise. Minus two points.
David, it says here you're supposed to eat the cherry first, not the whipped cream. Three points off.
She's my widdew tootsy-wootsy!
Mutual, I'm sure.
Oh well... here's a bed of lettuce. I guess I'll just take a little nap.
One for the price of two! Don't think about it, just buy it!
Snow DeWhite
That's better- The Amazon rainforest?!

447.s: Aubrey is so embarrassed by her parents that she does everything she can to keep them from showing up at a poetry reading--including not telling them about it at all.
q: You can show them your Winnie the Pooh impression! "Oh bother!"
Winnie the Pooh! Winnie the Pooh!

Oh no, I love it! I look like Laura Ingalls Wilderness in it. When she's out on the frontier herding turkeys and then some Indians, ah, I mean Native Americans, come out from behind the trees, armed with water balloons, and so she runs away, but her little dog Toto gets caught by Pocahontas, the last Mohican, and Laura runs to tell her Pa, who starts to cry, because he's going to abandon her and take part on the Byway to Heaven!
That's exactly what I thought of when we bought it!
Were Aubrey Shepard
They were. Aubrey, in fact, performed an exemplary rendition of works of mid-18th century poets.
Uh, where are they now?
Deceased, I believe.
Not the poets, Eugene — our daughters!

448.s: Two plays that Mandy has written are performed at the Little Theatre--starring the Whit's End crew as themselves!
q: Mega mega mega mega World... ride the rides and then you'll hurl!
Miss. Kendall, Miss. Kendall! Are you well? It sounded as though you were choking!

She ate some bad mayo on a sandwich and got sick, then on her way to the bathroom she slipped on her freshly-waxed floor, knocking over a huge hamster cage! She tried to pick the cage up and threw out her back, and the hamster was so mad it bit her on the hand! Can you imagine all that happening to the same person... at the same time?
My computer!
So, water does hurt those things?
<in Eugene Meltsner
Wow, the hamster of death!
You were a great Pontius Pilate.
Thanks. I think.
If you'll excuse me.
I've been trying to do that for years.
I heard that!
I heard that, too!

449.s: Aubrey Shepard takes an Imagination Station adventure to meet the biblical John the Baptist.
q: I am Micah. Son of Agun.
John the Baptist.
Nice to meet you. I'm Aubrey the Methodist. Or Episcopalian, I don't exactly remember.
Aren't you a little old to be swinging on a swing?
Well, now how old do you have to be?
449.t: Standing up for what you believe

450.s: Aubrey Shepard takes an Imagination Station adventure to meet the biblical John the Baptist.
q: Look, I'm John the Baptist
450.t: Standing up for what you believe

451.s: When Nathaniel Graham's family suddenly becomes very rich, he notices that the kids start to treat him differently.
q: Nathaniel Graham
How many bathrooms do you have?
I lost count after five and a half.
I mean, I'm happy to be your friend, but we'd rather not let the neighbors know.
We don't have to be your friends if it's embarrassing to you!
We have other friends we can visit, y'know!

Really? You could've fooled me. We've had to have the pinball machines recalibrated three times because you've been using them too much, and the filter in the pool had to be replaced four times because of excessive girl hair. I mean, I'm not complaining; we want to keep you as happy as possible. Without people like you on our side, who would pump our gas?
I wanted to be Nathaniel Graham
Just who do you think you are?!

I'm Nathaniel, that's who. You remember—Nathaniel, the kid who wears garage sale clothes, and is lousy in sports...and who just happens to have an indoor pool. That's all. I'm the same person I always was.
Look, I just want things to be like they were. I want to be your friend—or at least, as much as I was your friend before. Sometimes it was hard to tell.
Did Nathaniel Graham
He must have. My cheek just went numb!
We walked around trying to find Nathaniel Graham

452.s: Alex Jefferson becomes convinced that he should become a missionary like Jason Whittaker.
q: So, let me guess. You're wearing the torn shirt and pants that are too big so people will feel bad for you and give you more money?
Kinda. I noticed you did that on Sunday with that ratty tie and the mismatched shirt. It has a nice... needy effect to it.
Ratty tie? I love that tie!
You better not be talking to me.
But... it's dirty Oswald Heights
Alex, you were eating bugs yesterday.

453.s: Kids' Radio features a story about a young girl named Dotty who is transported to a strange land.
q: Oh! How Curious!
Now isn't that just peachy keen. So I'm a road-side curiosity now, huh?

And so, my question this ponder; what is truth? For truth, truly true truth, is found in the cow, in the strawberry, and the giant tooky-tooky bird. In all of us is found truth. In our left earlobe, it is found. In our bellybutton, it is found.
Alright already! Can we talk about something more pleasant? Like maybe in-grown toenails?
Silence! I am the Great Wishy Woz! And you are little pip-squeaks.
I'm looking for love. In all the wrong places, apparently.
I don't have a brain in my head. See?
Oh my, you don't?
Nope. Some folks are out of their mind, but my mind is out of me.
One day? Well that's only 22 hours. I don't know how we're gonna do it!
Thank you! (But they're really not my color...)
You're welcome! (Deal with it.)
I guess I could have figured out a way to get my legs back on myself. But after all, I'm just a dummy!
Mystic Mountain Lion! What do you want?
I want my mommy...

454.s: Kids' Radio features a story about a young girl named Dotty who is transported to a strange land.
q: Mr. Manny, this is your big chance to get your book.

Books? You want books? Ha! We've got books on hairy otters, on onions and on Mars. All the fungus you could care for plus three triple zillion stars. We've got books on flossing teeth, plus three books on tossing sheep. If we spent our lives just counting books, we'd never get to sleep. Hey!
Love is loving yourself enough to do the things that make you feel good. And doesn't it feel good to feel good about feeling good? I get kind of... choked up just thinking about it.
You're nothing but a little man with a great big head!
Well, actually, now, I'm quite proportionately mesomorphic.
I'll get you, my pretty — and your little frog, too!
Oh, whatever.

455.s: When Jason Whittaker is late to speak at the Timothy Center, Connie tries to keep a restless crowd calm.
q: Why can't ducks wear glasses?
Because they don't have EARS! HA, HA, HA!!
Row, row, row your boat. Row, row, row your — Oswald Heights

I was trapped by the invisible walls of my fate. Tricked by the idea that I could not escape. Chained up in a ghetto where my father died. Fooled into thinking I would never go outside. Imprisoned by my friends who knew nothing but war-shackled to everything that had gone on before. I would always be here in this dead-end life of mine, my heart turned back by a city limit sign. And yet...And yet I now see a way out of my concrete jail. A new way to soften a heart that's grown stale. No longer cursed in this place for the wealth. No longer fighting with man or myself. I understand now what it takes to get real; if you want to stand up- you have to learn how to kneel. I surrender. My weapons are down at my feet. Cause we'll never have freedom - when there's blood on the street.

456.s: Mandy Straussberg has one of those days when one thing after another goes wrong.
q: Hey, are you going to band auditions this afternoon?
Yep. My drums are ready to go.
You play the oboe.
I did play the oboe. My dad said it gave him a headache and thought I should take up another instrument.
Does he know that you decided on drums?
Not yet. I wanted to surprise him.
Are Mandy Straussberg
Stop! Stop! I just wanted one piece of ice!
That was awful!
It wasn't so bad. I could still make out The First Noel.
Great. But it was the National Anthem.
Uhh, yeah, I know. It was just the Christmas version of it.
Did you wear mismatching socks?
That's not a sin, Alex.
Did you wear stolen mismatching socks?
Please don't tell me that everything is going to be fine, or the day wasn't all that bad, or I should look at the bright side of things.

No, I was only going to say that bad days happen, to everyone. It doesn't mean that God doesn't love you, or that life will be bad forever. It means that sometimes, things just go wrong. But the sun will rise tomorrow, and you'll have a new day. Hopefully it will be a better day than today.

457.s: With the Timothy Center in a financial crisis, it seems like an answered prayer when a company called Novacom offers Tom Riley a lot of money to build a tower on his property.
q: You do have a suit, don't you?
Connie, I was mayor. It was kinda required.
Oh, yeah, I remember that suit. Maybe we should try something from a recent decade.
There's no point in second guessing the decision. It's done. Now all we can do is see how it plays out and have faith that even if we made a mistake that God will work through it.
But we pay for our mistakes, Whit.
I know, that's why I hope I'm wrong.
Ugh, I'll probably have to sell my blood or something.
Ooh, Aubrey, that's a great one! I'll add it to my list, too!

458.s: Alex Jefferson and his cousin, Cal Jordan, attempt to find out what Eugene is doing at Campbell College.
q: What d'you think they're doing in there?
They're probably punishing the last kid they caught standing here!
Are you crazy? Come back here! We could get arrested or shot or something!
You're so funny when you get scared!
You're so corkbrained when you get curious!

Somewhere out there is a professional hacker who's been repeatedly breaking into the college computer system over the past two weeks. We've been trying to follow the trail, but he—or she—is very slippery. However, thanks to Alex and Cal's little misadventure yesterday, we now have a name: AREM. And a possible way to catch our hacker.
A self-destructing modem! That's a clever feature.
Yeah, every modem should have one.
Okay, I confess! Cal Jordan

459.s: Mandy has a difficult time keeping control of the girls at her slumber party.
q: You have red-eyed monsters upstairs?
Not literally, Liz. I’m talking about me and Rachel Straussberg
But why are you red-eyed? Do you have an infection or something? Because my dad had pink eye and he used some great drops for it.
We’re tired, Liz. That’s all I meant.
Never mind, Dad.

Now, listen, you three. I told you before: you can stay up late if you keep it quiet, and you’re not keeping it quiet. Now settle down with a quiet game or something or you’ll have to go to bed now. Is that what you want?
How else would those poor tribal people in Africa heat up their pizza?
You really think you're better than everyone, don't you?
Well, now that you mention it, maybe I am. I'm kind and loyal and gentle and...
Liz, remember what we talked about earlier?
...and pretty and smart and almost perfect.
I agree, Sarah: you are better than everyone else. You're kind and loyal—sort of like my Golden Retriever, actually. It's just too bad the resemblance doesn't end there.

460.s: Novacom buys B-TV from Bernard. Meanwhile, Alex and Cal get jobs working for the company.
q: No, Alex. Keep your eyes closed. It's a surprise.
Well, I know I'm in the library, 'cause I smell books.
(Beeping noise) Huh? What was that? Oh, my computer. "Instant message from AREM. Do you wish to respond?" No, I wish to go home! Is there a button for that? Ah, forget it.
You asked what I thought.
Well, I'll know better next time.
Break your neck!
Thanks. I think you meant, "break your leg."

461.s: B-TV explores the topic of obedience with sketches about the biblical characters Gideon, Naaman, and Moses.
q: Sorry, Jonah. But our consolation prize is a trip to the middle of the ocean where you'll enjoy some deep sea diving while whale watching.
...Adam and Eve, uh, I don't seem to have your last name here.
Adam and Eve... Smith.
And from not quite as ancient Israel is Jonah—Uh... no last name either?
Arrr!... Smith.
Excuse me there, Mose.
What is it, Schlemiel?
I'm not into rules, man.
I'm Bob Field in the field.
And I'm Bob Booth in the booth.
Ew! Ew! What is that awful stench?!
Did you forget your deodorant again?
You must bathe.
That's it? What, did my mother call you?

462.s: To compete with the new Novacom Kids Center, Whit experiments with a massive overhaul to Whit's End and its attractions.
q: I just got back. What are you doing?
Oh, just taking a walk through your orchard.
Well, you're not gonna get very far standing on a ladder.
Alright, Here's number one, a climbing wall with ropes so no one gets hurt.
Ok, but what's the purpose?
It could teach a Bible story. It could be the climbing wall of Jericho.
(laughs) They didn't climb that wall. They marched around it and blew trumpets.
Well, that's no fun!
John Whittaker

463.s: Connie falls for a Novacom employee named Robert Mitchell. Bart Rathbone protests that Novacom's programming is immoral.
q: Uh, this is heavy! What’s in here?
Green eyes...
I’m Mitch, by the way. What’s your name?
Mitch... I mean, Connie!
Well, happy greetings everyone! What a beautiful day it is, ain’t it?
Well, it used to be.
Oh, great. Where's the "rest in peace" ribbon?
So, the riot was fun? I mean...
It was a riot.
"Robert Mitchell
It takes more that a John Whittaker
Hey, I didn't do nothin'! That rock slipped out of my hand while I was cleanin' it!
Pop's proposed doin' a handyman show on Novacom TV: What's Wrong with Bart Rathbone.
Now listen, it wasn't "What's wrong with Barthbone." It's "What's Wrong, Hosted by Bart Rathbone!"
What about our right to cheap speech?

464.s: Jack Allen and Whit tell Connie the story of how Whit met his wife in college.
q: I think we've gotten off on the wrong foot, apart from the one in my mouth. Maybe we should start over. I’m John Avery Whittaker, but my friends call me Whit.
I’m Guinevere Morrow. My friends call me Jenny. You can call me Guinevere.
Oh, uh... oh. Guinevere.
I love books, but I can't imagine being a teacher. I don't think I'd have the patience.

465.s: Jack Allen and Whit tell Connie the story of how Whit met his wife in college.
q: Jack? What's wrong?
I'm sorry, did I wake you?
No, I had to get up to answer the door anyway.
Maybe we should do the thing we were supposed to do all along.
You're right. Should I start?
Dear God.....
Uh oh. I know that tone. It's the same tone you used when you caught me playing matador with your father's bull.
You needed some straight talking then, and you need some straight talking now.

466.s: When school is canceled due to snow, Alex Jefferson accepts a job to deliver cookies to his grandmother. On the way, he must endure many trials and tribulations.
q: All right, it's time for plan zebra-alpha-Charlie-fettuccine-water buffalo!
Wow, sounds like a great plan!
Come on, the paper bag?
Okay, I guess maybe you can use it to cover his... face.
Alex, I bequeath to you my lime green glow in the dark yo-yo.
Cal, I don't want your yo-yo.
(reviving suddenly) What do you mean? It's a great yo-yo!
Snowflakes drifted down like dandruff from the sky…
The pond in the park was iced over and people were gliding around on ice skates like ballerinas wearing really slippery socks on a linoleum floor.
Mr Smiley... isn't with us anymore.
To put it gently, he was decimated by a sniper snowball.
Come on men! Are we warriors, or are we wimps?!
We are wimps, sir!
(Singing) Snow, snow snow, how Alex loves snow, snow snow snow snow snow snow snow snow snow. Snow snow snow snow snow snow snow snow snow snow snow snow snow snow snow...
How many fingers am I holding up?
Bozeman, Montana!

467.s: When a window gets broken at Whit's End, Whit puts Rodney, Sarah Prachett, and Alex on trial to see where the responsibility for fixing the window will fall.
q: Connie and Mitch, sitting in a tree, k-i-s-s-i—
We were just gonna talk.
Connie and Mitch, sitting in a tree, t-a-l-k-i-n-g.
We were not in a tree.
Connie and Mitch, sitting in a booth—
I think you two better stop now.
We're just practicing our spelling. S-p-l-l, I mean, s-p-i--
But you don't not know!
Yeah— I mean no, I don't not know, I guess...
So, if you don't not know, then you do know! And if you know that the answer isn't no, then you know that there's no way you can know I broke the window!
No further questions!
Court is now in recess!
Oh yeah! When the going gets tough, the tough go outside and play on the swings!
Do I look like I'm stupid?
Strike that from the record.
Thank you, I'm calling Rodney P. Rathbone to the stand.
Rodney, did you or did you not get kicked out of Whit's End yesterday?
Did you, or did you not try to get revenge?
Of course I did! What's your point?
I'd like to call Robert Mitchell
Where were Rodney Rathbone
I can't get a lawyer that soon! Uncle Louie

468.s: As construction begins on Whit's End in Connellsville, Whit learns that many people don't want his shop there after all.
q: We need to take the hint. We have to get out of Oswald Heights.

It just seems to me that the reason you did this was to reach more people. This would be your chance to connect with some that have hardly heard the name of Jesus. I know a few of these kids and they are tough, but they're reachable. They need a place like Whit's End more than anyone.

469.s: As construction begins on Whit's End in Connellsville, Whit learns that many people don't want his shop there after all.
q: Mary, how would you like to attend a neighborhood meeting in Oswald Heights?
Not a chance. Is that what you're doing?
I hope you get out alive.
You don't understand. I'm from South Dakota. We didn't have crime when I was growing up. Everyone was polite and kind and knives were used to cut pork chops.
Where are you going?
I was thinking Alaska. Live off moose meat for a while.
I trusted you.
That was your first mistake. Maybe this can be a lesson for you.
What's the lesson? That I'm not supposed to trust anyone?
That's a bad way to live your life. I'd rather believe in people.
It's not that easy.
Well I want to look for the correct definition of a- of a word.
Oh yeah sure. What word?
Just, uh, any word.
Ope! There it is. Unbelievable.
That's the word?
Why would someone put a camera in your office?
I don't know. But someone's awfully desperate to find out what we're doing over here.
But we're not doing anything. We're handing out ice cream. Do you think it's a spy from Dairy Dream or something?

Oh, my guess is that we've got worse problems than someone stealing our recipe for raspberry ripple. No the person who would go to such lengths to spy on us won't stop just because I pulled their dictionary off the shelf. They'll try again. We have to find out who they are, and what they want.

470.s: In an unfortunate accident, Cal Jordan loses control of his bike. He crashes into Walter Shakespeare, whose leg is broken as a result.
q: I'll... call a cab. ...Precisely how do you call a cab, Shakespeare?
With a phone, sir.
Perhaps if we promote the theater in more innovative ways, people will come to our productions.

Innovative? Say you're not thinking about those tacky little pins with our names printed along the edge or a pot holder with my face on it. I have no desire to have hot pans pressed against my face, Shakespeare!
Go on, go on! Read what's on it!
Made in Taiwan.
The other side.
I found myself doing "to be or not to be" in rap!
It... drew a crowd, sir.
Only because I threw out my back doing the hand gestures!
I'd have to have my brain replaced with a broccoli sprout to agree to such a thing!
Dr. Franklin
Already have one, sir.
I hadn't realized how much I depend on William Shakespeare

471.s: Alex breaks a miniature-golf record, which rockets him to local fame. Meanwhile, an Odyssey local who made it big in Hollywood returns for a visit.
q: Guys, Greg O Neil
If you don't stop changing my stations, I'm gonna call the exterminator!
Really. Is he the reason you got all dressed up?
Look at you: you're wearing a dress, you've got on make-up... What is that? Is that perfume?
It's called soap.
Oh, you know what I mean. Doesn't Connie Kendall
Hm, yes, yes... Oh no, no! Well, it's hard to tell with all this, uh, ice cream!
Thirty-seven, thirty-eight, thirty-nine.
You're slowing down. What's the problem?
I just don't understand what sit-ups have to do with golf.
Sit-ups have one thing to do with golf hole number six. You ain't getting the ball up that big hill with flabby stomach muscles like yours — now come on!
It's all in the wrist. Keep your arm straight, circular motion. Whats'a matter?
I guess I just don't understand what waxing your car has to do with... oh, never mind.
You're those kids who've been riding your bikes through my garden!
No, we're not!
You got the wrong guys!
I oughta smack you two a good one with my walking stick!
Wait, we didn't do anything!
Rotten kids!

472.s: When Wooton Bassett takes time out of his postal route to help at Whit's End, he gets fired for missing too much work.
q: ...Do you have any idea what time it is?
No, but if you let me punch out with my time card, I can show ya.
It's six p.m.
Wow! Shouldn't you be home for dinner?
Thanks, Wooton!
You're welcome, now shoo!
Who wants to see me make a chocolate milkshake in less than a minute without using my hands?
Ok, here goes. Alex! Make me a milkshake and make it fast!

473.s: As construction on the new Whit's End nears completion, Whit finds his time stretched to the limit.
q: To receive information about one of our products, press 1. To receive one of our informational products, press 2. To inform us that you have not received one of our products, press 3.
To be better informed and/or receive and/or produce one of our productive and/or informational products, press 5 and/or 6. To speak to someone in English, press 7.
Uh, Whit, do you have any idea how to get a bucket off of somebody's head?
Yeah, like the ones that those chocolate sprinkles come in?
Who has a bucket on their head?
Well, that's not really important.
Nick... do you have a bucket on your head?

474.s: Jason Whittaker returns to a missions project he set up months before and finds that things have gone terribly wrong.
q: Anyone else? Have you ever been told that you were too weak or too young or too old? Yeah, yeah, you in the back, do you have a testimony?
Yeah, once in the first grade my friends told me that I was too wimpy to eat four raw eggs and a snail in succession. Ha, I guess I showed them!
I’ve looked for the keys to enlightenment and I know not where else to look.
Search your heart, search your soul...
Search the top drawer of your nightstand. That’s where I always keep my keys.
I can't wait till I have to shave, so I can not shave, too.
This is the present you sent me. I put it next to my bed.
I sent this to you?
None of us knew what it was to be honest. But he kept it. I think it died or something. It shrunk up and got hard.
Well you know that was called cotton candy. And you were supposed to eat it.
No, no! Not now! Don't eat it now. You could probably break a tooth on it now.
Just be very careful what you say. These people are different now.
Manuel, a little talk shouldn't hurt.
Are you crazy? Luis (b)
These guys are gonna eat our dirt!

475.s: Jason Whittaker returns to a missions project he set up months before and finds that things have gone terribly wrong.
q: Señor Whittaker had nothing to do with it.
We'll let the police sort that out. Take these trespassers to jail.
Hey! I'm an American! I've got connections in the American Embassy.
I don't think anybody's listening.
Oh they're listening alright. They just... don't care.
Did you tell them where I was?
Yes, and no explanation would be enough. You are the founder of our church. Your place was on your knees praying with the rest of us. Not in here filling Luis (b)
Why has everybody turned on me?
You forgot what made us love you in the first place.
You taught us about Jesus. You gave us hope. You showed us how to be servants to others. You never once mentioned anything about revenge.

Let me finish. When you came this time, you didn't talk much about God. You talked a lot about how you were going to save us. I believe you were relying on yourself more than on the God who brought you here to begin with. And in fact, I think we all did. We worshiped you more than God, Jason. And you failed. So where were we to turn to?
Thanks for your help, mi amigo.
My help? No, Manuel. It had nothing to do with me.
Ah, Luis (b)

476.s: Spending a week at his grandparents' house seems like the end of the world to Alex Jefferson.
q: Maybe we could go somewhere after dinner.
I don't know. Somewhere fun.
We could go to the Hospital.
The hospital?
Good idea. We could have our stomachs pumped.
Do you fix everything with duct tape?
Well, it's better than calling a plumber and letting them charge you an arm and a leg.
You’re in my way, boy. Go on outside and play horseshoes.

I did as I was told, and “played horseshoes.” I threw the horseshoe, walked to the other stake, and threw it back, walked to the other stake, threw it again, and did this for about three hours. I could’ve gone longer, but I pulled a muscle in my arm, trying to heave it one hundred feet from one stake to the other. It hurt pretty bad, but Grandpa wrapped my arm in duct tape! And then it felt much … much worse.
Go on outside and play horseshoes.
Ugh! There's a toenail in my ketchup!

477.s: OT Action News reports on the story of Deborah and Barak and their battle against the Canaanites.
q: Our top O.T. Action News reporter, Alex Jefferson, is on the scene in the hill country of Ephraim. Alex, what's happening there?
Brink Chetley

478.s: Mandy Straussberg and Sarah Prachett go camping far from Odyssey and run into an old friend--Jared DeWhite! But Jared's explanation of his disappearance from Odyssey makes them wonder whether or not to believe him.
q: It wasn't a crazy person. It was Jared DeWhite
Did you hear what you just said?

479.s: A S.M.I.L.E. convention at the Timothy Center falls apart when the S.M.I.L.E. leader has a heart attack in the middle of the festivities.
q: I've been lookin' all over for you and Henry! Where is that happy guy?
Oh, he died last year.
Oh. Sorry to, uh, hear that.
Oh, it's OK. I just have to keep thinking poooositively!
You're so right.
I used to be a dried-up, cynical, prune-faced, miserable creature, just like you!
So you think that my group is made up of a bunch of phonies, people who aren't happy, but act like they are.
Yeah... I guess.
But here you are, in a situation that would make a lot of people happy, like your parents, but you act like you aren't.
Hey, I'm not pretending to be unhappy.
Hahaha. You aren't? Are you sure? Being miserable is an easy habit to take on.
And being happy is an easy thing to fake.
Hmm. Well then, I suppose that gives us both something to think about.

480.s: Rodney Rathbone discourages Austin O'Conner from hanging around Colby Cabrera because he's “weird.” Wooton Bassett and the kids try to win a Christmas decorating contest.
q: It didn't take no genius to figure it out.
Lucky for you.
And what does a roasting pan have to do with Christ'a'mas?

Oh, you know you see, I'm using it to show that even though the world is full of sin, and dirty car parts and roasting pans that God still sent his son to us in the middle of it cause he loves us an stuff and that's why we celebrate Christmas. Besides won't it look great when the lights are turned on?
You and your yard are an embarrassment to the whole neighborhood. This place is an eyesore. And everybody but you knows it.
Whoah. Everybody? Yeah, but I haven't heard anything from anyone else.

That's because I'm the only one around here, who doesn't have a problem with hurting other people's feelings. This is the ugliest Christ'a'mas display in the history of Odyssey and everybody agrees. I'm gonna prove it. I will prove it to ya!
I'm here on official business, not a social call.
Oh, official business? Wow, should I put on a tie?
Nah, that won't be necessarial.
Oh, that's good, cause I don't have a tie.
Let me ask you something. Who would you rather be Rodney Rathbone or Colby Cabrera?
Well, myself, of course.
Then that's who you should be. You know you can't stop being yourself because you get made fun of. I didn't stop being myself and look where it got me. Oh, maybe that's a bad illustration.
A car made out of popsicle sticks. That's weaker than zit cream.
First my yard wins most original because of you, and now your car. I guess it's been confirmed twice then.
There's no doubt about it, Colby: you're an original.
Wooton, what's with the flamingo in the stable?
Oh, she's not a flamingo anymore, Austin. Not since I painted her anyway. She's a cow.
[after watching Wooton win the competition] That proves it. There is nothing good on the T & V anymore!!
Oh... boy, do Wooton Bassett

481.s: Whit's End Connellsville opens amidst much fanfare. The celebration is cut short when Whit finds hidden cameras all over the shop.
q: What do you mean, "shhhh?"
We mean be quiet. Our napkin dispenser might be bugged.
Yup, I knew it would happen sooner or later. Too many video games--turns your brain into macaroni and cheese.
I've died and gone to heaven!
If you died, you probably wouldn't notice.

482.s: Whit's End Connellsville opens amid much fanfare. But celebration is cut short when more sinister happenings begin to unfold.
q: You know I wasn't sure about this bowling thing, but I'm kind of getting excited about it. Last time I went I got a 24! I wonder if I can beat it?
I feel like I should be waving a stick at a piñata.
Come on, printer, I could go faster with a stone tablet and a chisel!
Andromeda, spy cameras, a hidden modem, Eugene's project on brain waves and radio waves, AREM, Jared DeWhite
I don't know about you guys, but I think it's time we take this to someone who can tell us what's going on.
Mr. Whittaker!
It's still your turn.
And it will remain your turn until you bowl into our lane.
Hey, Connie Kendall
Oh, Eugene... What have you gotten yourself into?

483.s: Connie's relationship with Robert Mitchell is tested when she discovers the picture of another girl in his briefcase.
q: Hey, uh, Bernard Walton
Connie Kendall
Hi, can I help you?
Nick, it's me!
Connie? But your- What happened to your hair?
I'm experimenting with some different colors.
I don't think purple is the one you're looking for.
For your information, it's not purple. It's raspberry chestnut.
Well... it certainly catches one's attention.
Thank you! See, Nick?
Yeah, but Ronald McDonald catches one's attention too, you know!
This'll have to do.
Connie, that's a frozen pizza.
Oh, stop complaining and hold it against your nose.
Why? Give me one good reason of why I should trust you?
Because I think I'm falling in love with you, Connie!
(beat) Oh! Well! It looks like we're out of time for today! For Candid Conversations with Connie, I'm Connie Kendall! Goodbye!
Who wouldn't want to date Robert Mitchell
Well, I wouldn't wanna—
What girl wouldn't wanna date Mitch?
If Robert Mitchell

484.s: As tension increases and more pieces of a sinister plot come together, Whit and Connie find that Eugene has eloped with Katrina Shanks and left town.
q: Well, Eugene Meltsner
Eugene must have been in a hurry to get away...
Or else he was robbed by a vest lover.

485.s: Connie continues to investigate Eugene's disappearance and has to decide if she will trust Mitch. Or is he a spy for Novacom?
q: Mr. Whittaker, Robert Mitchell... is dead.
You've got all these secrets. I feel like I'm dating the Pentagon, and I don't even know how to ask you about any of it! I mean, my biggest secret is that I'm afraid of staplers!
You're not gonna tell anybody, are you?
I promise, but if you'll... you're afraid of staplers?
So you have no idea what the research involves?
When I asked Armitage, all he would say was that it would change our society.
For better or for worse?
Time will tell, I suppose. But if Andromeda has anything to do with it, I would expect the worst.
Sure, but I have a few questions for you. It sounds like a lot of weird stuff is happening around here.
Weirder than usual, you mean?
Rachel Jefferson
But then I got here and Cal Jordan
W-what? Wait. Who said who was safe?
And then I heard that Dr. Ichabodia
Where did that come from?
Wooton Bassett
Oh no. They're following us!
They're following us? Awesome! Do you want me to lose 'em?
Yes, yes. Uh, put the pedal to the metal!
I've been waiting my entire life for someone to say that!
Something tells me you have more hobbies than ice cream, John Whittaker
Well, I dabble a bit.
Don't listen to AREM

486.s: Connie mourns the loss of Mitch while Jack Allen and Whit try to retrieve a package with crucial information.
q: I have something to tell you.
Whit, what's wrong?
Connie, Robert Mitchell
Whit, what's going on here? People are breaking and entering, and disappearing and dying. What is this all about?
That's what I'm trying to find out. That package from Arthur Dent should have some answers.
One thing puzzles me, Jack Allen

487.s: Wooton Bassett helps Connie deal with Mitch's departure, while Whit collaborates with FBI Agent Bourland.
q: The dishrag sits on the counter, catching no one's eye. The polished bronze a reflection, clear as the cloudless sky. The dishrag is tossed, the laundry is its fate...
What's happening?!

Hello, everyone. Thanks for listening. But it's time for our broadcasting day to end. This is the bug at the soda fountain signing off. Oh, by the way, you may want to listen to the bug in Whit's End Library
I didn't realize Whittaker was such a comedian.
A two-hour conversation about socks can say "I love you" just as much as... well, saying "I love you."
EAT LASERS, PIG!
Maybe I should give up on relationships... enter a convent.
You really... you really took a lot of time out of your day to hang out with me. Thanks, Wooton.
Oh... oh, don't thank me. Thank all the people on my route that are gonna get their mail at ten o'clock tonight.
Think about it, Mr. Whittaker. Why do you think there's been so much activity around you? Modems, bugs, cameras in your office...
I don't know anything about it. Why are they after me?
That's what I'm trying to find out.
I can't wait for our long talk, Whit.
It's coming, Tom.
They'll find me and kill me.
The same people who killed Armitage Shanks! I have to go! They'll find out I'm here! Please, Whit!
You need to calm down.
But you don't understand what's happening! No one does! If I stay here I'll be dead before morning! Help me, Whit! You have to help me now!
Sometimes... we have to hope that God fills in the blanks for all the things we should have said.
Yeah... but we shouldn't expect Him to. I love you, Whit.
Oh, Connie... I love you, too.
I liked Robert Mitchell

488.s: An old friend pits Aubrey Shepard against her parents and their beliefs.
q: I mean, do you have any idea how many people go through life not knowing what a wobble-wedge can do for them?
So this is Whit's End.
It's not a good sign when they put help wanted on the door. We might have to wait a while to eat.
Connie, is everything alright?
Yeah, I'm sorry, Aubrey. It's just that John Whittaker
It's like a movie where the film breaks in the middle of a scene. I guess I'll never know how it would've turned out.
I think I'd be mad at God for letting something like Plan B, Part 2: Collision Course
Sometimes I am mad at God. Then I also believe what happened is all part of something bigger than I can understand right now. And somehow, deep inside, I trust him.
You've been at school two weeks and you're already locked into your little routine. Where's your sense of adventure?
Right here! A green chili cheeseburger.

489.s: An old friend pits Aubrey Shepard against her parents and their beliefs.
q: This is your moment, Aubrey Shepard
Aubrey, this is one of the hardest things I've ever had to do. I want to be your friend. But I can't—I mean I won't keep covering for you. This is for your own good.
What's for my own good?
I talked it over with John Whittaker
What does that mean?
What I'm saying is, I'm gonna have to... fire you.
Where'd you learn to drive?
I drove a lawn tractor at the Timothy Center.

I couldn't sit there very long, so I walked around outside for a little bit. Then I thought, I wish I knew God the way you do. I wish we had a place where I can talk with him just like I can talk with you here in the kitchen.
I know a place like that. And you know what? It's not in the chapel, or in the kitchen. It's inside you.
I don't think it's anywhere near as nice as the kitchen is right now.
Well, maybe not now, but it can be. He can make it that way. But he'll only come in if you invite him.
I'd like that. I wanna invite him in.
Here I was, trying to give you a second chance—trying to be a good influence! And you were using me to cover your tracks, just like Erica Colburn
Erica is more of a friend than you'll ever be!
Oh, I'm sure she is, if you think friendship is all about using people!

490.s: Jason Whittaker's stop in Alaska reveals strange problems affecting the members of the church. Meanwhile in Odyssey, Whit notices a strange surge of anger and violence.
q: Hey, hey, what's going on here?
You're making the dishes rattle!
Alex is having a nervous breakdown!
He put nuts on my sundae!
Walter, what's going on here?
All I can conclude is that we are in the middle of a spiritual battle.
Spiritual battle, alright. Seems to be a lot of that going around lately. I was in the middle of one in South America recently and believe me, I have learned my lesson. I know exactly what to do.
What's that?
Drop to our knees right now and pray.
Okay, Sam—calm down. I'll tell you what. I'll get rid of the TV if you come with me to the doctor.
No, no. You're treating the symptoms. The disease will destroy us all!

491.s: Jason Whittaker's stop in Alaska reveals strange problems affecting the members of the church. Meanwhile in Odyssey, Whit notices a strange surge of anger and violence.
q: Hi, Jason. Where are you?
I'm in Alaska.
Oh? What are you doing up there?
Freezing. And helping out with some problems with a church up here, which is why I called.
So how is this going to work?
I'm gonna take my piece out of the Imagination Station and replace it with theirs. And then I'll see what happens.
Won't that be dangerous?
I don't have a choice, Connie. I can't send anyone else in. I have to find out what's going on. Now if you hear anything out of the ordinary, use the emergency shut-off.
What happened, Whit?
Oh, Connie, it was awful—the most horrible thing I've ever experienced! In a matter of seconds, it was as if—as if I became the worst monsters in history!

I was Cain, standing over my dead brother! I was Pharaoh, ordering the murder of innocent babies all over the country... I was Herod and Stalin and—and Hitler! I felt hate... greed... utter contempt for all human life. I became pure evil!
So... that's what the black box is doing to people?
Well, perhaps not in such a concentrated dose, but... yes, I think so.

492.s: When Mr. Charles makes demands that Kevin Colburn finds uncomfortable, his daughter, Erica, takes things into her own hands.
q: Mr. Whittaker, what's wrong?
I have to call the police!
The police?! What happened?
Bennett Charles
It was my fault this happened.
It wasn't your fault. I think we were both duped as part of a plan. But you know what, Aubrey? I'm proud of you.

Well, you didn't lie or make up excuses. You were willing to take responsibility. I don't think you would have done that a couple of weeks ago. You're on a good path now, and I can see the difference.

493.s: Monica Stone tries to steal a disk from Jason, who is in Alaska. Back at Odyssey, Whit and Agent Bourland investigate Novacom.
q: You're using sticks? Now, where are the matches?
I couldn't find any. I don't need 'em anyway. I almost got it with these sticks!
Jason, have you ever made a fire before?
Look, Paula, I'll have you know, I survived a blizzard in Tibet because of my expert fire-making skills.
Really? Tibet, huh?
...Okay, Wisconsin. But they have some harsh winters up there too.
Jason's caveman fire making skills are just a little rusty since his trip to the Himalayas.
Well, it might help you to know that this is a gas fire place.
It turns on with this switch.
I'm not wasting time. I'm building up trust.
With Jason Whittaker
So, does he trust you?
Oh, yes. He may even be in love.
I'm not a criminal, I don't like pulling guns on people! I just—I know in the end it'll all be worth it, you'll see! I'm sorry.
You're sorry? How am I supposed to believe that? Everything you did was an act.

Actually, I found myself doing less acting as I went along. I mean, the more I got to know you, the harder it became to do this. And under different circumstances, I would have enjoyed getting to know you better.
Yeah, well, they'd have to be very different circumstances.

494.s: Novacom releases the Novabox, an amazing new technology that seems to heal Tom Riley’s wife, Agnes. Meanwhile, Whit discovers who really owns his shop in Connellsville.
q: So, what's Novacom
Quite simple, really. Operation Think Tank will enslave the human race. Would you like a muffin?
Isn't that what the enemy does sometimes? Tries to use our own goodness against us?

Jason, what I'm seeing is that I'm not spending enough time seeking God's wisdom and help. Novacom has planned everything to the finest detail, but God is bigger than Novacom, than Andromeda, and whatever else they have up their sleeves.
Thanks, Novacom
494.t: Putting faith in God, not science

495.s: Connie goes to Maine to talk to Robert "Mitch" Mitchell's sister. Working hard in Odyssey, the kids investigate unusual buying trends connected to the Novabox.
q: Strange. I wonder what's going on.
And how is this going to help us with our homework?
This is no longer just homework. I think we have a mystery on our hands.
A mystery! This'll be great. I'm in the mood for a little excitement.
Okay, but no computer hacking, breaking and entering, or even slightly bending the law on this one.
It's a long story.
Maybe they've all been hypnotized! You know, like that movie.
You know the one.
No, I don’t.
Sure you do—with what’s his name, that guy, and that girl with spiky hair.
You mean the one that carries that... thing around?
Are you guys talking in code?
No! It's that movie where the whole town gets hypnotized! All I'm saying is that this is just like that.
Hold on! Listen. I think it's still running!
Well, unplug it.
I did unplug it. It's running on its own!
You can't turn it off!
You can't say a word to anyone. It's dangerous. You don't know how dangerous it is.
What's dangerous? What are you talking about?
Connie, Robert Mitchell

496.s: Connie passes the kids’ Novabox information to Mitch, while Jason discovers that Monica Stone has a personal connection to the Novacom scheme.
q: Wait a minute. I'm confused. If it worked, why aren't you using the technology now? Isn't the Novabox supposed to help the handicapped?
I did use it. The benefits don't last.
All of the benefits of the Novabox - they reverse themselves... to the extent that people are worse off than they were before. It happened to me. It will happen to everyone else.
Please listen to me: even if it's for the right reasons, you've been working for the wrong side. Everything I know about Andromeda and this box of theirs is not the answer for Duncan Mathis
Well, it's the only answer I have.
You got an instant message.
I did? How funny. I'm sure it's not from who it says it's from.
Well, it says its from... Robert Mitchell
It's not what you thin—huh? Who's Robert Mitchell
Making him a slightly less reliable source than Mr. Potato Head.
If Mr. Potato Head had information right now, I'd take it.
Uh, don't come in here!
Why? Are you losing at solitaire again?

497.s: Using Connie’s information, Mitch makes a critical connection in proving what Novacom is doing, but the situation changes when the tower on Tom Riley’s property blows up.
q: I can't escape this nagging feeling that... we haven't even seen the worst of Novacom Saga
I've got no one to blame but myself. I'm the one. I let them do it.
Let who do what?
I let Novacom build their tower on my property. I'm just sorry that they ever came to town!
Some of us are trying to put a stop to it.
Well, Whit, I tell ya... if I could, I would pull that thing down, I swear I would, with my bare hands! I swear I would!
I'm here to stop you.
I mean it, Cal! This is one of those "kids don't try this at home" moments! You're gonna get hurt!
Cal? Get off the tower! It's rigged! It's gonna blow up!
Blow up?! I'm coming! I'm coming!

498.s: Whit and Alex Jefferson work to prove Tom’s innocence, and Jason learns that Novacom’s final scheme is about to be set in motion.
q: Arthur Dent? What are you doing here?
I saved the world!
Okay, boys, let's roll up our sleeves and get to work. Jason, Mitch--care to help, or did you just come along to gloat?
Both, actually.
I wouldn’t miss this for the world!
Dent blew up the wrong tower!
John Whittaker
Yeah, the wires weren't hooked up to anything.
Good grief--but that means--
That means we haven't stopped Novacom yet. The Launch Date

499.s: Whit, Tom, and Jason race to stop Novacom's launch date, but Mr. Charles has a way to stop them.
q: 19 minutes?! It takes me longer than 19 minutes to figure out my alarm clock, John Whittaker
John Whittaker
Dad! That'll destroy the machine!
I know, son!
Exactly what did I just do?
Hmm. You... saved the world.
Oh. I can't wait for our long talk, Whit.
Oh, it looks like your friend is back.
Robert Mitchell
No, the other one... Nick Mulligan
Hey, did you get your hair cut?
No, just styled it differently.
It looks awesome!
Thanks. You look great, too.
Part of the wall is sliding back! It's another room!
What's in it?
It's the Imagination Station!
Ugh. How can Connie Kendall

500.s: Five hundred episodes of Odyssey are remembered with highlights from hundreds of Odyssey clips and never-before-heard material.
q: Parents can listen to [Adventures in Odyssey] with their children and not feel embarrassed, but feel inspired.
Use your imagination, and anything can happen!
When I do Bart, it's more metallic and it's up there! But Tom, to give him that warmth and sensitivity...
And I told him forever, forever, even in the writing, it says on the paper, right there and I read it: don't call me pop!
Eh, sorry about that, Pop!
Adventures in Odyssey is... uh... over. Bye.

501.s: Take an exclusive look inside the production studio in honor of the 15th anniversary of Adventures in Odyssey!
q: Oh, hi there! I'm John Whittaker
How come Bart Rathbone
I think that was an act of Congress, come to think of it.
I don't know about you, but I'm gonna keep listening!
Okay, too perky.
What?! ...I can un-perk it! Watch this unperkiness... Hi, this is Chris. What do you think--

502.s: A live-set celebration of 25 years of Focus on the Family and the history of Whit's End through classic Kids' Radio sketches, talks with frequent customers, and more.
q: Oh, you are so modest! It's the 25th anniversary of Whit's End!

503.s: Connie wonders if she's spending too much time with Robert Mitchell. Then he gets an offer from the FBI … to move to Virginia.
q: Connie, are you wearing a muzzle tonight? You've hardly said a peep. What do you think of chapter twelve?
I thought it was... good!
Well, that's about as insightful as a dog in a sweater.
Are you planning on working today or just fogging up the window?
I'm here to work! Sorry I'm late, Robert Mitchell
Whit, I know what you're saying, and I don't need a lecture. I'm an adult and I know how to prioritize my time.
Oh, I know you do. But I also know that God wants some of that time.
I'm sure God understands. He's met Robert Mitchell
I like how your ears turn red when you're embarrassed.
I like how you always get whipped cream on your nose when you eat a sundae.
I like how that lock of hair falls across your forehead at such an adorably perfect angle.
Oh, Connie, I love the way your kidneys work. Oh, Mitch, your toenails grow with such amazing symmetry.
I have a habit of deciding of what God wants for me and then going after it. But I don't always leave it open for God to do what he wants to do.
I think we all struggle with that.
Where's Connie? She's leading tonight, isn't she?
She's later than a penguin in a body cast.
Peter Bourland
The FBI? Do you know how dangerous they are?
Sure, they killed me, remember?
What? Robert Mitchell
I said I had an itch in my left eye. What are you talking about?
I have Robert Mitchell
Maybe I can't keep dating you. There's not much of me left.
Just shows that love hurts.
Yeah, but it's not supposed to require stitches.
The sandwiches were so thick I had to...
...use a toothpick to hold them together.

504.s: A super-Christian named Seth Young makes Aubrey Shepard feel inadequate in her new faith.
q: Yo kids, it's ministry time!
What should I do with this silly robe? Should it be wet or dry?! Thank you.
504.t: Using our abilities to serve God

505.s: Ed Washington thinks about quitting his high-paying job to work at Whit's End. His family considers the sacrifices they'll have to make.
q: I think it'd be fun for you to work at Whit's End.
Me, too. We could get free ice cream instead of free toys!
What's the deal? Is the ice cream that good?
I don't know, but you can't really go wrong when it's free!
Free?! John Whittaker
No! It was sort of my idea!
Are you sure it was a good one?
No, I'm pretty sure it wasn't! I'm gonna bankrupt the shop, and I don't even work here!
You're a dinosaur.
I'm not a dinosaur. I'm a dad!
My life is not a political statement. It's a statement about the faithfulness of God.
C'mon, tell me. Deep down. You do think I'm crazy, don't you?
Deep down? No.

That's because deep down, I know you. You need people. So do I. [...] You wanted a get your hands dirty kind of ministry. Maybe this is your chance. You get to be with people and minister, face to face.
Ok, but there's something else too.
God may have nudged me in the opposite direction today. I got promoted.
Vice President of Acquisitions. It's supervisory, I wouldn't make my trips to Whit's End anymore. But it's a 20% raise!
Tw-tw-twenty percent?
So you wanna take back what you just said?
Kind of. ... But I guess I can't, huh?
Sure you can.
No, no. I won't. Because I know no matter what, God will take care of us.

506.s: Wooton Bassett wants to help Edwin Blackgaard with an upcoming production. Liz Horton tries to find something--anything--she can do better than others.
q: I've accepted the fact that I'm not good at anything.
Hey, would it cheer you up if I showed you how I can fit a pair of tongs up my nose?
Uh, maybe some other time.
So, what are you good at?
Well, I'm glad you asked! Hand me that pair of tongs!

Typical, typical! People will waste their time watching little terrors wandering around in pink pajamas with cotton balls on their rear ends, yet they neglect to appreciate authentic drama such as performed here at the Harlequin Theatre.
Perhaps we could learn something from them.
Shakespeare, I will not prance about in pink pajamas. Not my color.
So, why are you always in a good mood? Being bad at everything makes me miserable.
Well, I, uh, I try to remember that we're all good at something. I mean, God puts talent in everybody. It's kind of His job.
The place is packed!
A full house!
Oh, wow! And my first performance! Oh, no! I think I'm getting sick! Okay, good thoughts. Lime jello. Carburetors. Fresh stick anti-perspirant. Ant farms. Sea monkeys. Cheese.
I got it now! Oh! Me pardon that repeat you could...!

You know, all this talk about tryouts reminds me of my audition for Adventures in Odyssey. It went... something like this... Well, you can go ahead and write us then, at Adventures in-- Okay, alright. That's it!

507.s: Robert Mitchell searches for a job in Odyssey, but his work at Novacom scares away potential employers.
q: Right there—the perfect job for you! I circled it.
You want me to be a flight attendant?
Steven Cabrera
He has not! He's telling the truth! He didn't know anything about what was going on with Novacom!
Oh yeah, and Kennedy didn't know anything about the plot to kill John Wilkes Booth, Jr., either!
There was absolutely nothing historically accurate about that sentence.
You're just a—
You sure you wanna finish that sentence?
Don't bother, Colby; it's not worth it.
I'm finishing the sentence!
I'd love to hear the end!
I'll tell you what you are, Rodney!! You're nothin' but a—!
You Rodney Rathbone
I know that, Alex.
A sentence fragment would have been in order.
Yeah, right. "I was so shocked! When my boss talked about mind control, I thought he said 'mime control', and he just wanted to limit the number of street performers!" Give me a break.
I dunno, Mitch. I mean, after your experience working with Novacom, aren't you just a little worried about corruption in the workplace?
Oh, no, I've done a thorough background check on myself, and I'm clean!
Aren't you worried about you snitching on yourself? Word has it, you are quite a whistle-blower!
Oh, I welcome whistle-blowing! If I start doing anything illegal behind my back I'll be the first person to tell myself, I promise!
So, the interview went well?
Oh, I dazzled myself. I'm really a sharp guy, and I should be a great addition to my company.
Well, you probably wouldn't even have a company without you!
I'm still workin' out a nickname for you.
You don't have to bother.
No, I take my job as a bully very seriously. A lot of people don't realize how much paperwork's involved. So are you here today as a customer, or as a punching bag?

508.s: In the new Imagination Station, Marvin Washington hears a rarely told story from the American Revolutionary War (1775-1783).
q: Everything all right in there?
I guess so. I haven't gotten sick yet.
Good. Uh, one thing's still the same as the Imagination Station
Push the red button?
You got it. Have fun.
Hey. Since I play drums, maybe we can get together and jam sometime.
I've done me a fair amount of pickling in my time. Although my sisters do the jamming at our house.
Oink! The troops!

509.s: In the new Imagination Station, Marvin Washington hears a rarely told story from the American Revolutionary War (1775-1783).
q: Now I got a blister on my thumb.
Since you been talkin' all night, I'm surprised you don't have a blister on your tongue.
How do you do, Captain?
Everything in order here?
Well, other than the fact that we've had no sleep and we have hardly no ammunition and we're about to be wiped off the face of the earth... I'd say we're doing might fine, sir! Mighty fine.

510.s: Talia Bassett decides to get back at her father by spending a week in Odyssey with her uncle – Wooton!
q: Hey, remember how you used to laugh when I crossed my eyes and did this? (Spit kinda noise) Or this? (Car noise) Or how about when we rubbed noses while I went erwanga erwanga, erwanga wanga wanga!!
The last time you saw me, I was three months old. So now will you please remove your nose from mine?
Talia! Breakfast is ready!
Really, Uncle Wooton, is all that racket necessary?
Yeah, it's a breakfast gong.
A souvenir from overseas?
Nope, Gongs'R'Us.
You just offered me a completely repulsive jellybean-and-corn-chip casserole, but you don't allow caffeine?
Nope! Caffeine'll kill ya. The last time I drank it I started talking so fast I almost swallowed my tongue.
Let me help you with your luggage. Then I've got a surprise for you in the car.
A surprise? Oh, I do hope it's not a pony again, sir.
Not unless ponies come in cans.
Come on, climb over this net!
Okay—net? Why is there a net in the forest?

That's Joanne Allen?!
I'm curious, Joanne. Rose hasn't met with you for forty years. Why did you come today?
Because I promised I would. I've been coming every ten years, and each time I came I hoped she'd be here. And now she is. Rose, it means so much to me to see you again.
Yes, you too, Jo.
What do you mean?
Joanne, you looked exactly like Mandy when you were ten!

It’s a little squashed.
I was practically running a marathon with it.
Yeah, and it's... it’s sweaty.
Yeah, salt adds flavor.
Well, there’s gravel in it.
I dropped it once! Or, maybe twice.
Oh, that explains the shoe print.
Maybe that's something I should do. I'm pretty health conscious.
Oh yeah, she walks all the way to the restroom instead of taking the trolley.
Hoot! Holler! Hoot! Holler!

Really good cardboard, then.

Fruits and vegetables, remember?
Oh, Connie, I had a cherry on my hot fudge sundae! FRUIT!

I'd have to get better to die.

514.s: Liz Horton is excited to see her older brother, Mark, come home, until Mark makes a surprise announcement--he's engaged.

That seems awfully strong for someone you just met, Liz.
I knew you were a jerk ever since I met you. And thanks to Mr. Whittaker I know it for sure now!
Thanks to me?
I can understand why Mark joined the army. To get away from you!
Stop! Please Stop! I didn't mean to cause a war.
I'm sorry, Mr. Whittaker, it was Liz's idea.

515.s: Alex Jefferson turns a microphone on the B-TV crew to see what happens behind the scenes.
q: Can anyone here play the piano?
Oh sure, I can do that.
Can you really?
Yeah, I play for Mrs. Randolph's horse all the time.
Well, that's the only way he'll fall asleep.
What's the topic of today's show?
Mr. Walton is now experiencing bitter irony.
Oh, be quiet.
I am now walking down the hall to the green room where the actors wait before they go into the studio. Due to budget cuts the green room doubles as the first stall in the men's room.
Look, you can either have the cameras or the light. Your pick.
Just imagine it, a man of my acting stature reduced to a foot.
Really, you're much taller than that sir.
And where, I ask you, would the world be today without bellybuttons?!?
Thank you, Mr. Bellybutton.
This is Alex Jefferson, signing off.
All right, everyone, hold it! I'm tired of this chaos! Now straighten up, for goodness' sake!

516.s: Bernard Walton accompanies Wooton Bassett to Alaska for an unusual family reunion.

I say you're expecting too much pepperoni for a pretty small pizza.
Does your Grandpa Bassett

Well, then, we'll have to take turns at the wheel.

Well, wake up the queen and alert her to trespassers!
There's two of you?
You'd think there'd be a limit.
The buffet's not working for ya?
That's not a buffet, it's dirt on crackers.
The only thing harder to find than you in this house is a light switch.
Wellington Bassett

It's not that we don't make sense, it's that we have a different way of looking at things that do make sense.
Hey, look at that! You've framed the picture I drew of Grandma.
I've always favored that piece; it's the only picture I have of your grandma wearing a cape.

517.s: Connie starts a Kids' Radio advice show with Mitch. At school, Trent DeWhite worries that he's getting credit for something he didn't do.

I wouldn't sell mine for anything.
Do you think those are real birds up there? Because I just came across one with a very suspicious-looking beak...
If you ever do get locked in a trunk, you can kick out the brake lights and wave out the back to signal vehicles behind you.
And we're back. The best way, caller, to get lipstick out of a sweater is with Vaseline.
Ooh, how do I get the Vaseline out, then?
Oh... look at that! Time for another break.

518.s: When Liz Horton’s entire family abruptly goes missing, it's up to the kids of Odyssey (and a few of their friends) to solve the case.

What was it?
A pony. I'm not sure what it means yet, but I'm working on it.
It's great to be home. Isn't God great?

On the ground?

Yellowstone?

Put Joey out there. He can catch better than me.
But Joey's my left fielder.
Then put a porpoise in right field!
Dinner should be ready in about half an hour. And I'm not sliding under the bed. Goodness knows how long it would stay here!

A mouse, I just saw a mouse run across the floor over there!!

Wow. You're all stuck in jail!

Would you let that go?! I'm not going to hit you.
That's him! That's the guy who robbed me.
He robbed you?
Oh, it's not going to happen for another three years.
You want me to break into their house and take their TV?
No, I want you to break into their house and water their plants for them!

You want us to bless the baseballs?

Moose. The big guy. Right there in the backfield.
That's a human?!?!
And be careful. He clips; that's how Frank got his leg broke.
Do you know where you'd go?
If my pet died? Probably to the toilet to flush him.
But... wouldn't you want to make sure you both end up in a... happy place?
You callin' the toilet a happy place? That's just flat-out sick, Aubrey.

How about silent cop?
Remember, come for a car, leave with a friend!!

That they serve waffles?

You're just a bunch of ladies who want me to stay out of the rain so you won't feel guilty.
Who you callin' a lady?

You knew this was never gonna be a normal life.
Yeah, but...but somehow, I pictured it in my head as...abnormally normal—like, you'd go off and save the world during the day and then you'd come home at 5:00 for dinner.

But it's not really gonna be like that; I mean, the reality of it all is that you're in a job where you'll travel and move around a lot and—and people will want to put bags over your head and kidnap you for real. And more than that...you love it.
Yeah, you—you're right. And you're the one that pointed that out to me. You said I'm passionate about fighting for good and living in adventure.

And you need to be doing those things; I know that. But...I don't want to be the afterthought, the one you come home to occasionally. And I know that even when you're with me, your heart will still be on the field.
Bye, Connie. Take care.

Robert Mitchell
