So why might you be depressed?

Well, I just finished the latest issue of Powerboy and it was the one where he finally faced the three-eyed fish monster but it ended with him strapped in Dr. Ichobodia's torture chair and his power suit was disabled and he had no way to contact headquarters. I don't know how he'll ever get out of it.
So that's why you're depressed?
Oh my brain hurts just thinking about it.
Ey, this here's where John Whittaker

552.s: The Washingtons try to get to church on time, which leads to chaos in their home.
q: Innovative, but you're a little wrinkled.
So is Grandma, and no one makes her change for church!
I’m gonna lose the sticker contest!
I have a big hole on my head and I’m wearing dirty clothes!
What are you doing here?
Doris Rathbone
Oh. Engine parts in the dishwasher again?
No. Cheese Doodles in the shower.
What's in it for me [if I come to church]?
You get to sing songs.
You do any Willie Nelson?
Bart Rathbone
Don't you remember the snowflakes?!
Do you have your verse memorized?
Uh, yeah! Uh, "I pledge allegiance to the flag..."
Your verse, Marvin!
Maybe we could all shave our heads. That'll show unity!
We're not that unified.
Nice shirt, Bart. I have one just like it.
Yeah, yeah I know! It's yours.

553.s: When Trent is put in the gifted class at school, he wonders if he'll survive his first week. Meanwhile, Aubrey Shepard learns that she has a real talent with horses.
q: Trent, name the first man-made object to touch the moon.
The first man-made object? Uh... Neil Armstrong's shoe?
I could train you and you're a fast learner. I should talk to your parents about this and see what they think.
Thanks, Mr. Riley, but I don't need any more opportunities to look ridiculous. I appreciate it, though. I'll see you tomorrow!
We're not through talking about this! Not by a long shot.

Mustard is what's called a "condiment." You find mustard in supermarkets in the mustard aisle, and sometimes you find it on hamburgers. Mustard is yellow, except when it's brown. Here, I have a bottle of each!
Look! The pizza's almost gone. And if that goes, the only option is that mystery casserole the lunch lady cooked up.
This isn't the time to complain about trivial matters! I need to think of a way to get out of the gifted class!
How about you stop using phrases like "trivial matters?"

554.s: Connie’s cell phone is getting unusual messages from someone named Cindy who is desperate to reach “William.”
q: How do we figure out who she is? Do-do you have something to write on; I could make a sign and-and write her name on it...
Cindy!!! Cindy Bancroft!!! Paging Cindy Bancroft!!!
Or we could do that, yeah.
Do you think she heard me?
She probably heard you if she's leaving from the bus station in Connellsville.

555.s: Liz Horton tries to persuade Irving and Solly, two men from Odyssey Retirement Home, to come out of retirement to perform a magic act.
q: The early bird gets the worm...
... but it's the second mouse that gets the cheese!
Mr. Mendelson, I just bought a new hearing aid! It cost me $4,000, but it's the latest technology!
Really? What kind is it?

556.s: Tamika Washington takes her Sunday school lesson on honesty very seriously. At J & J Antiques, Jack Allen struggles to tell his new employee a difficult truth.
q: We're glad you're so excited. We're happy to have you.
Excited nothing. PJ now stands for "perfectly joyful."
Neato. This'll be like working where they hid the ark of the covenant.
I doubt you'll find that in here.
Then again, you never know with this place. Think you can handle it, PJ?
Are you kidding? From this point on PJ stands for "professional and judicious."
Can you say "wicked awesome cool," Mr. Allen?
I'm afraid I might sprain something. But that's great, PJ.
By the way, how did PJ Manning
You didn't see any of his work yet?
I'm afraid not. Though he did stop in to say that PJ now stood for Peanut Butter and Jelly or something like that.
We need to talk about the work you've done with the antiques. I'm glad you've been enjoying what you're doing...
Enjoying it? Are you kidding? PJ now stands for "pizza and joviality." I can hardly get to sleep at night I'm having so much fun.
Hello, Mr. Allen. I'm filling out my time cards. PJ stands for "prompt and just as diligent," after all.
You could fit my whole family in that bathtub!
You have a big family?
Nah. I'm an only child. But I have a split personality.

557.s: The Odyssey crew is involved in six interwoven stories about Christmas. It all begins when Tamika gives away her toy lamb for Christmas . . .
q: You have to grow up sometime.
We haven't sorted through this [stuff in the attic] in like--ten years!
I'm an adult, Liz Horton
Long way to go for a lamb.
In fact he gave his life for mine.
They wanted a funny injury.
Mike Mulligan

558.s: Trent finally gets the chance to audition for the Chamber Music Society, but things keep getting in the way, despite his prayers to God.
q: What happened?
Rodney Rathbone
Hey, are you going to eat those mashed potatoes?
No, you can have them.
Ready... aim...
No! I can't allow you to launch my mashed potatoes!
Now you've heard it on the T and V. You've seen it on the radio.
You look kind of like Powerboy did after he got locked in the Tweezers of Doom.
Sure. Except you still have your eyebrows.
What is that on the floor?!!

559.s: Wooton shoots a documentary about Marvin's new band, “The Cool Dogs.”
q: Marvin, we've been practicing for over five hours today. My string fingers have blisters on top of calluses, and we don't seem to be getting any better. I don't care about the "invisible groove of the soul"; I would be satisfied with anything remotely resembling music!
...I think what's going on here is called the "tension of harmony".
You made that one up, too!
Wooton, why are you filming up my nostrils?
Use the zoom, Wooton!
I'm the skeleton. Without the skeleton, your body would just...lie on the ground in a big mess.

This means we're going to be humiliated beyond repair! This means that I'm going to have to wear a paper bag over my head at school for the next seven years! And my children will have to change their names! And my children's children! And my children's children's pets!

Well, by the time the generator was fixed, everybody had kind of moved away from the gazebo. I guess their ears hurt or something. And so we ended up playing our last set for Aubrey and her grandfather. He seemed to like it.
Yeah, uh, he had his hearing aid turned down.
Do you hear that awful noise out there?
Oh, that only sounds awful; it's, ah...alternatively gonna sweep the nation!
Are you serious?
Uh, as serious as I am when I say that Marvin is gonna see this tape?
Fine, Marvin—you can just humiliate yourself all alone next weekend! I quit!
You can't quit!
He'll be back. Oh, you're back!
I forgot my cello.

560.s: Max Hampton demands that Trent DeWhite give up the key to the science lab… or else.
q: Whoa! That... was incredible! When you flexed your muscles, I felt a breeze!
Of course you did this. That's because I'm so massively perfect. In my movies I need a whole stunt man just to play my left arm!
You got the key?
Uh, no. Hey, what did the chewing gum say to the shoe?
I'm stuck on you. You've only got till tomorrow, you remember that, right?
Uh, I remember. Uh, what bird steals from the rich and...
You know that one too, huh?
Even Mr. Arnold has his limitations, Trent! Besides, I was thinking about getting out of the training and trying something different anyway.
You mean like politics?
What? I may be musclebound, but I'm not crazy. Ha!
Grandpa was in Odyssey too?

Of course he was! In a way, this is how it all began for your grandfather and I. We wouldn't marry for many years to come, but it was that valentine, and the kindness behind it, that started our friendship.
Well, I said I didn't know who the special valentine came from, but I was at school early that morning and I did see who delivered it...
Oh! Hi, Mandy! Yeah, um...
Where are you going with that heart?
Uh, nowhere.
That's right. The valentine was delivered by your grandpa, Grandpa Trent DeWhite
A box of sulfur! Looks like a brand new shipment. But why would he want sulfur? You can't wear it, you can't eat it—although Mrs. Colimbo's cooking does have a tendency...

561.s: Liz Horton wants to expose the Young Miss Odyssey beauty pageant as a sham. One problem: She must enter the contest to bring it down.
q: I see my face reflecting in the window as the rain falls. How many times have I seen that face staring in the glass? How many times have I wished that face was not my own? The rain fades softly away. A shaft of sun pierces the brooding clouds like a sword. And a thought pierces me as well. There is one who knows me deeper than the others. He knows how I cry inside while I put on a smile for the others. He knows how I remember mocking words and deeds. He knows how I dream of countries and castles far away. He calls me by name and smiles at me. He reaches out his hand for mine. He knows me. Because he made me. And now shows me life beyond the window.

Okay, how's this for my opening line? "March 1st, 10:32 AM. A teeming mass of humanity waits in anguish for a glimmer of hope—a hope that will soon be dashed to smithereens upon the rocks of deception!"
Sounds like the sinking of the Titanic.
She's freaking out about a stain on her dress. Can you believe that?
Actually, it sounds kind of familiar.
What's that supposed to mean?
A zit, a stain on your dress, I don't see much difference. But at least she really wanted to win from the beginning. You...you've changed.
What d'you mean?
What happened to taking a stand against the country's obsession with beautiful people? It just... it doesn't seem like you're taking a stand against anything. It seems like you're joining the team.

562.s: Kids' Radio tells the story about a priest who defies a third-century Roman emperor who outlaws marriage.
q: Do you, Paulina, take Titus (a)

563.s: Every Tuesday, Wooton Bassett meets with a mysterious kid who seems to be hiding something.
q: If you find them, tell them I'll make a German chocolate cake and bring it over. You know, it's Kristi McKay

Some of my best memories are from being a Boy Scout and doing all those fun "-ing" things—boating, camping, rafting, hiking, falling, hurting, bleeding, and yelling for help. It was the most fun I've ever had!
Hey, did you see that grape juice is on sale? It's supposed to improve your memory.
Yeah, you know, I think I've heard that somewhere before.
Yeah, well, see, if you drank your grape juice you'd remember exactly where!
So Grady McKay
Yes. And I'm pretty sure that's a w:Mail and wire fraud
I'm expecting something in the mail, and I've got to get it before someone else does!
Funny. I thought report cards didn't come out until next Monday.
How'd you rip your pants?
Oh, you know, just living by the mailman motto.
The one about rain, sleet, and snow?
No, no, the other one: Another day, another dog bite.

564.s: Whit is doing secret experiments in the Imagination Station. Is that why a government agent is watching Whit's End? Connie, Bernard Walton, and Tom Riley take action to find out what’s going on.
q: Mental health? Well then you must be watching Connie Kendall
What if John Whittaker
Oh, now, that's a good rationalization. I'd stick with that, if I were you.
What took you so long? Don't tell me you showered before you came.
Well, you don't expect me to come out in public with bed hair, did you?
Oh, poor Bernard.
Sounds like John Whittaker
Yeah, or you've got some very large mice.
Have you thought about what we're going to do if it isn't Whit?
You can protect me with the hooks in your fishing hat.
Go ahead, Connie. And if he disowns you, I'll still be your friend.
Are you doin' experiments on someone else, Whit?
It's that man from the NIH, isn't it? You two had a tussle and you've thrown him into the machine!
Oh, Bernard, you're being ridiculous.
No, no, no, I was being ridiculous when I agreed to this idea twelve hours ago. Now I'm being absurd!
Nocturnal felicitations.
It can't be! I don't believe it!
Stuff me with spinach and call me a soufflé.
It's Eugene Meltsner

565.s: Whit has to break the news to Connie, Bernard, and Tom about Eugene’s memory loss … and his risky plan to fix it.
q: Y'see, Maude Walton
No, Bernard, it was to convert brain waves to radio waves.

Leave it to me, Connie; you'll only confuse her. Anyway, Eugene was doing this top-secret project but what he didn't know was that the whole thing was a sneaky trick by an evil company to do mind control on—no, no, not mime control, Maude, mind control. Right, like Aunt Gertrude. Anyway, when Eugene figured out what was going on, he left Odyssey with the research and Katrina, and they got married and traveled around the world until they thought they were safe, and after that they went to Wisconsin.
Washington, D.C.
Right, Washington D.C., to the National Help Institute—
National Institute of Health.
Exactly. And that's where Eugene started back with his top-secret research to convert the—the watchacall—with the... jahoozey.
I was giving the information on a must-know basis.
Just like a man.
They say a blow to the head sometimes helps.
I have a shovel in my truck!
You look great, Mrs. Meltsner!
Thank you! You haven't changed.
I don't change. You should know that by now!

I made the foolish assumption that I would not miss what I could not remember, but it is now apparent that I'm missing out on so much! Knowing you as I once did—it's a terrible ache, a desperate longing! I really must succeed in restoring my memory, Mr. Whittaker!
We're doing our best, Eugene.
In essence, we're going to convert Eugene Meltsner
Wait a minute, Doctor. That's Eugene's technology.
Wait, wait. You mean it's the same technology that messed up Eugene's memory in the first place?

566.s: Eugene’s closest friends take drastic steps to bring him to a full recovery.
q: I was wondering—is it possible to select which memories he gets back? Can we leave some out?
Leave some out? Why would you want to do that?
Because some are rather bad... the kind I wish he wouldn't ever have to remember. The death of Armitage Shanks

Katrina... you know, even if I could, would you really want me to? God uses our memories, both good and bad, to shape who we are and who we'll become. To get rid of those parts of our life that cause us pain would rob God of one of the ways He works in our lives and hearts. Do you really want Eugene to be less than who he should be?
Of course not. But I love him and if I could spare him the pain of reliving certain memories, I would.
I'll do anything for Eugene, you know that. But I think you're goin' about this the wrong way.

Oh, come on, Whit. You're talking about relationship, about heart, and I'm wonderin'... what happened to praying? What happened to Eugene's relationship with God? How does He fit into all this technical mumbo jumbo?
I'm not leaving Him out, Tom. I'm praying about everything we're doing. But we have to do something. Why is it wrong to try?

Well, it's not wrong, I just don't agree with it. Now, if you want to manufacture a relationship through that machine of yours, that's up to you. But I think Eugene needs real relationships—with God, with us. And a lot of time, patience and prayer.
Hold on, Whit, don't stop it yet. This is the best fight I've seen since my Aunt Bertha threw away my Uncle Ted's golfing pants.
Excuse me, Mr. Whittaker?
Yes, that's me.
Mrs. Meltsner wanted you to know that her husband seems to be waking up.
Wonderful, wonderful. Is he alright?
It's hard to say. I had difficult time understanding him.
Sounds like he's alright to me!

567.s: Eugene panics when he accidentally damages Bernard’s prized truck.
q: You really have SIX separate boxes for vests?
They are sorted!
By what? Color, texture...
Occasion! One must wear a vest to fit the event!!! A sub-par vest simply wouldn't do at a formal event!!!
It's not that bad, Eugene.
Precisely what they told General Custer on the ride to Little Bighorn. It's bad enough! It hit a tree, a taillight's broken! How could this have happened? I'm sure I set the parking brake!
"Oh boy," Mr. Whittaker? There's sub-text in that phrase, I'm certain of it!
Well, the parking brake doesn't work. That's one of the quirks. You have to leave it in gear to keep it from rolling.
What am I gonna do?!
Wear your groveling vest! It'll be perfect for the occasion.
Should I have spoken in words Eugene Meltsner
The truck rolled down the hill because of the broken parking brake. You forgot to tell him about that, ah, aspect of its personality.
Oh, now, that's great, thanks, Whit. I'll let my doctor know you're doing your part to lower my blood pressure.
You're gonna have to tell Eugene Meltsner
Yeah, I know, I know. I'll tell him. I'd better get going. I've got places to go and windows to wash.
Okay, I'll see you, Bernard.
See ya, Whit. Sure, I'll tell Eugene. Maybe when I'm on my death bed.
Don't start with that again! Eugene Meltsner
The front of Eugene Meltsner
Are you in earnest?
No, I'm in a parking lot!

568.s: Kids' Radio presents a boxing match between David and Goliath, testimonials from users of an amazing treatment called the Pray Way, and Edwin Blackgaard’s rhyming tale of Samson.
q: Oh great, all I have is a jaw from a donkey. Wait, I can use this to... bonk ye!

569.s: Eugene teaches at Odyssey Middle School as a substitute. Meanwhile, Lester shows everyone his new pet – an invisible dog.
q: Greetings, fellow scholars and intellectual adventurers!
Due to Miss Grapple
I have this awful feeling in the cavity of my gastrointestinal region.
Uh, you mean the pit of your stomach?
Precisely—it's the feeling that I let my students down. And the worst part is, I'm not exactly sure what I did wrong!
I've never buried an invisible dog before.
Shh, the service is about to start.

Dear friends, we're gathered here to bury a faithful dog named Ralph. And although we didn't see much of Ralph, we're really here to support a special friend of ours named Lester. Lester, you've shown us all something about compassion. When God gives us compassion for someone we start to see things through their eyes. So Lester, thank you. Thank you for helping us see Ralph.

570.s: Eugene and Katrina finally plan to have a proper wedding. But the two wedding coordinators (Connie and Millie Shanks) engage in an epic battle of decision making.
q: Ah, there. Vest, suit, cufflinks, tie.
Let's change out of these tuxes before we die!
Did you book them?
Of course I did! It was my one and only job; I took it very seriously! Tom Riley
Where's the root beer? Everybody knows you're supposed to have root beer at a bachelor party!
Technically, I'm not actually a bachelor anymore.
Yeah, well, technically my great-grandmother's wake was livelier than this party!
Well, I suppose the gift would be... me?
You call that a gift? You see, this is why we register.
Well, we're writing our own vows; that's commensurately romantic, is it not?
Depends. Did your vows include the word "commensurately"?
Number two: Katrina Meltsner
Now, that was only due to the recurrence of an old chess club injury!
A chess club injury?
It was a very big club.
Now, you can be sensitive and caring all you want, but there comes a time when every woman wants to be rescued by a knight in shining armor.
But Katrina Meltsner
Doves? What in the world do you need doves for? We already know the Ark is on dry land!
At my wedding, they just threw rice!
Symbolizing an abundance of teriyaki chicken!
A sixteen piece orchestra?
That's a lot of pieces, isn't it? Do they even make that many instruments?
I don't think so.
Let's see, now, what am I gonna need? Tuba, drums, fiddle, electric banjo...even a bigger banjo?
Oh... Bernard, we're in trouble.
It's a Shanks wedding. It never rains on a Shanks wedding!
Uh... no, it's a Meltsner wedding! And trust me, it would rain on a Meltsner wedding.

571.s: Eugene and Katrina finally plan to have a proper wedding. But the two wedding coordinators (Connie and Millie Shanks) engage in an epic battle of decision making.
q: It's just a small fire! Nice to roast marshmallows by, really...
The flowers? Why, you could stock a dozen greenhouses with that many flowers!
And a few cemeteries!
Eugene, that next branch doesn't look very strong.
I could never break this branch. You heard what the doctor said about my weight; I practically disappear when I turn sideways!
Yes, but be careful!
Whose idea was it to do a soundcheck in the middle of an electrical storm, anyway?
Does it really matter who came up with the idea? Just to know that he's gonna be okay is enough for me!
Whose crazy idea was it to have a wedding for them anyway?! They're already married, for crying out loud!
I won't say, but her name starts with a C and sounds a little like Klonnie.
Eugene Meltsner
There's another Agnes Riley
Do you think they had stand-ins for us? Your mother and Connie Kendall
She's wearing my mother's dress—the one she wanted me to wear! Eugene... we missed our own wedding!

572.s: When America Sings! comes to Odyssey, many hopeful singers line up to audition.
q: February is my seventh favorite month!
Were you singing, or were you trying to hail a cab in rhinoceros language?!
Iiiiincredible! My ears haven't hurt this bad since I got my head stuck in the elevator door!
Why did you have to pick a judge who was so quick to quack?
I admit, I'm a quick quacker.
Can we move on now? I have a root canal I'd like to get to.
Electric Palace doo-dah song a-doo-dah...
And the name of our next town is...
Our next contestant is Harlow Doyle.
My card, my card, here's a twenty, heh, heh ran out of cards.
Rathbone! What are you doing?!
How did you know it was me? Ahem, ahah, AHEM, AHAH! How did you know it was me?
Your fake goatee fell off!
What about you? Did you like it?
Your intonation was really nice. Perhaps, though the song could have featured more references to love or longing or something that's not a household appliance.
So was I bad enough to get on the T'n'V?
If it was up to me, I'd put you on twice!

573.s: Finding a job becomes Eugene’s goal after learning he’s not needed at Campbell College. Wooton Bassett tries to help Grady McKay deal with changes at home when his mom starts a new job.
q: Wow, Grady McKay
Oh, I don't think you know what normal is. I am going to start camping out in the backyard if that toaster reprimands me one more time.
Now actually Katrina, the toaster has been quite polite.
I think I have been quite polite! Do you hear what that coffeemaker is saying to me?!
Wow. A Grady McKay

574.s: Eugene and Katrina Meltsner take a trip to visit a remote African tribe that believes its village is under a curse.
q: Journal entry; My trip to Africa changed my life forever.
Nothing to it. Just clear the plane and pull on this...cord. Hang on; that one's busted. You woulda dropped like a rock.
Oh yes, how unfortunate that would have been.
You know, this journal seems awfully familiar. Do you know his original name?
Yes. Leonard Meltsner
What did you say?
Leonard? That's my father's name!
Aman, Leonard Meltsner

575.s: The plot thickens as Eugene and Katrina find themselves caught in the struggle between two African tribes. But everything takes a sudden turn when Eugene discovers more about a connection to his own past.
q: I've gotta tell Katrina! If I dare say the words, my parents may still be alive!
I will give you supplies.
But you won't need them. You're journey will end at the river. And so will your lives.
You don't believe in hunches Eugene! If it's not provable by hard numbers you're not persuaded.
True. But if I've learned anything between the realm of science and belief. It's that sometimes you must walk by faith and not by sight. Something deep inside me tells me we should go upstream.
I'm right behind you.
I'm fine. Although I must admit, I would ask for a break if I wasn't worried about snakes attacking me.
Well if you see anything threatening, remember Aman gave me a knife.
I'm sorry for this. But I'm really having a difficult time imagining you using that knife on anything that wasn't served on a plate in a climate controlled restaurant.
So much for the curse.
Yes, it appears we've beaten it.
Come. You'll be my prisoners, and the leaders of my tribe will deal with you as they please.

576.s: Eugene and Katrina's African adventure comes to a thrilling climax. Eugene discovers more about his parents and their connection to this isolated village. But the couple realizes that their true purpose on this mission is overcoming the lies that imprison their new friends in Africa.
q: That's the difference between our Gods Yosef. Mine is a God of hope and freedom. And my God could find a thimble in the middle of an African jungle. Finding a man is mere child's play.
If your God is as determined as you are, I'm sure He could. But if He's that strong, He can also bring your father to you.
Father there is no water.
You're right. It should have come by now. What happened?
There's only one God. You should trust him with you life and the lives of your village.

577.s: The Washingtons can’t find time for family devotions, and Eugene’s new service organization has him running in circles!
q: ...Oh, and Doris Rathbone wants a pedicure.
Hey, Eugene Meltsner
If I were a father, I'd have to equip my children with homing devices!

578.s: When Coach Tom Riley doesn’t choose Ashley Jenkins for the local All-Star softball game, her father, former Mayor Jenkins, files a lawsuit.
q: I'm still wondering why Tamika Washington
Eugene, they don't allow calculators in the batter's box.
But you're not a lawyer!
Well, heh heh, not in the "professional" sense, of course but... but I took a civil law class during my time at college, and since then, I've continued to study law books for light bedtime reading.
Hire a lawyer or hire Eugene Meltsner
Oh yes, Eugene Meltsner
Well, I'm sure that's true, but I feel like I just let a pyromaniac borrow my lighter.
This is Eugene Meltsner we're talking about... he's about as intimidating as an unsalted cracker!
Wait! Don't you want me to tell you about subsection D?
I'll talk to you later.
But it has pie charts!

579.s: Aubrey Shepard prepares to leave home for college, but her little sister, Bethany, doesn’t want her to go.
q: Get on the horse.
Uh, Dad, I feel a little silly.
It's okay; there aren't any hidden cameras.
You're worried about me?
Bethany! What are you doing here?!
How bad was it?
Hmm. I'm grounded 'til I can vote.

580.s: Everyone at Whit's End is in an uproar when a former Bones of Rath gang member writes a scathing book about Odyssey.
q: I like my pants. They're comfortable. Is there something wrong with them?
I'm the Mozart of chewing people out.
Wow. I've decided to be an astronaut... or, a Eugene Meltsner
That was unbelievable!
How does it feel to have saved possibly hundreds of lives?
Great. Just great.
We don’t have the hard information to justify the use of tax money for the space program when it could be used to end poverty in America as we know it!

It’s simple, Miss Horton. Less than 1% is spent on space while over 30% is spent on government welfare programs for the poor. Even if you eliminated the space program altogether, the poor would only receive 3 cents on the dollar per person of that money. This is hardly going to end poverty as we know it. And, economically speaking, the underwriting of the space program is a long-term answer instead of a short-term fix. Now if you’ll excuse me, I’ve got urinals to scrub!
Eugene Meltsner
Mandy Straussberg
That's my Liz.

581.s: Eugene, Tom, Connie, and Whit get confused over who's giving which Christmas present to whom.
q: Connie Kendall
Someone even threw a doughnut at me, cream-filled!
Have you had a mechanic examine it? I mean, not the doughnut, but the vehicle?
But I got you a cheese basket, and it was on clearance.
I was wondering why this Swiss was so crunchy!
If I didn't have my alarm clock, I'd be late every day.
You are late every day!
Miss Kendall...

I'm speechless! This is the last thing I was expecting from you, it does humble me a bit as I merely purchased a scarf for you, which was certainly bought from the heart but, not nearly as elaborate as this generous gift for which I don't know how to thank you.
For bein' speechless, a lot of words sure came out!
Well, luckily, rush hour in Odyssey consists of a truck, a bike, and a dog with a limp!
Excuse me, but I am not late every day, Eugene.
You were late today, Connie.
My car stalled.
And yesterday?
My curling iron caught on fire.
Mm-hmm, and, uh, the day before?
My conditioner wouldn’t rinse!
And the day before that?
You are never gonna believe what happened this morning.
You confused your hairspray with your antiperspirant spray.
Like I'd make that mistake twice!

582.s: At home alone on Christmas Eve, Whit remembers holidays past that were difficult--but still made for treasured family memories.
q: It [the bird alarm clock] sounds like a dying moose!
I guess instead of a "choo-choo," we'll have to call it an "ooch-ooch."
Ah... Maude just did a belly flop in the pool. Woman needs to act her age.

583.s: Connie narrates the story of her last year at summer camp and how she got stuck in the midst of the annual prank war at Camp Jumonville.

You mean... you wrote this. You wrote "Jesus Loves Me?"
Well, I haven't really titled it...
Do you know how many people will hear this song?
What do you mean?
Kids in churches all over the world will sing it and everyone will know it!
Wow. That song had that big of an impact on you?
The love of God had that big of an impact on me. But that song made me realize it.

626.s: As her parents seem headed for divorce, Mandy Straussberg faces the future with a grim determination. Meanwhile, her father works on making his move to Chicago permanent.
q: We're going to look at houses, not candidates for your next date!
One never knows.
David. Seriously, why are you stalling?
Seriously, Dad, why would I stall? It's just you and me in Chicago, looking for a new place to live. Why would that be a problem?
Though I should ask: how do you feel about trailer parks?
...I'm waiting in the car.

627.s: As her parents seem headed for divorce, Mandy Straussberg faces the future with a grim determination. Meanwhile, her father works on making his move to Chicago permanent.
q: Don’t! Your laugh makes my leg hurt.
Well, I’ve never heard that before.
I can't tell you what to do about your marriage or how to make it work, but from son to father... yeah, I think you're wrong.

Why? Where do I begin? Because for my entire life, you and Mom have been my model for what a good marriage is supposed to be, flaws and all. And now... I'm trying to figure out where our faith fits into all of this. All that stuff in the Bible about sacrifice... your vows, that's another thing. Who cancels the vows you made in church all those years ago? Those were vows to God, right?
So, ah, where's the slacker?
Shhh! She might be asleep! It took some effort, but we got her up to bed.
Okay. I'll be quiet. Okay, wake up you little faker! I'll bet it wasn't even a car! You got knocked down by a kid on a tricycle! I WANT THE TRUTH!

628.s: Grady’s father, Carson McKay, returns to Odyssey after a long absence. The whole family must decide whether or not to trust him.
q: Surprised to see me?
With both your arms intact, yeah.
They're gonna have a bouncy house—with no age or weight restrictions! Woo-hoo!
He says he hasn't gambled in six months.

So he says. But you don't know your father. If it isn't gambling, it'll be something else. And he's always sorry for what he's done, over and over...after a while, you don't want to hear how sorry he is.
Grady! There are dirty dishes in the closet!
Closets aren't for dirty dishes either? What good are they?
I'm gonna be a hard sell. You know that, don't you?
Sure, sure. I-I do. But—but I'm not trying to sell you anything. I just want to make things right.
We'll see about that. ...Thanks for fixing my car.
And for you, ma'am?
Uh, a Maxi Deluxe cheeseburger with extra cheese, and cheesy fries, and a milk, please!
Why don't they just bring out the whole cow, Sam?
You know what? That sounds good! Bring me a cow, too!
I've become a verb here in Odyssey.
Yeah, if a kid is being silly, his parents tell them to quit 'Wooton' around!

629.s: Grady’s father, Carson McKay, returns to Odyssey after a long absence. The whole family must decide whether or not to trust him.
q: How far away from here can I get on a hundred bucks?
No one has ever beaten my record of thirty-one slides in fifteen minutes!
Of course, nobody else has sprayed cooking oil on their pants either.
Oh sure, go right ahead. Just be careful in the rec room. I'm not sure if the oatmeal's congealed yet.
I'd rather be like you.
Oh...an out-of-shape mailman who decorates with leftover garage sale items?
Okay, so how do we do this? What do we need? Water? Do I have to shave my head or something?
Oh, well, I mean... you can if you want, but it's not required, and praying won't give you razor burn.
You know, this is really cool, Grady; and here I thought finally getting a ten-pronged fork in the mail was gonna be the highlight of my day!
So... this is better, huh?
Yeah. This is the best, Grady.
I can't expect them to forgive me over and over. It's not fair to them!
No, no, it's not fair, but neither is abandoning them.
It's the lesser of two evils.

Now you're making excuses. Your mistakes don't let you off the hook from your responsibility as a father. The problem is that you think you can fix your mistakes on your own, and you can't, Carson. God is the only one who can fix what's wrong with you.
My family's never gonna take me back!
Give them a chance! This is your family, Carson. Do what's right.

You know what? I take that back. People do change. I've seen you do it. You used to be such a handful every day, rebellious and angry...and look at you. You've turned into this sweet little man. I wish your dad could do whatever you've been doing.
I was just listening to people like Mr. Whittaker and Wooton. They told me about God.
God? You mean you think going to church has changed you?
Yeah, sort of. I guess it helped to start some changes.
You'll forgive my saying so, Mr. Whittaker, but God's never shown much interest in what I'm going through. He doesn't know me.
On the contrary: the problem is that you don't know Him.

630.s: Connie must face her bitterness against Kelly. Meanwhile, Kelly learns about the importance of rules.
q: Eww, is it bad?
Well, it could use an air freshener or twelve.
Hey, um, Connie?
Yes, Kristyn?
What are you doing in the dumpster?
I'm thinking of building a summer home in here! What do you think?
What if you'd gotten hurt, or—I don't know, mugged?
We live on Sesame Street. Who is gonna mug me?

631.s: Connie narrates a documentary about the people and places in Odyssey against the backdrop of a search for a missing time capsule.
q: Odyssey – an idyllic, small Midwestern town.
Odyssey – a town that evokes days gone by; an America of the 1940’s or 1950’s.
Odyssey – where anyone would want to live.
You buried that canister of garbage beneath the pavement?
Oh... well, technically it's not garbage, it's just a collection of lunch bags, sandwich wrappers, soda cans, and uh... well, yeah; it's garbage.

On the east of Main Street, just bordering the vast expanse of McAlister Park, you’ll find a Victorian style ice cream parlor called Whit’s End – a play on words that reflects owner John Avery Whittaker’s background as an English teacher.
What do you think of the accusation that Odyssey is stuck in the past?

Stuck in the past? I don’t think we’re stuck there. But you know, there’s nothing wrong with trying to preserve the richness and beauty of what’s come before us. It’s a recurrent theme in the Bible for example, God constantly reminds the nation of Israel to remember. Not for the old time’s sake or nostalgia but because of what the past means to us today.
It would seem that in Odyssey at least; all roads lead to Whit’s End.

Odyssey is a town – like any town – that recognizes the value of the past, as that past teaches us and helps make today’s experiences that much richer. And whether it’s in a time capsule, or a talking gallery, or an ice cream sundae at an old fashioned parlor; the day-to-day moments we all experience wherever we live will soon be gone. Cherish them now – in the time capsule you carry with you always: your heart.

632.s: An editor from Home and Country Magazine announces that Odyssey is a contender for Best Small Town in America.
q: I'm here to give you some very important news, and I thought that you should be the first to know, Miss Kendall!
Me? That's never happened before.
Odyssey could be the best small town in America!

Howdy! Tom Riley here. We’re just gettin' ready for a time of wonder, adventure, and excitement. Would you like to join us? Than get ready, 'cause you never know what can happen when you have an Adventure in Odyssey! —Walker Edmiston's last episode.
How are yous today?
Lot o' weather we been havin' lately.
Yeah, I suppose so.
Hey, uh speakin' o' dat, are you the inspector?
Yeah with the purchase of dat dere stereo, we got a hotline you can call to ask us any questions, any time, I’m always available. Ooh, the inspector guy just come in!
Hey where’re you going? I got a question!
Can't help ya!
Just a token of my depreciation.
So, what did you think of Odyssey, Jill?
It meets all our qualifications. Rusty Gordon's book is just tabloid garbage. What he calls a laughable little town is actually a very charming, friendly place with lovely people!
Eugene, Eugene, do you know how many gutters I've fixed in my life?
Hey Blackgaard
Can I get a glass of water here?
No there's a hose out back, don't put you mouth on it.

Inspector, right! I inspect buildings for health and safety! I've been checking all the buildings in Odyssey! And I don't mind saying that you've got a death trap for a store, Mr. Rathbone! Missing support beams, corrosive rust...
Wait just a minute here!
Well, inspector or not, there's still no excuse for sleeping through my performance!
On a couch placed in a position that clearly impedes easy access to the fire escapes! And I have a few other notes about the condition of the stage—the light rigging, the wiring... shall I go on?
Oh... no need. I should have expected this from a fan of the Three Stooges.

633.s: For a historical exhibit, the Washington family must live as people on the frontier did.
q: Picnics in the rain are fun.
No... they’re not. They’re just... wet.
Don’t you see what you're doing? You’re mocking history! And you're mocking everyone who walks through that door when you do!
Can’t we just kill a bear, or at least go to the store for berries?
Ed, tell me about the Black Hawk War.
It was... awful... lots of fighting.
It hasn’t happened yet!
Keep studying.
I think I've got the scurvy!
I think history deserves to be treated well.
What do you mean?

This is how people lived their lives! They worked, they suffered, they made a home for themselves! They made a country for us! We’ve forgotten that. People nowadays, they — they know instant cash machines, and video games, and television, and eight-hour workdays! I respect history, and the people who made it.
[Pizza] delivery wasn’t as good as it is today. The nearest pizza place was like, two thousand miles away! They had a deal where, if you didn’t get your pizza in three days, it was free!

634.s: When Jason Whittaker is revealed publicly as an intelligence agent, an old nemesis named The Whisperer tracks him to Odyssey.
q: Odyssey has its own James Bond! That’s right, quaint little Odyssey has a field agent for the intelligence community living right there pretending to live a normal life. But then, he disappears and travels around the world on top secret missions. Yet to meet Jason Whittaker, you’d never guess it.
I don’t know what to say!
I do. I look like I have a double chin in that picture. Do I have a double chin?
Don’t be so overdramatic.
Overdramatic? I am the epitome of reserve!
I want Applesauce!
Mmmm. Good with pork chops.
Dad, I may be wrong, but I think you're supposed to put the worm on the hook, not your finger.
Stop calling me squirt!
Anger management. You might want to consider that, too.

So much for Jason's quiet life in Odyssey! What do you think will happen next? Will Jason escape the evil clutches of The Whisperer, or is this the end of our intrepid hero?? …Sorry, I got caught up in the drama.

635.s: When Jason Whittaker is revealed publicly as an intelligence agent, an old nemesis named The Whisperer tracks him to Odyssey.
q: So, when are you going to do it?
Do that thing you do to escape! You know, pull a bazooka out of your wristwatch, or click your heels together and eject us through the roof!
Sorry, I’m a gadget free agent.
Whereas I am a gadget filled villain!
Ah! Whit. At last we meet.
At last. Should I know you?
You have an awful lot of explosives around a kids' shop, Whittaker. Remind me not to send my nephews here.
You know, I always use my birthday.
You dirty, rotten traitor!
Yeah, whatever.
Step back. You don't know about my cane!
I don't care about your cane when I've got my fist!
Why didn't someone think of that before?!
Who'd have thought that killing me would be the best way to keep me safe?
Agent Brooke, get Huddleston out of my sight!
With pleasure!

636.s: Edwin Blackgaard puts on a “radio reenactment” of the founding of the town of Odyssey. Two of his actors, Mandy Straussberg and Trent DeWhite, are unhappy when they’re cast as a young couple in love.
q: No, no, NO, Shakespeare! When I say a ROARING fire, I want to FEEL it singeing my eyebrows!
Country bumpkin, am I? Ineffective, talentless muppet, am I!? Mr. Banquo, I stab at thee!
All right, children. Are you prepared for an experience you will never forget? No matter where your dull middle class suburban lives take you.
We don’t wanna be a married couple!
You don’t wanna? Oh dear me, how sad! Shakespeare, fetch me my violin.
Violin, coming up!
Couldn’t you just, you know...change the script a little?
Change Mr. Blackgaard’s script?!
No, they want to hear drama!
That’s right!
And the true story has none of those elements!
Isn’t keeping a good friend better than losing one because of what other kids think?
Mandy, are you willing to end your friendship with Trent just because a few people might tease you? Does your friendship mean so little?
Whatever we call it, the name should tell people that...that they’re in for the adventure of a lifetime! It’s in a beautiful valley, a place that everybody...everybody oughta see.

No one said anything more. And apart from a spelling change, that’s how our town has been known ever since. A town that survived its reputation as “the stinking swamp” became a town known for community and redemption--a town that all of us are happy to call our home and our dream – Odyssey.
When I think of home, I can't think of the word having any meaning without you there.
Oh, Bertha...you don't mean that. You don't want a poor, blind man.
You're my best friend, Wolfgang. How could I live anywhere without you? You're my constant and my touchstone.
And you're mine. I can't live without you, Bertha...will you marry me?
Yes, a thousand times, yes, I'll marry you!
Young lady, do I give you advice on hair scrunchies?
Hair scr-r-r-runchies. You appear to be an expert on them.
Imagine him, forcing me to do that story! It's...unreasonable! It's...it's...
Like he's making you do what he hired you to?

637.s: The plan to bury the new time capsule in the basement of Whit's End causes a “separation of church and state” conflict that jeopardizes the future of the shop.
q: Okay so, now I'm bored. Bored, bored, BORED! There's nothing to talk about! The most excitement around here is a little press conference with the mayor. According to the two people who actually attended, they've decided to bury the new time capsule back in the basement at Whit's End. Well, whoopedy, doopedy, doo!!
This is insane! They can't close down Whit's End after all these years!
It looks like they can, Bernard.
Really? Are you suggesting a conspiracy by members of our government to suppress the truth from the common man?
Well, I am! That's a lot more interesting than what you just said isn't it?
Hey, Bernard!
How would you like a squeegee shoved up your nose?
The two of you should take a look at this.
Our miracle!
Thank you for that very helpful and touching statement on behalf of Whit's End.
Did he say anything?
He did. As only Eugene can say it.
I thought I heard a sandwich calling my name.
What deed, Whit?
What deed indeed?
Quiet, Eugene!
Oh! I just can't stand to listen anymore.
Frankly I don't understand why you turned it on in the first place. One doesn't look to Cryin Brian Dern as a reliable source for news and information.
Yeah, in fact I don't consider him to be a reliable source for anything. Except stress headaches.

638.s: Lucy Cunningham-Schultz becomes the center of attention when Jimmy Barclay, Curt Stevens and Jack Davis return to Odyssey for a reunion – each young man determined to win her heart at last.
q: I...wrecked the flight simulator.
How did you do that? A flight simulator doesn’t move, right?
No, not normally.
Isn’t that kinda like crashing an exercise bike?
Yes, except this exercise bike cost three million dollars.
She really liked me.
What's not to like?
It's just a part of growing up - adjusting to the seasons we go through.
It does feel a little like winter in here all of a sudden.
I'm glad you asked, Connie. Has this ever happened to you? You're walking down the street, and you drop your keys. Isn't it a pain to bend down and get them?
Well, not real—
Exactly. Now with the new Vacu-Grab, you don't have to.
The Vacu-Grab?

It's portable, retractable, and can fit right into your purse. Just take it out, retract it, turn it on, grab the keys, un-retract it, open the special containment unit built right in, and voila! You've got your keys.
So, instead of going through all of that...why not just bend down and pick up your keys?
...It retracts, Jimmy.
You think being beaten by Egyptians or being chased by rebel soldiers is conducive to romantic discussion?

639.s: Lucy Cunningham-Schultz becomes the center of attention when Jimmy Barclay, Curt Stevens and Jack Davis return to Odyssey for a reunion – each young man determined to win her heart at last.
q: It's Lewis! Or maybe it's Clark...I can't figure out which is which...
Could you stop by Odyssey Elementary first?
Oh, it's kind of a surprise.
Okay, I'll be there in a few minutes.
Okay, I'll bring the dust pan.
Cause you might get swept away.
Mr. Whittaker?
Where did you people come from? This boat can't handle this much weight!
What's going on in here?
You, uh, want to go out with us?
"Why do birds suddenly appear every time you are near?"
You stole that!
I only had like, fifteen minutes! I spent all my time finding the sporks!
Maybe I should bow out and let you have her. I mean, Lucy deserves somebody who can make a decision.
Yeah, but that's not me. I can't make a decision. It takes me fifteen minutes just to pick out something off the value menu.
The lawn's on fire! The lawn's on fire! Who's got a fire extinguisher?
You were supposed to bring that!
I knew that!

640.s: The two finalists for “Best Small Town” are in a perfect tie. Each town is given one week to show the heart of the town to win the contest.
q: Mr. Doyle, is it true that you've been drawing Powerboy in secret for the last five years?
It must be true. I just heard it on the radio!
Why certainly, small child with a naturally deep voice!
Oh yeah, county not country. I always get those mixed up, which is why I always go on those weekend trips to Switzerland by accident.
Hello who's on Wooton's phone, howdy, howdy!

Actually, a whole bunch of characters in the comic are based on real people in Odyssey. Like there's this one character, oh, she's always late for stuff and she talks all the time and she says stuff she doesn't mean.
Who's she based on?
Uh, oh, she's also really good-looking and, uh, very cool.
I think I have what Powerboy would call a solution that would stand up to a diamond-lined bowling ball.
Jumpin' Jamaican gymnasts! I draw PowerBoy!? In my busy schedule, when did I ever find time to do that?
Wooton, why'd you just hit a pot with a fork?
This house doesn't have a high ceiling for my breakfast gong, it's in storage.
But you once said that you couldn't possibly have breakfast without that instrument.
I can't, Eugene. That's why I'm having 2 lunches everyday.

641.s: Kelly gets in a new version of the Imagination Station and experiences the story of the crucifixion of Jesus.
q: Master, I want to be a son of light.

He who believes in me believes not in me, but in him who sent me, and he who sees me sees him who sent me. I have come as light into the world, and whomever believes in me may not remain in darkness. Open your eyes, child. See me.
I can see! I can see! Father, I can see!
I don't like you very much!
Funny. Not many people do.

642.s: Kelly gets in a new version of the Imagination Station and experiences the story of the crucifixion of Jesus.
q: Not a peep, girl!
Get your big, smelly hands off me!

643.s: Mr. Whittaker creates a whole town run entirely by kids. Ryan and his friends decide that they must run the town right by establishing their own government, laws, and justice system.
q: This was our chance to see our role models in action! Instead it was about as exciting as sharpening pencils.
You got to sharpen pencils?
At one point, there was a guy who nearly fell asleep, while he was talking.
And I can invent things and do scientific experiments on live subjects?
Yes. Well, no not the experiment part.
No, no experiments on rats either.
How fast can this squad car go? Ever gone over 200?
Oh no. There's never much need to drive fast around Odyssey.
So do I get a piece?
A fire arm, a gun. You gonna give me a gun?
I'm a reporter with the Odyssey Times.
Oh yeah, I remember our telephone call, but I remember hearing you a little taller.
Now, what about taxes?
Can't we just avoid taxes?
In fact, I would like to teach the world to sing in perfect harfenspiel!

644.s: The town of Kidsboro Mr. Whittaker created is vandalized. Ryan and the other kids investigate and respond to the fallout.
q: The Kidsboro constitution can't be written on sticky notes!
What's next?! Suing someone because of bad breath?!
You better get one [court system], because one way or another I'm gonna get my money or Kidsboro is going down.
I won't have threats in my courtroom, Valerie Swanson
Objection, Valerie Swanson
Yeah, that's exactly what she's doing. I feel badgered.
I'm big on metaphors.

645.s: Mr. Whittaker creates a whole town run entirely by kids. Ryan and his friends decide that they must run the town right by establishing their own government, laws, and justice system.
q: So, let me get this straight: our national flower can't die, and our national bird is already dead?

646.s: Jack Allen gives Whit an old manuscript that tells of a mysterious house in the middle of the woods … and a pair of siblings lost in the strange world of Marus!
q: ...look, it's a house!

647.s: Kyle and Anna’s adventure gets stranger. The Old Judge rescues Anna, and Kyle is befriended by General Darien.
q: I take my orders from the King and his officers! You can't tell me what to do! You have no authority.
Let me tell you a little something about authority. It is given. Not taken. My authority comes from the Unseen One. From where does the king and his officers get their authority?
Well... uh...
One minute, I was in an old house in Odyssey, and the next I was in the king's closet!

648.s: The Old Judge teaches Anna about the Unseen One, and Kyle saves Darien’s life a second time.
q: The Unseen One is the creator and sustainer of all things; he is everywhere at all times: all-seeing, all-knowing, all powerful.
No, not like God; the Unseen One is God.

649.s: Under the tutelage of the Old Judge, Anna begins to have visions of the present and the future. Meanwhile, Darien and Kyle must try to make a daring escape from the king’s clutches.
q: What are you going to do?!
What else can I do? I'm going to bed!
Prince George
If he's your friend, then he knows it already.
The wheels are in motion, my son — nothing can be the way it was.
...we are still friends, no matter what happens...
Our friendship is secure, my brother. May the Unseen One be our witness.

650.s: The Old Judge sends Anna away with Darien and Kyle as they race to escape the king. Anna’s visions grow stronger, and Kyle senses danger again for Darien’s life.
q: We're in the hands of the Unseen One [God].
...often it's in suffering that we see the ancient ways of the Unseen One [God] most clearly.
You'll learn what you're willing to learn.
And you boy, what's your story?
I'm her sister...I mean she's my bro...I mean...I'm tired.
I'm sure you are.
These are the days of abandonment; when the leaders and their people turn away from the ancient ways and the Unseen One [God].
To be a voice for the Unseen One [God] can be a great burden. Sometimes it involves suffering; even sharing the suffering of others but, our faith in the Unseen One [God] carries us through.
I don't know if I have that kind of faith.
Perhaps not; but you will. You must feed the faith you have with prayer and study, silence and solitude. It is like a small seed that needs nurturing to blossom.

651.s: King Lawrence orders a massacre at the convent where Anna is staying. Meanwhile, Darien cooks up an elaborate plan to free the town of Kellen from the evil Palatians.
q: The ways of the Unseen One [God] don't always line up with what we hope or expect.
Lift your cups my good friends of Kellen. Mayor, this is a day of celebration. The Palatians are defeated, and Kellen is free!
To you Darien for your victory!
No, no, No, NO Mayor! May the Unseen One receive glory for our victory! To the Unseen One!

652.s: Darien and his loyal followers have a dramatic confrontation with King Lawrence in the Valley of the Rocks.
q: I'm in the hands of the Unseen One [God]. He will do with me whatever he will.
If the Unseen One is God, than he is God everywhere.
How's your stomach?
Ugh. I can't be his [Darien's] protector if he's going to do stuff like this.

653.s: The battle in the land of Marus takes an ugly turn as former friends become enemies and allies become foes. Young Kyle starts to doubt that the Unseen One is really watching out for them.
q: Being chosen doesn't mean doing exciting things all the time. It doesn't mean that we're always being used by the Unseen One [God]. Sometimes it means waiting and being patient.
But what if King Lawrence has you arrested — or you're killed?
Then we've all been terribly misled and the Unseen One didn't really choose me to be king.

654.s: Whit finishes reading the strange manuscript about Marus. In the story, Kyle and Anna try to return home, and King Lawrence races to escape the Palatians.
q: We were chosen for one thing in Marus, so we must be chosen for something else here.

655.s: Connie loves spending time in Whit's newest invention, the Inspiration Station. But when a glitch shuts down the machine, her obsession may go too far.
q: By the way, what do you call this invention?
The Inspiration Station.
If Matthew Parker
You can’t presume to know what you don’t know.
Tinkering with other people’s equipment is a very dangerous thing to do. If Matthew Parker
Learn what, Eugene? Aren’t you the one that Connie, Part 2
Well... yes. I'll get back to work.
Thanks, Eugene.
Boy! And my friends think living with a Camilla Parker
Does Connie Kendall
Where is... Where are all my phone numbers? My whole speed dial directory is gone! Matthew Parker
Slow to a stop.
Look now you listen to me, young lady.
You have arrived at your destination, Matthew Parker
Matthew? Oh, Matthew!!!
Who would erase all of our programs?!?
Well the last person I saw by the TV was...
Matthew Parker
What is that?
I don't know.
Oh, that's your phone, mom.
Is it going to explode?

656.s: Whit is concerned about The Inspiration Station's strange effects on Connie, but hopes the invention could be just the thing to inspire young Matthew Parker.
q: I understand if you're a little skittish about something new.
I'm not skittish — even if I knew what that meant.
I’m trying to describe how I feel.
Has that ever been a problem for you before?!

Greeting and salutations, listeners. I suggest we go to the phone lines where you should call in to discuss the uh... the uh... little dramatic vignette we just performed for your uh... edification and uh, perhaps mystification. I believe we have a caller on line one. Oh, please let there be a caller on line one.
A lot of you have been asking about my recent adventure in John Whittaker
I've got 3,456,270,496 rows of books, all alphabetized and numerically ordered to take care of.
I know, I know: don’t tinker around with stuff if you haven’t asked permission first.
Exactly, my boy. You’ve got perspict... er... perspir... perspaper... uh, you’re smart.
We all aspire to be better than we are. And it hurts to realize that we’re not there yet. We’ve got a long way to go.

There are places and times to seek inspiration, where we feel like we’re close to God and we can get a glimpse of what he can do in us. But every one of us has to come down for the mountain where the real work takes place; where He molds and shapes us.

657.s: After nearly being mauled by the junk in his own garage, David Parker declares that his family is going to have a yard sale. Will the entire Parker family survive parting with their treasures?
q: Now there's a find! A wood sander? Still in the box? David Parker
But first, I'm gonna get through this junk if it kills me.
Uh, Mr. Parker!?
Please, call me David.
David! Look out!
David Parker
How old is this sock? Did something die in it? It looks like it has rigor mortis!
You’re real big on catch phrases centered around farm animals, aren't you?
They make me smile like a fat tick on a skinny dog!
I thought family spontaneity was when we do something fun. This is more of a “spontaneous not-fun” kind of family thing.
What about you, Camilla? You’ve been awfully quiet. Do you have a woeful reason why you can’t help this weekend?
Nope. I just want to do what you want me to do. I love you Daddy.
I love you too honey, but I'm afraid that won't get you out of this cleanup.
Speaking of clutter, you should see the inside of my closet!

658.s: Simon Jones just wants the hedge trimmed, but his son Barrett can’t tear himself away from his portable video game — until it disappears without a trace!
q: Ah! Oh! That's it! Almost there! Ah, I got it! I got it! No, wait, I didn't get it. I did get it! I got it!! I beat the level!! Whooohooo!!!
Do you hear that?
I can hear the hedge calling your name. It's saying, "Come bring that great electric hedge trimmer to bane all that is untrimmed and untidy!"
That's not funny, dad.
Wait a minute. And I give you this, Hedge Bane the Horrible, half of my energy bar. It will aid you in mustering all of your strength!
With what? Scratching ant bites and playing Verminoids?
I'm not playing Verminoids! Who said I was playing Verminoids?
Well, I couldn't help but notice the concave indentations in your thumbs. About the size of the buttons on your game I would think.
Well, I hope this is good. Like a crashed space ship or a nest of radioactive snakes!
I think Verminoids is warping your brain.
The subconscious mind has a tendency to manipulate even casual conversation.
Thank you for the nature walk Matthew Parker
I'm sorry Em, but I think the cheese has finally slipped off your brother's cracker.
What's wrong Barrett?
Nothing, nada, not a thing.
You lost your Verminoids game.
What? How do you know that? I mean- IF I had been playing it in the first place, which I wasn't.
I noticed that your thumbs were repuffed.
Nicely observed.
Oh boy. Here we go again! Man this is so textbook. Denial, denial, denial! Shame is a prison, Nelson, and you are it's inmate!
a lawnmower!
More Than Likely...
But that means... DAAAAAAAD!
Yep, they're a regular Matthew Parker

659.s: Matthew Parker is Vance King’s “Target of the Week” – which means certain humiliation at the hands of the bully! Matthew decides to take matters into his own hands by getting revenge on Vance during an Odyssey Coyotes baseball game.
q: Haven't you noticed that people are staring at you?
Is there something hanging from my nose?
Tell him what he's won, Jay!
Well Vance, Matthew has won seven unforgettable days and nights of degradation, denigration and humiliation!
That's right, Jay! You'll be poked, pranked and prodded by some of the best in the business! You'll also receive physical harm at no extra cost!
Hey Matthew.
Ahhhhhhh!! Don't scare me like that!
I just said your name.
Well, warn me before you speak to me!

Actually, I did lose the game, and so did everybody else on our team. It would be easy to blame Matthew, and that was a pretty lousy thing for him to do. You know what? It wasn't all his fault. Just like it wasn't Vance's or mine. Though, I know I wasn't pitching my best. The fact is, we didn't play as a team in the 9th inning. We took it for granted that Odenton would be easy to beat. I mean, we thought we had the game won. We were overconfident and sloppy; it's that simple. So, maybe we should keep that in mind when we're passing the blame around; it wasn't any of us, it was all of us. Thanks for the award.

There is a flow, as the other team rolls like a river towards home plate, we want to disrupt that flow. Do you understand? We must drop a rock in their river cutting them off at second before we worry about first.
And for all those folks who have never heard a game on the radio before. Let me just give you a preview of what it'll sound like.
What were those sounds at the end?

Ah well you see the ball left the field, and hit the blades of a passing traffic helicopter, and so the ball got flung three miles and landed in the lion cage at the zoo. The mother lion was not that happy. Oh I'm really hoping something like that happens, Whit!
Maybe there's a witness protection program for kids like me.
Well, I don't even know that much about baseball and more than that I don't really like baseball.
Yeah, I mean, not everything about baseball.. Just the parts of the game when nothing is really happening.. Which if you think about in a three hour game is about... Oh, three hours.
Uh, Matthew.. It's a little cool out for bare feet, don't you think?
Oh Wow! Are you on the "no shoe diet" too?! You know it really works! I lost 17 oz. immediately after I took off my shoes but I put all the weight right back on.
Abort the mission, Abort!

660.s: Camilla Parker desperately wants a pet, but her family seems to suffer from the “Parker Family Pet Curse.” To prove her responsibility, Camilla takes care of a baby blue jay.
q: Oh, greetings Miss Parker!
Camilla. What are you doing?
You're just standing there in the middle of the park!
Oh, on the contrary! I'm not merely standing here: I'm basking in the glory of an exquisite day!
Wow! I never seen a bird do that before! It looked like it was aiming for your head!
Uh, Miss Parker take cover!...I've never tried out-running a bird before!!
And who here remembers the goldfish?
Oh! Spankie and Lester!
Dead within six weeks.
I think they had a suicide pact.
Pickles, Pickles! That wasn't my fault! Mom sat on him!
Well, what was he doing loose? And on the kitchen chair?
You called us all for dinner. He thought he was part of the family!
Hey, maybe Wooton knows.
Wow! Well, I never did before, but there's a first time for everything. What is it?
He was a Great Horned Owl named Doctor What.
Doctor... what?
Yeah, exactly. Doctor Who would have been a better name, but I think it’s trademarked.
Okay, here goes! Hair today, gone tomorrow.
And [the bird] bit Eugene and now he may have bird rabies, but I think he's just hungry.
Eugene’s hungry?

661.s: Emily Jones is usually right about everything – from solving mysteries to cooking chili. But when she decides to try her hand at matchmaking for her brother Barrett, the singing card she creates may have disastrous consequences.
q: Listen, Jay Smouse
Your trombone solo was really good today, Barrett.
Thanks! Your flute playing was really... uh, flutelike!
I was wrong?
It happens to the best of us.
Well, well, well, if it isn't Barrett. Skinny as a carrot, mangy like a ferret.
Huh? Oh. Hi, Jay.

662.s: The Parker family is in for a bumpy ride. It all starts when their grandmother comes to tell them that their Aunt Rosalita has decided to elope next week – in Odyssey, at their house!
q: Enjoy! Although I feel I should put a warning sign on you, Matthew. There's enough chocolate in that shake and brownie to energize a small Swiss village.
There was this spider the size of a Volkswagen under the house. That squeaky step will have to wait.
Me? No. She does great. I eat all I can stomach.
No, uh, that's not what I... that was supposed to come out in a good way and it didn't... no, Eva is, uh, muy... incredibliblo... cook.
She and her fiance decided to get married this week!
And she wants to be married here, in Odyssey.
At your house!

663.s: Doors are opening up for Olivia Parker – too many doors, actually! After signing up for guitar lessons with Eugene, she also agrees to star in Connie’s play.
q: You want me to practice for 18 hours?
Well, not all of it, you may sleep for 8 of those hours.
Whit will be playing the voice of God.
Great, you're into the role already!
Why is the ark made out of cinder blocks?
They're cubes. That's what Red Hollard
Aaah, right.
Great! Uh, what do I do?

664.s: A talking portrait of Frederick Douglass tells Olivia Parker the story of the famous Jubilee Singers of Fisk University.
q: If I could go to school and learn nothing but music, that would suit me just fine. See, I want to be a singer.
Hm. You remind me of Ella Sheppard. Though she didn't allow her love of music to keep her from pursuing an education.

665.s: Olivia continues to hear the story of the Jubilee Singers from a talking portrait of Frederick Douglass.
q: Olivia, I bet you're the kind of person that reads the last page of a book first. Ain't ya?
No. Well maybe sometimes.
Yeah, thought so.
Are you threatening me, sir?

666.s: Olivia hears the conclusion of the story of the Jubilee Singers from a talking portrait of Frederick Douglass.
q: Yes, things are dire, Thomas. But I believe God will not allow us to fail in so great a work. These are mere tests which all who seek to do His work must endure.

667.s: Eugene and Matthew investigate why the clock tower at City Hall seems to be stuck at 11:45. Could it have something to do with the anniversary of a lost love from twenty years ago?
q: Parking fine?
Oh, a complete misunderstanding regarding my bicycle.
Uh-huh. Cause and effect, right?
Those were a lot of stairs.
Thirty-nine to be precise.
And as you can hear, the clock has reset itself to 11:45. No big knob on the back, Matthew.
If you're gonna give a girl a rose, it shouldn't be black. Has Eugene been showing you old tombstones again?
I'm sorry to bother you again, but were any of you guys in the clock tower just now?
No, why do you ask?
Because the door to the staircase is standing wide open.
Whoa, it's freak-out time.
Matthew, tell Eugene, Connie is on the case.
Have you thought about turning the knob on the back of the clock?
I'll go see her right away.
We'll go see her.
Oh, yes. Me and my shadow.
Well Alicia, may I call you Alicia?
Has anyone gone into the programming code itself?
That's what I was going to suggest.
(referring Andrew) Because in the mysteries, the butler always does it. And he's kinda like a butler, you know, being janitor takes out the trash...

668.s: Eugene and Matthew investigate why the clock tower at City Hall seems to be stuck at 11:45. Could it have something to do with the anniversary of a lost love from twenty years ago?
q: That's my cell phone.
Sorry, that's mine. Excuse me.
It's Eugene.
Mine's...oh, I don't know who it is.
Don't mind me!
Oh, hi Veronica!
We have a countdown and I don't know if it's to a banquet of flowers, a big laugh, or a bomb!
You can't arrest me, I'm merely conducting a routine check on the system.
In a ski mask?
I was young, they shouldn't have trusted me to be their delivery girl.
Still they did. And you were trustworthy, for a time.
One moment of anger. One little mistake.
Indeed it boggles the mind. We make so many decisions in the course of our lives, most with little consequence. But others, entire lives could be changed from one moment from one act of emotion.

669.s: In a last-minute replacement, Wooton Bassett hosts his own Kids' Radio show and is forced to ad-lib for a half-hour. Will his show have a point?
q: I'm here with Red Hollard, who is a registered locksmith...
...So I'm going to break into your car to get your keys, so you can turn that alarm off.

Sounds great! And how are you going to do break into the car. I assume you have one of those long car breaker-into things like they use on TV where you slide it down along the window and pull up on the lock mechanism?
Uh, no. I wish I had one of those car breaker-into things.
Oh, then what are you going to use?
This brick!!
I know the significance of a particular spot 3 inches down from his left arm-pit.
It's where he's most ticklish!
With the push of this button on my remote control a giant projectile pencil will be launched at the giant balloon. And the deed will be done. Ready? Just say the magic word.
That's the one!
Our cast included Will Ryan as Eugene, Katie Leigh as Connie, Andre Stojka as Whit, and Jess Harnell as... No, that can't be right.
So what do you think of car alarms, Harlow?
I don't belong to that group.
Wait! Back to our dramatic news insert! Siege at Whit's End!
Hello! Harlow Doyle Here!
Hi, Harlow Doyle Here!
Look who just walked in! Oh, you can't look; this is radio.
Hi, I'm Thug Clockripper, and I approve of this commercial.

670.s: Barrett is excited about getting the lead role in the school play. But when his first practice is interrupted by a mysterious booming voice, Emily must investigate the “phantom of the school play.”
q: Rue the day!
There's no business like show business, especially if that business leads to MURDER!! Okay, maybe not murder.
...I call it, The Mystery of the Phantom of the School Musical. Nah, too many words. Never mind. Hey! We could call it Stage Fright. Yeah!

I'll be the first to admit that my brother is pretty amazing. Talented, charming, personable, but when it comes to moments of fear. Well, let's just say he has issues. Remind me later and I'll tell you about how much he hates clowns.
You're kidding me. The whole cast is afraid?
Uh huh. Someone is supposed to tell Miss Adelaide this afternoon. We voted and decided that Barrett should do it. Since he was the loudest screamer.
You voted me to represent you guys? Wow, that's an honor. I'll do it.
I don't wanna go. I heard that Hartley lost his head and rides a horse.
That's Ichabod Crane. Stop being such a coward. There's no headless phantom of the theater.
What about the swoosh? How do you explain the swoosh?
I didn't know about a swoosh.
We got swooshed yesterday. Very cool, but very creepy.
Twenty-two trombones led the marching band! Twenty-two trombones, all at my command! I just want to say that I'd hold you all day if I didn't need 2 arms to play!

671.s: Wooton, Eugene, Connie, and Matthew try to apply the discipline of fasting and, through their comedic antics, realize that it’s far more difficult than they imagined.
q: I know! Connie Kendall
Hey, what do Matthew Parker
Specifically, I wish to curb my desire to exhibit my perspicacity.
Have you tried deodorant?
Last week you made a less than succinct argument that I might be overly... uh...
Rectangular?!
Maladjusted to the elevation!
Whit, is Eugene Meltsner
I don't know. Why?
Well, the door's locked, and I keep hearing someone whimpering!
Of course we notice you, Connie Kendall
What is the predominate interaction for mega-voltage radiation therapy energies?
I fasted using verbs once. There was very little action that day.
I'm fasting computers.
Interesting choice. Why that?
My Eva Parker

Okay, say a prayer every time I think about junk food. (sniffs the air) Ohhh. Somebody is barbecuing hot-dogs! Oops! Uh okay, Dear God thank you for wonderful smells such as barbecued hot-dogs and all the other foods that I will not have the pleasure of eating Amen!

672.s: Odyssey Middle School’s “Opposite Day” inspires Olivia to become friends with a girl who is nothing like her. Meanwhile, Barrett becomes obsessed with getting as many online friends as possible.
q: How was school today, Barrett?
It was okay, but I lost a friend.
Uh, did you check your locker?
I lost a Club Kid-Chat friend. And I can't figure out who un-friended me.
They didn't tell you?
No. I logged in this morning and instead of having 523 friends, I only had 522!
Are you still doing Club Kid-Chat?
Yeah. I posted an update this morning saying that I felt kinda down.
Wow. Any responses yet?
Four. One suggesting a self-help book, one asking who I was, one telling me to meditate more and one saying that I could earn $80,000 a year working from home!
So I get to practice acting. Amber (b)
It's a weird-weird.
Well, someday when I'm playing a geographist on Broadway, you'll look back on this day and say "Yes, I remember when she practiced this part years and years ago."
Geologist. It's called a geologist.
By the way, Matthew Parker
I've been playing Igloo-Rama on Club Kid-Chat with my new friend from Guam for the past four hours.
Can you believe it? I have a friend in Guam. I'm up to 523 friends now.
Barrett! I am so glad to see you!
You speak English!
Are you a cloud?
Nope. Try again.
An inside out sheep?
Nope, I'm mashed potatoes.
I get it, but I don't get why.

Well, it's Mailman Spirit Week. Today is Dress Like Your Favorite Vegetable Day. I really struggled between mashed potatoes and stuffed tomatoes. But surprisingly a tomato is actually a fruit. Go figure. Wonder what it would be like in a pie.
Gravity is boring? That's like saying oxygen is a luxury item!

673.s: When the Odyssey Middle School basketball team’s mascot is stolen, they suddenly start losing all their games. The team considers drastic measures to get back their good luck charm.
q: Princess Baba is the twin of Prince Jessup!
Hoo! Hoo! Let's go, Odyssey!
You can be your own mascot. Rub your own heads.
You want information? Well, tell them to watch the owl.
Watch the owl? That's it? Not watch for the itching powder I put in their shorts before the game? Or watch how their best player gets handcuffed to a fire hydrant in Albuquerque?
Whoa, whoa, whoa. That's amateur stuff. We're dealing in advanced psychology.
Listen to me team. To shoot the ball, you must be shot through the hoop yourself. Be the ball. Be the hoop. Be the scoreboard increasing by two after you shoot yourself through yourself.
Do not despair, my team. Losing 78 to 72 is nothing to be ashamed of. Pure victory is the most elusive prize of all. Like shooting stars or photographic evidence of Bigfoot.
I thought I was intense. This is going to be a long detention.
Yes, it will be. Repeat after me. Wax on, wax off.

674.s: Matthew joins a mysterious new club and refuses to tell Emily about their activities. Emily decides that this is a mystery that she must solve.
q: So, where does that put you in the club?
Back to square one.
Somebody fell into my garbage can booby trap!
You've got microwaves, blenders, electric pencil sharpeners! This must be where machines go when they die!

675.s: On a snowy Thanksgiving Day, Whit, Connie, Eugene, and a few of their friends end up stuck at Whit's End. To pass the time, they tell a zany story of the Scrunch and his plan for “Thankstaking.”
q: Hot chocolate?! How can anyone think of hot chocolate at a time like this?!
I suppose things could be worse.
Oh, yeah? Like how?
Uh, oh! What was that?
Uh, well, the power could go off.
Yep, that would be worse alright.
Don't worry, the, uh, generator should kick in any minute.
Uh, you mean the generator I've been trying to fix?
Merry Christmas!
Uh, Harlow, I hate to tell you this, but, it's not Christmas.
Well then, Happy New Year!
No, it's not New Year's either!
Um...joyous Arbor Day?
Well, we should do something fun instead of feeling sorry for ourselves.
I dunno, I kinda like feeling sorry for myself.
Turkeys get married?!.

Wait, so you're saying Thanksgiving is OK after all?I knew it! I totally knew it! I could've been watching football and eating pies and playing games,it could've been so great! I've been robbed,I want restitution!

They decided to fast and not feast on that day, to honor the giver and taker away. Come Thanksgiving, come each day, into our hearts and what we say. Of all our grumbling we humbly repent, for you, Lord, are faithful 100 percent.

676.s: The Parker family kids are convinced that they are too grown-up for a babysitter. A parents’ night out, a nanny named Maria, and the neighbor’s dog Bruno may be their opportunity to prove themselves.
q: Black pudding?!
Oh, yes, it's a delicious blood sausage!
I didn't know English people were cannibals! No wonder George Washington threw you out of the country!
Why does the word "nanny" make me feel even more like a baby?
You broke the smoke alarm!
Well, that was one way to stop it!
Now sit down. It's time for a family meeting.
In front of a stranger?
Maria's a unofficial member of the family now.
Baptized by fire, so to speak.
I take full responsibility for everything that's happened.
Thanks, Olivia. She's right Dad, it's all her fault.
Works for me!
…and Kari Wahlgren as Maria. …Or was that ‘Charlotte’?

677.s: A piñata filled with delicious chocolate goes missing from Whit's End. Only a few people were in the room at the scene of the crime, leading Emily Jones to investigate “whodunit!”
q: I didn't ask you here for a fight.
Then, why are we here?
Emily Sherlock Jones is about to solve the case.
...the case of the chocolatey, maltball-goodness pinata, that someone took.
That's not going to work. Honestly, you are the worst at naming these mysteries.
You're not done til' I'm done.
Hey wait a minute, I didn't do anything wrong this time, I admitted I fell asleep! hahaha, Good for me.
Yeah enjoy it while you can.
Someone ate all of the maltballs out of the pinata last night..
You stole them! How would you know that someone ate them unless that someone that ate them was you!
I just assumed that...
Put him in irons, throw away the key!
I slept like a rock. Does that count?
And I’m Chris, hoping you’ll join us again next time for more Adventures in Odyssey! …Is anyone gonna eat that last maltball?

678.s: The Parker’s grandma comes for a Christmas visit, in the middle of an elaborate Christmas celebration cooked up by Eugene and Connie. The Parker family parents wonder if it’s possible to have a Christmas without stress.
q: Ready...set...Feliz Navidaaad!
Sorry, darling. There's no steamer in here.
And I'm running out of steam.
Grandma! I mean, Nanna! I mean, innkeeper! Innkeeper! Let us in!
And then we exchanged white elephant gifts.
You exchanged white elephants? Did you grow up in a zoo?

679.s: A plane crashes in Gower's Field and both Emily and Matthew make surprising discoveries nearby. Meanwhile, both Whit and Wally Haggler meet friends from the past.
q: You're kidding, right?! You come into my shop and pull a gun on me?! Where'd you learn your manners?!
