1000.s: Cooper and Suzu attend an unveiling at Henri's Art Gallery that leads to unexpected controversy. Meanwhile, Emily faces serious accusations from a fellow student, and Morrie insists that she enlist the team to prove her innocence.

1001.s: Emily struggles with the fallout of the situation at school and tries to decide what role the team should play in her life going forward. Meanwhile, Cooper, Morrie and Suzu continue to investigate an unusual art crime.

1002.s: Buck and Katrina adjust to their new life in Baltimore as they start relationships with families from a local church. Buck hopes to get another chance to join the football team, while Katrina connects with a group of like-minded moms.

1003.s: Buck and Katrina both face challenges when dark secrets from the past come to light, endangering their new lives in Baltimore, as well as Buck's new friendship with a young boy named Chase.

1004.s: Buck makes a pivotal decision about how to deal with a situation at his school. Meanwhile, Katrina tries to keep him on the right path in both his friendships and his spiritual journey. Past deeds and present bonds collide as the Meltsners face a turning point.

1005.s: Renee's convictions are put to the test when she finds herself a hero to both a young Christian and a college-aged atheist.
q: I canna believe you did that to me John Whittaker
You were right about about the middle of the road being a good place to get hit by a car. I just never thought you'd be the one driving it. Excuse me.

1006.s: Olivia gets a chilly reception from an old friend during a weeklong visit to a nearby prep school.

1007.s: Trey Calhoun wants to prove he can bake with the best of them. So when a popular reality show and its rude host pull into town, he and Red Hollard team up to compete on TV. It looks like Trey's prayers have been answered... or have they?

1008.s: Ron's unit takes enemy fire in Rakistan, where one Marine's convictions change lives forever.

1009.s: The Perkins family finally learns the cause of Ron's injury, and meets the man he holds responsible.

1010.s: Struggling to forgive and find new purpose, Ron Perkins is challenged to confront his bitterness.

1011.s: Buddy vows to protect Emily, convinced that bitter students want to sabotage her yearbook photo.
q: You know about glitter, don't you? It's pesky stuff. It'll never come off in time for your picture.

1012.s: After finding an unlikely accomplice, Jules carries out a risky plan for revenge on Bridget. But as her plan spirals out of control, she must decide how far she's willing to go.
q: I guess that answers my first question. Jules is still depressed about the breakup.
Jillian, she only eats hummus and plays the same sad song over and over, and she won’t talk to me. I still don’t even know why Buck broke up with her.
Alright, Jules, in these bags I have everything we need for a night of breakup grieving.
I’m fine, Connie. Really. You don’t need to do anything.

Well, we have ice cream, more ice cream, sour candies, sweet candies, dark chocolate, milk chocolate, chocolate milk, extra salty potato chips to replace sodium filled tears, three boxes of tissues, one, two, three, and a little plaque to hang on the wall, see.
”Be my rock of refuge to which I can always go, save me for you are my fortress and deliver. Psalm 71:3.” Hmm, I love that verse.
I’ll need to call your guardian, Connie Kendall, right?
And notify her that beginning tomorrow you’ll be placed on a three day suspension
Suspend… Mr. Solly, please, can I make up for it some other way?
I am being gracious. I’d be justified in assigning you a much worse punishment.
Burke, my car! Look at this dent. Do you know how long I had to beg the commissioner to get a new car?
I do. You started dropping hints around Groundhog Day, and then in March
Rhetorical question. And the sniffling cretin who hit me had the audacity to leave the scene of the crime.
Go inside and get all the footage from the security cameras. I’ll call Rhona.
Rhona, Polehaus. There’s been a hit and run on my new car. I want everyone on this stat! No one gets away with hitting my car!

1013.s: Jules' plans begin to unravel as Connie and Jillian grow suspicious. Tensions escalate and relationships are strained as the Kendall sisters face critical decisions.
q: What about Jules’s car?
Well, that worked out better than I expected. I called Bill Kendall
Sure thing. Wow, definitely worked out well for Jules.
Okay, a little suspicious. What’s your recommendation?
It’s time for a stakeout. We’re following her to the library.
It is kind of fun stake outing with you, quality roommate time and all.
Right, though we call it staking out in the biz not stake outing. That would be two rib eyes going on a date.
I don’t want my sister to go to prison at all.
But if you admit it was us, we both could end up in Juvie. We wouldn’t be able to graduate. It would effect our college admissions. Our whole lives.
I know, but Connie
If she knew the truth, she’d probably want you to take the out. She wouldn’t want you to ruin your life.
I don’t know. I told Jillian I’d go the police station right away to see Connie, so I need to get going.
Remember what I always admired about you. You go after what you want and you don’t let anything get in your way.
Even the truth?
Even the truth.
That’s very nice of you, Jules. I really, really appreciate your support.
Of course. Anything for my big sister.
How about the truth?
Alright, I’ve heard enough.
You’re free to go, Connie. I’ll let you know when the Juvenile court date for Jules is.
Wait, the police were listening in?
Ever hear of a two-way mirror?
You tricked me.
No. You were caught in your own lies.
I can’t believe you’d do this to me.
Well, right now, the feeling is mutual.
Dad bought it. You didn’t deserve it and your license is suspended for six months anyway.
Still, you can’t just get rid of it.
Actually, I can. Dad agreed.
I hate you, Connie.
Don’t say that.
I never should have come here. I never should have thought my big sister would want to help me out. All you do is judge me, ground me, have me arrested, and, and hang placards of verses on the walls.
Put that back, Jules.
This is what I think of your stupid verses.
Alright, clean that up and then go to your room until you calm down.
You clean it up. I’m out of here.

1014.s: Mr. Whittaker sends Morrie and Suzu on a secret mission—one designed to teach valuable lessons. But the siblings have secrets of their own.

1015.s: At Whit’s End, Renee Carter wrestles with one of life’s oldest and hardest questions: Why would a good God allow terrible things to happen?

1016.s: After an argument with the band, Jules and Gunner drive off to destinations unknown. As Connie uncovers more about the situation, she resolves to find her sister.
q: Can you please slow down?
No one else is out here, why does it even matter?
Maybe because of the canyon on one side?
When did you become such a chicken, Jules?
Gunner, slow down.
Just relax. You need to trust me. I’ve been driving for like over two years.
Gunner, I’m serious.
So am I. There’s nothing to worry about. Whoa.
I know, but we’re safe. We’re okay.
But they might have seen us if they saw the car on the cliff. How are they gonna see us now?
Who’s they, Gunner? No one knows we’re out here.
Thanks for coming by, Detective Polehaus. I could have gone down to the station to do the police report.
No, no, no, it’s fine. Someone brought limburger cheese in for lunch, so the whole place smells like feet.
Ugh, I needed to get out of there.
You know, did I ever tell you the story about when Connie tried to take me camping?
I never knew you camped.
Tried is the key word. When I first came from California I was a bit of a diva.
I had my Tommy two shoes, my ping purses, Tillsburg sunglasses, all the designer dresses you could imagine.
So, not exactly camping clothes.
Yeah. We drove two hours to our campsite. Connie set up the tent horribly, but it was up. Pulled out the cooler and started a fire. Then we realized we didn’t have sleeping bags.
She forgot those?
Well, she told me to grab them, but I had heard get the sweet ping bags, and I brought my whole collection of designer purses instead. I thought it was because we were going shopping on the way.
Not the best for a night’s sleep.

Really tough to fit into a coin purse. I was so embarrassed. You know, she didn’t make feel like an idiot, though. She just laughed it off. We packed up our camp and went and got our nails done instead. Oh, I had forgotten about that.
If we’re going to die, what would you want to tell your family?
I’d tell my parents, I’m angry at them. I wish they loved me more. I wish they loved me at all.
And what about Connie?
I’d say, please come help me.

1017.s: As Jules faces a desperate situation, Connie and Whit's search intensifies, driven by a growing sense that something is terribly wrong.
q: They probably think we just road tripped away like the airheads we are, like I've done a dozen times before. Why would this time be any different, huh? Gunner? Gunner? We're actually gonna die here, aren't we? Wow. Next Summer when hiking starts up again, they'll come across the car, and the police will see it was reported missing. They'll start an investigation, and they'll find us on this ledge, just two bodies, long gone. No one will even care at that point. Sure, my parents will feel bad, Connie's gonna cry, but ultimately, life goes on for everyone else, doesn't it? Nothing really changes, because my life didn't matter much. I've probably caused way more harm than good. I never did much good at all.

Gunner. Gunner, if you can hear me, don't move, okay? There's not much ledge left over there, and I can't reach you anymore. There's, there's nothing left underneath me. Gunner! Gunner, wake up please! Okay, so it's just me, just me, the dark, some stars and maybe God. Are you here? You wanna say, I told you so? This is what I deserve. That's probably what Connie would be saying. You know, actually, she wouldn't be. But, if she did say that she'd be right. I wish I'd been different; I do. I would do everything differently. Oh, I'm going crazy, talking to the wind. I'm so tired. I could fall off of this tree at any minute, and I almost don't care. You know, I always thought I had a lot of time. I could have my fun, never answer to anyone, then maybe someday I'd take time to think about that deeper meaning of life. I didn't wanna just give up the things I liked because some old guy glaring down from heaven is shaking his finger when I say or do the wrong thing. Yeah, sorry about calling you old. I probably could have used some finger shaking. I probably could have used, well, you. And I see you tried. And Connie tried really hard. I'm sorry. I am. I'm really sorry for not seeing you. What? I must be delusional. Come on, pull it together, Jules.
Connie, there's no way to tell completely what kind of impact we've had on other people. At least not on this side of heaven.
I don't feel like I've had any influence, Whit. Judging from where things stand, Jules seems worse off now then she's ever been.
It may seem that way, but even if that's true, God's not worried. He knows exactly where she's at in her journey, and a way for her to find her way home.
I know you're right, but I can't help wondering if she'll ever want that.
We're not the only ones looking for Jules right now, God is too. She matters to him even more than she matters to you.

Looks like it will be a pretty sunrise. Never appreciated those much. What was that verse on the plaque Connie hung up? "Be my rock of refuge to which I can always go." I can't go anywhere else right now. "Save me. Save me for you are my fortress and deliverer." Save me. Save me. God, I'm sorry, really, really, sorry for all the dumb stuff I've done, for being so selfish, for lying, for everything. I'm so sorry. Will you forgive me? I don't know how to say this but, I need you. The things Connie told me about Jesus dying for me, I see that now. I believe it. I do believe it. Wow. Now that is a sunrise. Thank you.

Okay. Hold on as long as I can but I wish I could talk to my parents, and to Buck about you. They're just as stubborn as I am, but they need you too. And Connie, I wish, I wish I could tell her how much I appreciate her, that I love her. Somehow, can you let Connie know I became a Christian, please? I know she'll be so worried about that. I can just imagine her walking into heaven and seeing me. "What, you became a Christian. I'm always the last one to know everything." Yeah, that'll be more fun.
That's it. I am hugging you forever.
So, I survive a near death experience, only to be sufficated by my sister.
Connie, I didn't think I'd ever see you again.
Hey, you're stuck with me, whether you like it or not.
I like it. And I'm really sorry for how I treated you.
It happened on the mountain. God met me there. Connie, I wasn't alone, not even for a second. I was never alone.
No, you weren't. You're a Christian. But, you have to really mean it, Jules. It just can't be bargaining with God because you're scared or whatever.
No, it was real. The realest thing I've ever done. I almost didn't care what happened to me, I just knew I needed Jesus, and I still do.
Thank you, Lord. My sister is my Sister in Christ now, too.
So, how is our patient doing?
Really good. Jules Kendall
That's fantastic.
Come with me, I have a gift for her.
Right behind you.
She really had an experience out there.
It seems that God was working on her this whole time. He's been the author of her story.
Yeah. The author and perfecter of our faith.
I'm glad you got a replacement. I'm so sorry I broke the first one.
Well, this one is yours, so you always remember.
Thank you, Connie. Thank you for everything.

Sisters in Christ. What a wonderful moment for Jules, Connie, and the Angels who are rejoicing in heaven. I can't wait to see how Jules' decision changes her whole life, including her relationship with Connie. In 1 Kings 19, the prophet Elijah needed to hear from God in what seemed to be a life and death situation. As he stood on a mountain a mighty wind came and broke the rocks into pieces, but God wasn't in the wind. Then the earth shook, but God wasn't in the earthquake. After that came a fire. Nothing. Finally, the Lord spoke to Elijah in a still small voice. God whispers to us more often than we realize, using his still small voice to draw us to him. I'm glad Jules finally reached a place where she could hear it. Have you heard that voice? Even if it isn't out loud, is God calling to you right now? Maybe he's telling you that, like Jules, it's time to ignore all the distractions of this world and focus on living a life, an eternal life for him.

1018.s: A shady new app reveals which person is investing more in a friendship ... in the Twilife Zone.

1019.s: When coworkers take a test to learn their strengths, surprising results take on a life of their own.
q: Expectations are very powerful things.
Does that mean we should ignore them?
No, no, no, not all of them. Over time you'll learn which ones to pay attention to. You have the Holy Spirit in your life now, Jules. He'll give you the ability to discern the good from the bad.

1020.s: A difficult relative reenters the Perkins' lives, which challenges them to put their newfound faith into action.

1021.s: Follow Cooper Calhoun into the pages of 1 Samuel where he'll team up with an unsung hero of the faith. Witness leadership in action-good and bad. Plus, see battles, buddies and betrayal.

1022.s: Paired up for a charity drive, Bridget and Jules can't avoid discussing their strained relationship.
q: We're cool now, me and Connie. Better than ever, actually.
No, it's true. She's forgiven me completely and I apologized.
And she bought it.
Has she suddenly gotten naive in the last week? Because if I were her I would not trust you at...
I became a Christian.
You're kidding.
About a week ago. I almost died in a car accident.
What? Where have I been? Were you hurt?
Well, there's a cast under this sleeve because I broke my arm, but other than that fine. Gunner was in the hospital for a couple of days. He had a concussion among other things, but he's okay now.
He was driving?
Yeah. Anyway, it made me think about my life and how pathetic it was, and I became a Christian.
Wow, it's like the flu around here. Everybody's getting saved.
It was the best decision I ever made.
I'm sorry. I shouldn't have said that. You're a really good singer. You're not expendable.
No, you should have said it exactly like that. I'm glad you did.

It shows me what kind of Christian you're actually gonna be. One of those that goes to church, talks about the right stuff around the right people, but when it comes down to it, your life and actions are pretty much going to be the same as they always were. I like it. I might be able to tolerate you.
But that's not the kind of Christian I want to be.
So, you want to be intolerable.
I just don't want to slip into the same habits.
I liked your old habits.

All I know is a week ago I was standing on a cliff overlooking a demolished car that I could have been inside, and I had no hope. So, I gave my life to Jesus, and since then, I don't know, it's different. I don't slam my fist on my steering wheel anymore.

My drive to school was always so tense and angry. People on the road going too slow or too fast. Or my car making weird expensive noises. I would slam my steering wheel and give myself bruises. But, I don't do that anymore. I've given up stuff I didn't need. There are different and better songs in my head now. I promise you, Bridget, for some reason, my feet feel lighter when I walk. And I know I have Jesus who loves me and has a place for me in heaven, where I'm never gonna worry about shoes and popularity and jealousy and Algebra ever again. So what is so bad about me wanting that for you? Knowing what I know, wouldn't it be worse if I didn't try and help you get that?
I'm going to pray for you. Does that make you mad?
Nah. I've got so many people praying for me right now. It's all white noise at this point.
I don't believe you.

Because Connie has prayed for me every day since I got here. I made fun of her for it. I got mad at her for it. But, I'm glad she didn't stop. For your information, I was being real with you. Everything I said was true. That I want to be friends with you, that I miss you, that I care about you.
I believe you.

1023.s: There's tension and tinsel when Zoe joins Jay for a chaotic family gathering during the holidays.

1024.s: With Buck visiting Odyssey, Jules braces to tell him she has become a Christian. Meanwhile, a nursing home ministry has an unsettling similarity to a dark detail from Buck's past.
q: Okay, Connie. I just pulled up to the restaurant. I need to figure out what to tell Buck. Of course I’m going to tell him I’m a Christian, but I need to do it carefully, you know? Oh, he’s going to be so weirded out by it. I mean, things have already been awkward since we broke up and I’m just surprised that he even wanted to meet me while he’s here. Well, it just felt like we were the only two non-Christians in town and that really bonded us. It’s probably why we became such good friends in the first place. Now what’s he gonna think of me? It’s even more of a wedge between us. Oh, hey, he’s walking up now. I gotta go, bye.
You know, it’s really good to see you.
You, too. Thanks for meeting up with me. My parents showed me the news article about your accident. That must have been a terrifying thing to go through.
You know, it was something. Did you, uh, hear anything else?
That they finally decided to construct railings along that area of the national forest? Is that what you mean?

1025.s: Old connections and fresh clues converge, pushing Buck toward answers about the case- and about himself.
q: Wait, wait, wait, wait, wait, wait.
I know Jules, I know, we weren’t falling for it, but…
No, you. You can’t have become a Christian.
When I heard about your accident I knew I had to talk to you. God protected you, Jules. He’s the reason you’re here.
You don’t have to tell me, Buck.
But I do. Now that I know Jesus, I want to...
Stop, you don’t have to tell me because I already believe.
I became a Christian, too.
Yes, for real.
That night of the accident, huddled on the side of the cliff.
You always were one for drama.

1026.s: In the wake of Jules' recent choices, Connie's comfortable routine starts to unravel. Meanwhile Renee learns that Whit built a computer program that could shed light on her long-standing questions.
q: I’ve been thinking about what you’ve been telling me lately about anyone old enough to drive is old enough to get herself to school on time, and I decided, well, you’re right. Connie, are you okay? Connie, are you there?
Uh, sorry. I dropped my phone. Did you just say I’m right?
Yeah, I did. Okay, very funny. Ha, ha, ha.
I just can’t believe it.
Well, you shouldn’t have to wake me up every morning. That’s on me. I can’t expect you to watch after me forever. You need to get on with your own life. Will you cut that out?
Rats, I think I scratched my screen.
Yeah, in fact, you, you've been a little, well, moody lately.
I guess I have been at that. I'm sorry, Jules, I've just had a lot on my mind of late. You, for instance.
Me? You were thinking about me?
Of course, and why not? After all, you were in a car crash.
Oh, right. But you don't have to worry. I'm fine, better than ever, in fact.
Darcy said something similar after her accident. Can you unpack that a bit?
Well, for me, my physical injuries are almost healed, but more than that, I've had an even greater healing inside. I became a Christian.
Greetings, Renee, and welcome. I’m your host. My name is Leonid.

To start, I know of the conflict you’ve been feeling of late. Now that your sister is also a daughter of the King, you’re torn between the steady everydayness of the present and the unknown paths of the future.
Then all that stuff with Jules Kendall
What do you think?
I knew it. I knew it.

1027.s: Inside the Imagination Station, Renee follows a philosopher who grants her greatest wish… with unexpected results. Meanwhile, Connie takes her own journey with a long lost friend.
q: Ladies and gentlemen, friends, family and honored guests, welcome to this year’s Nobel Prize Ceremony
I’m at the Nobel prizes. I’ve always wanted to attend the ceremony.
There’s more to it than merely attending. The Nobel Prize in Mathematics is awarded to Renee D. Carter
You brought me to downtown Odyssey. I thought we were going on an adventure, not to some place I see almost every day.
Well, there’s no need for you to go on an adventure when you’re already in one.
I’m in an adventure?
Of course. The greatest adventure you could ever ask for.
Your perfect future isn’t heaven, it’s knowledge. To know, and now you do. You know your future, your life after death, because you programmed it. You did this.
But that’s not fair.
Beg to differ. You’re getting exactly what’s fair, exactly what you deserve. Pick a door, Renee.
You must pick a door.
Pick a door!
No!!! End program! End program! End program! I need to get out of here.

Each person through the smallest deeds and tiniest actions or inactions is helping others progress towards the light, or the darkness. It’s the simple acts of kindness and love, of willing the good of other people. That is the greatest, most noble, most important adventure of all.
I must have fallen asleep. It’s so peaceful here. At least it was. Hi, Jules.
Connie, where are you?
The Riley-Clemmens farm. I took your advice and went for a drive. Why, where are you?
At Whit’s End.
Hey, it’s only 12:30. You weren’t scheduled till three.
Well, I forgot the day was a half day at school, teacher in-service. So, I came in early, and it’s a good thing that I did because I had to open.
What, why? Where’s Renee?
You’ve got me. She hasn’t shown up and the noon rush has started. I need help.
Yeah, okay, okay, I’m on my way.

1028.s: Connie and Jules look for ways to help Renee as she sets out on her most serious path yet - one that leads to places she's not sure she wants to go.
q: Is it really that big of a deal, even if she actually went on this adventure?
Jules, the Life After Death program is nothing to mess around with. It terrified both Tom Riley and Eugene Meltsner
He was in the hospital in a coma.
Connie, I didn’t know it was dangerous, I promise.
It’s not your fault, Jules. It’s more my fault. I noticed she was acting strangely, but I never asked her about it.
Think about it. Where did both of us go when we were faced with something we didn’t want to deal with?
We went back to California.
Exactly. To the place that made sense to us.
So you think Renee Carter
It looks that way.
You can’t take a bus to Scotland.
No. But there’s a bus from Odyssey to a place that has an international airport.
She’s on her way to Chicago.
I need to make a call.
God, I don’t know if you are out there, which is why I’m in this situation. But, if you are there, then I’m asking you to help me calm down. Or better yet, help me forget, please.
What is it that we all believe?

There are things in life that are eternal and they point to an eternal God. It is how we know there is right and wrong in the world, and that it’s worth protecting the right and fighting the wrong. It’s what inspired Galileo and Kepler and so many of the founders of higher learning institutions. It fosters true beauty, joy, and unconditional hope.
It’s what made me forgive a drunken man for hurting me.
It’s what makes me love you despite our disagreements. It’s what gives life meaning and purpose, and all the knowledge and intellect in the world can’t hold a candle to it.
You’re not making much sense.
Aye. Cause none of it makes sense. All I truly know is that when I got on the bus I did not think I needed a savior. And now that I am off it, I know I do.
Dear, dear Mr. Whittaker, will you please tell me what must I do to be saved?
Are you sure?
Oh, Renee, of course I will.

1029.s: When a local fire and a clipped quote put Whit in the media crosshairs, he takes a step back to hear how his friends' lives have been changed by God.
q: Were those fire trucks?
Yeah. I wonder where they're headed.
It must be bad for them to send two trucks.
There's smoke above the trees! Something is on fire in downtown Odyssey!
I have a counselor in my heart now. He's teaching me the right words. It's made me less anxious and stronger. I might even go so far as to say He's made me a better mom.

I know. And that used to be me. Not willing to change even though I wasn't going anywhere in life. I look back at the old songs I used to write, really depressing and hopeless, but last week I wrote one that had a verse about that moment after you go to the optometrist and they dilate your eyes. Afterword, the whole world seems brighter. The lyrics might be silly, I know, but I feel like that's my life since I came to Christ, brighter, more beautiful.

Years ago, I was given a choice whether or not to re-enlist or stop being an active Marine. I didn't hesitate. I re-enlisted. I told Carla it was because I wasn't done serving my country, which was true. But there was another reason. I didn't know my purpose. I thought my life would be pointless if I wasn't actively serving.
Yeah, yeah, I understand.
But the other night, I was reading the Bible with Wyatt. We came across a verse that neither of us understood, and that's when I called you.
Ah, the Philippians 2 phone call.

Right, right. After you explained it to us, Wyatt and I talked about it and we prayed together. As soon as I said amen, I realized something: that there weren't many things I had done in my life that were more important than what I had just done: studying the Bible with my son.
So, Whit, I asked everybody here to come and pray for you.
How wonderful. Yes, this is something I need, always.
For my birthday?
Well, yes, for that and one other thing. Buck and I are getting baptized on Sunday.
That’s the best news I’ve heard in a long time.

The fact that I'm getting in the water on Sunday and telling everyone that I'm trusting God to be in control of my entire life, well, that's pretty big for me. If I'm going to get anywhere in life, I have to learn to trust. And I do now. But this time, I'm trusting in exactly the one person I should be: Jesus.

I want everyone to look around at the people in this circle. Not long ago, most of you wouldn't have been here. Think about that: Ron, Wyatt, Jules, Buck, Carla. And just this week, Renee and I prayed together in a bus station. All have come to faith in Christ in such a short time. God's doing something really special in Odyssey. There's no denying it. We need to remember that, no matter what's happening around us or to us. Connie, you've been very concerned about my feelings these past few days. I appreciate it. But the truth is, my joy isn't dependent on my circumstances. It's dependent on God. He is the source of our hope, our faith, and our joy.
You've suffered a terrible loss, Gloria. But God loves you and wants a relationship with you. He'll bless you just like He has so many people in Odyssey, if you let Him.
Thank you, Mr. Whittaker.

1030.s: In his latest “Knox On” podcast, Pastor Wilson shares stories about giving and how God is faithful to meet our needs.

1031.s: Mr. Whittaker promotes Connie to manager of Whit's End, leaving her to hire a new employee as he prepares to leave town.
q: So, you’ll hire someone then?
I was actually thinking the new manager would.
New manager?
If she takes the job. What do you say?
Me, a manager? I don’t know, that’s a big responsibility.
Well, you’ve learned a lot here. You are ready for this.
Well, how did it go?
Pretty sure I bombed the interview.
You gave the interview.
It was 50-50.
More important than that, it’s because of what we can do for Paxton
What’s that?
